- `821-dispute-resolution-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-negotiation-ladders-mediation-expert-determination-jurisdiction-maps-continuity-orders-and-no-heavy-power-by-hostage-dispute.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, **what information chain belongs to it**, **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**, and **what decision-rule chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what dispute-resolution chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should rely on recorded negotiation and visible member-side escalation, shared-service backbones should use negotiation-first ladders with mediation, technical determination, continuity protection, and public-law endpoints, bounded functional authorities should publish jurisdiction maps and interim continuity orders, and general-purpose territorial tiers should rely on ordinary justice and constitutional routes rather than permanent bargaining by hostage dispute.
- `822-asset-and-liability-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-member-owned-infrastructure-ring-fenced-balance-sheets-handback-maps-contingent-obligations-and-no-heavy-power-by-orphaned-balance-sheet.md` — When the archive has already established that a cross-boundary problem is real, chosen the honest form, and said who governs, pays, operates, votes, and hears disputes, it should still require one compact **asset-and-liability chain**: thin connectors should own almost nothing beyond trivial co-ordination tools; shared-service backbones should keep political title with the principals unless a clearly bounded common vehicle is justified; bounded functional authorities may hold and steward system-critical assets and named liabilities inside a ring-fenced public balance sheet; and general-purpose territorial tiers should carry visible asset, debt, reserve, and handback constitutions rather than hiding real sovereignty in host property, off-book obligations, or exit chaos.
- `823-contracting-boundary-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-light-support-buying-principal-owned-commissioning-chartered-concessions-change-control-and-no-heavy-power-by-contract-escape-hatch.md` — When the archive has already established that a cross-boundary problem is real, chosen the honest form, and said who governs, pays, operates, votes, hears disputes, owns the assets, and can unwind the map, it should still require one compact **contracting-boundary chain**: thin connectors may buy only light support and must not become hidden commissioners of core public systems; shared-service backbones may buy pooled administrative tools and support services while political title remains visibly with the principals; bounded functional authorities may procure, franchise, or concession the named system they are chartered to govern, but only through a visible commissioner spine, hard change-control, and full public review; and general-purpose territorial tiers may use contracts as delivery instruments without letting procurement, concessions, PPPs, or managed-service deals become constitutional escape hatches for powers that should remain politically owned.
- `824-regulatory-and-enforcement-boundary-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-signal-routing-joined-up-inspections-bounded-permitting-public-sanctions-and-no-heavy-power-by-shared-badge.md` — When the archive has already established that a cross-boundary problem is real, chosen the honest form, and said who governs, pays, operates, votes, publishes, contracts, owns, and can unwind the arrangement, it should still require one compact **regulatory-and-enforcement-boundary chain**: thin connectors may align standards proposals, share risk signals, and route cases but must not issue permits or sanctions in their own name; shared-service backbones may pool intake, inspection support, and specialist process while the political principals retain visible legal title to permissions and coercive acts; bounded functional authorities may license, inspect, direct, and sanction only inside a named public remit with risk-based proportionality, separation from operation, and live review routes; and general-purpose territorial tiers may carry broader permitting and enforcement constitutions without letting host badges, fee addiction, or delegated vendor discipline become hidden sovereignty.
- `826-mandate-source-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-assembly-voice-council-confidence-metro-public-mandates-regional-investiture-national-confidence-and-treaty-delegation.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should governing authority at each scope get its mandate?** with scale-matched defaults rather than a direct-election fetish: assembly voice and recallable stewardship at micro-local scale, elected councils as the primary democratic source in municipalities, whole-territory public mandates for metropolitan governments that can bind a real urban system, assembly-invested regional government where a region genuinely carries platform functions, parliamentary or assembly-confidence national government as the default source of executive authority, and treaty- or charter-derived delegation with bounded parliamentary and public complements for plurilateral and global bodies.
- `832-oversight-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-witness-municipal-scrutiny-metro-audit-national-watchdogs-and-treaty-review.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should each scope ordinarily be scrutinized and corrected once it has real public authority?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one watchdog fetish: **micro-local bodies should rely mainly on open meetings, visible records, rotation, and cheap escalation rather than a miniature oversight state; municipalities should be the first level with a full public oversight kit of chamber scrutiny, independent external audit, complaint or ombuds routes, disclosure, and ordinary legality review; metropolitan and regional governments should own equally real audit and redress lanes rather than borrowing them permanently from a host city or ministry; national government should carry the fullest fourth-branch and court-backed oversight constitution; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound but still face visible member scrutiny, independent audit and evaluation, complaint and ethics channels, and published review cycles rather than secretariat self-marking**.
- `833-coercion-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-witness-municipal-civil-enforcement-regional-police-platforms-national-force-monopoly-and-treaty-bound-restraint.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should coercive and enforcement power ordinarily live at each scope?** with scale-matched restraint rather than one badge fetish: **micro-local bodies should default to witness, de-escalation, and referral rather than general coercive authority; municipalities should be the first ordinary home of civil enforcement, inspections, nuisance abatement, and everyday public-order administration under ordinary law; metropolitan governments should hold only those bounded cross-boundary enforcement and emergency-coordination powers that shared systems actually require; regional or provincial governments may honestly house large territorial police, emergency, and regulatory platforms where the constitutional order truly assigns them; national government should carry the thickest monopoly over criminal law, armed force, borders, and exceptional emergency concentration under the strongest rights and review discipline; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound, relying mainly on inspection, reporting, sanctions, certification, and tightly authorized operations rather than ambient upper-state police sovereignty**.

## anti-corruption-governance

- `534-extractive-resources-by-scope-local-consent-regional-cumulative-impacts-national-public-rents-and-global-just-transition-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat subsoil wealth as a temporary public endowment rather than a permanent license for frontier sacrifice: affected communities and Indigenous peoples should hold real consent, monitoring, grievance, and benefit-sharing power close to the site; regional bodies should govern cumulative impacts on water, housing, health, roads, labour markets, tailings, and emergency corridors across the wider extraction zone; nations should own licensing architecture, contract disclosure, beneficial-ownership rules, royalties, sovereign wealth or stabilization policy, closure liability, anti-corruption enforcement, and diversification strategy; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in transparency standards, trade and due-diligence rules, conflict prevention, and just-transition principles rather than letting a scramble for critical minerals recreate colonial extraction under green branding.
- `556-police-services-by-scope-neighborhood-legibility-municipal-or-county-operations-metropolitan-serious-crime-bureaus-national-standards-and-no-police-self-investigation.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **police services** as a **civilian, rights-bound, externally answerable public service** rather than as a self-defining armed caste: keep neighborhood contact and ordinary response close enough to communities to stay legible, size police organizations and custody/investigation support large enough to resist tiny-jurisdiction capture, push serious-crime, forensic, and cross-border investigation to metropolitan or regional institutions, reserve national government for legal floors, training, anti-corruption and narrow specialist support, and never allow **police self-investigation** or militarized political policing to masquerade as democratic order.
- `563-public-procurement-institutions-and-review-by-scope-local-needs-regional-shared-buying-national-rules-independent-challenges-and-no-government-by-emergency-sole-source-fog.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat public procurement as a governed public institution rather than a clerical back office: keep need definition, user-facing specification, and day-to-day contract management close to the service; use metropolitan, county, provincial, state, or other regional shared-buying bodies where market structure, scarce expertise, or repeated categories make pooling sensible; reserve national government for the procurement code, standard documents, core e-procurement rails, integrity controls, supplier-access baselines, independent complaint review design, and open-contracting discipline; keep the global layer narrow in interoperable standards, anti-rigging and anti-corruption cooperation, and fair cross-border conditions of competition; and never let emergency exemptions, framework sprawl, or vendor dependence turn public spending into shadow executive power.
- `564-anti-corruption-bodies-and-integrity-commissions-by-scope-local-routing-regional-case-development-national-specialization-and-no-government-by-heroic-commission.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not rely on one heroic anti-corruption commission: keep local complaint intake, disclosure routing, whistleblower handoff, and ordinary integrity advice close enough to be usable; place regional or state-level investigative and inspection capacity where corruption markets, procurement webs, and patronage chains cross municipalities or where tiny jurisdictions are too captured to investigate themselves; reserve national government for the preventive architecture required by law, high-level and cross-regional corruption, asset-declaration verification, beneficial-ownership tracing, international cooperation, and strategy coordination; keep the global layer narrow in standards, peer review, and transnational case support; and never let anti-corruption institutions become either decorative ethics theater or unreviewable prosecutor-states.
- `709-challenge-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-entry-routes-complaints-petitions-second-look-lanes-feedback-duties-and-no-public-voice-by-consultation-theater.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, and an evidence packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **challenge packet** naming who may raise what kind of challenge, through which front door, with what triage into complaint, petition, appeal, ombuds, whistleblowing, or regulatory lanes, on what clocks, with what feedback and anti-retaliation duties, so the field can be corrected by the governed instead of merely observed by them.
- `768-whistleblower-protection-and-reporting-person-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-safe-channels-confidentiality-triage-anti-retaliation-remedy-and-no-integrity-by-punishing-disclosure.md` — Ideal governments should treat whistleblower protection as **a protected truth-telling lane inside the constitutional integrity system rather than a moral appeal to personal courage**: people who report wrongdoing on reasonable grounds should have safe internal and external channels, confidentiality or anonymity where lawful, trained intake and triage, protection against retaliation, interim support while disputes are live, and real corrective remedies, so institutions cannot purchase silence by making disclosure personally ruinous.

## appeals

- `404-contestable-automation-and-appeals-routing.md` — No consequential automated system should be allowed to operate without a visible path from **notice** to **reason** to **override** to **appeal** to **remedy**.
- `419-production-monitoring-fed-by-complaints-appeals-and-user-feedback.md` — A public automated system is not adequately monitored if it only watches internal metrics. **Complaints, appeals, operator reports, and affected-user feedback** should be treated as first-class operational telemetry and folded into the system’s monitoring, evaluation, and review loop.
- `421-public-impact-assessment-dossiers-and-peer-review-before-live-use.md` — Before public automated decisions go live, operators should publish a compact **assessment dossier** that combines impact scoring, context-specific rights analysis, independent review, and accountable sign-off.
- `425-portable-appeal-packets-and-log-retention.md` — Contestability fails when the evidence trail is scattered or ephemeral; every consequential AI-assisted decision should leave behind a portable review packet built from logs, provenance, and operator actions.
- `434-override-telemetry-escalation-queues-and-second-look-sampling.md` — Human oversight is not real unless overrides, disagreements, and stop decisions are counted, reviewed, and turned into operating changes instead of disappearing as private friction.
- `436-redaction-gateways-protected-attribute-filters-and-exception-registers.md` — Public AI systems should default to **redaction before inference**: block or strip unnecessary personal data, prohibit protected-attribute and emotion inference by default, and require a named, reviewable exception register for the rare cases law explicitly permits.
- `439-legal-authority-maps-scope-gates-and-jurisdiction-labels.md` — A public AI system should not reach consequential use until the operating team can name the **decision it affects, the authority that permits it, the scope test that brings it under governance, and the review route that governs challenges to it**.
- `442-maker-checker-separation-independent-challenge-and-fallback-review.md` — Consequential public AI should separate **builders, operators, approvers, and reviewers** enough that no single role can quietly tune, approve, and act on the same system without an independent second look or documented compensating control.
- `444-privileged-access-tiers-role-restricted-logs-and-admin-session-review.md` — Public AI should restrict sensitive administration and log access by role, record privileged actions in detail, and subject elevated sessions to routine review so governance evidence is not left inside an unexamined operator back room.
- `445-explicit-release-decisions-frozen-public-surfaces-and-no-release-records.md` — Consequential public AI should not move from “reviewed” to live use by implication; institutions should record an explicit publish, hold, or no-release decision and preserve the exact public-facing governance surface that was in force at that moment.
- `447-audience-exact-disclosure-classes-exposure-boundaries-and-review-lanes.md` — Governance artifacts for consequential public AI should carry exact audience and exposure labels so public, affected-person, operator, reviewer, regulator, supplier, and privileged-admin lanes cannot be silently mixed or widened.
- `448-governance-state-honesty-request-review-approval-and-live-separation.md` — Consequential public AI should not collapse roster presence, active review request, completed review, approval, queued release, and live operation into one fuzzy status; each state should mean one thing, stay scoped to a named basis, and surface explicit repair when that basis goes stale.
- `450-contemporaneous-decision-witnesses-what-was-shown-and-dispute-reconstruction.md` — Consequential public AI should preserve a compact contemporaneous witness of what the system showed, decided, and relied on at the moment of action so later appeals, incidents, and audits do not have to reconstruct governing state from overwritten traces and memory.
- `454-preview-sufficiency-omitted-governance-non-inference-and-next-honest-action.md` — A snippet, card, toast, queue row, portal tile, or case preview for consequential public AI should state what the preview is sufficient for, what governance-bearing facts are omitted, which tempting inferences are refused, and what the next honest action is.
- `456-history-preserving-public-record-navigation-stable-anchors-and-honest-fragment-failure.md` — Consequential public-AI records, notice pages, case portals, and appeal surfaces should preserve stable addresses and anchors, create browser history only when the user crossed a meaningful state boundary, and fail honestly when a cited deep link or fragment no longer resolves.
- `458-dependence-aware-assurance-counts-shared-origin-witnesses-and-pseudo-independence-guards.md` — Public-AI assurance should record shared origins across tests, judges, vendors, datasets, prompts, and reviewers so multiple agreeing checks are not mistaken for multiple independent grounds for trust.
- `459-approval-freshness-classes-no-renewal-by-use-and-rereview-clocks.md` — Consequential public-AI approvals, waivers, elevated grants, and standing adoption decisions should carry explicit freshness classes and rereview clocks, and continued use or silence should not silently renew them.
- `468-fused-governance-rollups-blocker-inventories-and-macrostate-decomposition.md` — Consequential public-AI dashboards, queue summaries, and readiness badges should decompose into named substates and live blocker inventories rather than one fused macrostate, so a green rollup cannot hide stale evidence, blocked disclosure, or missing review.
- `470-intake-failure-classification-handoff-vs-artifact-and-manual-fallback-lanes.md` — When consequential notices, appeals, evidence packets, or supplier submissions fail to arrive, open, or register, the archive should distinguish bad artifact from bad delivery or handoff and preserve a typed manual fallback lane so rights do not disappear into one broken digital path.
- `472-case-lineage-withdrawal-cancellation-supersession-and-reopen-receipts.md` — Consequential public-AI cases, appeals, incidents, and review requests should preserve typed lineage across withdrawal, cancellation, supersession, duplicate-merge, expiry, and reopening, with predecessor-successor links and reasoned receipts, so no rights-bearing matter silently disappears.
- `477-basis-locked-pending-states-drift-guards-and-explicit-reissue.md` — Consequential public-AI requests, reviews, approvals, queue entries, and ready states should stay locked to the exact basis they were issued against, and should fall back to stale-or-reissue-needed rather than silently following later drift, retargeting, or rebuild.
- `478-structured-decision-traces-minimal-bindings-reason-codes-and-safe-explain-surfaces.md` — Consequential public-AI actions should leave behind a stable decision-trace object that records the governing basis, route, inputs used, matched rule or model context, reason codes, obligations, and redactions in a compact safe form, so explanations, appeals, and incident review do not depend on backend folklore or prose reconstruction.
- `479-governance-diff-surface-registries-canonical-review-planes-and-drift-funnels.md` — Consequential public-AI programs should maintain a canonical registry of governance diff surfaces so review, release, and audit can say which change planes exist, which ones were checked, and which new surface types require explicit admission instead of silently creating fresh drift territory.
- `482-queue-dwell-honesty-service-clocks-and-anti-starvation-escalation.md` — Rights-bearing requests, reviews, appeals, exceptions, and incident items should expose when their clock started, what service window or expectation applies, whether they are merely queued or actively worked, what is blocking progress, and how escalation happens when dwell exceeds thresholds, so “under review” cannot launder starvation.
- `484-epistemic-status-tags-evidence-classes-and-no-authority-by-hedge.md` — Consequential public-AI claims, notices, summaries, incident updates, and review packets should mark each load-bearing statement as observed, measured, attested, reported, inferred, disputed, or unknown, with an explicit confidence class tied to evidence completeness, so hedged prose cannot quietly launder uncertainty into authority.
- `487-subsidiarity-by-default-burden-of-proof-for-upward-scope-and-recallable-delegation.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should allocate power by a rebuttable subsidiarity rule: default to the smallest scope that can solve the problem, move upward only when spillovers, pooling, rights floors, common-pool integrity, or peace-and-standards needs require it, and keep upward delegation explicit, reviewable, and reversible where possible.
- `491-adaptive-boundaries-functional-geographies-prior-consultation-and-no-frozen-maps.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat boundaries as governed instruments rather than sacred relics: review them when functional geographies drift, consult affected communities before changing them, prefer overlap or joint authority where clean redrawing is impossible, and never let inherited lines quietly dictate today’s housing markets, watersheds, or service systems.
- `494-remedy-stack-by-scope-local-ombuds-administrative-justice-constitutional-review-and-subsidiarity-safe-access.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should give people remedies at the closest level that can actually cure the problem while preserving escalation paths upward: frontline complaint and ombuds channels for ordinary maladministration, administrative and ordinary courts for legal error, constitutional and federal review for rights and competence conflicts, and only subsidiary supranational or treaty review where domestic remedies have been exhausted or are unavailable.
- `514-justice-by-scope-local-resolution-city-legal-aid-regional-courts-national-codes-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern justice by keeping low-stakes dispute resolution, legal help, and problem sensing close to daily life; sizing trial and appellate institutions to real catchments rather than arbitrary municipal lines; reserving criminal codes, procedural guarantees, judicial independence, prosecution architecture, and equal access floors to the nation; and treating the global layer as a narrow guarantor of rights, cooperation, and last-resort review rather than as a substitute domestic judiciary.
- `537-outer-space-and-orbital-commons-by-scope-local-hosting-regional-spaceports-national-authorization-and-global-sustainability-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat outer space as a global commons of use rather than a frontier of silent enclosure: local communities should hold real say over launch sites, tracking stations, astronomy impacts, land use, emergency planning, and public benefit where space infrastructure touches the ground; regional institutions should coordinate spaceport corridors, environmental review, disaster interfaces, and research ecosystems where activities spill across jurisdictions; nations should authorize and continuously supervise national activities in space, register objects, govern liability, spectrum and orbital use discipline, public research, procurement, and security constraints, and prevent private launch markets from becoming lightly regulated sovereignty proxies; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in non-appropriation, peaceful use, registration, debris mitigation, conjunction information-sharing, and long-term sustainability rather than letting orbit become an unmanaged congestion market.
- `542-intergovernmental-machinery-lawful-councils-compacts-formula-finance-and-no-government-by-summit.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern the spaces **between** levels through lawful intergovernmental machinery—standing councils, mandatory consultation, rule-bound compacts, formula finance, shared operational forums, and independent dispute routes—so coordination is continuous, reviewable, and bounded rather than a contest of press conferences, emergency bargaining, and grant blackmail.
- `543-special-purpose-authorities-and-arms-length-bodies-narrow-remits-hard-charters-open-books-and-sunset-review.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should use special-purpose authorities, public corporations, and arm’s-length bodies only where a bounded cross-municipal or regional function — such as transit, utilities, watershed management, market regulation, or other impartial technical tasks — genuinely requires them; give them narrow remits, hard-law charters, published financing, public accountability, and periodic review; and never let them become shadow governments, patronage shelters, or constitutional escape hatches.
- `545-regulators-inspections-and-enforcement-role-clarity-risk-based-proportionality-due-process-and-no-government-by-shakedown.md` — An ideal polity should treat regulators and inspectorates as bounded public-law institutions whose job is to reduce real harm, preserve fair conditions, and keep essential systems trustworthy; give them clear missions, enough independence to resist improper influence, enough accountability to remain public servants, risk-based and proportionate enforcement tools, visible appeal routes, and budgets not addicted to penalties; and never let licensing, inspection, or fines become a substitute tax system, a patronage machine, or a theatre of arbitrary power.
- `546-public-enterprises-and-state-owned-enterprises-explicit-rationales-separated-roles-hard-budget-constraints-and-open-books.md` — An ideal polity may own and operate enterprises where public ownership is genuinely justified — for natural monopolies, essential network infrastructure, strategic resilience, mission-critical finance, or other clearly stated public purposes — but it should publish why it owns them, separate ownership from regulation and policy-making, state public-service obligations explicitly, compensate them transparently, impose hard budget constraints, keep boards and books professional and visible, and review the portfolio often enough that public enterprise does not become a hiding place for patronage, off-balance-sheet debt, or anti-competitive favoritism.
- `548-legislatures-by-scope-neighborhood-assemblies-municipal-councils-metro-chambers-federal-shared-rule-and-no-government-by-decree.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should fit its legislative institutions to scale: use direct assemblies and recallable delegates for micro-local stewardship, elected municipal and metropolitan councils where visible services and shared systems need contestable public rulemaking, regional and federal chambers where territory and shared rule must be represented, and national parliaments strong enough to legislate, budget, scrutinize, and police delegated law rather than surrendering government to executives, party cartels, or decree.
- `550-judiciaries-by-scope-neighborhood-entry-regional-trial-courts-national-apex-review-and-global-rights-backstops.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should keep justice entry and informal problem-sensing close to daily life, organize ordinary first-instance and specialized courts at the smallest catchment that can sustain independence and competence, reserve apex review, constitutional interpretation, judicial-appointment safeguards, and equality before the law to the national level, and treat supranational or global courts as narrow rights and treaty backstops rather than as substitutes for a functioning domestic judiciary.
- `551-public-prosecution-by-scope-local-diversion-regional-ordinary-charging-national-integrity-cases-and-no-government-by-prosecutor.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should keep prosecution lawful, impartial, and scale-matched: use community-near intake and diversion for ordinary low-level harm, size ordinary charging offices to regional or metropolitan court catchments large enough for competence and independence, reserve national prosecutors for public-corruption, state-integrity, and interjurisdictional serious crime, and keep cross-border prosecutorial cooperation narrow, reviewable, and rights-bound so neither local vendetta nor central spectacle can govern by charge.
- `552-electoral-administration-by-scope-local-voter-service-municipal-operations-regional-tabulation-national-standards-and-no-government-by-partisan-referee.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat electoral administration as a permanent, professional, and politically impartial public function: keep voter-facing service and polling logistics close enough to work, size counting and tabulation to real operational catchments, reserve core rulemaking and national certification architecture to a permanent central authority bounded by law, route disputes quickly to competent review bodies, and never let the government of the day become the referee of its own election.
- `557-detention-corrections-and-reentry-by-scope-local-contact-and-release-links-regional-custody-probation-national-rights-floors-and-no-government-by-warehousing.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **detention, corrections, and reentry** as a **strictly limited, rights-bound, reintegration-oriented part of justice** rather than as a hidden warehousing system: keep local roles focused on family contact, service continuity, diversion support, and release preparation rather than long-term cage sovereignty; use metropolitan or regional institutions for most remand custody, prisons, probation, parole, health continuity, and professionally managed inspectionable facilities; reserve national government for penal law, decarceration incentives, independent monitoring, and non-negotiable humane-treatment floors; and never allow **jails, prisons, or release systems to become opaque human storage insulated from courts, health systems, and society**.
- `559-access-to-information-and-data-protection-institutions-by-scope-local-records-help-municipal-disclosure-discipline-regional-casework-national-independence-and-no-government-by-secrecy-or-panopticon.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **access-to-information and data-protection institutions** as a **paired constitutional circuit for democratic legibility and personal autonomy**: keep records help, routine request handling, and privacy-aware service design close to agencies and municipalities; use metropolitan, provincial, state, or other regional commissioners for much ordinary appeals and complaint casework where scale permits; reserve national government for the rights themselves, commissioner independence, common standards, difficult cross-sector investigations, and cross-border coordination; and never allow the same line ministries that benefit from secrecy or mass data collection to act as the final judges of openness and privacy.
- `561-districting-and-boundary-commissions-by-scope-local-polling-areas-municipal-wards-regional-mapmaking-national-equal-suffrage-rules-and-no-government-by-incumbent-cartography.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat districting and seat allocation as a periodic, law-bound integrity function: keep polling-area maintenance close to real voter-service geography, place most ward and constituency mapmaking in independent local or regional boundary bodies sized to the polity they serve, reserve national government for equal-suffrage rules, census-to-seat apportionment, protected exceptions, and judicially reviewable backstops, and never let incumbents quietly draw the map that chooses their next electorate.
- `563-public-procurement-institutions-and-review-by-scope-local-needs-regional-shared-buying-national-rules-independent-challenges-and-no-government-by-emergency-sole-source-fog.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat public procurement as a governed public institution rather than a clerical back office: keep need definition, user-facing specification, and day-to-day contract management close to the service; use metropolitan, county, provincial, state, or other regional shared-buying bodies where market structure, scarce expertise, or repeated categories make pooling sensible; reserve national government for the procurement code, standard documents, core e-procurement rails, integrity controls, supplier-access baselines, independent complaint review design, and open-contracting discipline; keep the global layer narrow in interoperable standards, anti-rigging and anti-corruption cooperation, and fair cross-border conditions of competition; and never let emergency exemptions, framework sprawl, or vendor dependence turn public spending into shadow executive power.
- `564-anti-corruption-bodies-and-integrity-commissions-by-scope-local-routing-regional-case-development-national-specialization-and-no-government-by-heroic-commission.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not rely on one heroic anti-corruption commission: keep local complaint intake, disclosure routing, whistleblower handoff, and ordinary integrity advice close enough to be usable; place regional or state-level investigative and inspection capacity where corruption markets, procurement webs, and patronage chains cross municipalities or where tiny jurisdictions are too captured to investigate themselves; reserve national government for the preventive architecture required by law, high-level and cross-regional corruption, asset-declaration verification, beneficial-ownership tracing, international cooperation, and strategy coordination; keep the global layer narrow in standards, peer review, and transnational case support; and never let anti-corruption institutions become either decorative ethics theater or unreviewable prosecutor-states.
- `573-administrative-procedure-permits-and-licenses-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-front-doors-regional-technical-review-national-procedure-codes-and-no-government-by-permit-maze.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **administrative procedure, permits, and licenses** as the **constitutional authorization layer** of government: keep lived fact-finding, pre-application help, and ordinary place-based intake close to communities and municipalities; pool specialist review and cross-boundary technical assessment regionally where risks or spillovers justify it; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the core procedural guarantees, common clocks, appeal architecture, and recognition rules that make the whole system legible; and use continental and global layers for interoperability, evidence exchange, and mutual recognition rather than for a fantasy of one world permit desk.
- `576-base-registries-identifiers-reference-data-and-interoperability-by-scope-community-error-surfacing-municipal-data-stewardship-regional-brokers-national-authoritative-sources-and-no-government-by-contradictory-copies.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **base registries, identifiers, reference data, and interoperability** as the **constitutional integration layer** of government: keep error surfacing, assisted correction, and local fact challenge close to people and firms; use municipalities and other frontline bodies as disciplined stewards and consumers of authoritative data rather than rival sovereign databases; pool interconnection, exchange infrastructure, and semantic support above fragmented local jurisdictions where scale adds competence; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for designating authoritative sources, assigning identifier rules, governing access, and maintaining shared code lists and metadata; and keep continental or global roles narrow enough to support cross-border evidence exchange, schemas, and semantic alignment without becoming a world master database.
- `580-asymmetric-decentralization-special-status-territories-and-no-one-size-fits-all-stack.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **asymmetry** as a disciplined constitutional tool rather than as a taboo or a patronage trick: keep a clear default stack for ordinary places, but allow differentiated powers, institutions, and finance for metropolitan areas, capital districts, islands, remote regions, indigenous or plurinational territories, and other genuinely exceptional geographies when functional scale, capacity, history, identity, remoteness, or constitutional settlement justify it; pair that flexibility with equal-rights floors, transparent criteria, published finance rules, review clocks, and routes into and out of special status; and reject both one-size-fits-all map worship and ad hoc dealmaking that turns territorial difference into permanent favoritism.
- `581-mandate-finance-congruence-unfunded-mandates-vertical-fiscal-imbalance-and-no-decentralization-by-fiscal-theater.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **mandate-finance congruence** as constitutional law rather than budget etiquette: no level of government should be assigned a durable public function unless the same settlement also names the revenue basket, transfer formula, equalization rule, borrowing limits, and capability backstop that make the function actually dischargeable; delegated tasks must come with commensurate resources, local self-government must include at least some real own-source fiscal room, and upward rescue must be visible and reviewable rather than leaving decentralization to degrade into blame-shifting.
- `583-subnational-distress-administrative-supervision-special-measures-handback-clocks-and-no-silent-recentralization.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **intervention in failing local or regional government as a lawful last-resort ladder**: ordinary supervision should be legality-bound and proportionate, support and co-production should come before takeover, financial distress and service collapse should trigger explicit temporary special measures only under published legal thresholds, essential services and rights routes must remain protected throughout, and every intervention should carry a reviewable restoration-and-handback path so rescue does not harden into permanent tutelage.
- `584-common-floors-local-headroom-explicit-preemption-rules-and-no-silent-override-by-upper-tier-convenience.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **preemption and override as explicit constitutional instruments rather than as ambient higher-tier privilege**: upper levels may set rights floors, solidarity guarantees, interoperability rules, and protections against genuine cross-border harms, but they should leave subnational governments real room to go further or adapt locally unless a law clearly names the conflict, states the protected interest, consults affected governments, provides transition and finance where duties are displaced, and subjects any ceiling preemption or field occupation to review rather than letting uniformity spread by habit.
- `586-function-transfer-packs-staff-assets-records-contracts-liabilities-and-no-reassignment-by-legal-text-alone.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **any transfer of a public function across levels of government as a full transfer pack rather than a sentence in a law**: whenever a competence moves, the same settlement should also name the effective date, service standard, staff lane, asset and lease inventory, contract and procurement treatment, records and data custody, ongoing-case handoff, fiscal lane, liability rule, transition authority, dispute route, and review clock, so that decentralisation or recentralisation cannot occur by moving the headline power while leaving the receiving government to inherit an empty shell.
- `592-local-ordinance-power-bylaws-framework-laws-review-lanes-and-no-self-government-by-administration-only.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should give **general-purpose local governments** a real but bounded **local ordinance / by-law power** within framework law — enough to make binding local rules on genuinely local matters, subject to legality review, rights floors, and explicit upper-tier reservations — so self-government does not collapse into mere administration of other people’s rules.
- `593-local-self-government-judicial-remedy-constitutional-standing-interim-relief-and-no-autonomy-without-recourse.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should guarantee **local and regional governments** a real **right of recourse to judicial remedy** — including standing against executive interference, a route to constitutional review where laws themselves wound self-government, and timely interim relief against irreversible harm — so autonomy is defended by law rather than left to negotiation, prestige, or endurance.
- `595-territorial-reorganization-incorporation-mergers-splits-status-change-and-no-map-surgery-by-managerial-fiat.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the creation, merger, split, annexation, abolition, and status change of territorial authorities as constitutional surgery rather than managerial tidying, so map reform remains lawful, consultative, alternatives-tested, continuity-safe, and reviewable instead of becoming a shortcut around self-government.
- `603-order-of-operations-for-ideal-multilevel-government-vocation-assignment-kits-connectors-asymmetry-and-no-reform-by-layer-shopping.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should be designed in a disciplined order: start from the class of problems and the real geography they inhabit, assign responsibilities by explicit scope tests, fit each chosen level with a minimum complete institutional kit, bind that kit to finance and capability, add coordination/review/equalization connectors, and only then allow principled asymmetry and transfer rules; reject reforms that start by picking a favored level first and inventing reasons afterward.
- `604-diagnosing-scope-misfit-overbuild-underbuild-duplicate-chains-orphan-functions-and-no-government-by-institutional-furniture.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should **periodically diagnose scope misfit** rather than merely inherit its jurisdictional stack: detect overbuilt levels, underbuilt levels, duplicate chains, orphan functions, paper metros or paper regions, false localism, and false centralism by testing whether each public problem has a real governing vocation, a visible lead for each lane of work, a minimum complete institutional kit, matched money and capability, and lawful connectors and review paths.
- `610-accountability-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-scrutiny-audit-disclosure-complaints-review-and-no-government-by-jurisdictional-gap.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **accountability home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, and administrative one: its own scrutiny forum, named records-and-disclosure duties, internal control and audit proportionate to risk, external audit and integrity jurisdiction, complaint and review routes that ordinary people can actually find, and explicit accountability for operators and contractors so the territory is not really governed in the gaps between municipalities, agencies, and the state.
- `616-planning-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-territorial-plans-plan-hierarchies-conformity-and-no-government-by-vision-deck.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **planning home** as well as democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, and service ones: a territorial planning authority with a real public plan, a declared hierarchy with municipal and state plans, visible conformity or compatibility rules, infrastructure-and-land-use coupling, amendment and review clocks, and no territorial government by advisory strategy deck.
- `618-regulatory-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-licensing-permits-standards-inspection-enforcement-and-no-government-by-operator-rulebook.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **regulatory home** as well as democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, service, planning, and capital ones: a visible territorial rulebook, named licensing and permitting lanes where risk demands them, a clear separation among rule-maker, regulator, operator, and reviewer, proportionate inspection and enforcement, and no government by operator rulebook.
- `623-redress-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-complaints-hearings-appeals-ombuds-and-no-government-by-jurisdiction-hunt.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **redress home** as well as democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, service, planning, capital, regulatory, contract, workforce, digital-operating, and emergency ones: one visible territorial path for complaint, reconsideration, hearing, appeal, ombuds, and judicial review, with reasons, clocks, and no government by jurisdiction hunt.
- `624-territorial-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-boundaries-membership-accession-exit-review-and-no-government-by-opt-in-map.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it should stop living on voluntary membership residue, project geography, or host-city convenience and instead acquire an explicit territorial home: a publicly declared boundary, named member units, clear rules for accession, exit, annexation or detachment, periodic but not perpetual review, and one authoritative map that matches the powers, money, plans, and obligations the territory actually carries.
- `625-temporal-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-pilot-clocks-review-amendment-succession-and-no-government-by-immortal-pilot.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it should stop living in indefinite provisional status and acquire an explicit temporal home: a declared start basis, time-bounded pilot and transition rules where experimentation is still honest, published review clocks, visible renewal and amendment routes, sunset for temporary derogations, and lawful succession or dissolution rules so the polity does not govern for decades as an “interim” arrangement that nobody ever formally chose to keep.
- `628-honesty-tests-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-vocation-complete-kits-constitutional-upgrade-and-no-jurisdictional-cosplay.md` — An ideal government at any scope is not defined by prestige, inherited labels, or institutional symmetry, but by an honest fit among governing vocation, territorial reality, democratic legitimacy, administrative capacity, money, review routes, and upgrade triggers: micro-local units should stay signal-rich and light; municipalities should be the first full governments of ordinary life; metropolitan and regional tiers should harden once shared territorial power is real; nations should guarantee equal citizenship, solidarity, and constitutional order without swallowing the stack; and continental and global bodies should remain competence-bounded compact and treaty narrow waists rather than drifting into jurisdictional cosplay.
- `632-scope-audit-triggers-review-packets-evaluation-lanes-and-no-constitutional-sleepwalk.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should keep a standing **scope audit registry** that uses territorial-impact, fiscal, democratic, and operational tripwires to trigger a typed **review packet** whenever real responsibility drifts away from the nominal map, so repair begins from evidence and laddered choice rather than from crisis improvisation or silent constitutional sleepwalk.
- `633-canonical-scope-registers-responsibility-matrices-exception-ledgers-and-no-government-by-jurisdiction-folklore.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should keep one **canonical public scope register** that shows, for each major function and lane of authority, the default legal home, territorial footprint, finance path, real delivery chain, exceptions, temporary deviations, review route, and next review date, so the stack is governed as an inspectable object rather than inferred from scattered statutes, grants, habits, and insider folklore.
- `635-scope-diff-packets-before-after-register-amendments-and-no-constitutional-change-by-side-effect.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require any legally or operationally material change to who governs what to ship with a public **scope-diff packet** against the canonical scope register, showing the before-and-after allocation, legal lane, consultation or consent route, jurisprudence impact, exception clocks, and review duties, so the stack cannot be rewired by side effect across statutes, grants, budgets, software, or emergency residue.
- `636-scope-opinions-clearance-lanes-signed-reasons-and-no-stack-change-by-self-certification.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require any materially stack-altering proposal to receive one public **scope opinion** from a named review lane that classifies whether the measure leaves the scope stack untouched, changes it lawfully through an ordinary lane, requires stronger consultation or consent, or is not adoption-ready at all, so the constitutional map cannot be rewritten by sponsor self-certification.
- `637-scope-overrides-explicit-departure-statements-review-clocks-and-no-constitutional-clearance-by-quiet-disregard.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should allow departure from a negative or conditional **scope opinion** only through one explicit public **scope-override statement** naming the disagreement, legal authority, reasons, rejected alternatives, temporary or permanent status, review and challenge clocks, and required register updates, so the review lane is neither a hidden veto nor a decorative memo and the stack cannot be changed by quiet disregard.
- `640-post-launch-scope-observability-variance-ledgers-rollback-lanes-and-no-stack-change-by-runtime-custom.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat materially stack-altering reforms as **actively observable after go-live**, with one linked post-launch variance ledger, short review clocks, named correction and rollback lanes, and explicit closure criteria, so the lived operation of budgets, staff, systems, supervision, and remedies cannot quietly become a different constitutional settlement by runtime custom.
- `642-scope-retirement-certificates-repeal-cleanup-successor-crosswalks-and-no-constitutional-ghosting.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require one public **scope-retirement certificate** whenever a materially stack-bearing competence, exception, body, supervisory lane, or temporary upper-tier hold is repealed, handed back, merged away, or superseded: retirement should close legal authority, budgets, systems, public channels, and review routes together, preserve historical memory, and refuse any afterlife of government by leftover residue.
- `645-scope-standstill-defaults-suspensory-effect-interim-relief-and-no-stack-change-by-racing-the-clock.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should give timely, credible challenges to materially stack-altering acts a visible **scope-standstill** or equally fast **interim-relief lane**, so the live constitutional stack cannot be rewritten simply because deployment moved faster than review.
- `647-scope-remand-discipline-cure-instructions-bounded-reopening-and-no-stack-redesign-by-reconsideration.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat **remand** in materially stack-altering disputes as a **bounded cure lane**, not as an open invitation to redesign the scope stack: a reviewing body that sends a package back for correction should specify exactly what defect must be cured, what remains frozen or intact, what consultation or consent must be rerun, and when the matter has crossed the line into a fresh packet, opinion, override, or constituent decision.
- `648-scope-functional-equivalence-rules-anti-circumvention-tests-and-no-stack-change-by-relabeling.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should classify **materially stack-altering moves by their real effect rather than by their chosen label**: if a grant condition, procurement framework, software default, model contract, coordination protocol, “pilot”, guidance note, or emergency instruction functionally reallocates who decides, who must comply, who pays, who may object, or which tier now governs in practice, it should travel through the same packet, opinion, override, register, and review lanes as any openly named scope change.
- `650-scope-estoppel-limits-reliance-sunk-cost-benefit-retention-and-no-stack-change-by-dependence.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should refuse to let **reliance, sunk cost, operational dependence, accepted benefits, or delayed objection manufacture constitutional title**: when a materially stack-altering move lacked the right authority, the right consent, or the right public lane, the answer should be cure, remand, override, rollback, or fresh authorization — not estoppel by familiarity, expense, or service dependency.
- `651-scope-prescription-limits-delay-bars-adverse-possession-and-no-stack-change-by-time-alone.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should not let **mere duration, delayed challenge, or long unlawful exercise** manufacture constitutional title: materially stack-altering arrangements may need continuity management, evidentiary caution, or prospective settlement after long operation, but they should not acquire lawful authority simply because they lasted, were hard to unwind, or went unchallenged for too long.
- `652-scope-desuetude-limits-abandonment-fictions-and-no-stack-change-by-atrophy.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should not let **non-use, weak use, under-enforcement, dormancy, or degraded capacity** silently extinguish protected competence: materially stack-bearing authority may require review, repair, reactivation, or even lawful reassignment, but it should not be treated as lost merely because it was not exercised often, boldly, or recently enough.
- `655-scope-retroactivity-limits-future-only-defaults-curative-acts-and-no-stack-change-by-backdating.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat **materially stack-altering acts as future-facing by default**: if a sponsor wants retroactive effect, retroactive validation, or a backdated effective date, it should have to travel through an unusually narrow, explicit, legally justified lane with preserved **review routes**, **judicial remedy**, and clear **legal authority** rather than letting the stack change by historical rewrite.
- `656-scope-transition-rules-for-pending-matters-cutover-queues-file-transfer-and-no-stack-change-by-midstream-grab.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require every **materially stack-altering act** to carry explicit transition rules for pending applications, permits, investigations, appeals, contracts, liabilities, records, and service queues — with named cutover dates, forum rules, file-transfer duties, and clock-preservation — so old matters do not silently jump sovereigns, stall in limbo, or get re-decided by midstream grab.
- `660-canonical-government-matrix-by-scope-legislature-executive-civil-service-fiscal-base-review-participation-and-no-full-stack-rewrite-for-every-tier.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should reuse one **canonical scope matrix** rather than reinventing every tier from scratch: micro-local units for witness and stewardship, municipalities for ordinary place government, metropolitan authorities for functional urban systems, regions for major territorial platforms and shared rule, nations for equal citizenship and redistribution, continental bodies for bounded cross-border compacts, and global institutions for treaty-bound peace, commons, alerting, and interoperability — each with a scope-matched decision forum, executive spine, civil-service density, fiscal base, review lane, and participation channel.
- `664-obligation-and-funding-formulas-by-problem-class-capacity-to-pay-equalization-polluter-pays-beneficiary-pays-risk-solidarity-and-no-one-formula-federalism.md` — Ideal multilevel and global governance should match each shared obligation to the right **apportionment rule** — capacity to pay for common institutions, equalization for rights floors, polluter-pays for harm control, beneficiary-pays for optional service gains, risk-based pooling for insurance and emergency reserves, and differentiated duties where histories and capabilities materially differ — so solidarity is explicit and reviewable rather than smuggled through arbitrary shares, annual bargaining, or one formula pasted across every tier and problem.
- `665-external-commitment-landing-paths-signature-ratification-transposition-direct-effect-operational-owners-and-no-treaty-by-press-release.md` — Cross-border and global commitments should not stop at signature or ratification: an honest polity should show the full **landing path** from external commitment to domestic legal effect, operational owners, budgeting, reporting, review, and subnational fit, so treaty participation does not masquerade as implementation.
- `666-compliance-ladders-for-shared-regimes-reporting-peer-review-inspection-dispute-settlement-remediation-suspension-and-no-treaty-by-voluntary-vibes.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **graduated compliance ladder** matched to the problem class — from reporting and peer review through technical verification, corrective action, dispute settlement, and where necessary suspension or other consequence — so co-operation does not depend on vibes and enforcement does not jump straight from silence to punishment.
- `667-differentiated-commitments-in-shared-regimes-reservations-opt-outs-derogations-transition-periods-territorial-application-review-clocks-and-no-uniformity-by-false-claim.md` — Shared regimes should maintain a **typed differentiation register** that distinguishes reservations, interpretive declarations, opt-outs, temporary derogations, transition periods, territorial applications, and enhanced-cooperation rings — with legal basis, scope, duration, review clock, and accession or withdrawal path — so a regime can use lawful variable geometry without lying that every member carries the same obligation.
- `668-shared-regime-change-ladders-review-conferences-amendments-protocols-annex-updates-tacit-acceptance-version-registers-and-no-regime-rewrite-by-secretariat-faq.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed change ladder** that distinguishes political guidance, interpretive guidance, implementing decisions, annex or technical updates, formal amendments, optional protocols, and refounding texts — each with its own adoption body, consent rule, objection or non-acceptance lane, entry-into-force logic, version register, and domestic landing path — so the regime can evolve without either paralysis or quiet constitutional rewrite by circular, dashboard, or FAQ.
- `669-shared-regime-entry-ladders-observers-signatories-provisional-application-accession-admission-thresholds-depositaries-entry-into-force-and-no-membership-by-affiliation-claim.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed participation ladder** that distinguishes observer, applicant, signatory, provisional applier, party/member, and deeper-module participant — with actor eligibility, admission body, deposited instrument, effective date, rights bundle, and reviewable public status — so the public can tell who is merely near a regime and who is actually bound.
- `671-shared-regime-representation-ladders-credentials-chief-delegates-alternates-observers-speaking-rights-committee-access-and-no-state-voice-by-self-appointment.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed representation ladder** that separates party or member status from delegate credentials, chief delegates from alternates and advisers, participants from observers, and speaking rights from voting rights — with accrediting authority, challenge lane, substitution rules, public roster, and functional-independence protections — so no one can conjure state or member voice by badge, donor access, press credential, or self-appointment.
- `675-shared-regime-initiative-and-text-sponsorship-ladders-agenda-items-proposals-amendments-cosponsorship-withdrawal-financial-screening-and-no-law-by-ghost-draft.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed initiation constitution** that separates agenda items, draft texts, amendments, explanatory memoranda, cosponsorship, withdrawal, late-paper handling, and **budget, financial, or administrative implications review** — so law does not enter the system by ghost draft, ambush paper, or sponsorless secretariat residue.
- `676-shared-regime-subsidiary-body-constitutions-committees-working-groups-expert-panels-terms-of-reference-report-back-sunset-and-no-shadow-regime-by-working-party.md` — Shared regimes should create **subsidiary bodies through explicit delegation instruments** that name mandate, composition, officer rules, procedure inheritance, publication and records rules, report-back duty, review or sunset, and non-delegable matters — so committees and working parties do not become permanent shadow constitutions.
- `678-shared-regime-independence-and-conflict-discipline-declarations-recusal-confidentiality-secondments-donor-firebreaks-and-no-expertise-by-capture.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed integrity constitution** that separates disclosure, assessment, management, recusal, exclusion, confidentiality, secondment controls, donor firebreaks, and post-service limits — so expertise, review, and advisory work do not harden into captured governance.
- `686-shared-regime-administrative-justice-constitutions-ethics-ombuds-investigations-management-evaluation-tribunals-and-no-secretariat-by-untestable-discipline.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed administrative-justice constitution** that separates confidential advice, ombuds or informal resolution, protected disclosure, investigations, interim protection, management review, disciplinary decision, independent tribunal review, and public jurisprudence memory — so the secretariat is not governed by rumor, retaliation fear, or untestable disciplinary power.
- `687-shared-regime-privileges-and-immunities-constitutions-functional-independence-jurisdiction-tax-customs-inviolability-waiver-and-no-sovereignty-cosplay.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed privileges-and-immunities authority map** that separates juridical personality, inviolability, immunity from legal process, archives and communications protection, fiscal and customs facilities, visa and entry support, category-specific treatment for representatives and officials, waiver authority, and abuse-control lanes — so institutional independence is protected without decaying into sovereignty cosplay, perk inflation, or unreviewable impunity.
- `688-shared-regime-private-law-claims-constitutions-contracts-torts-procurement-disputes-standing-claims-bodies-arbitration-insurance-and-no-immunity-without-remedy.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed review-and-remedy constitution** for private-law disputes that separates contract claims, procurement complaints, property and personal-injury claims, insurance recovery, amicable settlement, standing claims bodies where needed, arbitration clauses, waiver decisions, and payment authority — so the regime can preserve functional immunity from ordinary local courts without sliding into immunity without remedy.
- `689-shared-regime-territorial-presence-constitutions-headquarters-regional-offices-country-offices-liaison-posts-service-hubs-host-instruments-review-clocks-and-no-regime-by-landlord-permission.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed territorial-presence constitution** that separates headquarters, regional offices, country offices, liaison posts, service hubs, hosted outposts, and temporary mission footprints — with a named host instrument, mandate fit, reporting line, support package, review clock, and closure path for each — so institutional presence stays functional and reviewable instead of hardening into landlord permission, prestige geography, or office sprawl by habit.
- `691-shared-regime-information-classification-and-disclosure-constitutions-public-on-request-internal-confidential-strict-harm-tests-downgrading-external-sharing-and-no-secrecy-by-folder-folklore.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed information-classification-and-disclosure constitution** that separates public, request-only, internal working, confidential, strictly confidential, personal-data, and security-sensitive lanes — with named marking authority, handling rules, external-sharing conditions, review clocks, and request-and-review paths — so information is governed by visible rules instead of folder folklore, indiscriminate secrecy, or accidental disclosure by habit.
- `693-shared-regime-personal-data-and-privacy-constitutions-legal-basis-purpose-limits-minimization-subject-rights-transfers-breach-response-and-no-mission-by-data-drift.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed personal-data-and-privacy constitution** that separates lawful basis, purpose limitation, necessity and minimization, role allocation, sensitive-data treatment, retention, transfer rules, subject-rights handling, breach response, and accountability review — so mission work does not quietly become mission by data drift, uncontrolled onward sharing, or privacy promises with no operating spine.
- `695-shared-regime-enterprise-risk-and-internal-control-constitutions-risk-appetite-owners-registers-control-testing-exceptions-assurance-maps-and-no-governance-by-unknown-exposure.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed enterprise-risk-and-internal-control constitution** that separates risk appetite, risk taxonomy, owner assignment, principal-risk review, key-control design, control testing, exception handling, assurance mapping, and governing-body reporting — so operational exposure does not disappear into unknown exposure, stale registers, control folklore, or audit surprise government.
- `696-shared-regime-evaluation-and-learning-constitutions-workplans-independence-management-response-recommendation-tracking-after-action-review-and-no-regime-by-report-shelf.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed evaluation-and-learning constitution** that separates workplan setting, commissioning, evaluator independence, evaluation from audit or monitoring, management response, recommendation tracking, public release, and structured learning loops such as after-action review — so institutional learning does not decay into report shelfware, recommendation theater, or “lessons learned” with no decision route.
- `697-shared-regime-strategic-planning-and-results-constitutions-general-programmes-programme-budgets-theories-of-change-baselines-targets-reviews-and-no-mission-by-project-pile.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed strategic-planning-and-results constitution** that separates long-horizon strategy, medium-term programme budgets, theories of change, outcome and output ladders, indicator and baseline rules, target-setting, reprogramming, and mid-cycle review — so the institution does not drift into mission by project pile, target theater, dashboard government, or budget without strategy.
- `698-shared-regime-implementing-partner-and-pass-through-constitutions-due-diligence-workplans-cash-transfer-assurance-suspension-closeout-and-no-mission-by-subaward-fog.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed implementing-partner-and-pass-through constitution** that separates partner eligibility, due diligence, engagement risk, workplans, funding modality, milestone and expenditure reporting, assurance activity, corrective action, suspension, and closeout — so delivery through external partners does not dissolve into subaward fog, unreviewed dependency, or mission by pass-through habit.
- `704-control-plane-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-priorities-common-ledger-exception-queues-and-no-hidden-center-by-coordination.md` — Once the archive has split a field into lane-sized governments and published the seam rules between them, it should also publish one narrow **control-plane packet** for the field as a whole — naming the common goals, rights floors, shared metrics, review rhythm, exception queue, budget and capacity crosswalk, and upgrade triggers — so the stack can be steered and inspected as one public system without quietly inventing an undeclared super-tier that governs by coordination alone.
- `707-sunset-packets-for-obsolete-government-lanes-bodies-and-temporary-machinery-review-triggers-successor-homes-residue-registers-closure-proof-and-no-immortal-institutions-by-inherited-backlog.md` — Once a field has repair packets, it should also publish one **sunset packet** whenever review shows that a lane, body, or temporary governance machine no longer deserves to exist in live form — naming the trigger, the successor home or true extinction rule, the rights and service floors that still bind during wind-down, the residue register for cases, contracts, assets, staff, records, data, debt, and public-facing channels, the closure proof, and the reactivation rule — so obsolete institutions do not stay alive merely because they still have backlog, leases, websites, or logos.
- `708-evidence-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-shared-indicators-trigger-maps-blind-spot-registers-assurance-rhythm-and-no-government-by-dashboard-vibes.md` — Lane-typed government fields should publish one compact **evidence packet** that names the shared indicators, signal owners, trigger map, blind-spot register, and assurance rhythm used to judge the field — so control planes, mode shifts, repair packets, and sunset reviews run on explicit evidence with known gaps rather than on anecdotes, heroic operator memory, or dashboard theater.
- `709-challenge-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-entry-routes-complaints-petitions-second-look-lanes-feedback-duties-and-no-public-voice-by-consultation-theater.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, and an evidence packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **challenge packet** naming who may raise what kind of challenge, through which front door, with what triage into complaint, petition, appeal, ombuds, whistleblowing, or regulatory lanes, on what clocks, with what feedback and anti-retaliation duties, so the field can be corrected by the governed instead of merely observed by them.
- `710-participation-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-agenda-windows-method-fit-inclusion-duties-response-ledgers-and-no-public-input-by-one-off-hearing.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, an evidence packet, and a challenge packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **participation packet** naming which design and priority questions are open to public participation, at which policy-cycle phase, by which method, with which inclusion and response duties, so public input shapes the field before harm, drift, or redesign battles are forced into the complaint system.
- `711-oversight-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-audit-inspection-ombuds-parliamentary-scrutiny-follow-up-ledgers-and-no-self-certification-by-the-same-office.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, an evidence packet, a challenge packet, and a participation packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **oversight packet** naming which independent bodies outside the live control plane may inspect which questions, on what triggers and calendars, with what access powers, response duties, and follow-up ledger, so the field is not left certifying itself by the same office that designed, funded, or operated it.
- `712-amendment-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-change-classes-ratification-ladders-version-ledgers-drift-logs-and-no-field-redesign-by-memo.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, an evidence packet, challenge and participation packets, and an oversight packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **amendment packet** naming which changes are merely tuning and which are constitutional, who may propose them, what participation and scrutiny gates apply, what ratification ladder adopts them, when they take effect, and what version ledger plus drift log keeps the field from being redesigned by memo, queue custom, temporary exception, or software default.
- `713-delegation-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-principal-lane-reserved-powers-operator-chains-step-in-rights-and-no-public-duty-by-outsourced-wrapper.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, and amendment discipline for a field, it should also publish one narrow **delegation packet** saying which slice of the field is still constitutionally owned by the public lane, which execution work may be delegated to public bodies, contractors, concessionaires, nonprofits, co-operatives, or platforms, what powers remain non-delegable, what contract-management and records capacity the principal must retain, what step-in and handback rights keep continuity real, and what review route prevents public duty from disappearing into an outsourced wrapper.
- `714-fiscal-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-operating-base-equalization-spine-reserves-capital-lanes-and-no-government-by-grant-fog.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, and delegation rules for a field, it should also publish one narrow **fiscal packet** saying what recurring operating base actually funds the field, which lane holds budget and treasury authority, what equalization or solidarity rule corrects uneven burdens, what reserve and contingency ladder keeps shocks from becoming constitutional panic, what capital and debt lane is lawful, and what grants may supplement but not substitute for an honest money constitution.
- `715-capability-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-employer-lane-merit-floor-training-ladders-surge-rosters-and-no-government-by-borrowed-payroll.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, and a fiscal packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **capability packet** saying which lane is the employer of record and capability steward, what minimum in-house core the field must retain, what merit and qualification floor applies, what training and profession ladders sustain scarce skills, what secondment and surge rules are allowed, and what vacancy or churn triggers open repair or redesign — so the field does not rely on borrowed payroll, consultant memory, or permanent emergency staffing to remain governmental at all.
- `716-information-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-canonical-case-home-access-model-sharing-boundaries-retention-clocks-and-no-government-by-portal-shell.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, and a capability packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **information packet** saying where the field’s canonical case and record homes live, which surface is the system of record and which are only presentation or intake layers, what role-and-access model governs staff and delegates, what sharing boundaries and information agreements apply, what retention/export/handback rules preserve public memory, and what recovery path keeps the field governable when platforms, vendors, or host systems fail — so the field does not become government by portal shell, spreadsheet relay, or vendor-admin shadow.
- `717-asset-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-estate-fleet-equipment-condition-discipline-handback-and-no-government-by-orphan-assets.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, and an information packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **asset packet** saying which lane owns and stewards the field’s estate, fleet, equipment, depots, labs, stores, and critical spares; who holds custody, maintenance, calibration, and replacement duty; what condition and resilience floor applies; what lease, host-site, or operator dependencies exist; and what handback rule survives exit or transfer — so the field does not decay into government by orphan assets, lease camouflage, or maintenance exile.
- `718-service-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-whole-service-front-doors-route-classes-service-floors-continuity-and-no-government-by-front-door-scatter.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, an information packet, and an asset packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **service packet** saying what outcome the field’s service actually promises, which lane owns that promise, what front doors and route classes the public may use, what clocks and service floors bind, how channels and operators compose into one whole service, and what continuity and fallback rules survive overload, outage, provider failure, or redesign — so the field does not decay into government by front-door scatter, route roulette, or service-standard theater.
