- `541-government-by-scope-micro-local-stewardship-municipal-professionalism-metropolitan-democracy-regional-capacity-national-guarantees-and-global-narrow-waists.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not ask every scale to be the same kind of government: micro-local units should be light stewardship and signal institutions, municipalities should be general-purpose democratic governments with professional administration, metropolitan governments should be directly legitimated coordinators of shared urban systems, regional governments should carry landscape and major-service capacity, national governments should guarantee equal citizenship, redistribution, macro-stability, and constitutional rights, and global bodies should remain narrow, treaty-bound organs for peace, commons, alerting, and interoperability rather than aspiring to one undifferentiated world state.
- `555-independent-human-rights-and-equality-institutions-by-scope-local-access-regional-reach-national-paris-principles-cores-and-no-government-by-self-certified-rights-compliance.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **independent human rights and equality institutions** as part of the constitutional checking system rather than as decorative values offices: keep rights access and discrimination complaint entry close to ordinary life, use regional or state-level bodies where territorial scale and constitutional structure justify them, anchor a broad, pluralist, independent national human rights institution in strong law, give equality bodies real investigatory and assistance powers, coordinate specialised monitors across the rights ecosystem, and never let governments drift into **self-certified rights compliance**.
- `574-electronic-identification-signatures-seals-and-document-authentication-by-scope-community-attestation-municipal-enrollment-regional-federation-national-trust-frameworks-and-no-government-by-unverifiable-file.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **electronic identification, trust services, signatures, seals, time-stamps, and document authentication** as the **constitutional trust layer** of government: keep assisted enrollment, local fact correction, and ordinary witnessing close to people and firms; allow municipal and other frontline offices to serve as practical entry points into proofing and service use; pool federation and shared technical operations where subnational scale genuinely adds capacity; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the legal trust framework, assurance levels, authoritative source linkage, trusted lists, revocation discipline, and long-term verifiability of state acts; and use continental and global layers for standards, narrow recognition, and document authentication across borders rather than for a fantasy of one world identity stack.
- `583-subnational-distress-administrative-supervision-special-measures-handback-clocks-and-no-silent-recentralization.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **intervention in failing local or regional government as a lawful last-resort ladder**: ordinary supervision should be legality-bound and proportionate, support and co-production should come before takeover, financial distress and service collapse should trigger explicit temporary special measures only under published legal thresholds, essential services and rights routes must remain protected throughout, and every intervention should carry a reviewable restoration-and-handback path so rescue does not harden into permanent tutelage.
- `596-special-purpose-authorities-utility-districts-metro-agencies-and-no-government-by-quango-sprawl.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should use special-purpose authorities only as tightly bounded tools for real network, basin, corridor, or technical-governance problems, so shared systems can be run at the right scale without letting single-purpose bodies metastasize into a shadow constitution of opaque boards, off-budget debt, and blame-proof government.
- `602-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-steward-cells-municipal-general-government-metropolitan-systems-democracy-regional-territorial-platforms-national-guarantor-states-continental-compacts-and-global-treaty-narrow-waists.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should give each scope a distinct governing vocation and a minimum complete kit: micro-local units as visible stewardship and signal cells; municipalities as the first full general-purpose governments of ordinary life; metropolitan governments as democratically legitimated operators of shared urban systems; regional, provincial, or state governments as territorial-platform governments for landscapes, hospitals, grids, universities, and shared rule; nations as guarantor states for equal citizenship, redistribution, macro-stability, and constitutional settlement; continental bodies as bounded compact governments for cross-border mobility, markets, and infrastructures; and global institutions as treaty-bound narrow waists for peace, commons, alerting, and standards rather than as a fake world domestic state.
- `649-scope-waiver-discipline-authorized-consent-and-no-stack-change-by-silence-side-letter-or-wrong-organ.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat **any purported consent to a materially stack-altering move as valid only when it comes from the right organ, through the right public act, in the right lane, and with the right scope and duration**: consultation is not the same as surrender, operational co-operation is not the same as constitutional waiver, and no grant signature, side-letter, emergency reliance, platform click-through, budget acceptance, or failure to object quickly should count as lawful consent to permanent rescoping.
- `665-external-commitment-landing-paths-signature-ratification-transposition-direct-effect-operational-owners-and-no-treaty-by-press-release.md` — Cross-border and global commitments should not stop at signature or ratification: an honest polity should show the full **landing path** from external commitment to domestic legal effect, operational owners, budgeting, reporting, review, and subnational fit, so treaty participation does not masquerade as implementation.
- `692-shared-regime-digital-and-cyber-operating-constitutions-system-owners-identity-and-access-admin-tiers-change-windows-incident-response-vulnerability-disclosure-backups-recovery-vendor-lanes-and-no-secretariat-by-shared-password.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed digital-and-cyber operating constitution** that separates system ownership, identity and access, privileged administration, change and release control, incident response, vulnerability disclosure, vendor and cloud access, backup and restoration, recovery targets, and degraded-mode continuity — so the regime is not actually run through shared passwords, orphan systems, incident backlog, or recovery theater.
- `725-ideal-governance-stack-from-block-to-planet-territorial-tiers-functional-authorities-compact-unions-and-no-empty-tier-fetish.md` — An ideal governance stack from block to planet is not a neat ladder of identical states but a mixed constitutional order: micro-local bodies for witness and stewardship, municipalities for ordinary place government, metropolitan and regional tiers where urban systems or territorial platforms are real, nations for equal citizenship and solidarity, continental compacts for recurrent cross-border problems, global institutions for peace, alerting, commons, and interoperability, and bounded functional authorities in between whenever a watershed, corridor, grid, basin, port, or referral network plainly outruns ordinary administrative geography.
- `726-default-function-routing-table-for-ideal-governments-everyday-place-shared-systems-guarantor-duties-compact-unions-and-treaty-narrow-waists.md` — The archive should keep one compact **default routing table** for common public functions: route witness, stewardship, and micro-commons to micro-local units; ordinary daily place government to municipalities; shared urban systems to metropolitan government or narrow utilities; basin, hospital, university, corridor, and ecological platforms to regions or typed functional authorities; equal citizenship, redistribution, macro-stability, and constitutional settlement to nations; bounded cross-border markets, mobility, and corridors to compact unions; and genuinely planetary peace, alerting, interoperability, and commons baselines to treaty-bound global narrow waists — while forcing mixed fields to declare lead scope, support scopes, fiscal logic, and upgrade tests instead of choosing a level from scratch every time.
- `728-sideways-authority-packets-for-ideal-governments-bounded-remit-footprint-logic-board-fiscal-lane-review-clocks-and-no-functional-wrapper-without-constitutional-kit.md` — When the archive routes a function **sideways** into a bounded functional authority rather than into an ordinary territorial tier, it should default to one compact **sideways-authority packet** naming the real system footprint, the exact remit and exclusions, the principal public lane that still owns the wider constitutional bargain, the legitimacy and fiscal model, the review and participation routes, and the upgrade-or-exit triggers — so basins, corridors, grids, ports, referral networks, and similar in-between institutions stay governable without pretending to be full territorial governments or dissolving into quango fog.
- `735-rollback-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-failed-stabilization-return-authority-pending-matters-record-lineage-and-no-reversal-by-headline-alone.md` — Once the archive can say how a function should be routed (`726`-`728`), ratified (`729`), kept continuous (`730`), witnessed at cutover (`731`), temporarily hosted (`732`), cleanly closed (`733`), and tested through a bounded independent-live window (`734`), it should also keep one compact **rollback packet** for the case where the successor does not hold: classify the rollback type, name the interim principal and public route, preserve the legal and evidentiary state of pending matters, move money/staff/systems/keys with the reversal rather than by headline alone, and refuse both automatic restoration folklore and disguised permanent recentralization.
- `747-register-deconsolidation-and-standalone-restoration-packets-for-absorbed-tombstones-reversible-grouping-object-specific-re-expansion-and-no-permanent-flattening-by-catalog-convenience.md` — Once the archive can absorb standalone tombstones into grouped historical registers (`745`) and later move those grouped registers across homes or catalogues (`746`), it should also keep one compact **register-deconsolidation and standalone-restoration packet**: one bounded proof object for pulling one absorbed dead-object entry back out into its own standalone memorial surface when grouping proves too lossy, disputed, high-traffic, symbolically weighty, or operationally confusing, so the polity does not mistake one successful consolidation step for permission to keep every dead authority permanently flattened inside a catalogue.

## budget-governance

- `420-drift-budgets-rollback-paths-and-decommission-thresholds.md` — Public automation should not merely be monitored; it should come with **predefined thresholds for rollback, deactivation, or retirement**. A system that drifts past its risk tolerance should face a governed response path, including fallback operation and, where necessary, decommissioning.
- `465-confusability-budgets-disambiguation-floors-and-alias-collision-registers.md` — Consequential public-AI archives should budget confusability across system names, case states, model families, source labels, and decision routes, and require explicit disambiguation when nearby labels could cause misrouting or mistaken authority.
- `480-diagnostic-probe-budgets-targeted-capture-expiry-and-residue-attestation.md` — When consequential public-AI systems escalate from ordinary monitoring into deeper diagnostic capture, they should do so through a named probe plan with explicit scope, minimization, approval, expiry, export posture, and residue attestation, so incident response and troubleshooting do not quietly become open-ended surveillance or permanent debug residue.
- `504-defense-by-scope-civilian-control-civil-defense-no-subnational-war-machines-and-narrow-waist-collective-security.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should place war-making and armed defense at the national level under democratic civilian control and legislative budget authority, give subnational governments civil-defense and resilience roles without autonomous war machines, keep the military distinct from routine domestic order, and rely on treaty-bound regional alliances and a narrow global collective-security layer for external peace and aggression response rather than romanticizing either total sovereignty or world-state militarism.
- `505-land-and-housing-by-scope-secure-tenure-municipal-place-making-metro-housing-markets-regional-landscapes-and-national-fairness.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat housing and land as a scale-matched constitutional domain: micro-local institutions steward shared places and surface need; municipalities handle parcels, streets, permits, and neighborhood upgrading; metropolitan bodies govern the real housing market and fair-share growth; regions protect landscapes, basins, and food land; nations guarantee rights, anti-segregation floors, and housing finance; and global institutions supply rights baselines, data, and crisis support rather than pretending to zone the planet.
- `506-health-by-scope-primary-care-regional-capacity-national-risk-pools-and-global-alerts.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat health as a layered public good: neighborhoods and municipalities support prevention and the social conditions of health; community-facing systems deliver primary care as close as feasible to daily life; regions run hospital, laboratory, ambulance, and surge platforms; nations guarantee universal coverage, workforce strategy, medicines policy, and equitable finance; and global institutions coordinate alerts, standards, and outbreak response without pretending to administer ordinary care everywhere.
- `508-education-and-learning-by-scope-local-belonging-metropolitan-desegregation-regional-systems-national-rights-and-global-knowledge.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat education as a scale-matched constitutional domain: families, neighborhoods, and schools keep learning visible and belonging real; municipalities make attendance, facilities, and school-community life workable; metropolitan and regional bodies handle desegregation, transport, teacher labor markets, and specialized systems that outrun one town; nations guarantee the right to education, curricular floors, equalization, and qualification frameworks; and global institutions protect rights, support recognition, and widen access to knowledge without dictating one world syllabus.
- `510-networked-utilities-by-scope-local-access-metropolitan-mobility-basin-and-grid-coordination-national-universal-service-and-cross-border-interoperability.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern networked infrastructure by scale and function: neighborhoods and local institutions surface last-mile failure and build community resilience; municipalities manage rights-of-way, local distribution interfaces, streets, buses, water and sanitation operations where appropriate, and practical access; metropolitan bodies integrate mobility and other citywide networks that cross municipal borders; regions and basins govern watersheds, transmission corridors, balancing areas, and flood or drought constraints; nations guarantee universal service, backbone finance, regulation, and strategic resilience; and cross-border or global institutions set interoperability, shared-resource, and connectivity rules without pretending to run every local network.
- `513-food-systems-by-scope-local-access-regional-foodsheds-national-guarantees-and-fair-global-rules.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern food as a rights-bearing system rather than as a commodity silo: neighborhoods and local institutions surface hunger, diet, and access failures; municipalities shape markets, meals, land-use interfaces, waste reduction, and emergency food continuity; regional institutions govern foodsheds, logistics, processing, watershed and disease spillovers, and some fisheries or farming systems; nations guarantee the right to food, farm and labour law, food safety, social protection, strategic reserves, and coherent agrifood policy; and global institutions should coordinate standards, evidence, and crisis solidarity without subordinating food security to opaque trade power.
- `514-justice-by-scope-local-resolution-city-legal-aid-regional-courts-national-codes-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern justice by keeping low-stakes dispute resolution, legal help, and problem sensing close to daily life; sizing trial and appellate institutions to real catchments rather than arbitrary municipal lines; reserving criminal codes, procedural guarantees, judicial independence, prosecution architecture, and equal access floors to the nation; and treating the global layer as a narrow guarantor of rights, cooperation, and last-resort review rather than as a substitute domestic judiciary.
- `518-public-investment-and-procurement-by-scope-local-maintenance-metro-systems-national-capital-discipline-and-narrow-global-standards.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern public investment by keeping routine maintenance, small capital works, and user-visible asset stewardship close to the institutions that see failure first; using metropolitan and regional bodies for networked systems and place-wide project coordination; reserving capital budgeting rules, appraisal standards, equalizing finance, strategic procurement discipline, and infrastructure pipeline governance to the nation; and keeping the global layer narrow, focused on open technical standards, development finance, and anti-rigging or integrity cooperation rather than remote project micromanagement.
- `520-care-and-support-by-scope-household-reciprocity-municipal-services-regional-care-systems-national-social-insurance-and-global-worker-protection.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat care as civic infrastructure rather than private fallout: households, kin, and neighbors can contribute reciprocity but should not be the welfare state; municipalities should make childcare, disability support, elder support, and respite actually reachable; regional bodies should coordinate workforce pipelines, specialist and long-term-care systems, and discharge pathways that cross municipal lines; nations should guarantee paid leave, cash and service entitlements, labour standards, and financing pools; and the global layer should stay narrow but real in labour standards, migrant-care-worker protection, and knowledge exchange rather than pretending families can absorb demographic change forever.
- `521-disability-and-accessibility-by-scope-local-barrier-removal-municipal-universal-design-regional-supports-national-rights-and-global-standards.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern disability through rights, accessibility, and support rather than pity, segregation, or medical gatekeeping: neighborhoods and local institutions should surface barriers and support ordinary inclusion; municipalities should make streets, transit, schools, public information, housing interfaces, and service counters accessible by design; regional bodies should coordinate specialized mobility, communication, personal-assistance, safeguarding, and referral systems that cross local borders; nations should guarantee equal legal capacity, anti-discrimination law, benefits, assistive-technology coverage, and enforceable accessibility obligations; and the global layer should maintain disability-rights norms, interoperable standards, and humanitarian inclusion rather than leaving disability to domestic discretion.
- `522-culture-and-heritage-by-scope-local-belonging-municipal-institutions-regional-ecologies-national-pluralism-and-global-commons.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern culture as a rights-bearing public good rather than propaganda, luxury, or folklore storage: neighborhoods and communities keep living practices, memory, and language-use close to life; municipalities should sustain libraries, museums, venues, festivals, archives, arts education links, public space, and fair local cultural access; regional bodies should support linguistic and heritage ecologies, touring circuits, landscape-scale memory, and cultural production systems that outrun one city; nations should guarantee cultural rights, artistic freedom, public support, restitution and heritage law, and plural national institutions without imposing one official culture; and the global layer should protect humanity’s shared heritage, support cultural diversity, and coordinate anti-trafficking and cooperation without becoming a world ministry of taste.
- `523-gender-equality-and-bodily-autonomy-by-scope-local-safety-municipal-access-regional-referral-national-equality-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat gender equality and bodily autonomy as constitutional infrastructure rather than a private lifestyle dispute: households, schools, clinics, workplaces, and neighborhoods should surface risk and practice non-domination; municipalities should make prevention, safe mobility, childcare links, crisis help, and sexual-and-reproductive-health access actually reachable; regional bodies should coordinate specialist referral, shelters, forensic capacity, and hospital catchments that outrun one city; nations should guarantee equal legal status, anti-violence law, labour and care equality, and bodily-autonomy rights; and the global layer should keep a narrow but serious role in rights norms, cross-border accountability, evidence, and anti-backsliding solidarity.
- `524-children-and-youth-by-scope-local-belonging-municipal-voice-regional-opportunity-national-guarantees-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern childhood and youth as a full citizenship-building architecture rather than a sentimental side issue: families, peers, schools, and neighborhood institutions should make belonging and safety real; municipalities should build child-friendly streets, services, and participation channels; regional bodies should coordinate transport, child protection pathways, specialist services, and opportunity systems that outrun one town; nations should guarantee rights, income floors, education and care baselines, and fair transitions to adulthood; and the global layer should protect child-rights norms, anti-exploitation baselines, and cross-border solidarity without becoming a world parent.
- `525-civil-society-and-association-by-scope-local-mutual-aid-municipal-civic-space-regional-networks-national-freedom-and-global-solidarity.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat civil society and freedom of association as constitutional infrastructure rather than decorative consultation: neighborhoods and communities should be able to form associations, unions, clubs, and mutual-aid institutions without fear; municipalities should keep civic space practically usable through permits, venues, information access, and non-hostile administration; regional bodies should support federations, service networks, and advocacy ecosystems that outrun one locality; nations should guarantee freedom of association and assembly, fair legal personality, charitable and union rights, due-process limits on restriction, and plural routes into policymaking; and the global layer should defend civic space, cross-border solidarity, and safe participation in international forums without pretending every NGO is a world government.
- `526-older-persons-and-ageing-by-scope-local-belonging-municipal-age-friendly-design-regional-supports-national-income-security-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat longer life as a civic achievement rather than a private burden: households, kin, and neighbors can offer reciprocity but should not become the hidden welfare state; municipalities should make everyday life age-friendly through reachable services, barrier removal, social infrastructure, and usable local navigation; regional bodies should coordinate specialist geriatrics, abuse response, mobility and housing transitions, and care pathways that outrun one municipality; nations should guarantee income security, anti-age-discrimination law, retirement and work rules, legal-capacity safeguards, and equal access to core supports; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in human-rights norms, anti-ageism, portable learning, and knowledge exchange rather than pretending there can be a world pension ministry.
- `527-end-of-life-and-death-care-by-scope-local-accompaniment-municipal-death-administration-regional-palliative-capacity-national-rights-and-global-pain-relief.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat dying, death care, and bereavement as governed phases of civic life rather than hospital leftovers: households, friends, and community institutions can accompany the dying and mourn the dead but should not be left alone to navigate pain, paperwork, and impossible choices; municipalities should make death registration, burial or cremation access, bereavement navigation, and culturally plural local practice legible and reachable; regional bodies should coordinate palliative-care networks, hospice and specialist capacity, coronial or medical-examiner functions, and referral pathways that outrun one city; nations should guarantee consent law, advance directives, surrogate decision rules, equitable palliative access, medicine availability, and vital-registration baselines; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in essential pain-relief access, rights norms, and knowledge exchange rather than pretending to legislate every intimate end-of-life question for the whole world.
- `528-freedom-of-conscience-and-religion-by-scope-local-coexistence-municipal-neutrality-regional-fairness-national-rights-and-global-protection.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat freedom of conscience, religion, and belief as plural civic infrastructure rather than a privilege of dominant traditions or a project of militant homogenization: households, associations, and communities should be free to form, change, practice, criticize, or refuse belief without coercion; municipalities should keep ordinary civic life neutral and usable through fair permits, equal access, cemetery and calendar accommodation, and non-discriminatory service interfaces; regional bodies should coordinate fairness across hospitals, prisons, schools, and other institutions whose catchments outrun one city; nations should guarantee legal personality, anti-discrimination law, equal citizenship, education and service neutrality, hate-crime and incitement baselines, and rights-safe rules for conscientious objection; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in rights norms, persecution response, and anti-incitement principles rather than trying to govern theology from afar.
- `530-language-and-linguistic-pluralism-by-scope-local-use-municipal-service-access-regional-language-ecologies-national-rights-and-global-support.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat language as civic infrastructure rather than as a badge of dominance or a private burden of translation: households, associations, and communities should be free to use, transmit, revive, and change their languages in everyday life; municipalities should make frontline services, signage, interpretation, naming, and basic public interfaces actually usable in the languages that structure local life; regional bodies should sustain language ecologies that outrun one town through media, teacher pipelines, courts, hospitals, universities, and cultural institutions; nations should define official-language settlements, guarantee minority and Indigenous language rights, fund multilingual education and translation capacity, and prevent language-based exclusion from citizenship, justice, or public work; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in language-rights norms, endangered-language support, digital standards, and shared linguistic infrastructure rather than trying to impose one administrative tongue on humanity.
- `531-rural-remote-and-peripheral-places-by-scope-local-agency-intermunicipal-service-backbones-regional-catchments-national-territorial-solidarity-and-global-learning.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat rural, remote, island, mountain, and other peripheral places not as residual territories waiting to shrink quietly but as legitimate political communities with distinct distance, sparsity, ecology, and production constraints: local institutions should set priorities, steward place knowledge, and surface service failure early; intermunicipal compacts should provide the shared administrative and service backbones that low-density places often need to remain capable; regional bodies should govern labour markets, referral systems, transport, watershed and land-use spillovers, and adaptation systems that cross many small jurisdictions; nations should guarantee territorial solidarity through fiscal equalization, connectivity, service floors, fair resource revenue, and public employment and investment rules that do not punish distance; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in fair trade, climate and connectivity support, and shared learning rather than imposing metro-centric metrics on every place.
- `532-water-and-sanitation-by-scope-local-access-municipal-stormwater-basin-governance-national-rights-and-transboundary-cooperation.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat water as both a daily service and a shared ecological system: households, farms, and neighbourhood institutions can surface failures, conserve, and steward local sources but should not be left to absorb utility risk alone; municipalities should guarantee drinking water, sanitation, stormwater, leak response, and ordinary public-space water safety; basin or regional authorities should govern aquifers, rivers, drought, flood, wastewater spillovers, and allocation conflicts at the hydrological scale that actually exists; nations should guarantee the human rights to water and sanitation, finance universal access, regulate quality, affordability, extraction, and public-health protection, and prevent postcode hydrology from becoming lower citizenship; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in transboundary waters, comparable standards, early warning, and upstream-downstream cooperation rather than pretending one local utility can solve a shared basin.
- `533-waste-and-materials-by-scope-local-collection-regional-recovery-national-producer-responsibility-and-global-hazard-controls.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat waste as failed material design rather than municipal fate: households, shops, workplaces, and neighbourhood institutions can sort, return, repair, and surface illegal dumping but should not carry the whole burden of circularity; municipalities should guarantee clean streets, universal collection, public-space litter control, reuse access points, and safe everyday interfaces with residents; regional bodies should run the real recovery geography of transfer stations, composting, remanufacturing, recycling markets, and final disposal capacity that usually outruns one city; nations should shift cost and design responsibility upstream through product standards, extended producer responsibility, deposit and take-back systems, right-to-repair rules, public procurement, data reporting, and labour protections; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in hazardous-waste controls, waste-trade rules, and common floor disciplines that prevent one country’s circular rhetoric from becoming another country’s toxic burden.
- `535-transport-and-logistics-by-scope-local-streets-metro-transit-regional-corridors-national-networks-and-global-interoperability.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat transport as a lived access system and a strategic circulation system at the same time: neighbourhoods and households can surface danger, exclusion, curb conflict, and last-mile need but should not be left to self-organize mobility; municipalities should govern streets, sidewalks, cycling, bus priority, curb use, traffic calming, road safety, and visible access to daily destinations; metropolitan authorities should own mass transit integration, fare systems, freight interfaces, and land-use coordination across one labour and housing market; regional institutions should govern intercity corridors, ports, inland waterways, airports, and resilience across the geography through which people and goods actually move; nations should own network finance, safety baselines, decarbonization strategy, essential-service guarantees, and major modal balance; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in aviation and maritime rules, cross-border interoperability, and fair technical standards rather than pretending one city can regulate the skies or the sea lanes.
- `537-outer-space-and-orbital-commons-by-scope-local-hosting-regional-spaceports-national-authorization-and-global-sustainability-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat outer space as a global commons of use rather than a frontier of silent enclosure: local communities should hold real say over launch sites, tracking stations, astronomy impacts, land use, emergency planning, and public benefit where space infrastructure touches the ground; regional institutions should coordinate spaceport corridors, environmental review, disaster interfaces, and research ecosystems where activities spill across jurisdictions; nations should authorize and continuously supervise national activities in space, register objects, govern liability, spectrum and orbital use discipline, public research, procurement, and security constraints, and prevent private launch markets from becoming lightly regulated sovereignty proxies; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in non-appropriation, peaceful use, registration, debris mitigation, conjunction information-sharing, and long-term sustainability rather than letting orbit become an unmanaged congestion market.
- `538-money-and-payments-by-scope-local-cash-access-municipal-acceptance-national-public-money-and-global-interoperability.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat money and payments as constitutional infrastructure: households and neighbourhood institutions can surface exclusion, fraud, outage, and cash-access failures but should not mint rival monies for ordinary public life; municipalities should guarantee practical payment usability in everyday government, including cash access and acceptance where law protects it, legible public-payment channels, and inclusive collection design; metropolitan and regional institutions should coordinate shared payment touchpoints where commuting, service markets, and public agencies cross borders; nations should own legal tender, central bank money, payment-system oversight, public-payment rails, consumer protection, anti-fraud baselines, and resilience; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in message standards, cross-border interoperability, remittance quality, and data-friction reduction rather than pretending that local service design or national monetary legitimacy can be outsourced.
- `541-government-by-scope-micro-local-stewardship-municipal-professionalism-metropolitan-democracy-regional-capacity-national-guarantees-and-global-narrow-waists.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not ask every scale to be the same kind of government: micro-local units should be light stewardship and signal institutions, municipalities should be general-purpose democratic governments with professional administration, metropolitan governments should be directly legitimated coordinators of shared urban systems, regional governments should carry landscape and major-service capacity, national governments should guarantee equal citizenship, redistribution, macro-stability, and constitutional rights, and global bodies should remain narrow, treaty-bound organs for peace, commons, alerting, and interoperability rather than aspiring to one undifferentiated world state.
- `544-delegated-public-functions-contractors-concessions-nonprofits-and-platforms-cannot-be-constitutional-escape-hatches.md` — An ideal polity may delegate bounded execution to contractors, concessionaires, nonprofit operators, co-operatives, or digital platforms when doing so is genuinely useful, but it should never outsource the state’s continuing duties to set rights-respecting rules, preserve public capacity, keep money and risk legible, maintain records and remedies, guarantee continuity, and retake control when delegation fails; public obligations should follow the public function rather than disappearing into private legal form.
- `545-regulators-inspections-and-enforcement-role-clarity-risk-based-proportionality-due-process-and-no-government-by-shakedown.md` — An ideal polity should treat regulators and inspectorates as bounded public-law institutions whose job is to reduce real harm, preserve fair conditions, and keep essential systems trustworthy; give them clear missions, enough independence to resist improper influence, enough accountability to remain public servants, risk-based and proportionate enforcement tools, visible appeal routes, and budgets not addicted to penalties; and never let licensing, inspection, or fines become a substitute tax system, a patronage machine, or a theatre of arbitrary power.
- `546-public-enterprises-and-state-owned-enterprises-explicit-rationales-separated-roles-hard-budget-constraints-and-open-books.md` — An ideal polity may own and operate enterprises where public ownership is genuinely justified — for natural monopolies, essential network infrastructure, strategic resilience, mission-critical finance, or other clearly stated public purposes — but it should publish why it owns them, separate ownership from regulation and policy-making, state public-service obligations explicitly, compensate them transparently, impose hard budget constraints, keep boards and books professional and visible, and review the portfolio often enough that public enterprise does not become a hiding place for patronage, off-balance-sheet debt, or anti-competitive favoritism.
- `547-budgeting-treasury-and-public-accounts-credible-ceilings-legislative-authority-one-treasury-and-no-government-by-fund-fog.md` — An ideal polity should turn public money into a lawful cycle of strategy, appropriation, controlled execution, and audited account: set clear fiscal objectives and medium-term ceilings, present one comprehensive budget rather than a maze of side funds, give the legislature real time and analytic capacity to approve totals and appropriations, execute through a unified treasury, chart of accounts, commitment controls, and cash planning, publish in-year reports and year-end financial statements, disclose fiscal risks honestly, and route audit findings back into correction so the state cannot govern through supplementary fog, arrears, or off-budget improvisation.
- `548-legislatures-by-scope-neighborhood-assemblies-municipal-councils-metro-chambers-federal-shared-rule-and-no-government-by-decree.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should fit its legislative institutions to scale: use direct assemblies and recallable delegates for micro-local stewardship, elected municipal and metropolitan councils where visible services and shared systems need contestable public rulemaking, regional and federal chambers where territory and shared rule must be represented, and national parliaments strong enough to legislate, budget, scrutinize, and police delegated law rather than surrendering government to executives, party cartels, or decree.
- `553-supreme-audit-institutions-and-external-public-audit-by-scope-local-books-regional-state-audit-national-independence-and-no-government-by-self-audit.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should keep bookkeeping, internal control, and managerial accountability inside every public body, but place **external audit** in institutions independent of the auditee: make local books and records unavoidable, size municipal and state/provincial external audit to real government tiers and catchments, give the national supreme audit institution constitutional standing, access, budget, and publication rights, require legislatures and executives to follow up publicly, and never let the government audit itself in secret and call that accountability.
- `560-official-statistics-and-census-institutions-by-scope-local-administrative-data-discipline-regional-capacity-national-independence-and-no-government-by-partisan-numbers.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **official statistics and census institutions** as a **constitutional public-facts system**: keep administrative-data quality, respondent support, and local enumeration logistics close to where people and records actually are; use provincial, state, regional, or other intermediate statistical institutions where territorial scale or federal structure justifies durable subject-matter capacity; reserve national government for the legal guarantees of professional independence, statistical confidentiality, census authority, coordination of the national statistical system, common methods and classifications, and public release calendars; and never allow the government of the day to decide the country’s facts by press office, police apparatus, or ministry convenience.
- `567-public-borrowing-and-debt-by-scope-no-neighborhood-debt-municipal-capital-discipline-metro-infrastructure-national-stabilization-and-no-government-by-hidden-guarantees.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat borrowing as a scale-matched constitutional power rather than a general permission slip: micro-local bodies should usually not borrow at all, municipalities and regions should borrow mainly for long-lived capital under hard disclosure and restructuring rules, national governments should own macro-stabilization and sovereign debt management openly rather than laundering risk through off-book vehicles, and continental or global borrowing should remain narrow, charter-bound, and formula-backed instead of pretending a thin treaty body is already a full fiscal state.
- `573-administrative-procedure-permits-and-licenses-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-front-doors-regional-technical-review-national-procedure-codes-and-no-government-by-permit-maze.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **administrative procedure, permits, and licenses** as the **constitutional authorization layer** of government: keep lived fact-finding, pre-application help, and ordinary place-based intake close to communities and municipalities; pool specialist review and cross-boundary technical assessment regionally where risks or spillovers justify it; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the core procedural guarantees, common clocks, appeal architecture, and recognition rules that make the whole system legible; and use continental and global layers for interoperability, evidence exchange, and mutual recognition rather than for a fantasy of one world permit desk.
- `579-scope-allocation-by-level-intimacy-spillovers-coercion-solidarity-infrastructure-commons-and-no-government-by-level-confusion.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should allocate functions by a compact **scope-allocation grammar** rather than by inherited prestige or map inertia: keep voice, stewardship, and context-heavy discretion as close to people as possible; shift authority upward when spillovers outrun local borders, when network infrastructures require shared operation, when equal-rights floors and due-process guarantees require stronger uniformity, when risk-pooling and redistribution need a wider base, and when cross-border commons or security problems cannot be solved domestically; and treat continental and global layers as **narrow-waist coordination regimes** for shared problems rather than as imitation nation-states.
- `581-mandate-finance-congruence-unfunded-mandates-vertical-fiscal-imbalance-and-no-decentralization-by-fiscal-theater.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **mandate-finance congruence** as constitutional law rather than budget etiquette: no level of government should be assigned a durable public function unless the same settlement also names the revenue basket, transfer formula, equalization rule, borrowing limits, and capability backstop that make the function actually dischargeable; delegated tasks must come with commensurate resources, local self-government must include at least some real own-source fiscal room, and upward rescue must be visible and reviewable rather than leaving decentralization to degrade into blame-shifting.
- `584-common-floors-local-headroom-explicit-preemption-rules-and-no-silent-override-by-upper-tier-convenience.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **preemption and override as explicit constitutional instruments rather than as ambient higher-tier privilege**: upper levels may set rights floors, solidarity guarantees, interoperability rules, and protections against genuine cross-border harms, but they should leave subnational governments real room to go further or adapt locally unless a law clearly names the conflict, states the protected interest, consults affected governments, provides transition and finance where duties are displaced, and subjects any ceiling preemption or field occupation to review rather than letting uniformity spread by habit.
- `593-local-self-government-judicial-remedy-constitutional-standing-interim-relief-and-no-autonomy-without-recourse.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should guarantee **local and regional governments** a real **right of recourse to judicial remedy** — including standing against executive interference, a route to constitutional review where laws themselves wound self-government, and timely interim relief against irreversible harm — so autonomy is defended by law rather than left to negotiation, prestige, or endurance.
- `596-special-purpose-authorities-utility-districts-metro-agencies-and-no-government-by-quango-sprawl.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should use special-purpose authorities only as tightly bounded tools for real network, basin, corridor, or technical-governance problems, so shared systems can be run at the right scale without letting single-purpose bodies metastasize into a shadow constitution of opaque boards, off-budget debt, and blame-proof government.
- `597-local-participation-rights-petitions-initiatives-referendums-deliberative-mini-publics-and-no-direct-democracy-by-ambush.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **participation in local and regional affairs as a bounded constitutional layer of self-government**: people should have low-friction rights to petition, place issues on the agenda, join structured consultations, take part in participatory budgeting and civic monitoring where appropriate, and in some cases trigger or vote in referendums — but each channel should have a clear legal purpose, a visible response duty, and strong protections against capture, rights injury, and plebiscitary short-circuiting of representative government.
- `599-local-and-regional-assembly-scrutiny-rights-agenda-power-questions-committee-capacity-and-no-majoritarian-blackout.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the **scrutiny rights of local and regional assemblies as constitutional operating equipment rather than as optional etiquette**: councils and assemblies should control the budgetary and rulemaking core, all members should have enforceable rights to meetings, agendas, questions, information, and proportionate committee work, opposition and minority blocs should be able to scrutinise without begging the executive for oxygen, and executive accountability should be structured so local democracy cannot be reduced to periodic elections plus majority blackout.
- `609-administrative-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-own-executive-own-staff-records-treasury-planning-core-and-no-government-by-secondment-maze.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **administrative home** as well as a democratic and fiscal one: a legally visible executive center, its own staff and records, a durable core for planning/finance/procurement/legal/data work, interoperable but non-subordinate interfaces with component governments and the state, and enough administrative continuity that the territory is not really governed through borrowed personnel, rotating mayoral bandwidth, consultants, or agency shrubbery.
- `613-participatory-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-petitions-hearings-mini-publics-territorial-notice-and-no-metropolitan-participation-by-postcode.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **participatory home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, and intergovernmental one: territory-wide notice, petition and question routes, public hearings and consultations, bounded co-prioritisation and participatory-budget lanes where suitable, representative deliberative processes for complex trade-offs, and visible response duties — so residents can influence the shared tier directly rather than relying on borrowed municipal channels, host-city publicity, or consultation theatre.
- `614-knowledge-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-observatories-territorial-indicators-basemaps-scenario-capacity-and-no-government-by-fragmented-spreadsheets.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **knowledge home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, and participatory one: a territorially coherent observatory, common basemaps and boundary files, a published indicator set at the scale actually being governed, lawful data-sharing and evaluation capacity, open methods and release discipline, and visible routes from evidence into plans and budgets — so the shared tier stops governing through municipal spreadsheet fragments, ministry leftovers, vendor dashboards, and dueling numbers.
- `628-honesty-tests-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-vocation-complete-kits-constitutional-upgrade-and-no-jurisdictional-cosplay.md` — An ideal government at any scope is not defined by prestige, inherited labels, or institutional symmetry, but by an honest fit among governing vocation, territorial reality, democratic legitimacy, administrative capacity, money, review routes, and upgrade triggers: micro-local units should stay signal-rich and light; municipalities should be the first full governments of ordinary life; metropolitan and regional tiers should harden once shared territorial power is real; nations should guarantee equal citizenship, solidarity, and constitutional order without swallowing the stack; and continental and global bodies should remain competence-bounded compact and treaty narrow waists rather than drifting into jurisdictional cosplay.
- `635-scope-diff-packets-before-after-register-amendments-and-no-constitutional-change-by-side-effect.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require any legally or operationally material change to who governs what to ship with a public **scope-diff packet** against the canonical scope register, showing the before-and-after allocation, legal lane, consultation or consent route, jurisprudence impact, exception clocks, and review duties, so the stack cannot be rewired by side effect across statutes, grants, budgets, software, or emergency residue.
- `638-clear-statement-rules-for-scope-change-interpretive-backstops-and-no-rescoping-by-ambiguity.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should adopt one public **clear-statement rule for scope change**: ambiguous statutes, grants, budgets, guidance, compacts, or software defaults should not be interpreted as materially reallocating protected competences, narrowing local or regional discretion, or creating durable new stack relations unless the instrument says so explicitly and travels with the linked scope packet, opinion, and override path where required.
- `639-scope-conformance-before-go-live-implementation-attestations-readiness-gates-and-no-stack-change-by-deployment-drift.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require one public **scope-conformance attestation before go-live** for any materially stack-altering measure: budgets, regulations, grants, contracts, staffing, digital workflows, supervisory routines, public communications, and remedy routes should be checked against the adopted packet, opinion, override, and live register so that implementation cannot quietly move power farther than law and consent actually authorised.
- `640-post-launch-scope-observability-variance-ledgers-rollback-lanes-and-no-stack-change-by-runtime-custom.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat materially stack-altering reforms as **actively observable after go-live**, with one linked post-launch variance ledger, short review clocks, named correction and rollback lanes, and explicit closure criteria, so the lived operation of budgets, staff, systems, supervision, and remedies cannot quietly become a different constitutional settlement by runtime custom.
- `641-scope-settlement-certificates-provisional-to-settled-promotion-and-no-constitutional-permanence-by-elapsed-time.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require one public **scope-settlement certificate** before any materially stack-altering reform moves from **provisional live** to **settled live** status: the certificate should say whether the authorised settlement truly survived contact with budgets, staff, systems, supervision, and remedies, retire or carry forward every temporary exception openly, and refuse constitutional permanence by mere elapsed time.
- `642-scope-retirement-certificates-repeal-cleanup-successor-crosswalks-and-no-constitutional-ghosting.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require one public **scope-retirement certificate** whenever a materially stack-bearing competence, exception, body, supervisory lane, or temporary upper-tier hold is repealed, handed back, merged away, or superseded: retirement should close legal authority, budgets, systems, public channels, and review routes together, preserve historical memory, and refuse any afterlife of government by leftover residue.
- `644-scope-nullity-rules-void-voidable-cure-freeze-lanes-and-no-constitutional-laundering-by-fait-accompli.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should distinguish **void**, **voidable**, and **curable** defects in materially stack-altering acts, and should require one public **scope-nullity ruling** or equivalent settlement object when a reform skipped the required scope lane: illegality should not ripen into constitutional fact merely because budgets spent, portals launched, or officials kept operating.
- `649-scope-waiver-discipline-authorized-consent-and-no-stack-change-by-silence-side-letter-or-wrong-organ.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat **any purported consent to a materially stack-altering move as valid only when it comes from the right organ, through the right public act, in the right lane, and with the right scope and duration**: consultation is not the same as surrender, operational co-operation is not the same as constitutional waiver, and no grant signature, side-letter, emergency reliance, platform click-through, budget acceptance, or failure to object quickly should count as lawful consent to permanent rescoping.
- `653-scope-source-hierarchies-authority-ladders-and-no-stack-change-by-the-loudest-surface.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should settle disputes about **who governs what** against a declared **source hierarchy** rather than against whichever surface is loudest, newest, easiest to find, or already wired into daily operations: constitutional and statutory text, authoritative judgments, and explicit scope acts should outrank derivative registers, and derivative registers should outrank budgets, contracts, software behavior, dashboards, FAQs, and public-relations residue.
- `663-cross-border-integration-ladders-information-sharing-minimum-standards-mutual-recognition-common-enforcement-budget-tools-and-no-union-by-slogan.md` — Ideal continental or plurilateral governance should climb an explicit **integration ladder** — information exchange, benchmarking, minimum standards, mutual recognition, shared operational rails, pooled enforcement, common financing, and only then deeper legislative or fiscal union where truly necessary — so polities can co-govern real spillovers without pretending every problem requires the same depth of union or drifting by slogan into competence creep.
- `665-external-commitment-landing-paths-signature-ratification-transposition-direct-effect-operational-owners-and-no-treaty-by-press-release.md` — Cross-border and global commitments should not stop at signature or ratification: an honest polity should show the full **landing path** from external commitment to domestic legal effect, operational owners, budgeting, reporting, review, and subnational fit, so treaty participation does not masquerade as implementation.
- `675-shared-regime-initiative-and-text-sponsorship-ladders-agenda-items-proposals-amendments-cosponsorship-withdrawal-financial-screening-and-no-law-by-ghost-draft.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed initiation constitution** that separates agenda items, draft texts, amendments, explanatory memoranda, cosponsorship, withdrawal, late-paper handling, and **budget, financial, or administrative implications review** — so law does not enter the system by ghost draft, ambush paper, or sponsorless secretariat residue.
- `683-shared-regime-budget-constitutions-assessed-and-voluntary-funds-appropriations-working-capital-arrears-audit-and-no-governance-by-donor-patchwork.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed budget constitution** that separates adopted appropriations, assessed contributions, voluntary or earmarked funds, working-capital and reserve instruments, arrears consequences, internal and external audit, and public follow-through — so the regime is not governed by donor patchwork, cash panic, or audit afterlife.
- `697-shared-regime-strategic-planning-and-results-constitutions-general-programmes-programme-budgets-theories-of-change-baselines-targets-reviews-and-no-mission-by-project-pile.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed strategic-planning-and-results constitution** that separates long-horizon strategy, medium-term programme budgets, theories of change, outcome and output ladders, indicator and baseline rules, target-setting, reprogramming, and mid-cycle review — so the institution does not drift into mission by project pile, target theater, dashboard government, or budget without strategy.
- `704-control-plane-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-priorities-common-ledger-exception-queues-and-no-hidden-center-by-coordination.md` — Once the archive has split a field into lane-sized governments and published the seam rules between them, it should also publish one narrow **control-plane packet** for the field as a whole — naming the common goals, rights floors, shared metrics, review rhythm, exception queue, budget and capacity crosswalk, and upgrade triggers — so the stack can be steered and inspected as one public system without quietly inventing an undeclared super-tier that governs by coordination alone.
- `714-fiscal-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-operating-base-equalization-spine-reserves-capital-lanes-and-no-government-by-grant-fog.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, and delegation rules for a field, it should also publish one narrow **fiscal packet** saying what recurring operating base actually funds the field, which lane holds budget and treasury authority, what equalization or solidarity rule corrects uneven burdens, what reserve and contingency ladder keeps shocks from becoming constitutional panic, what capital and debt lane is lawful, and what grants may supplement but not substitute for an honest money constitution.
- `715-capability-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-employer-lane-merit-floor-training-ladders-surge-rosters-and-no-government-by-borrowed-payroll.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, and a fiscal packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **capability packet** saying which lane is the employer of record and capability steward, what minimum in-house core the field must retain, what merit and qualification floor applies, what training and profession ladders sustain scarce skills, what secondment and surge rules are allowed, and what vacancy or churn triggers open repair or redesign — so the field does not rely on borrowed payroll, consultant memory, or permanent emergency staffing to remain governmental at all.
- `716-information-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-canonical-case-home-access-model-sharing-boundaries-retention-clocks-and-no-government-by-portal-shell.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, and a capability packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **information packet** saying where the field’s canonical case and record homes live, which surface is the system of record and which are only presentation or intake layers, what role-and-access model governs staff and delegates, what sharing boundaries and information agreements apply, what retention/export/handback rules preserve public memory, and what recovery path keeps the field governable when platforms, vendors, or host systems fail — so the field does not become government by portal shell, spreadsheet relay, or vendor-admin shadow.
- `717-asset-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-estate-fleet-equipment-condition-discipline-handback-and-no-government-by-orphan-assets.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, and an information packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **asset packet** saying which lane owns and stewards the field’s estate, fleet, equipment, depots, labs, stores, and critical spares; who holds custody, maintenance, calibration, and replacement duty; what condition and resilience floor applies; what lease, host-site, or operator dependencies exist; and what handback rule survives exit or transfer — so the field does not decay into government by orphan assets, lease camouflage, or maintenance exile.
- `718-service-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-whole-service-front-doors-route-classes-service-floors-continuity-and-no-government-by-front-door-scatter.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, an information packet, and an asset packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **service packet** saying what outcome the field’s service actually promises, which lane owns that promise, what front doors and route classes the public may use, what clocks and service floors bind, how channels and operators compose into one whole service, and what continuity and fallback rules survive overload, outage, provider failure, or redesign — so the field does not decay into government by front-door scatter, route roulette, or service-standard theater.
- `727-routing-override-triad-for-ideal-governments-downward-intimacy-upward-guarantees-sideways-functional-authorities-and-no-scope-choice-by-prestige.md` — Once the archive has a default routing table for common public functions, departures from that default should occur only through one explicit override triad: **downward** when intimacy, place variance, or rapid correction dominates; **upward** when rights floors, solidarity, macro-risk, security, or interoperability dominates; and **sideways** into a bounded functional authority when the real system footprint mismatches ordinary civic territory.
- `730-continuity-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-staff-budget-records-cases-contracts-assets-cutover-and-no-ratification-by-theory-alone.md` — Once the archive has a default routing table (`726`), an override grammar (`727`), a sideways-authority packet (`728`), and a ratification packet for moving functions across scopes (`729`), it should also keep one compact **continuity packet** for the move itself: no scope shift is constitutionally honest until the polity can show who employs the people, holds the money, owns the contracts, keeps the files, answers the live cases, preserves the review routes, and runs the cutover without dropping rights, services, or accountability.
- `731-cutover-witness-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-effective-state-old-holder-new-holder-exception-ledger-and-no-transfer-by-folklore.md` — Once the archive has a continuity packet for scope shifts (`730`), it should also keep one compact **cutover witness packet** for the handoff moment itself: every materially consequential move across scopes should leave behind one contemporaneous public-and-reviewable witness saying what changed, when it changed, which holder lost authority, which holder gained authority, what remained transitional, which queues, records, contracts, and budgets were still in flight, which exceptions stayed live, and what fallback path still existed — so later review does not have to reconstruct the transfer from rumor, screenshots, or contradictory portal residue.
- `759-independent-institutions-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-referee-functions-bounded-mandates-appointment-discipline-budget-protection-review-lanes-and-no-fourth-branch-sprawl.md` — Ideal governments should create independent institutions only where a function genuinely requires **credible distance from day-to-day political command**—as referee, guardian, watchdog, or integrity backstop—and should then give that institution a bounded mandate, protected but not blank-cheque resources, multi-actor appointment and removal discipline, transparent duties, reviewable powers, and a constitutional place that prevents both ministerial capture and fourth-branch sprawl.
- `762-official-opposition-and-legislative-minority-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-recognition-scrutiny-rights-agenda-oxygen-committee-chairs-evidence-capacity-and-no-government-by-majority-blackout.md` — Ideal governments should treat the opposition and legislative minority as **constitutional scrutiny equipment rather than a tolerated inconvenience**: they should guarantee recognition, speaking and questioning rights, proportional committee presence, some agenda oxygen, evidence and staffing capacity, and in key oversight domains opposition-led scrutiny, so democratic government remains accountable between elections and does not collapse into rule by majority blackout.
- `775-administrative-compensation-and-public-liability-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-claims-boards-prompt-payment-fault-vs-strict-zones-and-no-quash-only-rights.md` — Ideal governments should pair review of unlawful or harmful public action with **a visible public-liability and compensation constitution**: when administrative decisions, omissions, delays, operational failures, dangerous public activities, or non-execution of judgments cause loss, there should be a low-friction route to reparation — by compensation or another appropriate remedy — with typed liability rules, settlement or claims-board capacity, prompt payment, and budget discipline, so people do not win legality on paper while carrying the actual loss alone.
- `777-execution-of-administrative-and-judicial-decisions-against-public-authorities-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-compliance-clocks-budget-home-escalation-and-no-judgment-by-non-execution.md` — Ideal governments should treat **execution of administrative and judicial decisions against public authorities** as part of the rule-of-law core rather than as post-judgment housekeeping: when a ministry, municipality, agency, regulator, police body, prison authority, benefits office, land registrar, or treasury loses, the system should have clear compliance clocks, named responsible officials, budget and payment homes, interest and penalty rules, supervisory escalation, and user-visible follow-up so the state cannot turn delay, fragmentation, or lack-of-funds claims into a second victory after losing on the merits.
- `790-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-answer-key-micro-local-voice-municipal-full-kit-metropolitan-democracy-regional-platforms-national-guarantees-continental-compacts-and-global-narrow-waists.md` — The archive should now treat the question **what would the ideal government at each scope be?** as having one default answer-key: **micro-local institutions for voice, witness, and upkeep; municipalities as the first full-spectrum governments of ordinary life; metropolitan governments for shared urban systems; regional or provincial governments for major territorial platforms and shared rule; national government for equal citizenship, solidarity, macro-capacity, and constitutional guarantee; continental bodies for bounded cross-border compacts; and global bodies for narrow treaty-bound coordination of peace, commons, alerting, and interoperability**.
- `802-management-responses-and-corrective-action-ledgers-for-scope-governance-finding-by-finding-owners-dependencies-budget-closure-proof-and-no-verdict-without-a-repair-docket.md` — The archive should pair its assessment-mission and finding-register notes with one compact **management-response grammar**: **every material scope finding should receive a finding-by-finding response that states acceptance posture, named owner at the right scope, dependency chain, budget and legal posture, delivery clock, closure proof, and escalation rule, so review does not end in literary recommendations, political nodding, or an unowned pile of next steps**.
- `814-fiscal-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-dues-and-service-payments-assigned-revenues-equalization-keys-capital-lanes-and-no-heavy-power-by-shadow-treasury.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary form is honest** and **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what fiscal chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should live on modest dues and project-preparation money with no disguised distributive budget, shared-service backbones should run on principal-owned service payments and declared cost-sharing plus reserve rules, bounded functional authorities should use assigned revenues, user charges, or rule-bound transfers matched to their narrow charter with explicit capital discipline, and general-purpose territorial tiers should have a public budget constitution with own-source or rule-bound shared revenues, equalization, and visible borrowing limits rather than living by discretionary grants, annual pleas, or off-book vehicles.
- `827-mandate-duration-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-short-local-rotation-municipal-and-metro-stability-national-renewal-windows-and-treaty-review-clocks.md` — The archive should answer the question **how long should governing mandates last at each scope?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one calendar idol: short and recallable mandates for micro-local stewardship, medium terms for municipalities and metropolitan governments that need enough runway to budget and deliver, regional and national renewal windows that are usually long enough to govern but short enough to correct, and plurilateral or global bodies that live on fixed review and reauthorization clocks rather than ambient permanence.
- `831-fiscal-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-tiny-commons-municipal-own-source-metro-shares-regional-equalization-national-solidarity-and-treaty-dues.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should each scope ordinarily be financed?** with scale-matched fiscal defaults rather than one treasury fetish: micro-local bodies should live on tiny discretionary funds, member contributions, and visible small grants rather than debt or payroll empires; municipalities should be the first level with meaningful own-source revenue, rule-bound transfers, ordinary operating reserves, and capital access for durable local assets; metropolitan governments should use assigned revenue shares, formula transfers, and user-charge lanes where systems justify them rather than annual pleas from member municipalities; regional and provincial governments should combine own revenues, shared taxes, equalization, and platform-scale capital budgets; national government should carry the broad tax base, macro-stabilization, and solidarity machinery; and continental or global bodies should usually rely on treaty dues, assessed contributions, and tightly bounded common finance rather than counterfeit world taxation or donor-whim constitutions.
- `836-participation-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-assembly-municipal-dockets-metro-territorial-hearings-national-petition-ladders-and-treaty-observers.md` — If the archive already knows **what government should exist at each scope**, **how it is chosen**, **how it is financed**, **how it is scrutinized**, **where force lives**, **where records live**, and **what emergency lane fits it**, it should also know **how public voice honestly re-enters that government at each scale**: direct and reachable assembly voice at micro-local scale; petitions, hearings, consultations, bounded participatory-budget lanes, and occasional deliberative mini-publics at municipal scale; territory-wide participation homes for metropolitan and regional bodies that govern real shared systems; parliamentary hearing, petition, consultation, and rare constitution-level referendum lanes at national scale; and structured observer, submission, hearing, and stakeholder-participation routes for continental and global bodies rather than fake world-plebiscitary theater.
- `838-guarantee-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-dignity-municipal-nondiscrimination-regional-implementation-national-equal-citizenship-and-treaty-backstops.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should guarantees and rights floors honestly live at each scope?** with scale-matched defaults rather than rights vapor or rights monocentrism: **micro-local institutions should witness harm, include people, and route claims upward rather than pretending to author a tiny bill of rights; municipalities should be the first operational guarantee tier of daily dignity, non-discrimination, accessibility, and reasons-giving in ordinary administration; metropolitan and regional governments with real platform power should carry typed implementation guarantees for the systems they actually govern without fragmenting equal citizenship; national government should hold the thickest enforceable floor of equal citizenship, limitation discipline, due process, and justiciable rights guarantee; and continental or global bodies should function mainly as treaty-bound rights backstops, monitoring, and complaints machinery rather than as counterfeit world guarantor states**.

## care-governance

- `506-health-by-scope-primary-care-regional-capacity-national-risk-pools-and-global-alerts.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat health as a layered public good: neighborhoods and municipalities support prevention and the social conditions of health; community-facing systems deliver primary care as close as feasible to daily life; regions run hospital, laboratory, ambulance, and surge platforms; nations guarantee universal coverage, workforce strategy, medicines policy, and equitable finance; and global institutions coordinate alerts, standards, and outbreak response without pretending to administer ordinary care everywhere.
- `512-biodiversity-by-scope-local-stewardship-municipal-ecology-regional-landscapes-national-law-and-global-commons.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern biodiversity as a whole-territory constitutional question rather than as a parks afterthought: local and Indigenous or community institutions steward place-based knowledge and care; municipalities integrate biodiversity into everyday land-use, water, and public-space decisions; regional and basin scales govern corridors, landscapes, seascapes, and cumulative extraction pressures; nations set conservation law, restoration duties, species protection, finance, and national biodiversity strategies; and global institutions define common goals, migratory-species and commons rules, and accountability frameworks without pretending to micromanage each ecosystem from abroad.
- `520-care-and-support-by-scope-household-reciprocity-municipal-services-regional-care-systems-national-social-insurance-and-global-worker-protection.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat care as civic infrastructure rather than private fallout: households, kin, and neighbors can contribute reciprocity but should not be the welfare state; municipalities should make childcare, disability support, elder support, and respite actually reachable; regional bodies should coordinate workforce pipelines, specialist and long-term-care systems, and discharge pathways that cross municipal lines; nations should guarantee paid leave, cash and service entitlements, labour standards, and financing pools; and the global layer should stay narrow but real in labour standards, migrant-care-worker protection, and knowledge exchange rather than pretending families can absorb demographic change forever.
- `523-gender-equality-and-bodily-autonomy-by-scope-local-safety-municipal-access-regional-referral-national-equality-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat gender equality and bodily autonomy as constitutional infrastructure rather than a private lifestyle dispute: households, schools, clinics, workplaces, and neighborhoods should surface risk and practice non-domination; municipalities should make prevention, safe mobility, childcare links, crisis help, and sexual-and-reproductive-health access actually reachable; regional bodies should coordinate specialist referral, shelters, forensic capacity, and hospital catchments that outrun one city; nations should guarantee equal legal status, anti-violence law, labour and care equality, and bodily-autonomy rights; and the global layer should keep a narrow but serious role in rights norms, cross-border accountability, evidence, and anti-backsliding solidarity.
