- `817-participation-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-open-dockets-hearings-user-councils-deliberative-mini-publics-response-ledgers-and-no-heavy-power-by-consultation-theater.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **who owns it**, **how money moves through it**, **where its operating spine lives**, and **where scrutiny and redress live**, it should also be able to say **what participation chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should publish open dockets and simple input windows rather than staging fake popular mandates, shared-service backbones should run structured user and accessibility input without pretending pooled operations are a substitute for elected politics, bounded functional authorities should carry recurring hearings and response duties plus deliberative methods where long-horizon tradeoffs justify them, and general-purpose territorial tiers should own a full participation constitution rather than borrowing legitimacy from consultation theater.
- `818-information-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-shared-facts-observatories-record-homes-official-statistics-links-publication-calendars-and-no-heavy-power-by-private-dashboard.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, and **what participation chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what information chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should use open shared-indicator rooms and light observatories, shared-service backbones should keep principal-readable service telemetry plus declared case and record routes, bounded functional authorities should keep authoritative operational data homes with method notes and publication calendars, and general-purpose territorial tiers should carry a fuller public-knowledge constitution rather than governing through host-held or vendor-held dashboards.
- `819-boundary-and-membership-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-accession-gates-territory-rules-amendment-thickness-exit-protocols-dissolution-paths-and-no-map-by-one-way-ratchet.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, and **what information chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should use open and reversible participation with no hidden territorial claim, shared-service backbones should declare member classes, accession formulas, notice periods, and unwind rules, bounded functional authorities should use chartered territories plus staged accession and constrained exit, and general-purpose territorial tiers should rely on statutory boundary change with public consultation, transition machinery, and no map by one-way ratchet.
- `820-decision-rule-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-ordinary-majorities-qualified-majorities-unanimity-reserves-deadlock-breakers-and-no-heavy-power-by-procedural-veto.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, **what information chain belongs to it**, and **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what decision-rule chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should seek consensus for advisory work and require visible member ratification for anything binding, shared-service backbones should use ordinary-majority operating rules with reserved supermajority or member-ratification gates for portfolio, burden, and liability shifts, bounded functional authorities should use public standing orders with ordinary-majority defaults plus qualified-majority or double-key gates for tariffs, debt, land, remit, and boundary changes, and general-purpose territorial tiers should govern by ordinary democratic majorities with narrowly cabined supermajority reserves and explicit deadlock routes rather than by permanent veto geography.
- `821-dispute-resolution-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-negotiation-ladders-mediation-expert-determination-jurisdiction-maps-continuity-orders-and-no-heavy-power-by-hostage-dispute.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, **what information chain belongs to it**, **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**, and **what decision-rule chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what dispute-resolution chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should rely on recorded negotiation and visible member-side escalation, shared-service backbones should use negotiation-first ladders with mediation, technical determination, continuity protection, and public-law endpoints, bounded functional authorities should publish jurisdiction maps and interim continuity orders, and general-purpose territorial tiers should rely on ordinary justice and constitutional routes rather than permanent bargaining by hostage dispute.
- `823-contracting-boundary-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-light-support-buying-principal-owned-commissioning-chartered-concessions-change-control-and-no-heavy-power-by-contract-escape-hatch.md` — When the archive has already established that a cross-boundary problem is real, chosen the honest form, and said who governs, pays, operates, votes, hears disputes, owns the assets, and can unwind the map, it should still require one compact **contracting-boundary chain**: thin connectors may buy only light support and must not become hidden commissioners of core public systems; shared-service backbones may buy pooled administrative tools and support services while political title remains visibly with the principals; bounded functional authorities may procure, franchise, or concession the named system they are chartered to govern, but only through a visible commissioner spine, hard change-control, and full public review; and general-purpose territorial tiers may use contracts as delivery instruments without letting procurement, concessions, PPPs, or managed-service deals become constitutional escape hatches for powers that should remain politically owned.
- `834-information-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-ledgers-municipal-record-homes-metro-observatories-national-statistics-and-treaty-registries.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should authoritative public facts, records, and decision visibility ordinarily live at each scope?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one dashboard fetish: **micro-local bodies should keep simple minutes, noticeboards, steward ledgers, and escalation logs rather than miniature data states; municipalities should be the first level with a full public information constitution of clerks or record stewards, open meeting packets, service and permit records, publication calendars, and reusable public data; metropolitan and regional governments should own their own observatories, geospatial baselines, and cross-boundary performance records rather than parasitic dependence on a host city or ministry; national government should carry the thickest official-statistics, gazette, archive, and interoperability spine; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound but still maintain comparability standards, registries, alerting channels, and shared reporting rather than private dashboards or counterfeit world omniscience**.
- `840-preemption-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-headroom-metro-primacy-federal-bargain-locks-national-floors-and-treaty-bounded-override.md` — The archive should usually prefer different override grammars by scale: **micro-local bodies should remain subject to municipal law and charter while keeping visible voice lanes; municipalities should enjoy broad headroom above common floors unless preemption is explicit, proportionate, and reviewable; metropolitan governments should hold named primacy inside real shared urban systems; regional governments should keep constitutionally real autonomy except where the federal bargain openly assigns paramount power elsewhere; national governments may impose rights floors, solidarity rules, and interoperability baselines but should face a higher burden before using ceilings or field occupation; and continental or global bodies should override only through explicit treaty commitments rather than ambient upper-tier drift**.

## civil-registration-governance

- `527-end-of-life-and-death-care-by-scope-local-accompaniment-municipal-death-administration-regional-palliative-capacity-national-rights-and-global-pain-relief.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat dying, death care, and bereavement as governed phases of civic life rather than hospital leftovers: households, friends, and community institutions can accompany the dying and mourn the dead but should not be left alone to navigate pain, paperwork, and impossible choices; municipalities should make death registration, burial or cremation access, bereavement navigation, and culturally plural local practice legible and reachable; regional bodies should coordinate palliative-care networks, hospice and specialist capacity, coronial or medical-examiner functions, and referral pathways that outrun one city; nations should guarantee consent law, advance directives, surrogate decision rules, equitable palliative access, medicine availability, and vital-registration baselines; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in essential pain-relief access, rights norms, and knowledge exchange rather than pretending to legislate every intimate end-of-life question for the whole world.
- `562-civil-registration-vital-statistics-and-legal-identity-institutions-by-scope-local-event-capture-municipal-service-access-regional-backstops-national-trust-frameworks-and-no-government-by-documentary-erasure.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat civil registration, vital statistics, and legal identity as a linked but non-collapsed public infrastructure: keep event notification and ordinary registration close to births, deaths, marriages, divorces, and residence reality; make municipal or county-level offices, health interfaces, and mobile service routes the ordinary access layer; use regional or provincial backstops where geography, federalism, or sparse settlement require them; reserve national government for the legal-status framework, secure and privacy-bounded identity trust architecture, interoperability rules, consular extension, and systemwide statistics coordination; and never let personhood, kinship, or access to basic rights depend on surviving a hostile documentary maze.
- `570-legal-entity-business-and-beneficial-ownership-registries-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-entry-desks-regional-coordination-national-public-truth-and-no-government-by-paper-shell.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat organizational identity as constitutional infrastructure rather than clerical residue: communities can help witness real economic and associational life, municipalities or counties should usually provide the reachable entry desk for ordinary business-facing registrations and permits, regional or state layers should coordinate where federal structure or market geography requires it, national or constitutional-state law should own the authoritative registry of legal persons and the rules for unique identifiers, lifecycle events, disclosure, and strike-off, beneficial ownership should be held through a public authority or tightly governed equivalent with rapid lawful access and strong update discipline, and continental or global bodies should provide interoperability rails rather than pretending there can be one sovereign company register for the world.

## civil-service-governance

- `408-procurement-clauses-for-exit-escrow-and-public-continuity.md` — Public procurement should treat **continuity at supplier exit** as a design requirement from day one, with contract clauses, tested handovers, and fallback assets that make the public service survivable.
- `426-equivalent-human-channels-and-assisted-digital-parity.md` — A public service does not stay fair merely because an AI path exists; people need reachable, timely, equivalently functional human or non-AI alternatives.
- `496-civil-service-by-scope-stewardship-without-patronage-municipal-professionalism-metro-capacity-and-constitutional-merit-cores.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not use one staffing model at every scale: it should pair light, recallable stewardship at the micro-local level with professional merit administration where continuity and technical competence matter, give metropolitan and regional bodies their own real operating capacity when they wield real powers, protect a constitutional core civil service against spoils and purge cycles, and keep plurilateral and global secretariats thin, expert, and mandate-bound.
- `501-public-sphere-by-scope-community-media-public-service-independence-ownership-transparency-and-civic-information-commons.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat a plural information order as constitutional infrastructure: community and local media should have legal room and sustainable support, public service media should be editorially independent and publicly accountable rather than government-controlled, media ownership and state support should be transparent, and digital distribution rules should protect access to diverse public-interest information instead of quietly collapsing the public sphere into either oligarchy or platform dependence.
- `528-freedom-of-conscience-and-religion-by-scope-local-coexistence-municipal-neutrality-regional-fairness-national-rights-and-global-protection.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat freedom of conscience, religion, and belief as plural civic infrastructure rather than a privilege of dominant traditions or a project of militant homogenization: households, associations, and communities should be free to form, change, practice, criticize, or refuse belief without coercion; municipalities should keep ordinary civic life neutral and usable through fair permits, equal access, cemetery and calendar accommodation, and non-discriminatory service interfaces; regional bodies should coordinate fairness across hospitals, prisons, schools, and other institutions whose catchments outrun one city; nations should guarantee legal personality, anti-discrimination law, equal citizenship, education and service neutrality, hate-crime and incitement baselines, and rights-safe rules for conscientious objection; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in rights norms, persecution response, and anti-incitement principles rather than trying to govern theology from afar.
- `531-rural-remote-and-peripheral-places-by-scope-local-agency-intermunicipal-service-backbones-regional-catchments-national-territorial-solidarity-and-global-learning.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat rural, remote, island, mountain, and other peripheral places not as residual territories waiting to shrink quietly but as legitimate political communities with distinct distance, sparsity, ecology, and production constraints: local institutions should set priorities, steward place knowledge, and surface service failure early; intermunicipal compacts should provide the shared administrative and service backbones that low-density places often need to remain capable; regional bodies should govern labour markets, referral systems, transport, watershed and land-use spillovers, and adaptation systems that cross many small jurisdictions; nations should guarantee territorial solidarity through fiscal equalization, connectivity, service floors, fair resource revenue, and public employment and investment rules that do not punish distance; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in fair trade, climate and connectivity support, and shared learning rather than imposing metro-centric metrics on every place.
- `545-regulators-inspections-and-enforcement-role-clarity-risk-based-proportionality-due-process-and-no-government-by-shakedown.md` — An ideal polity should treat regulators and inspectorates as bounded public-law institutions whose job is to reduce real harm, preserve fair conditions, and keep essential systems trustworthy; give them clear missions, enough independence to resist improper influence, enough accountability to remain public servants, risk-based and proportionate enforcement tools, visible appeal routes, and budgets not addicted to penalties; and never let licensing, inspection, or fines become a substitute tax system, a patronage machine, or a theatre of arbitrary power.
- `549-civil-service-and-public-workforce-merit-neutrality-capability-fair-pay-and-no-government-by-patronage.md` — An ideal government should build a professional public workforce that is mostly recruited and promoted on merit, protected against undue political interference yet accountable for lawful performance, paid and trained well enough to attract and retain capability, open to worker voice and fair discipline, and clearly separated from the small political layer that is entitled to choose direction but not to colonize the state.
- `556-police-services-by-scope-neighborhood-legibility-municipal-or-county-operations-metropolitan-serious-crime-bureaus-national-standards-and-no-police-self-investigation.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **police services** as a **civilian, rights-bound, externally answerable public service** rather than as a self-defining armed caste: keep neighborhood contact and ordinary response close enough to communities to stay legible, size police organizations and custody/investigation support large enough to resist tiny-jurisdiction capture, push serious-crime, forensic, and cross-border investigation to metropolitan or regional institutions, reserve national government for legal floors, training, anti-corruption and narrow specialist support, and never allow **police self-investigation** or militarized political policing to masquerade as democratic order.
- `577-public-service-delivery-one-stop-shops-and-assisted-digital-access-by-scope-community-navigation-municipal-front-counters-regional-shared-service-centers-national-service-standards-and-no-government-by-channel-maze.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **public service delivery** as the **constitutional execution layer** of government: keep trusted navigation, assisted digital help, and ordinary human contact close to communities and municipalities; pool shared service centers, call centers, translation, queue balancing, and specialist case support above fragmented local jurisdictions where scale adds competence; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for service standards, life-event integration, channel parity, common status semantics, and the core rails that let services feel like one government rather than a pile of agencies; and keep continental or global roles narrow enough to support cross-border information, procedures, assistance, and evidence exchange without becoming a world ministry of customer service.
- `609-administrative-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-own-executive-own-staff-records-treasury-planning-core-and-no-government-by-secondment-maze.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **administrative home** as well as a democratic and fiscal one: a legally visible executive center, its own staff and records, a durable core for planning/finance/procurement/legal/data work, interoperable but non-subordinate interfaces with component governments and the state, and enough administrative continuity that the territory is not really governed through borrowed personnel, rotating mayoral bandwidth, consultants, or agency shrubbery.
- `620-workforce-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-employer-status-recruitment-training-labor-relations-and-no-government-by-borrowed-payroll.md` — Real metropolitan or regional government needs its own **employer constitution**: a named employer of record, merit-based staffing and progression, explicit pay and labor-relations rules, bounded reliance on secondment, visible workforce metrics, and a transition path out of borrowed payroll.
- `660-canonical-government-matrix-by-scope-legislature-executive-civil-service-fiscal-base-review-participation-and-no-full-stack-rewrite-for-every-tier.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should reuse one **canonical scope matrix** rather than reinventing every tier from scratch: micro-local units for witness and stewardship, municipalities for ordinary place government, metropolitan authorities for functional urban systems, regions for major territorial platforms and shared rule, nations for equal citizenship and redistribution, continental bodies for bounded cross-border compacts, and global institutions for treaty-bound peace, commons, alerting, and interoperability — each with a scope-matched decision forum, executive spine, civil-service density, fiscal base, review lane, and participation channel.
- `678-shared-regime-independence-and-conflict-discipline-declarations-recusal-confidentiality-secondments-donor-firebreaks-and-no-expertise-by-capture.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed integrity constitution** that separates disclosure, assessment, management, recusal, exclusion, confidentiality, secondment controls, donor firebreaks, and post-service limits — so expertise, review, and advisory work do not harden into captured governance.
- `684-shared-regime-secretariat-workforce-constitutions-appointments-merit-geographic-balance-secondments-conduct-separation-and-no-regime-by-patronage.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed secretariat workforce constitution** that separates political head selection from career staffing, makes merit and integrity the paramount recruitment rule, gives geographic balance a visible but bounded place, constrains secondments and related-party hiring, and types conduct, reassignment, discipline, and separation lanes — so the regime is not governed by patronage, donor-owned posts, or borrowed-capacity fog.
- `715-capability-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-employer-lane-merit-floor-training-ladders-surge-rosters-and-no-government-by-borrowed-payroll.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, and a fiscal packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **capability packet** saying which lane is the employer of record and capability steward, what minimum in-house core the field must retain, what merit and qualification floor applies, what training and profession ladders sustain scarce skills, what secondment and surge rules are allowed, and what vacancy or churn triggers open repair or redesign — so the field does not rely on borrowed payroll, consultant memory, or permanent emergency staffing to remain governmental at all.
- `716-information-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-canonical-case-home-access-model-sharing-boundaries-retention-clocks-and-no-government-by-portal-shell.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, and a capability packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **information packet** saying where the field’s canonical case and record homes live, which surface is the system of record and which are only presentation or intake layers, what role-and-access model governs staff and delegates, what sharing boundaries and information agreements apply, what retention/export/handback rules preserve public memory, and what recovery path keeps the field governable when platforms, vendors, or host systems fail — so the field does not become government by portal shell, spreadsheet relay, or vendor-admin shadow.
- `717-asset-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-estate-fleet-equipment-condition-discipline-handback-and-no-government-by-orphan-assets.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, and an information packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **asset packet** saying which lane owns and stewards the field’s estate, fleet, equipment, depots, labs, stores, and critical spares; who holds custody, maintenance, calibration, and replacement duty; what condition and resilience floor applies; what lease, host-site, or operator dependencies exist; and what handback rule survives exit or transfer — so the field does not decay into government by orphan assets, lease camouflage, or maintenance exile.
- `718-service-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-whole-service-front-doors-route-classes-service-floors-continuity-and-no-government-by-front-door-scatter.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, an information packet, and an asset packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **service packet** saying what outcome the field’s service actually promises, which lane owns that promise, what front doors and route classes the public may use, what clocks and service floors bind, how channels and operators compose into one whole service, and what continuity and fallback rules survive overload, outage, provider failure, or redesign — so the field does not decay into government by front-door scatter, route roulette, or service-standard theater.
- `760-public-appointments-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-merit-vs-political-trust-open-competition-mixed-selection-confirmation-discipline-and-no-office-by-patronage-default.md` — Ideal governments should treat public appointments as a **typed constitutional lane rather than one generic power of disposal**: elected offices should be filled by voters, political-trust offices should be few and plainly political, most administrative and service-delivery posts should be filled through open merit-based recruitment, constitutionally sensitive or independence-bearing offices may justify mixed nominating and confirmation arrangements, and no polity should let patronage, vacancy manipulation, or prestige theatrics become the real appointments constitution.
- `765-access-to-information-and-information-commissioner-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-requester-neutrality-narrow-exceptions-publication-schemes-appeal-powers-delay-discipline-and-no-right-to-know-without-an-enforcer.md` — Ideal governments should treat access to official information as **a standing constitutional right with its own operating system rather than a discretionary transparency favour**: everyone should be able to request records without proving motive, exceptions should be lawful and narrow, publication schemes should proactively release core information, delays should be time-bound and reviewable, and an independent appeal or commissioner lane should be able to order disclosure, monitor compliance, and publish performance data, so the right to know does not dissolve into polite non-response.
- `807-assessment-team-independence-and-conflict-discipline-for-scope-reviews-recusal-rosters-secondment-firebreaks-host-picked-experts-donor-pathways-and-no-constitutional-judgment-by-interested-mission.md` — The archive should pair its assessment-mission, evidence-register, contestability, and close-out notes with one compact **mission-integrity grammar**: **every serious scope review should declare who is judging, who is only informing, what interests and funding pathways each reviewer carries, what firebreaks apply to secondees and host-nominated specialists, when recusal is mandatory, and how outsiders can challenge the composition of the team before findings harden into the live constitution, so the archive does not mistake expertise, proximity, or funding convenience for independence**.

## civil-society-governance

- `525-civil-society-and-association-by-scope-local-mutual-aid-municipal-civic-space-regional-networks-national-freedom-and-global-solidarity.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat civil society and freedom of association as constitutional infrastructure rather than decorative consultation: neighborhoods and communities should be able to form associations, unions, clubs, and mutual-aid institutions without fear; municipalities should keep civic space practically usable through permits, venues, information access, and non-hostile administration; regional bodies should support federations, service networks, and advocacy ecosystems that outrun one locality; nations should guarantee freedom of association and assembly, fair legal personality, charitable and union rights, due-process limits on restriction, and plural routes into policymaking; and the global layer should defend civic space, cross-border solidarity, and safe participation in international forums without pretending every NGO is a world government.
- `528-freedom-of-conscience-and-religion-by-scope-local-coexistence-municipal-neutrality-regional-fairness-national-rights-and-global-protection.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat freedom of conscience, religion, and belief as plural civic infrastructure rather than a privilege of dominant traditions or a project of militant homogenization: households, associations, and communities should be free to form, change, practice, criticize, or refuse belief without coercion; municipalities should keep ordinary civic life neutral and usable through fair permits, equal access, cemetery and calendar accommodation, and non-discriminatory service interfaces; regional bodies should coordinate fairness across hospitals, prisons, schools, and other institutions whose catchments outrun one city; nations should guarantee legal personality, anti-discrimination law, equal citizenship, education and service neutrality, hate-crime and incitement baselines, and rights-safe rules for conscientious objection; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in rights norms, persecution response, and anti-incitement principles rather than trying to govern theology from afar.
- `530-language-and-linguistic-pluralism-by-scope-local-use-municipal-service-access-regional-language-ecologies-national-rights-and-global-support.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat language as civic infrastructure rather than as a badge of dominance or a private burden of translation: households, associations, and communities should be free to use, transmit, revive, and change their languages in everyday life; municipalities should make frontline services, signage, interpretation, naming, and basic public interfaces actually usable in the languages that structure local life; regional bodies should sustain language ecologies that outrun one town through media, teacher pipelines, courts, hospitals, universities, and cultural institutions; nations should define official-language settlements, guarantee minority and Indigenous language rights, fund multilingual education and translation capacity, and prevent language-based exclusion from citizenship, justice, or public work; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in language-rights norms, endangered-language support, digital standards, and shared linguistic infrastructure rather than trying to impose one administrative tongue on humanity.
- `544-delegated-public-functions-contractors-concessions-nonprofits-and-platforms-cannot-be-constitutional-escape-hatches.md` — An ideal polity may delegate bounded execution to contractors, concessionaires, nonprofit operators, co-operatives, or digital platforms when doing so is genuinely useful, but it should never outsource the state’s continuing duties to set rights-respecting rules, preserve public capacity, keep money and risk legible, maintain records and remedies, guarantee continuity, and retake control when delegation fails; public obligations should follow the public function rather than disappearing into private legal form.
- `558-public-defense-and-legal-aid-by-scope-local-entry-municipal-navigation-regional-provider-capacity-national-independence-and-no-justice-by-unaffordable-counsel.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **public defense and legal aid** as a **core constitutional capacity for equal justice** rather than as charity or courthouse aftercare: keep first contact, rights information, and navigable entry close to daily life; use metropolitan, county, provincial, state, or other regional institutions for most ordinary defender offices, provider networks, and specialist capacity; reserve national government for the right itself, independent legal-aid authority design, fair funding, quality floors, and territorial equalization; and never allow **freedom, family life, housing, status, or civil survival to depend on whether a person can privately purchase counsel on short notice**.
- `570-legal-entity-business-and-beneficial-ownership-registries-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-entry-desks-regional-coordination-national-public-truth-and-no-government-by-paper-shell.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat organizational identity as constitutional infrastructure rather than clerical residue: communities can help witness real economic and associational life, municipalities or counties should usually provide the reachable entry desk for ordinary business-facing registrations and permits, regional or state layers should coordinate where federal structure or market geography requires it, national or constitutional-state law should own the authoritative registry of legal persons and the rules for unique identifiers, lifecycle events, disclosure, and strike-off, beneficial ownership should be held through a public authority or tightly governed equivalent with rapid lawful access and strong update discipline, and continental or global bodies should provide interoperability rails rather than pretending there can be one sovereign company register for the world.
- `594-local-authority-associations-consortia-transfrontier-co-operation-and-no-self-government-in-isolation.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the right of local authorities to co-operate, form delivery consortia, join representative associations, and work with counterparts across borders as part of self-government itself, so municipalities and regions can pool capacity, defend common interests, and solve cross-boundary problems without being reduced to isolated administrative fragments.
- `622-emergency-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-emergency-operations-continuity-mutual-aid-recovery-and-no-government-by-crisis-summit.md` — Real metropolitan or regional government needs its own **emergency constitution**: a named territorial emergency authority, an all-hazards risk picture, predefined escalation and mutual-aid rules, continuity of government and essential services, exercised communication and warning routes, recovery and handback discipline, and bounded extraordinary powers — not government by crisis summit.
- `713-delegation-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-principal-lane-reserved-powers-operator-chains-step-in-rights-and-no-public-duty-by-outsourced-wrapper.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, and amendment discipline for a field, it should also publish one narrow **delegation packet** saying which slice of the field is still constitutionally owned by the public lane, which execution work may be delegated to public bodies, contractors, concessionaires, nonprofits, co-operatives, or platforms, what powers remain non-delegable, what contract-management and records capacity the principal must retain, what step-in and handback rights keep continuity real, and what review route prevents public duty from disappearing into an outsourced wrapper.
- `776-court-fees-fee-waivers-cost-protection-and-public-interest-costs-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-affordability-merits-screening-security-for-costs-discipline-and-no-rights-by-priced-out-review.md` — Ideal governments should treat **court fees, fee waivers, cost protection, and adverse-cost rules** as part of the justice constitution rather than as neutral finance: filing costs, hearing fees, expert-cost exposure, security-for-costs demands, and loser-pays rules should be calibrated so ordinary people, small firms, associations, and qualified public-interest claimants can bring serious administrative and rights-bearing cases without financial terror, while weak or abusive claims are filtered by proportionate screening, contribution, and case-management tools rather than by pricing lawful challenge out of existence.
- `835-emergency-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-readiness-municipal-incident-command-regional-civil-protection-national-derogation-discipline-and-treaty-alerting.md` — The archive should answer the question **what emergency and exception grammar should ordinarily fit each scope?** with scale-matched escalation rather than one panic state fetish: **micro-local bodies should default to readiness, warning, mutual aid, and witness rather than emergency sovereignty; municipalities should be the first ordinary home of incident command, continuity, sheltering, and short-horizon emergency operations under ordinary law; metropolitan governments should carry shared-system disruption management where the functional city is one risk field; regional or provincial governments may honestly house civil-protection, wildfire, flood, logistics, and mutual-aid platforms where those risks are territorially real; national government should hold the thickest declaration, derogation, reserve, and exceptional coordination powers under legislative renewal, judicial review, and strict handback discipline; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound, specializing in alerting, coordination, standards, pooled assistance, and tightly authorized collective action rather than becoming ambient permanent emergency government**.

## climate-governance

- `407-public-algorithm-incident-command.md` — When an automated or model-assisted public system starts causing harm, instability, or loss of control, government should respond with **incident command**, not slow-motion policy theater.
- `437-subgroup-floor-metrics-public-harm-registries-and-thresholds.md` — Public AI systems should not pass on aggregate accuracy alone: they need **subgroup floor metrics**, visible harm registries, and predefined thresholds that trigger mitigation, fallback, or suspension when particular groups are carrying disproportionate risk.
- `504-defense-by-scope-civilian-control-civil-defense-no-subnational-war-machines-and-narrow-waist-collective-security.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should place war-making and armed defense at the national level under democratic civilian control and legislative budget authority, give subnational governments civil-defense and resilience roles without autonomous war machines, keep the military distinct from routine domestic order, and rely on treaty-bound regional alliances and a narrow global collective-security layer for external peace and aggression response rather than romanticizing either total sovereignty or world-state militarism.
- `510-networked-utilities-by-scope-local-access-metropolitan-mobility-basin-and-grid-coordination-national-universal-service-and-cross-border-interoperability.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern networked infrastructure by scale and function: neighborhoods and local institutions surface last-mile failure and build community resilience; municipalities manage rights-of-way, local distribution interfaces, streets, buses, water and sanitation operations where appropriate, and practical access; metropolitan bodies integrate mobility and other citywide networks that cross municipal borders; regions and basins govern watersheds, transmission corridors, balancing areas, and flood or drought constraints; nations guarantee universal service, backbone finance, regulation, and strategic resilience; and cross-border or global institutions set interoperability, shared-resource, and connectivity rules without pretending to run every local network.
- `511-climate-by-scope-local-adaptation-metropolitan-form-regional-resilience-national-transition-and-global-carbon-limits.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern climate by splitting powers according to where they actually bite: neighborhoods and local institutions surface risk and build resilience in daily life; municipalities shape buildings, land use, local mobility, heat, flooding, and service continuity; metropolitan and regional bodies govern commutes, airsheds, catchments, and strategic adaptation systems that cross municipal borders; nations set binding transition rules, carbon and industrial policy, just-transition finance, and national adaptation plans; and the global layer sets temperature and reporting baselines, climate-finance duties, and narrow coordination rules rather than pretending to run every place-based transition itself.
- `519-innovation-and-industrial-policy-by-scope-local-entrepreneurship-regional-clusters-national-missions-and-open-global-coordination.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern innovation and industrial policy by keeping entrepreneurship support, practical diffusion, local supplier development, and maker or skills ecosystems close to firms and workers; using metropolitan and regional institutions to cultivate clusters, applied research linkages, transition strategies, and shared innovation infrastructure; reserving mission setting, major R&D finance, competition-safe sector policy, strategic trade and resilience choices, and national innovation floors to the nation; and keeping the global layer narrow, focused on open science, standards, subsidy transparency, technology cooperation, and anti-arbitrage trade rules rather than a world ministry of industry.
- `531-rural-remote-and-peripheral-places-by-scope-local-agency-intermunicipal-service-backbones-regional-catchments-national-territorial-solidarity-and-global-learning.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat rural, remote, island, mountain, and other peripheral places not as residual territories waiting to shrink quietly but as legitimate political communities with distinct distance, sparsity, ecology, and production constraints: local institutions should set priorities, steward place knowledge, and surface service failure early; intermunicipal compacts should provide the shared administrative and service backbones that low-density places often need to remain capable; regional bodies should govern labour markets, referral systems, transport, watershed and land-use spillovers, and adaptation systems that cross many small jurisdictions; nations should guarantee territorial solidarity through fiscal equalization, connectivity, service floors, fair resource revenue, and public employment and investment rules that do not punish distance; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in fair trade, climate and connectivity support, and shared learning rather than imposing metro-centric metrics on every place.
- `532-water-and-sanitation-by-scope-local-access-municipal-stormwater-basin-governance-national-rights-and-transboundary-cooperation.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat water as both a daily service and a shared ecological system: households, farms, and neighbourhood institutions can surface failures, conserve, and steward local sources but should not be left to absorb utility risk alone; municipalities should guarantee drinking water, sanitation, stormwater, leak response, and ordinary public-space water safety; basin or regional authorities should govern aquifers, rivers, drought, flood, wastewater spillovers, and allocation conflicts at the hydrological scale that actually exists; nations should guarantee the human rights to water and sanitation, finance universal access, regulate quality, affordability, extraction, and public-health protection, and prevent postcode hydrology from becoming lower citizenship; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in transboundary waters, comparable standards, early warning, and upstream-downstream cooperation rather than pretending one local utility can solve a shared basin.
- `535-transport-and-logistics-by-scope-local-streets-metro-transit-regional-corridors-national-networks-and-global-interoperability.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat transport as a lived access system and a strategic circulation system at the same time: neighbourhoods and households can surface danger, exclusion, curb conflict, and last-mile need but should not be left to self-organize mobility; municipalities should govern streets, sidewalks, cycling, bus priority, curb use, traffic calming, road safety, and visible access to daily destinations; metropolitan authorities should own mass transit integration, fare systems, freight interfaces, and land-use coordination across one labour and housing market; regional institutions should govern intercity corridors, ports, inland waterways, airports, and resilience across the geography through which people and goods actually move; nations should own network finance, safety baselines, decarbonization strategy, essential-service guarantees, and major modal balance; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in aviation and maritime rules, cross-border interoperability, and fair technical standards rather than pretending one city can regulate the skies or the sea lanes.
- `536-oceans-coasts-and-fisheries-by-scope-local-stewardship-regional-seascapes-national-jurisdiction-and-global-high-seas-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the ocean as both a lived coast and a shared planetary system: coastal communities, ports, and small-scale fishers should hold real stewardship, monitoring, harbour, and livelihood voice close to place; regional or sea-basin institutions should govern migratory stocks, coastal erosion, estuaries, shipping spillovers, marine protected networks, and cumulative seascape impacts at the ecological scale that actually exists; coastal states should own marine spatial planning within their jurisdiction, fisheries law, labour and safety enforcement, port-state control, public marine science, and fair distribution of marine rents; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in the law of the sea, high-seas biodiversity, shipping pollution, seabed restraint, and shared fish-stock rules rather than letting coastal nationalism or flag-of-convenience arbitrage hollow out the ocean commons.
- `537-outer-space-and-orbital-commons-by-scope-local-hosting-regional-spaceports-national-authorization-and-global-sustainability-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat outer space as a global commons of use rather than a frontier of silent enclosure: local communities should hold real say over launch sites, tracking stations, astronomy impacts, land use, emergency planning, and public benefit where space infrastructure touches the ground; regional institutions should coordinate spaceport corridors, environmental review, disaster interfaces, and research ecosystems where activities spill across jurisdictions; nations should authorize and continuously supervise national activities in space, register objects, govern liability, spectrum and orbital use discipline, public research, procurement, and security constraints, and prevent private launch markets from becoming lightly regulated sovereignty proxies; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in non-appropriation, peaceful use, registration, debris mitigation, conjunction information-sharing, and long-term sustainability rather than letting orbit become an unmanaged congestion market.
- `538-money-and-payments-by-scope-local-cash-access-municipal-acceptance-national-public-money-and-global-interoperability.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat money and payments as constitutional infrastructure: households and neighbourhood institutions can surface exclusion, fraud, outage, and cash-access failures but should not mint rival monies for ordinary public life; municipalities should guarantee practical payment usability in everyday government, including cash access and acceptance where law protects it, legible public-payment channels, and inclusive collection design; metropolitan and regional institutions should coordinate shared payment touchpoints where commuting, service markets, and public agencies cross borders; nations should own legal tender, central bank money, payment-system oversight, public-payment rails, consumer protection, anti-fraud baselines, and resilience; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in message standards, cross-border interoperability, remittance quality, and data-friction reduction rather than pretending that local service design or national monetary legitimacy can be outsourced.
- `545-regulators-inspections-and-enforcement-role-clarity-risk-based-proportionality-due-process-and-no-government-by-shakedown.md` — An ideal polity should treat regulators and inspectorates as bounded public-law institutions whose job is to reduce real harm, preserve fair conditions, and keep essential systems trustworthy; give them clear missions, enough independence to resist improper influence, enough accountability to remain public servants, risk-based and proportionate enforcement tools, visible appeal routes, and budgets not addicted to penalties; and never let licensing, inspection, or fines become a substitute tax system, a patronage machine, or a theatre of arbitrary power.
- `546-public-enterprises-and-state-owned-enterprises-explicit-rationales-separated-roles-hard-budget-constraints-and-open-books.md` — An ideal polity may own and operate enterprises where public ownership is genuinely justified — for natural monopolies, essential network infrastructure, strategic resilience, mission-critical finance, or other clearly stated public purposes — but it should publish why it owns them, separate ownership from regulation and policy-making, state public-service obligations explicitly, compensate them transparently, impose hard budget constraints, keep boards and books professional and visible, and review the portfolio often enough that public enterprise does not become a hiding place for patronage, off-balance-sheet debt, or anti-competitive favoritism.
- `564-anti-corruption-bodies-and-integrity-commissions-by-scope-local-routing-regional-case-development-national-specialization-and-no-government-by-heroic-commission.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not rely on one heroic anti-corruption commission: keep local complaint intake, disclosure routing, whistleblower handoff, and ordinary integrity advice close enough to be usable; place regional or state-level investigative and inspection capacity where corruption markets, procurement webs, and patronage chains cross municipalities or where tiny jurisdictions are too captured to investigate themselves; reserve national government for the preventive architecture required by law, high-level and cross-regional corruption, asset-declaration verification, beneficial-ownership tracing, international cooperation, and strategy coordination; keep the global layer narrow in standards, peer review, and transnational case support; and never let anti-corruption institutions become either decorative ethics theater or unreviewable prosecutor-states.
- `581-mandate-finance-congruence-unfunded-mandates-vertical-fiscal-imbalance-and-no-decentralization-by-fiscal-theater.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **mandate-finance congruence** as constitutional law rather than budget etiquette: no level of government should be assigned a durable public function unless the same settlement also names the revenue basket, transfer formula, equalization rule, borrowing limits, and capability backstop that make the function actually dischargeable; delegated tasks must come with commensurate resources, local self-government must include at least some real own-source fiscal room, and upward rescue must be visible and reviewable rather than leaving decentralization to degrade into blame-shifting.
- `613-participatory-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-petitions-hearings-mini-publics-territorial-notice-and-no-metropolitan-participation-by-postcode.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **participatory home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, and intergovernmental one: territory-wide notice, petition and question routes, public hearings and consultations, bounded co-prioritisation and participatory-budget lanes where suitable, representative deliberative processes for complex trade-offs, and visible response duties — so residents can influence the shared tier directly rather than relying on borrowed municipal channels, host-city publicity, or consultation theatre.
- `662-global-institution-toolkit-by-problem-class-assemblies-secretariats-scientific-panels-registries-inspection-compliance-funds-and-no-world-state-monoculture.md` — The ideal global layer should be built from a **small toolkit of treaty-bound institutional forms matched to problem class** rather than from one fantasy model of world government: use assemblies and councils for norm-setting, secretariats and focal-point networks for continuous coordination, scientific panels for shared factual baselines, registries and reporting systems for comparability, inspection or verification where cheating matters, dispute and compliance lanes where interpretation recurs, and dedicated funds where solidarity is required — while refusing both fake world-state domesticity and empty declarations with no operating spine.
- `672-shared-regime-decision-rules-agenda-gates-quorum-consensus-simple-majority-qualified-majority-double-majority-veto-limits-and-no-governance-by-fake-unanimity.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed decision constitution** that separates agenda adoption, proposal circulation, quorum to open, quorum to decide, consensus practice, simple-majority procedure, qualified-majority substantive voting, double-majority shared-rule decisions, unanimity or veto for only narrow sovereignty-sensitive questions, and deadlock breakers — so bodies can act without either fake-unanimity theater or casual majoritarian override.
- `680-shared-regime-jurisprudence-memory-and-consistency-holdings-digests-departure-reasons-advisory-opinions-and-no-random-walk-governance.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed jurisprudence-memory constitution** that separates binding force, persuasive reasoning, holdings, summaries, digests, advisory opinions, and departure rules — so interpretation develops through visible continuity rather than random walk, citation theater, or stealth precedent.
- `690-shared-regime-field-security-and-continuity-constitutions-designated-officials-risk-tiers-clearance-crisis-cells-stockpiles-evacuation-and-no-presence-by-hope.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed field security-and-continuity constitution** that separates risk assessment, travel and deployment clearance, duty-station roles, premises security, crisis management cells, incident logging, logistics and stockpiles, evacuation or hibernation choices, and continuity of records and core services — so territorial presence is sustained by visible duty-of-care and continuity architecture rather than by courage theater, local improvisation, or hope.
- `692-shared-regime-digital-and-cyber-operating-constitutions-system-owners-identity-and-access-admin-tiers-change-windows-incident-response-vulnerability-disclosure-backups-recovery-vendor-lanes-and-no-secretariat-by-shared-password.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed digital-and-cyber operating constitution** that separates system ownership, identity and access, privileged administration, change and release control, incident response, vulnerability disclosure, vendor and cloud access, backup and restoration, recovery targets, and degraded-mode continuity — so the regime is not actually run through shared passwords, orphan systems, incident backlog, or recovery theater.
- `694-shared-regime-statistics-and-indicator-constitutions-designation-methodology-metadata-revisions-quality-assurance-release-calendars-and-no-governance-by-number-theater.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed statistics-and-indicator constitution** that separates designated official series from exploratory analytics, indicator ownership from political sponsorship, methodology from messaging, metadata from headline numbers, revisions from corrections, and release discipline from communications convenience — so evidence does not decay into number theater, indicator shopping, or policy-by-dashboard without professional standards.
- `696-shared-regime-evaluation-and-learning-constitutions-workplans-independence-management-response-recommendation-tracking-after-action-review-and-no-regime-by-report-shelf.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed evaluation-and-learning constitution** that separates workplan setting, commissioning, evaluator independence, evaluation from audit or monitoring, management response, recommendation tracking, public release, and structured learning loops such as after-action review — so institutional learning does not decay into report shelfware, recommendation theater, or “lessons learned” with no decision route.
- `697-shared-regime-strategic-planning-and-results-constitutions-general-programmes-programme-budgets-theories-of-change-baselines-targets-reviews-and-no-mission-by-project-pile.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed strategic-planning-and-results constitution** that separates long-horizon strategy, medium-term programme budgets, theories of change, outcome and output ladders, indicator and baseline rules, target-setting, reprogramming, and mid-cycle review — so the institution does not drift into mission by project pile, target theater, dashboard government, or budget without strategy.
- `708-evidence-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-shared-indicators-trigger-maps-blind-spot-registers-assurance-rhythm-and-no-government-by-dashboard-vibes.md` — Lane-typed government fields should publish one compact **evidence packet** that names the shared indicators, signal owners, trigger map, blind-spot register, and assurance rhythm used to judge the field — so control planes, mode shifts, repair packets, and sunset reviews run on explicit evidence with known gaps rather than on anecdotes, heroic operator memory, or dashboard theater.
- `709-challenge-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-entry-routes-complaints-petitions-second-look-lanes-feedback-duties-and-no-public-voice-by-consultation-theater.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, and an evidence packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **challenge packet** naming who may raise what kind of challenge, through which front door, with what triage into complaint, petition, appeal, ombuds, whistleblowing, or regulatory lanes, on what clocks, with what feedback and anti-retaliation duties, so the field can be corrected by the governed instead of merely observed by them.
- `717-asset-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-estate-fleet-equipment-condition-discipline-handback-and-no-government-by-orphan-assets.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, and an information packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **asset packet** saying which lane owns and stewards the field’s estate, fleet, equipment, depots, labs, stores, and critical spares; who holds custody, maintenance, calibration, and replacement duty; what condition and resilience floor applies; what lease, host-site, or operator dependencies exist; and what handback rule survives exit or transfer — so the field does not decay into government by orphan assets, lease camouflage, or maintenance exile.
- `718-service-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-whole-service-front-doors-route-classes-service-floors-continuity-and-no-government-by-front-door-scatter.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, an information packet, and an asset packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **service packet** saying what outcome the field’s service actually promises, which lane owns that promise, what front doors and route classes the public may use, what clocks and service floors bind, how channels and operators compose into one whole service, and what continuity and fallback rules survive overload, outage, provider failure, or redesign — so the field does not decay into government by front-door scatter, route roulette, or service-standard theater.
- `760-public-appointments-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-merit-vs-political-trust-open-competition-mixed-selection-confirmation-discipline-and-no-office-by-patronage-default.md` — Ideal governments should treat public appointments as a **typed constitutional lane rather than one generic power of disposal**: elected offices should be filled by voters, political-trust offices should be few and plainly political, most administrative and service-delivery posts should be filled through open merit-based recruitment, constitutionally sensitive or independence-bearing offices may justify mixed nominating and confirmation arrangements, and no polity should let patronage, vacancy manipulation, or prestige theatrics become the real appointments constitution.
- `786-right-to-be-heard-and-oral-hearing-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-notice-of-adverse-case-paper-default-credibility-triggers-remote-option-and-no-decision-by-unanswered-file.md` — Ideal governments should require that **no materially adverse administrative decision is taken without a real chance to answer the adverse case**, while also treating **oral hearing as a triggered safeguard rather than a theatrical default**: written procedure can be the ordinary lane for many routine matters, but live hearing becomes necessary when credibility, disputed facts, severe sanction, stigma, complex expert conflict, or serious irreversibility make paper process too thin to be fair.
- `792-stress-test-and-drill-cards-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-essential-service-continuity-command-legibility-fiscal-buffers-rights-discipline-rescoping-signals-and-no-paper-constitution-by-calm-weather.md` — The archive should pair its ideal-government answer key and benchmark cards with one compact **stress-test and drill-card format** for each scope — essential-service continuity, command and escalation legibility, reserve and surge discipline, intergovernmental handoff integrity, legality and rights restraint under pressure, public communication, and recovery or handback triggers — so governments are judged not only by their steady-state design but by whether they remain honest under flood, blackout, outbreak, fiscal shock, cyber disruption, or constitutional strain.
- `800-assessment-missions-for-ideal-governments-by-scope-self-assessment-desk-review-site-visits-public-hearings-evidence-rooms-management-response-and-no-benchmark-by-questionnaire-alone.md` — The archive should pair its answer-key, benchmark, stress-test, maintenance, proof-pack, contestability, comparator, and temporary-object notes with one compact **assessment-mission grammar**: **every serious scope judgment should declare its review method, combine self-assessment with desk review, site or field verification, stakeholder hearings, contradiction logging, and a reasoned management-response path, so governments are not benchmarked by questionnaire alone or by prestige-site theater instead of evidence**.
- `809-research-frontier-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-settled-defaults-live-thresholds-morphology-uncertainty-fiscal-floor-tests-legitimacy-triggers-and-no-false-precision-by-constitutional-confidence-theater.md` — The archive should now separate **settled default doctrine** from **live research questions**: it can state with high confidence the vocation, minimum kit, and anti-cosplay limit of each scope, but it should keep threshold questions — when a functional city truly needs metro democracy, when sparse territories need county-style pooling, when a region is a real platform rather than decorative duplication, how much fiscal congruence is enough, when intervention should trigger, and how thick upper-tier institutions may become — inside one compact research frontier rather than pretending the whole stack is equally settled.
- `817-participation-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-open-dockets-hearings-user-councils-deliberative-mini-publics-response-ledgers-and-no-heavy-power-by-consultation-theater.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **who owns it**, **how money moves through it**, **where its operating spine lives**, and **where scrutiny and redress live**, it should also be able to say **what participation chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should publish open dockets and simple input windows rather than staging fake popular mandates, shared-service backbones should run structured user and accessibility input without pretending pooled operations are a substitute for elected politics, bounded functional authorities should carry recurring hearings and response duties plus deliberative methods where long-horizon tradeoffs justify them, and general-purpose territorial tiers should own a full participation constitution rather than borrowing legitimacy from consultation theater.
- `835-emergency-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-readiness-municipal-incident-command-regional-civil-protection-national-derogation-discipline-and-treaty-alerting.md` — The archive should answer the question **what emergency and exception grammar should ordinarily fit each scope?** with scale-matched escalation rather than one panic state fetish: **micro-local bodies should default to readiness, warning, mutual aid, and witness rather than emergency sovereignty; municipalities should be the first ordinary home of incident command, continuity, sheltering, and short-horizon emergency operations under ordinary law; metropolitan governments should carry shared-system disruption management where the functional city is one risk field; regional or provincial governments may honestly house civil-protection, wildfire, flood, logistics, and mutual-aid platforms where those risks are territorially real; national government should hold the thickest declaration, derogation, reserve, and exceptional coordination powers under legislative renewal, judicial review, and strict handback discipline; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound, specializing in alerting, coordination, standards, pooled assistance, and tightly authorized collective action rather than becoming ambient permanent emergency government**.
- `836-participation-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-assembly-municipal-dockets-metro-territorial-hearings-national-petition-ladders-and-treaty-observers.md` — If the archive already knows **what government should exist at each scope**, **how it is chosen**, **how it is financed**, **how it is scrutinized**, **where force lives**, **where records live**, and **what emergency lane fits it**, it should also know **how public voice honestly re-enters that government at each scale**: direct and reachable assembly voice at micro-local scale; petitions, hearings, consultations, bounded participatory-budget lanes, and occasional deliberative mini-publics at municipal scale; territory-wide participation homes for metropolitan and regional bodies that govern real shared systems; parliamentary hearing, petition, consultation, and rare constitution-level referendum lanes at national scale; and structured observer, submission, hearing, and stakeholder-participation routes for continental and global bodies rather than fake world-plebiscitary theater.

## contestability

- `404-contestable-automation-and-appeals-routing.md` — No consequential automated system should be allowed to operate without a visible path from **notice** to **reason** to **override** to **appeal** to **remedy**.
- `419-production-monitoring-fed-by-complaints-appeals-and-user-feedback.md` — A public automated system is not adequately monitored if it only watches internal metrics. **Complaints, appeals, operator reports, and affected-user feedback** should be treated as first-class operational telemetry and folded into the system’s monitoring, evaluation, and review loop.
- `421-public-impact-assessment-dossiers-and-peer-review-before-live-use.md` — Before public automated decisions go live, operators should publish a compact **assessment dossier** that combines impact scoring, context-specific rights analysis, independent review, and accountable sign-off.
- `424-point-of-interaction-notice-explanation-and-accessible-format.md` — Any public AI touchpoint that can affect a person should announce itself early, explain itself meaningfully when it matters, and do so in formats the affected person can actually use.
- `425-portable-appeal-packets-and-log-retention.md` — Contestability fails when the evidence trail is scattered or ephemeral; every consequential AI-assisted decision should leave behind a portable review packet built from logs, provenance, and operator actions.
- `429-material-change-notice-and-public-record-refresh-discipline.md` — When a consequential public AI system changes in scope, data, model, provider, phase, or operating context, every public record about it should be refreshed before or at the moment the change takes effect.
- `434-override-telemetry-escalation-queues-and-second-look-sampling.md` — Human oversight is not real unless overrides, disagreements, and stop decisions are counted, reviewed, and turned into operating changes instead of disappearing as private friction.
- `436-redaction-gateways-protected-attribute-filters-and-exception-registers.md` — Public AI systems should default to **redaction before inference**: block or strip unnecessary personal data, prohibit protected-attribute and emotion inference by default, and require a named, reviewable exception register for the rare cases law explicitly permits.
- `439-legal-authority-maps-scope-gates-and-jurisdiction-labels.md` — A public AI system should not reach consequential use until the operating team can name the **decision it affects, the authority that permits it, the scope test that brings it under governance, and the review route that governs challenges to it**.
- `442-maker-checker-separation-independent-challenge-and-fallback-review.md` — Consequential public AI should separate **builders, operators, approvers, and reviewers** enough that no single role can quietly tune, approve, and act on the same system without an independent second look or documented compensating control.
- `444-privileged-access-tiers-role-restricted-logs-and-admin-session-review.md` — Public AI should restrict sensitive administration and log access by role, record privileged actions in detail, and subject elevated sessions to routine review so governance evidence is not left inside an unexamined operator back room.
- `445-explicit-release-decisions-frozen-public-surfaces-and-no-release-records.md` — Consequential public AI should not move from “reviewed” to live use by implication; institutions should record an explicit publish, hold, or no-release decision and preserve the exact public-facing governance surface that was in force at that moment.
- `446-durable-case-state-cues-transient-notice-limits-and-persistent-status-surfaces.md` — Consequential public AI should not communicate controlling meaning only through disappearing toasts, snackbars, or transient status messages; important outcomes, warnings, and next-step cues should remain durably visible and backed by accessible status semantics after the message moment passes.
- `447-audience-exact-disclosure-classes-exposure-boundaries-and-review-lanes.md` — Governance artifacts for consequential public AI should carry exact audience and exposure labels so public, affected-person, operator, reviewer, regulator, supplier, and privileged-admin lanes cannot be silently mixed or widened.
- `448-governance-state-honesty-request-review-approval-and-live-separation.md` — Consequential public AI should not collapse roster presence, active review request, completed review, approval, queued release, and live operation into one fuzzy status; each state should mean one thing, stay scoped to a named basis, and surface explicit repair when that basis goes stale.
- `454-preview-sufficiency-omitted-governance-non-inference-and-next-honest-action.md` — A snippet, card, toast, queue row, portal tile, or case preview for consequential public AI should state what the preview is sufficient for, what governance-bearing facts are omitted, which tempting inferences are refused, and what the next honest action is.
- `456-history-preserving-public-record-navigation-stable-anchors-and-honest-fragment-failure.md` — Consequential public-AI records, notice pages, case portals, and appeal surfaces should preserve stable addresses and anchors, create browser history only when the user crossed a meaningful state boundary, and fail honestly when a cited deep link or fragment no longer resolves.
- `458-dependence-aware-assurance-counts-shared-origin-witnesses-and-pseudo-independence-guards.md` — Public-AI assurance should record shared origins across tests, judges, vendors, datasets, prompts, and reviewers so multiple agreeing checks are not mistaken for multiple independent grounds for trust.
- `459-approval-freshness-classes-no-renewal-by-use-and-rereview-clocks.md` — Consequential public-AI approvals, waivers, elevated grants, and standing adoption decisions should carry explicit freshness classes and rereview clocks, and continued use or silence should not silently renew them.
- `468-fused-governance-rollups-blocker-inventories-and-macrostate-decomposition.md` — Consequential public-AI dashboards, queue summaries, and readiness badges should decompose into named substates and live blocker inventories rather than one fused macrostate, so a green rollup cannot hide stale evidence, blocked disclosure, or missing review.
- `470-intake-failure-classification-handoff-vs-artifact-and-manual-fallback-lanes.md` — When consequential notices, appeals, evidence packets, or supplier submissions fail to arrive, open, or register, the archive should distinguish bad artifact from bad delivery or handoff and preserve a typed manual fallback lane so rights do not disappear into one broken digital path.
- `472-case-lineage-withdrawal-cancellation-supersession-and-reopen-receipts.md` — Consequential public-AI cases, appeals, incidents, and review requests should preserve typed lineage across withdrawal, cancellation, supersession, duplicate-merge, expiry, and reopening, with predecessor-successor links and reasoned receipts, so no rights-bearing matter silently disappears.
- `475-official-communications-as-evidence-correction-chains-and-channel-registries.md` — Consequential public-AI communications should be treated as first-class evidence surfaces with an official-channel registry, explicit correction linkage, and capture rules for what was said where and when, so public notice cannot drift into silent edits, split-view updates, or screenshot folklore.
- `477-basis-locked-pending-states-drift-guards-and-explicit-reissue.md` — Consequential public-AI requests, reviews, approvals, queue entries, and ready states should stay locked to the exact basis they were issued against, and should fall back to stale-or-reissue-needed rather than silently following later drift, retargeting, or rebuild.
- `478-structured-decision-traces-minimal-bindings-reason-codes-and-safe-explain-surfaces.md` — Consequential public-AI actions should leave behind a stable decision-trace object that records the governing basis, route, inputs used, matched rule or model context, reason codes, obligations, and redactions in a compact safe form, so explanations, appeals, and incident review do not depend on backend folklore or prose reconstruction.
- `479-governance-diff-surface-registries-canonical-review-planes-and-drift-funnels.md` — Consequential public-AI programs should maintain a canonical registry of governance diff surfaces so review, release, and audit can say which change planes exist, which ones were checked, and which new surface types require explicit admission instead of silently creating fresh drift territory.
- `482-queue-dwell-honesty-service-clocks-and-anti-starvation-escalation.md` — Rights-bearing requests, reviews, appeals, exceptions, and incident items should expose when their clock started, what service window or expectation applies, whether they are merely queued or actively worked, what is blocking progress, and how escalation happens when dwell exceeds thresholds, so “under review” cannot launder starvation.
- `484-epistemic-status-tags-evidence-classes-and-no-authority-by-hedge.md` — Consequential public-AI claims, notices, summaries, incident updates, and review packets should mark each load-bearing statement as observed, measured, attested, reported, inferred, disputed, or unknown, with an explicit confidence class tied to evidence completeness, so hedged prose cannot quietly launder uncertainty into authority.
- `485-effective-state-resolution-correction-graphs-and-no-authority-by-feed-order.md` — When consequential public-AI notices, status updates, corrections, withdrawals, and superseding records accumulate over time, the institution should compute and publish one deterministic effective current state from explicit lineage links, and should treat forks or unresolved ambiguity as incidents rather than letting feed order, CMS recency, or whichever copy looks newest decide authority.
