- `807-assessment-team-independence-and-conflict-discipline-for-scope-reviews-recusal-rosters-secondment-firebreaks-host-picked-experts-donor-pathways-and-no-constitutional-judgment-by-interested-mission.md` — The archive should pair its assessment-mission, evidence-register, contestability, and close-out notes with one compact **mission-integrity grammar**: **every serious scope review should declare who is judging, who is only informing, what interests and funding pathways each reviewer carries, what firebreaks apply to secondees and host-nominated specialists, when recusal is mandatory, and how outsiders can challenge the composition of the team before findings harden into the live constitution, so the archive does not mistake expertise, proximity, or funding convenience for independence**.
- `808-calibration-packs-moderation-loops-and-precedent-banks-for-scope-assessments-score-anchors-difficult-case-conferences-documented-departures-and-no-benchmark-by-reviewer-mood.md` — The archive should pair its benchmark, mission, evidence-register, and mission-integrity notes with one compact **review-calibration grammar**: **every serious scope assessment should keep a small calibration pack with lane-specific score anchors, worked examples, threshold splits, precedent notes, moderation checkpoints, and documented departures, so that different review teams can reach comparably disciplined judgments without collapsing everything into one blended score or one charismatic reviewer’s mood**.
- `816-oversight-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-member-scrutiny-external-audit-ombuds-routes-judicial-review-and-no-heavy-power-by-self-marking.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **who owns it**, **how money moves through it**, and **where its operating spine lives**, it should also be able to say **what oversight chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should remain mainly reviewable through the member governments that delegate into them, shared-service backbones should preserve visible principal-side scrutiny plus independent audit and complaint routes, bounded functional authorities should carry named external audit, maladministration review, legality or regulatory checks, and judicial remedy proportionate to their power, and general-purpose territorial tiers should own a full public oversight constitution rather than marking themselves through internal committees alone.
- `819-boundary-and-membership-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-accession-gates-territory-rules-amendment-thickness-exit-protocols-dissolution-paths-and-no-map-by-one-way-ratchet.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, and **what information chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should use open and reversible participation with no hidden territorial claim, shared-service backbones should declare member classes, accession formulas, notice periods, and unwind rules, bounded functional authorities should use chartered territories plus staged accession and constrained exit, and general-purpose territorial tiers should rely on statutory boundary change with public consultation, transition machinery, and no map by one-way ratchet.
- `823-contracting-boundary-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-light-support-buying-principal-owned-commissioning-chartered-concessions-change-control-and-no-heavy-power-by-contract-escape-hatch.md` — When the archive has already established that a cross-boundary problem is real, chosen the honest form, and said who governs, pays, operates, votes, hears disputes, owns the assets, and can unwind the map, it should still require one compact **contracting-boundary chain**: thin connectors may buy only light support and must not become hidden commissioners of core public systems; shared-service backbones may buy pooled administrative tools and support services while political title remains visibly with the principals; bounded functional authorities may procure, franchise, or concession the named system they are chartered to govern, but only through a visible commissioner spine, hard change-control, and full public review; and general-purpose territorial tiers may use contracts as delivery instruments without letting procurement, concessions, PPPs, or managed-service deals become constitutional escape hatches for powers that should remain politically owned.
- `824-regulatory-and-enforcement-boundary-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-signal-routing-joined-up-inspections-bounded-permitting-public-sanctions-and-no-heavy-power-by-shared-badge.md` — When the archive has already established that a cross-boundary problem is real, chosen the honest form, and said who governs, pays, operates, votes, publishes, contracts, owns, and can unwind the arrangement, it should still require one compact **regulatory-and-enforcement-boundary chain**: thin connectors may align standards proposals, share risk signals, and route cases but must not issue permits or sanctions in their own name; shared-service backbones may pool intake, inspection support, and specialist process while the political principals retain visible legal title to permissions and coercive acts; bounded functional authorities may license, inspect, direct, and sanction only inside a named public remit with risk-based proportionality, separation from operation, and live review routes; and general-purpose territorial tiers may carry broader permitting and enforcement constitutions without letting host badges, fee addiction, or delegated vendor discipline become hidden sovereignty.
- `827-mandate-duration-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-short-local-rotation-municipal-and-metro-stability-national-renewal-windows-and-treaty-review-clocks.md` — The archive should answer the question **how long should governing mandates last at each scope?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one calendar idol: short and recallable mandates for micro-local stewardship, medium terms for municipalities and metropolitan governments that need enough runway to budget and deliver, regional and national renewal windows that are usually long enough to govern but short enough to correct, and plurilateral or global bodies that live on fixed review and reauthorization clocks rather than ambient permanence.
- `832-oversight-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-witness-municipal-scrutiny-metro-audit-national-watchdogs-and-treaty-review.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should each scope ordinarily be scrutinized and corrected once it has real public authority?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one watchdog fetish: **micro-local bodies should rely mainly on open meetings, visible records, rotation, and cheap escalation rather than a miniature oversight state; municipalities should be the first level with a full public oversight kit of chamber scrutiny, independent external audit, complaint or ombuds routes, disclosure, and ordinary legality review; metropolitan and regional governments should own equally real audit and redress lanes rather than borrowing them permanently from a host city or ministry; national government should carry the fullest fourth-branch and court-backed oversight constitution; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound but still face visible member scrutiny, independent audit and evaluation, complaint and ethics channels, and published review cycles rather than secretariat self-marking**.
- `833-coercion-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-witness-municipal-civil-enforcement-regional-police-platforms-national-force-monopoly-and-treaty-bound-restraint.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should coercive and enforcement power ordinarily live at each scope?** with scale-matched restraint rather than one badge fetish: **micro-local bodies should default to witness, de-escalation, and referral rather than general coercive authority; municipalities should be the first ordinary home of civil enforcement, inspections, nuisance abatement, and everyday public-order administration under ordinary law; metropolitan governments should hold only those bounded cross-boundary enforcement and emergency-coordination powers that shared systems actually require; regional or provincial governments may honestly house large territorial police, emergency, and regulatory platforms where the constitutional order truly assigns them; national government should carry the thickest monopoly over criminal law, armed force, borders, and exceptional emergency concentration under the strongest rights and review discipline; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound, relying mainly on inspection, reporting, sanctions, certification, and tightly authorized operations rather than ambient upper-state police sovereignty**.
- `834-information-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-ledgers-municipal-record-homes-metro-observatories-national-statistics-and-treaty-registries.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should authoritative public facts, records, and decision visibility ordinarily live at each scope?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one dashboard fetish: **micro-local bodies should keep simple minutes, noticeboards, steward ledgers, and escalation logs rather than miniature data states; municipalities should be the first level with a full public information constitution of clerks or record stewards, open meeting packets, service and permit records, publication calendars, and reusable public data; metropolitan and regional governments should own their own observatories, geospatial baselines, and cross-boundary performance records rather than parasitic dependence on a host city or ministry; national government should carry the thickest official-statistics, gazette, archive, and interoperability spine; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound but still maintain comparability standards, registries, alerting channels, and shared reporting rather than private dashboards or counterfeit world omniscience**.
- `835-emergency-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-readiness-municipal-incident-command-regional-civil-protection-national-derogation-discipline-and-treaty-alerting.md` — The archive should answer the question **what emergency and exception grammar should ordinarily fit each scope?** with scale-matched escalation rather than one panic state fetish: **micro-local bodies should default to readiness, warning, mutual aid, and witness rather than emergency sovereignty; municipalities should be the first ordinary home of incident command, continuity, sheltering, and short-horizon emergency operations under ordinary law; metropolitan governments should carry shared-system disruption management where the functional city is one risk field; regional or provincial governments may honestly house civil-protection, wildfire, flood, logistics, and mutual-aid platforms where those risks are territorially real; national government should hold the thickest declaration, derogation, reserve, and exceptional coordination powers under legislative renewal, judicial review, and strict handback discipline; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound, specializing in alerting, coordination, standards, pooled assistance, and tightly authorized collective action rather than becoming ambient permanent emergency government**.
- `837-adjudication-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-pre-legal-entry-municipal-administrative-justice-regional-ordinary-courts-national-apex-review-and-treaty-tribunals.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should adjudication itself honestly live at each scope?** with scale-matched defaults rather than court fetish or courthouse minimalism: **micro-local bodies should offer witness, record, mediation, and easy entry into law rather than pretending to be sovereign courts; municipalities should be the first scale with a legible administrative-justice front door for ordinary daily disputes, but not the last word on legality against themselves; metropolitan and regional governments with real cross-boundary power should have equally real ordinary-court, tribunal, or legality-review homes rather than sending people on a host-city treasure hunt; national government should carry the apex and constitutional-review layer that secures rights, uniform due-process floors, and competence settlement across the stack; and continental or global bodies should use treaty-bound courts and tribunals only where the mandate is genuinely real, without pretending to be either a world judiciary of everything or a diplomacy-only zone immune from law**.
- `840-preemption-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-headroom-metro-primacy-federal-bargain-locks-national-floors-and-treaty-bounded-override.md` — The archive should usually prefer different override grammars by scale: **micro-local bodies should remain subject to municipal law and charter while keeping visible voice lanes; municipalities should enjoy broad headroom above common floors unless preemption is explicit, proportionate, and reviewable; metropolitan governments should hold named primacy inside real shared urban systems; regional governments should keep constitutionally real autonomy except where the federal bargain openly assigns paramount power elsewhere; national governments may impose rights floors, solidarity rules, and interoperability baselines but should face a higher burden before using ceilings or field occupation; and continental or global bodies should override only through explicit treaty commitments rather than ambient upper-tier drift**.

## corrections-governance

- `485-effective-state-resolution-correction-graphs-and-no-authority-by-feed-order.md` — When consequential public-AI notices, status updates, corrections, withdrawals, and superseding records accumulate over time, the institution should compute and publish one deterministic effective current state from explicit lineage links, and should treat forks or unresolved ambiguity as incidents rather than letting feed order, CMS recency, or whichever copy looks newest decide authority.
- `528-freedom-of-conscience-and-religion-by-scope-local-coexistence-municipal-neutrality-regional-fairness-national-rights-and-global-protection.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat freedom of conscience, religion, and belief as plural civic infrastructure rather than a privilege of dominant traditions or a project of militant homogenization: households, associations, and communities should be free to form, change, practice, criticize, or refuse belief without coercion; municipalities should keep ordinary civic life neutral and usable through fair permits, equal access, cemetery and calendar accommodation, and non-discriminatory service interfaces; regional bodies should coordinate fairness across hospitals, prisons, schools, and other institutions whose catchments outrun one city; nations should guarantee legal personality, anti-discrimination law, equal citizenship, education and service neutrality, hate-crime and incitement baselines, and rights-safe rules for conscientious objection; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in rights norms, persecution response, and anti-incitement principles rather than trying to govern theology from afar.
- `556-police-services-by-scope-neighborhood-legibility-municipal-or-county-operations-metropolitan-serious-crime-bureaus-national-standards-and-no-police-self-investigation.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **police services** as a **civilian, rights-bound, externally answerable public service** rather than as a self-defining armed caste: keep neighborhood contact and ordinary response close enough to communities to stay legible, size police organizations and custody/investigation support large enough to resist tiny-jurisdiction capture, push serious-crime, forensic, and cross-border investigation to metropolitan or regional institutions, reserve national government for legal floors, training, anti-corruption and narrow specialist support, and never allow **police self-investigation** or militarized political policing to masquerade as democratic order.
- `557-detention-corrections-and-reentry-by-scope-local-contact-and-release-links-regional-custody-probation-national-rights-floors-and-no-government-by-warehousing.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **detention, corrections, and reentry** as a **strictly limited, rights-bound, reintegration-oriented part of justice** rather than as a hidden warehousing system: keep local roles focused on family contact, service continuity, diversion support, and release preparation rather than long-term cage sovereignty; use metropolitan or regional institutions for most remand custody, prisons, probation, parole, health continuity, and professionally managed inspectionable facilities; reserve national government for penal law, decarceration incentives, independent monitoring, and non-negotiable humane-treatment floors; and never allow **jails, prisons, or release systems to become opaque human storage insulated from courts, health systems, and society**.
- `586-function-transfer-packs-staff-assets-records-contracts-liabilities-and-no-reassignment-by-legal-text-alone.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **any transfer of a public function across levels of government as a full transfer pack rather than a sentence in a law**: whenever a competence moves, the same settlement should also name the effective date, service standard, staff lane, asset and lease inventory, contract and procurement treatment, records and data custody, ongoing-case handoff, fiscal lane, liability rule, transition authority, dispute route, and review clock, so that decentralisation or recentralisation cannot occur by moving the headline power while leaving the receiving government to inherit an empty shell.
- `626-public-communication-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-canonical-channels-corrections-inclusive-reach-and-no-government-by-press-release-federation.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it should acquire an explicit **public-communication home**: a named official communications function distinct from party or campaign messaging; one canonical set of channels for notices, updates, warnings, and explanations; correction and version trails; multilingual and accessible publication discipline; clear docking between general information and legal notice; and archival capture of official statements so the territory does not govern through host-city press offices, operator fragments, screenshots, and rumor.
- `647-scope-remand-discipline-cure-instructions-bounded-reopening-and-no-stack-redesign-by-reconsideration.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat **remand** in materially stack-altering disputes as a **bounded cure lane**, not as an open invitation to redesign the scope stack: a reviewing body that sends a package back for correction should specify exactly what defect must be cured, what remains frozen or intact, what consultation or consent must be rerun, and when the matter has crossed the line into a fresh packet, opinion, override, or constituent decision.
- `650-scope-estoppel-limits-reliance-sunk-cost-benefit-retention-and-no-stack-change-by-dependence.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should refuse to let **reliance, sunk cost, operational dependence, accepted benefits, or delayed objection manufacture constitutional title**: when a materially stack-altering move lacked the right authority, the right consent, or the right public lane, the answer should be cure, remand, override, rollback, or fresh authorization — not estoppel by familiarity, expense, or service dependency.
- `657-scope-successor-accountability-legacy-acts-liabilities-records-and-no-blame-laundering-by-rescoping.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat **future competence, predecessor accountability, successor service continuity, records custody, litigation defence, and fiscal liability as separate questions that must each be typed explicitly whenever a function moves**, so rescoping cannot become a way to enjoy new power while laundering blame for old acts, omissions, debts, broken files, or unremedied harms.
- `658-scope-evidentiary-continuity-record-provenance-and-no-proof-laundering-by-migration.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require every **materially stack-altering reform** to preserve **evidentiary continuity** across record transfer, system migration, redaction, archival cutover, and platform replacement — with stable identifiers, provenance metadata, chain-of-custody, transformation logs, and certified retrieval routes — so responsibility can still be proven after a function moves and rescoping cannot dissolve proof through administrative or technical migration.
- `670-shared-regime-exit-ladders-denunciation-withdrawal-suspension-expulsion-savings-clauses-wind-down-duties-and-no-perpetual-membership-fiction.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed exit ladder** that distinguishes withdrawal or denunciation, temporary suspension, lawful expulsion where the constituting text allows it, module exit, territorial rollback, and post-exit survival clauses — with trigger, notice lane, decision body, effective date, pending-case rule, continuing liabilities, record duties, and re-entry path — so participation can end without pretending either that membership is irrevocable or that exit erases prior obligations.
- `674-shared-regime-records-and-publicity-public-private-sessions-document-registers-meeting-records-vote-records-authentic-texts-corrections-and-no-governance-by-missing-papertrail.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed documentary constitution** that separates session publicity, agenda and paper circulation, official document registers, meeting-record formats, vote records, authentic texts, correction notices, and retention or access rules — so public authority does not vanish into missing minutes, unofficial drafts, or document folklore.
- `694-shared-regime-statistics-and-indicator-constitutions-designation-methodology-metadata-revisions-quality-assurance-release-calendars-and-no-governance-by-number-theater.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed statistics-and-indicator constitution** that separates designated official series from exploratory analytics, indicator ownership from political sponsorship, methodology from messaging, metadata from headline numbers, revisions from corrections, and release discipline from communications convenience — so evidence does not decay into number theater, indicator shopping, or policy-by-dashboard without professional standards.
- `717-asset-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-estate-fleet-equipment-condition-discipline-handback-and-no-government-by-orphan-assets.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, and an information packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **asset packet** saying which lane owns and stewards the field’s estate, fleet, equipment, depots, labs, stores, and critical spares; who holds custody, maintenance, calibration, and replacement duty; what condition and resilience floor applies; what lease, host-site, or operator dependencies exist; and what handback rule survives exit or transfer — so the field does not decay into government by orphan assets, lease camouflage, or maintenance exile.
- `723-review-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-reconsideration-appeal-remand-interim-relief-finality-and-no-government-by-remedy-maze.md` — Once the archive has challenge, decision, notice, and effect packets for a field, it should also publish one narrow **review packet** saying which second-look lanes exist, which acts must pass through reconsideration before appeal and which may go straight outward, who hears each route, what record and standard of review apply, what interim relief or stay is available, what remand or substitution powers exist, and when finality blocks endless reopening — so the field does not decay into government by remedy maze, sponsor-friendly reconsideration, or hidden no-review zones.
- `736-temporary-neutral-custody-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-contested-handoffs-rights-bearing-queues-record-spines-credential-escrow-and-no-settlement-by-possession.md` — Once the archive can say how a function should be routed (`726`-`728`), ratified (`729`), kept continuous (`730`), witnessed at cutover (`731`), temporarily hosted (`732`), cleanly closed (`733`), tested through an independent-live window (`734`), and rolled back when stabilization fails (`735`), it should also keep one compact **temporary neutral-custody packet** for the harder interval where neither old holder nor new holder can honestly be treated as fully settled: appoint a bounded custodian for named control surfaces, preserve the public route and evidentiary spine, freeze or escrow high-risk powers, keep pending matters legible, and refuse to let mere possession of live systems, records, or credentials masquerade as constitutional settlement.
- `737-release-packets-for-ideal-government-neutral-custody-full-partial-and-phased-release-receiver-readiness-residual-safeguards-and-no-custody-exit-by-impatience.md` — Once the archive has a temporary neutral-custody packet (`736`), it should also keep one compact **custody-release packet** for the moment named surfaces leave custody and re-enter ordinary government: classify the release type, prove receiver readiness surface by surface, preserve case and record lineage, state what safeguards remain temporarily in force, and refuse to end custody merely because a deadline, press statement, or impatient principal wants the appearance of settlement.
- `738-custodian-discharge-packets-for-ideal-government-neutral-custody-final-account-residual-liabilities-record-seal-and-no-shadow-government-by-finished-interim.md` — Once the archive can place named surfaces into temporary neutral custody (`736`) and release them out again (`737`), it should also keep one compact **custodian-discharge packet** for the moment the custodian itself stands down: prove every custodial surface has been released, lawfully retired, or explicitly rehomed; freeze one final account of residue, liabilities, and records; preserve lookup and challenge routes after the custodian disappears; and refuse to let a finished interim body linger as hidden operator, archive gatekeeper, or excuse sink.
- `739-residual-estate-packets-for-post-custody-government-closeout-shells-claims-record-access-financial-tail-review-clocks-and-no-ghost-state-by-leftover-residue.md` — Once the archive can place named surfaces into temporary neutral custody (`736`), release them out again (`737`), and discharge the custodian itself (`738`), it should also keep one compact **residual-estate packet** for the narrower afterlife that sometimes honestly remains: a typed closeout shell for surviving claims, residual funds, record-access duties, litigation or audit tails, and other bounded obligations, with one public route, one residue ledger, one accountable owner, and one termination proof so a leftover estate does not quietly become a ghost state by residue.
- `740-residual-estate-termination-certificates-for-post-custody-government-closeout-shells-zero-residue-proof-final-routing-and-no-ghost-state-by-never-ending-tail.md` — Once the archive can admit a bounded residual estate after custody discharge (`739`), it should also keep one compact **residual-estate termination certificate** proving when that tail is actually over: zero open residue or explicitly rehomed last fragments, final accounts and closure disclosures, exhausted or lawfully rerouted claims, sealed record and disclosure homes, revoked residual powers, retired public routes, and one durable historical certificate — so a closeout shell cannot linger forever as ghost state by never-ending tail.
- `777-execution-of-administrative-and-judicial-decisions-against-public-authorities-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-compliance-clocks-budget-home-escalation-and-no-judgment-by-non-execution.md` — Ideal governments should treat **execution of administrative and judicial decisions against public authorities** as part of the rule-of-law core rather than as post-judgment housekeeping: when a ministry, municipality, agency, regulator, police body, prison authority, benefits office, land registrar, or treasury loses, the system should have clear compliance clocks, named responsible officials, budget and payment homes, interest and penalty rules, supervisory escalation, and user-visible follow-up so the state cannot turn delay, fragmentation, or lack-of-funds claims into a second victory after losing on the merits.
- `796-intervention-ladders-for-failing-governments-of-each-scope-support-first-proportional-supervision-special-measures-handback-clocks-and-no-permanent-emergency-custody.md` — When a government-by-scope arrangement keeps failing its benchmark, stress, maintenance, or proof duties, the archive should not jump straight from diagnosis to permanent takeover. It should use one compact **intervention ladder**: **support first, escalate by law and proportionality, separate own-competence supervision from delegated-task control, keep any special measures temporary and reviewable, and pair every intervention with a handback or formal rescoping test so rescue does not harden into quiet permanent custody**.

## culture-governance

- `522-culture-and-heritage-by-scope-local-belonging-municipal-institutions-regional-ecologies-national-pluralism-and-global-commons.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern culture as a rights-bearing public good rather than propaganda, luxury, or folklore storage: neighborhoods and communities keep living practices, memory, and language-use close to life; municipalities should sustain libraries, museums, venues, festivals, archives, arts education links, public space, and fair local cultural access; regional bodies should support linguistic and heritage ecologies, touring circuits, landscape-scale memory, and cultural production systems that outrun one city; nations should guarantee cultural rights, artistic freedom, public support, restitution and heritage law, and plural national institutions without imposing one official culture; and the global layer should protect humanity’s shared heritage, support cultural diversity, and coordinate anti-trafficking and cooperation without becoming a world ministry of taste.
- `527-end-of-life-and-death-care-by-scope-local-accompaniment-municipal-death-administration-regional-palliative-capacity-national-rights-and-global-pain-relief.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat dying, death care, and bereavement as governed phases of civic life rather than hospital leftovers: households, friends, and community institutions can accompany the dying and mourn the dead but should not be left alone to navigate pain, paperwork, and impossible choices; municipalities should make death registration, burial or cremation access, bereavement navigation, and culturally plural local practice legible and reachable; regional bodies should coordinate palliative-care networks, hospice and specialist capacity, coronial or medical-examiner functions, and referral pathways that outrun one city; nations should guarantee consent law, advance directives, surrogate decision rules, equitable palliative access, medicine availability, and vital-registration baselines; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in essential pain-relief access, rights norms, and knowledge exchange rather than pretending to legislate every intimate end-of-life question for the whole world.
- `529-indigenous-peoples-and-self-government-by-scope-community-authority-municipal-consent-regional-co-governance-national-plurinational-constitutionalism-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat Indigenous peoples as peoples and governing authorities rather than as cultural stakeholders inside someone else’s map: Indigenous communities and nations should retain authority over identity, membership, internal institutions, culture, and many matters of everyday law according to their own traditions and evolving consent; municipalities should share space, services, permits, and practical coexistence through negotiated respect rather than zoning override or paternal inclusion; regional bodies should co-govern watersheds, forests, transport, health, education, and other shared systems whose real catchments outrun one settlement; nations should constitutionally recognize Indigenous peoples, lands, treaties, restitution claims, fiscal powers, and free, prior and informed consent rather than forcing all authority through a unitary citizenship mold; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in rights norms, anti-extractive scrutiny, and cross-border Indigenous solidarity rather than pretending a world body can govern each people’s internal life.
- `530-language-and-linguistic-pluralism-by-scope-local-use-municipal-service-access-regional-language-ecologies-national-rights-and-global-support.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat language as civic infrastructure rather than as a badge of dominance or a private burden of translation: households, associations, and communities should be free to use, transmit, revive, and change their languages in everyday life; municipalities should make frontline services, signage, interpretation, naming, and basic public interfaces actually usable in the languages that structure local life; regional bodies should sustain language ecologies that outrun one town through media, teacher pipelines, courts, hospitals, universities, and cultural institutions; nations should define official-language settlements, guarantee minority and Indigenous language rights, fund multilingual education and translation capacity, and prevent language-based exclusion from citizenship, justice, or public work; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in language-rights norms, endangered-language support, digital standards, and shared linguistic infrastructure rather than trying to impose one administrative tongue on humanity.
- `571-public-records-archives-and-official-publications-by-scope-community-memory-municipal-record-discipline-regional-repositories-national-gazettes-and-no-government-by-disappearing-state.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **public records, archives, and official publication** as a **constitutional memory layer**: keep firsthand witnessing, local minutes, notice, and records help close to communities and municipalities; pool preservation, repository, and disaster-recovery capacity at regional scale where fragmentation would otherwise erase public memory; reserve national or constitutional-state law for records duties, transfer rules, authentic promulgation, and archival independence; and use continental and global layers for interoperability, documentary-heritage protection, and common access norms rather than for a fantasy of one world archive sovereign.
- `662-global-institution-toolkit-by-problem-class-assemblies-secretariats-scientific-panels-registries-inspection-compliance-funds-and-no-world-state-monoculture.md` — The ideal global layer should be built from a **small toolkit of treaty-bound institutional forms matched to problem class** rather than from one fantasy model of world government: use assemblies and councils for norm-setting, secretariats and focal-point networks for continuous coordination, scientific panels for shared factual baselines, registries and reporting systems for comparability, inspection or verification where cheating matters, dispute and compliance lanes where interpretation recurs, and dedicated funds where solidarity is required — while refusing both fake world-state domesticity and empty declarations with no operating spine.

## data-governance

- `411-diffable-public-rules-version-windows-and-change-logs.md` — Public rules should be **dated, versioned, diffable, and announced with compatibility windows** so people, agencies, and vendors can tell what changed, when it changed, and how long they have to adapt.
- `422-serious-incident-clocks-public-case-logs-and-corrective-action.md` — When public automated systems cause or plausibly cause serious harm, response should run on explicit **incident clocks** and a visible corrective-action track, not on vague promises to “look into it”.
- `425-portable-appeal-packets-and-log-retention.md` — Contestability fails when the evidence trail is scattered or ephemeral; every consequential AI-assisted decision should leave behind a portable review packet built from logs, provenance, and operator actions.
- `431-data-provenance-chains-and-ai-ready-dataset-declarations.md` — Public-sector AI should maintain a provenance chain for every consequential dataset and publish a compact dataset declaration that names source, collection method, transformations, representativeness limits, legal basis, sharing constraints, and reuse conditions.
- `436-redaction-gateways-protected-attribute-filters-and-exception-registers.md` — Public AI systems should default to **redaction before inference**: block or strip unnecessary personal data, prohibit protected-attribute and emotion inference by default, and require a named, reviewable exception register for the rare cases law explicitly permits.
- `438-citation-gated-public-chatbots-approved-source-hierarchies-and-abstention.md` — Public AI assistants should answer only when they can stay inside an **approved source hierarchy** and return an authoritative citation; when they cannot, they should abstain, hand off, or route the user to the right wizard, form, or human channel instead of improvising.
- `441-record-schedules-hold-safe-deletion-and-discovery-ready-ai-logs.md` — Prompts, retrieved sources, outputs, feedback, and operational logs from public AI should be treated as **scheduled records with clear deletion rules, hold behavior, access controls, and export paths**, not as disposable exhaust.
- `444-privileged-access-tiers-role-restricted-logs-and-admin-session-review.md` — Public AI should restrict sensitive administration and log access by role, record privileged actions in detail, and subject elevated sessions to routine review so governance evidence is not left inside an unexamined operator back room.
- `449-artifact-authorship-classes-generated-content-authority-labels-and-mixed-lineage.md` — Governance artifacts for consequential public AI should declare who authored the bytes — institution, supplier, affected person, system, or mixed compiler path — so machine-generated or third-party material cannot silently inherit official authority it has not earned.
- `451-canonical-disclosure-heads-frozen-citation-tips-and-stale-copy-warnings.md` — If consequential public-AI disclosures exist in multiple versions, mirrors, excerpts, or derived summaries, the institution should publish one canonical current head, preserve citation-frozen heads for historical reference, and visibly warn when a stale or branched copy is no longer authority-bearing.
- `452-authority-allowlists-integrity-pins-and-fail-closed-external-evidence-imports.md` — Consequential public AI should treat external evidence, supplier assurances, and authoritative-source materials as governed inputs with narrow authority allowlists, integrity or version pins where needed, and fail-closed blocking when authenticity or exact identity cannot be established.
- `458-dependence-aware-assurance-counts-shared-origin-witnesses-and-pseudo-independence-guards.md` — Public-AI assurance should record shared origins across tests, judges, vendors, datasets, prompts, and reviewers so multiple agreeing checks are not mistaken for multiple independent grounds for trust.
- `461-repair-ladders-restored-record-uncertainty-and-recovery-proof-boundaries.md` — When consequential public-AI records, logs, indexes, or service state are damaged, institutions should publish a least-destructive repair ladder and label restored artifacts with continuity and uncertainty classes instead of letting recovery masquerade as untouched truth.
- `467-native-evidence-lanes-normalized-packets-and-no-semantic-reownership.md` — Consequential public-AI archives should keep native logs, vendor exports, raw witnesses, replay references, normalized packets, and downstream summaries in distinct evidence lanes so portability does not silently rewrite source semantics, missingness, or authority.
- `472-case-lineage-withdrawal-cancellation-supersession-and-reopen-receipts.md` — Consequential public-AI cases, appeals, incidents, and review requests should preserve typed lineage across withdrawal, cancellation, supersession, duplicate-merge, expiry, and reopening, with predecessor-successor links and reasoned receipts, so no rights-bearing matter silently disappears.
- `474-stewardship-transfers-publisher-continuity-and-no-inherited-trust-by-move.md` — When a third-party model, dataset, API, repository, document host, or supplier changes steward, publisher, domain, or ownership, prior trust and approval should not silently carry forward; stewardship transfer should trigger continuity proof or trust reset.
- `478-structured-decision-traces-minimal-bindings-reason-codes-and-safe-explain-surfaces.md` — Consequential public-AI actions should leave behind a stable decision-trace object that records the governing basis, route, inputs used, matched rule or model context, reason codes, obligations, and redactions in a compact safe form, so explanations, appeals, and incident review do not depend on backend folklore or prose reconstruction.
- `485-effective-state-resolution-correction-graphs-and-no-authority-by-feed-order.md` — When consequential public-AI notices, status updates, corrections, withdrawals, and superseding records accumulate over time, the institution should compute and publish one deterministic effective current state from explicit lineage links, and should treat forks or unresolved ambiguity as incidents rather than letting feed order, CMS recency, or whichever copy looks newest decide authority.
- `486-authoritative-time-sources-timestamp-confidence-and-invalid-time-quarantine.md` — Any public-AI governance system that depends on clocks for deadlines, queue age, freshness, sequencing, signatures, retention, or incident ordering should declare its authoritative time basis, timestamp confidence, tolerated drift, and quarantine behavior when time trust degrades, so chronology cannot silently become a hidden source of injustice.
- `487-subsidiarity-by-default-burden-of-proof-for-upward-scope-and-recallable-delegation.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should allocate power by a rebuttable subsidiarity rule: default to the smallest scope that can solve the problem, move upward only when spillovers, pooling, rights floors, common-pool integrity, or peace-and-standards needs require it, and keep upward delegation explicit, reviewable, and reversible where possible.
- `499-public-integrity-by-scope-local-disclosure-conflict-checks-lobbying-transparency-asset-declarations-and-anti-capture-routing.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat integrity as institutional infrastructure rather than moral decoration: small governments need simple, enforceable disclosure and procurement rules; larger governments need stronger conflict controls, lobbying transparency, asset declarations, cooling-off periods, and independent verification; and audit, prevention, prosecution, and adjudication should remain distinct enough that no one office becomes both ethics mascot and political weapon.
- `518-public-investment-and-procurement-by-scope-local-maintenance-metro-systems-national-capital-discipline-and-narrow-global-standards.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern public investment by keeping routine maintenance, small capital works, and user-visible asset stewardship close to the institutions that see failure first; using metropolitan and regional bodies for networked systems and place-wide project coordination; reserving capital budgeting rules, appraisal standards, equalizing finance, strategic procurement discipline, and infrastructure pipeline governance to the nation; and keeping the global layer narrow, focused on open technical standards, development finance, and anti-rigging or integrity cooperation rather than remote project micromanagement.
- `551-public-prosecution-by-scope-local-diversion-regional-ordinary-charging-national-integrity-cases-and-no-government-by-prosecutor.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should keep prosecution lawful, impartial, and scale-matched: use community-near intake and diversion for ordinary low-level harm, size ordinary charging offices to regional or metropolitan court catchments large enough for competence and independence, reserve national prosecutors for public-corruption, state-integrity, and interjurisdictional serious crime, and keep cross-border prosecutorial cooperation narrow, reviewable, and rights-bound so neither local vendetta nor central spectacle can govern by charge.
- `561-districting-and-boundary-commissions-by-scope-local-polling-areas-municipal-wards-regional-mapmaking-national-equal-suffrage-rules-and-no-government-by-incumbent-cartography.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat districting and seat allocation as a periodic, law-bound integrity function: keep polling-area maintenance close to real voter-service geography, place most ward and constituency mapmaking in independent local or regional boundary bodies sized to the polity they serve, reserve national government for equal-suffrage rules, census-to-seat apportionment, protected exceptions, and judicially reviewable backstops, and never let incumbents quietly draw the map that chooses their next electorate.
- `563-public-procurement-institutions-and-review-by-scope-local-needs-regional-shared-buying-national-rules-independent-challenges-and-no-government-by-emergency-sole-source-fog.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat public procurement as a governed public institution rather than a clerical back office: keep need definition, user-facing specification, and day-to-day contract management close to the service; use metropolitan, county, provincial, state, or other regional shared-buying bodies where market structure, scarce expertise, or repeated categories make pooling sensible; reserve national government for the procurement code, standard documents, core e-procurement rails, integrity controls, supplier-access baselines, independent complaint review design, and open-contracting discipline; keep the global layer narrow in interoperable standards, anti-rigging and anti-corruption cooperation, and fair cross-border conditions of competition; and never let emergency exemptions, framework sprawl, or vendor dependence turn public spending into shadow executive power.
- `564-anti-corruption-bodies-and-integrity-commissions-by-scope-local-routing-regional-case-development-national-specialization-and-no-government-by-heroic-commission.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not rely on one heroic anti-corruption commission: keep local complaint intake, disclosure routing, whistleblower handoff, and ordinary integrity advice close enough to be usable; place regional or state-level investigative and inspection capacity where corruption markets, procurement webs, and patronage chains cross municipalities or where tiny jurisdictions are too captured to investigate themselves; reserve national government for the preventive architecture required by law, high-level and cross-regional corruption, asset-declaration verification, beneficial-ownership tracing, international cooperation, and strategy coordination; keep the global layer narrow in standards, peer review, and transnational case support; and never let anti-corruption institutions become either decorative ethics theater or unreviewable prosecutor-states.
- `568-land-administration-and-cadastre-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-parcel-service-regional-coordination-national-tenure-rules-and-no-government-by-documentary-dispossession.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat land administration as a scale-matched constitutional infrastructure rather than a clerical property office: community and customary institutions should help witness real people-to-land relationships, municipal or county offices should be the ordinary parcel-service front door, metropolitan or regional layers should pool cadastre and geospatial coordination where fragmentation would break the map, national or constitutional-state law should own tenure forms, identifiers, interoperability, and register integrity, and continental or global bodies should provide standards and support rather than pretending a world cadastre exists.
- `576-base-registries-identifiers-reference-data-and-interoperability-by-scope-community-error-surfacing-municipal-data-stewardship-regional-brokers-national-authoritative-sources-and-no-government-by-contradictory-copies.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **base registries, identifiers, reference data, and interoperability** as the **constitutional integration layer** of government: keep error surfacing, assisted correction, and local fact challenge close to people and firms; use municipalities and other frontline bodies as disciplined stewards and consumers of authoritative data rather than rival sovereign databases; pool interconnection, exchange infrastructure, and semantic support above fragmented local jurisdictions where scale adds competence; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for designating authoritative sources, assigning identifier rules, governing access, and maintaining shared code lists and metadata; and keep continental or global roles narrow enough to support cross-border evidence exchange, schemas, and semantic alignment without becoming a world master database.
- `578-open-data-and-public-information-reuse-by-scope-community-scrutiny-municipal-publishing-regional-aggregation-national-standards-and-no-government-by-pdf-fog.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **open data and public-information reuse** as the **constitutional public-reuse layer** of government: keep community scrutiny, correction demand, and context close to the people and places described by the data; require municipalities and frontline bodies to publish routine local information in genuinely reusable ways rather than as decorative PDF dumps; pool regional aggregation, comparison, and cross-boundary publication where fragmented local release would make the public blind to shared systems; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the legal framework on reuse, licensing, metadata, machine-readable publication, privacy and confidentiality boundaries, high-value dataset rules, and catalog standards; and keep continental or global roles narrow enough to support interoperable metadata, cross-border discovery, and common high-value publication patterns without becoming one world data ministry.
- `610-accountability-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-scrutiny-audit-disclosure-complaints-review-and-no-government-by-jurisdictional-gap.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **accountability home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, and administrative one: its own scrutiny forum, named records-and-disclosure duties, internal control and audit proportionate to risk, external audit and integrity jurisdiction, complaint and review routes that ordinary people can actually find, and explicit accountability for operators and contractors so the territory is not really governed in the gaps between municipalities, agencies, and the state.
- `650-scope-estoppel-limits-reliance-sunk-cost-benefit-retention-and-no-stack-change-by-dependence.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should refuse to let **reliance, sunk cost, operational dependence, accepted benefits, or delayed objection manufacture constitutional title**: when a materially stack-altering move lacked the right authority, the right consent, or the right public lane, the answer should be cure, remand, override, rollback, or fresh authorization — not estoppel by familiarity, expense, or service dependency.
- `653-scope-source-hierarchies-authority-ladders-and-no-stack-change-by-the-loudest-surface.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should settle disputes about **who governs what** against a declared **source hierarchy** rather than against whichever surface is loudest, newest, easiest to find, or already wired into daily operations: constitutional and statutory text, authoritative judgments, and explicit scope acts should outrank derivative registers, and derivative registers should outrank budgets, contracts, software behavior, dashboards, FAQs, and public-relations residue.
- `658-scope-evidentiary-continuity-record-provenance-and-no-proof-laundering-by-migration.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require every **materially stack-altering reform** to preserve **evidentiary continuity** across record transfer, system migration, redaction, archival cutover, and platform replacement — with stable identifiers, provenance metadata, chain-of-custody, transformation logs, and certified retrieval routes — so responsibility can still be proven after a function moves and rescoping cannot dissolve proof through administrative or technical migration.
- `659-scope-evidentiary-break-presumptions-burden-allocation-and-no-stack-change-by-missing-file.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat any **unrepaired evidentiary break inside a materially stack-altering reform** as a burden-allocation event rather than a neutral accident — keeping the burden on the authority that claims the scope change, continuity, legality, or harmlessness, and refusing to let missing files, broken migration, or lost metadata manufacture constitutional title by opacity.
- `674-shared-regime-records-and-publicity-public-private-sessions-document-registers-meeting-records-vote-records-authentic-texts-corrections-and-no-governance-by-missing-papertrail.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed documentary constitution** that separates session publicity, agenda and paper circulation, official document registers, meeting-record formats, vote records, authentic texts, correction notices, and retention or access rules — so public authority does not vanish into missing minutes, unofficial drafts, or document folklore.
- `678-shared-regime-independence-and-conflict-discipline-declarations-recusal-confidentiality-secondments-donor-firebreaks-and-no-expertise-by-capture.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed integrity constitution** that separates disclosure, assessment, management, recusal, exclusion, confidentiality, secondment controls, donor firebreaks, and post-service limits — so expertise, review, and advisory work do not harden into captured governance.
- `680-shared-regime-jurisprudence-memory-and-consistency-holdings-digests-departure-reasons-advisory-opinions-and-no-random-walk-governance.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed jurisprudence-memory constitution** that separates binding force, persuasive reasoning, holdings, summaries, digests, advisory opinions, and departure rules — so interpretation develops through visible continuity rather than random walk, citation theater, or stealth precedent.
- `684-shared-regime-secretariat-workforce-constitutions-appointments-merit-geographic-balance-secondments-conduct-separation-and-no-regime-by-patronage.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed secretariat workforce constitution** that separates political head selection from career staffing, makes merit and integrity the paramount recruitment rule, gives geographic balance a visible but bounded place, constrains secondments and related-party hiring, and types conduct, reassignment, discipline, and separation lanes — so the regime is not governed by patronage, donor-owned posts, or borrowed-capacity fog.
- `685-shared-regime-procurement-constitutions-competition-thresholds-exceptions-award-records-protest-debarment-and-no-regime-by-sole-source-habit.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed procurement constitution** that separates planning, solicitation methods, competition defaults, threshold rules, emergency and sole-source exceptions, award records, debriefing, complaint or protest lanes, vendor-sanctions logic, contract-change control, and exit capacity — so the regime is not governed by incumbent vendors, emergency habit, or off-book buyer discretion.
- `693-shared-regime-personal-data-and-privacy-constitutions-legal-basis-purpose-limits-minimization-subject-rights-transfers-breach-response-and-no-mission-by-data-drift.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed personal-data-and-privacy constitution** that separates lawful basis, purpose limitation, necessity and minimization, role allocation, sensitive-data treatment, retention, transfer rules, subject-rights handling, breach response, and accountability review — so mission work does not quietly become mission by data drift, uncontrolled onward sharing, or privacy promises with no operating spine.
- `694-shared-regime-statistics-and-indicator-constitutions-designation-methodology-metadata-revisions-quality-assurance-release-calendars-and-no-governance-by-number-theater.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed statistics-and-indicator constitution** that separates designated official series from exploratory analytics, indicator ownership from political sponsorship, methodology from messaging, metadata from headline numbers, revisions from corrections, and release discipline from communications convenience — so evidence does not decay into number theater, indicator shopping, or policy-by-dashboard without professional standards.
- `712-amendment-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-change-classes-ratification-ladders-version-ledgers-drift-logs-and-no-field-redesign-by-memo.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, an evidence packet, challenge and participation packets, and an oversight packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **amendment packet** naming which changes are merely tuning and which are constitutional, who may propose them, what participation and scrutiny gates apply, what ratification ladder adopts them, when they take effect, and what version ledger plus drift log keeps the field from being redesigned by memo, queue custom, temporary exception, or software default.
- `716-information-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-canonical-case-home-access-model-sharing-boundaries-retention-clocks-and-no-government-by-portal-shell.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, and a capability packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **information packet** saying where the field’s canonical case and record homes live, which surface is the system of record and which are only presentation or intake layers, what role-and-access model governs staff and delegates, what sharing boundaries and information agreements apply, what retention/export/handback rules preserve public memory, and what recovery path keeps the field governable when platforms, vendors, or host systems fail — so the field does not become government by portal shell, spreadsheet relay, or vendor-admin shadow.
- `717-asset-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-estate-fleet-equipment-condition-discipline-handback-and-no-government-by-orphan-assets.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, and an information packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **asset packet** saying which lane owns and stewards the field’s estate, fleet, equipment, depots, labs, stores, and critical spares; who holds custody, maintenance, calibration, and replacement duty; what condition and resilience floor applies; what lease, host-site, or operator dependencies exist; and what handback rule survives exit or transfer — so the field does not decay into government by orphan assets, lease camouflage, or maintenance exile.
- `718-service-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-whole-service-front-doors-route-classes-service-floors-continuity-and-no-government-by-front-door-scatter.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, an information packet, and an asset packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **service packet** saying what outcome the field’s service actually promises, which lane owns that promise, what front doors and route classes the public may use, what clocks and service floors bind, how channels and operators compose into one whole service, and what continuity and fallback rules survive overload, outage, provider failure, or redesign — so the field does not decay into government by front-door scatter, route roulette, or service-standard theater.
- `719-case-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-intake-triage-state-model-lineage-notice-duty-and-no-government-by-unofficial-casework.md` — Once the archive has a service packet for a lane-typed government field, it should also publish one narrow **case packet** saying what unit of work counts as a case, how a matter becomes one, what intake and triage rules apply before and after acknowledgement, which visible states and clocks bind, what lineage and notice duties survive pause, transfer, merge, withdrawal, supersession, or reopen, and where the authoritative status truth lives — so the field does not decay into government by unofficial casework, invisible queues, or closure by folklore.
- `720-decision-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-determination-class-reason-giving-effectivity-appeal-linkage-and-no-government-by-outcome-letter-alone.md` — Once the archive has service and case packets for a lane-typed government field, it should also publish one narrow **decision packet** saying what counts as a consequential determination, which decision classes exist, who may make and sign them, what minimum findings, reasons, legal basis, conditions, effect dates, implementation duties, and review links must travel with them, and how correction, withdrawal, supersession, and reconsideration preserve lineage — so the field does not decay into government by outcome letter alone, silent conditions, or appeal clocks detached from the act they challenge.
- `735-rollback-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-failed-stabilization-return-authority-pending-matters-record-lineage-and-no-reversal-by-headline-alone.md` — Once the archive can say how a function should be routed (`726`-`728`), ratified (`729`), kept continuous (`730`), witnessed at cutover (`731`), temporarily hosted (`732`), cleanly closed (`733`), and tested through a bounded independent-live window (`734`), it should also keep one compact **rollback packet** for the case where the successor does not hold: classify the rollback type, name the interim principal and public route, preserve the legal and evidentiary state of pending matters, move money/staff/systems/keys with the reversal rather than by headline alone, and refuse both automatic restoration folklore and disguised permanent recentralization.
- `737-release-packets-for-ideal-government-neutral-custody-full-partial-and-phased-release-receiver-readiness-residual-safeguards-and-no-custody-exit-by-impatience.md` — Once the archive has a temporary neutral-custody packet (`736`), it should also keep one compact **custody-release packet** for the moment named surfaces leave custody and re-enter ordinary government: classify the release type, prove receiver readiness surface by surface, preserve case and record lineage, state what safeguards remain temporarily in force, and refuse to end custody merely because a deadline, press statement, or impatient principal wants the appearance of settlement.
- `745-tombstone-consolidation-and-register-absorption-packets-for-retired-government-bodies-scopes-and-shells-directory-merge-alias-preservation-correction-chain-retention-and-no-disappearance-by-tidying.md` — Once the archive can create a tombstone (`741`), reroute it (`742`), correct it (`743`), and steward it (`744`), it should also keep one compact **tombstone-consolidation and register-absorption packet**: one bounded proof object for folding a standalone dead-page surface into a broader historical register, catalogue, or directory without losing discoverability, correction history, or the plain statement that the old authority is dead, so the polity does not mistake tidier information architecture for permission to erase institutional memory.
- `746-historical-register-rehousing-and-cross-catalog-migration-packets-for-absorbed-tombstones-register-home-change-stable-entry-identifiers-alias-continuity-and-no-disappearance-by-replatforming.md` — Once the archive can absorb standalone tombstones into grouped historical registers (`745`), it should also keep one compact **historical-register rehousing and cross-catalog migration packet**: one bounded proof object for moving absorbed dead-object entries from one register, catalogue, directory, or memorial platform to another without losing individually addressable identity, alias coverage, correction lineage, or the plain statement that the authority is dead, so the polity does not mistake platform migration for permission to break historical lookup.
- `759-independent-institutions-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-referee-functions-bounded-mandates-appointment-discipline-budget-protection-review-lanes-and-no-fourth-branch-sprawl.md` — Ideal governments should create independent institutions only where a function genuinely requires **credible distance from day-to-day political command**—as referee, guardian, watchdog, or integrity backstop—and should then give that institution a bounded mandate, protected but not blank-cheque resources, multi-actor appointment and removal discipline, transparent duties, reviewable powers, and a constitutional place that prevents both ministerial capture and fourth-branch sprawl.
- `766-lobbying-transparency-and-revolving-door-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-registers-meeting-logs-gift-rules-cooling-off-advice-lanes-and-no-policy-by-invisible-influence.md` — Ideal governments should treat lobbying and influence as **a legitimate democratic input that becomes dangerous when it is invisible, unequal, or privately entangled with officeholding**: they should disclose who seeks to influence whom, on whose behalf, about what, through which channels, under which gift and hospitality rules, and with what pre- and post-public-employment constraints, so policy is not quietly written by invisible influence.
- `767-conflict-of-interest-and-asset-and-interest-disclosure-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-risk-tiering-recusal-divestment-verification-publication-and-no-office-with-a-private-shadow-ledger.md` — Ideal governments should treat conflicts of interest and asset-and-interest disclosure as **a live decision-integrity system rather than a yearly paperwork ritual**: officials in risk-bearing roles should disclose relevant interests and assets under tiered rules, update them when circumstances change, recuse from affected decisions, divest or use stronger separation tools where conflicts are not manageable, and face real verification and sanction, so office is not shadowed by a private ledger the public never sees.
- `768-whistleblower-protection-and-reporting-person-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-safe-channels-confidentiality-triage-anti-retaliation-remedy-and-no-integrity-by-punishing-disclosure.md` — Ideal governments should treat whistleblower protection as **a protected truth-telling lane inside the constitutional integrity system rather than a moral appeal to personal courage**: people who report wrongdoing on reasonable grounds should have safe internal and external channels, confidentiality or anonymity where lawful, trained intake and triage, protection against retaliation, interim support while disputes are live, and real corrective remedies, so institutions cannot purchase silence by making disclosure personally ruinous.
- `791-benchmark-cards-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-vocation-fit-kit-floors-fiscal-congruence-review-lanes-tripwires-and-no-admiration-without-scoring.md` — The archive should pair its canonical scope matrix and answer-key notes with one compact **benchmark-card format** for each scope — vocation fit, minimum complete kit, fiscal and capability congruence, spillover or solidarity fit, review and remedy integrity, participation and scrutiny proportionality, and named upgrade or handback tripwires — so real constitutions, reform proposals, and case studies can be compared tersely against the ideal stack without reopening the whole theory.
- `792-stress-test-and-drill-cards-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-essential-service-continuity-command-legibility-fiscal-buffers-rights-discipline-rescoping-signals-and-no-paper-constitution-by-calm-weather.md` — The archive should pair its ideal-government answer key and benchmark cards with one compact **stress-test and drill-card format** for each scope — essential-service continuity, command and escalation legibility, reserve and surge discipline, intergovernmental handoff integrity, legality and rights restraint under pressure, public communication, and recovery or handback triggers — so governments are judged not only by their steady-state design but by whether they remain honest under flood, blackout, outbreak, fiscal shock, cyber disruption, or constitutional strain.
- `806-evidence-registers-and-provenance-chains-for-scope-assessments-exhibit-ids-source-typing-redaction-ledgers-finding-links-and-no-verdict-by-orphaned-exhibit.md` — The archive should pair its assessment-mission, sampling, tracer-route, finding-register, and close-out notes with one compact **evidence-register grammar**: **every serious scope review should keep a stable exhibit register that says what each evidence object is, where it came from, what version or date it belongs to, what was redacted or withheld, which finding it supports or contradicts, and how later reviewers can reuse it, so constitutional judgments are not built from orphaned exhibits, floating screenshots, or unverifiable quotations**.
- `807-assessment-team-independence-and-conflict-discipline-for-scope-reviews-recusal-rosters-secondment-firebreaks-host-picked-experts-donor-pathways-and-no-constitutional-judgment-by-interested-mission.md` — The archive should pair its assessment-mission, evidence-register, contestability, and close-out notes with one compact **mission-integrity grammar**: **every serious scope review should declare who is judging, who is only informing, what interests and funding pathways each reviewer carries, what firebreaks apply to secondees and host-nominated specialists, when recusal is mandatory, and how outsiders can challenge the composition of the team before findings harden into the live constitution, so the archive does not mistake expertise, proximity, or funding convenience for independence**.
- `808-calibration-packs-moderation-loops-and-precedent-banks-for-scope-assessments-score-anchors-difficult-case-conferences-documented-departures-and-no-benchmark-by-reviewer-mood.md` — The archive should pair its benchmark, mission, evidence-register, and mission-integrity notes with one compact **review-calibration grammar**: **every serious scope assessment should keep a small calibration pack with lane-specific score anchors, worked examples, threshold splits, precedent notes, moderation checkpoints, and documented departures, so that different review teams can reach comparably disciplined judgments without collapsing everything into one blended score or one charismatic reviewer’s mood**.
- `811-scope-verdict-packets-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-settled-holdings-frontier-thresholds-benchmark-findings-repair-routes-public-proof-and-no-applied-judgment-by-scattered-cross-reference.md` — When the archive uses its ideal-governments-by-scope stack on a **real polity, proposal, or case study**, it should emit one compact **scope verdict packet** that bundles the settled scope holding, any live threshold holdings, the benchmark finding, material stress or maintenance modifiers, the active repair or intervention path, and the public-proof class — so later applied judgments stay portable, comparable, and compact instead of dissolving into essay recap or a trail of scattered note citations.
- `834-information-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-ledgers-municipal-record-homes-metro-observatories-national-statistics-and-treaty-registries.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should authoritative public facts, records, and decision visibility ordinarily live at each scope?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one dashboard fetish: **micro-local bodies should keep simple minutes, noticeboards, steward ledgers, and escalation logs rather than miniature data states; municipalities should be the first level with a full public information constitution of clerks or record stewards, open meeting packets, service and permit records, publication calendars, and reusable public data; metropolitan and regional governments should own their own observatories, geospatial baselines, and cross-boundary performance records rather than parasitic dependence on a host city or ministry; national government should carry the thickest official-statistics, gazette, archive, and interoperability spine; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound but still maintain comparability standards, registries, alerting channels, and shared reporting rather than private dashboards or counterfeit world omniscience**.

## delegated-governance

- `427-third-party-model-and-supplier-registers-for-public-ai.md` — If a public AI system depends on outside models, APIs, vendors, or managed services, those dependencies should be inventoried, attributable, and governable as a live public risk surface rather than hidden implementation detail.
- `538-money-and-payments-by-scope-local-cash-access-municipal-acceptance-national-public-money-and-global-interoperability.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat money and payments as constitutional infrastructure: households and neighbourhood institutions can surface exclusion, fraud, outage, and cash-access failures but should not mint rival monies for ordinary public life; municipalities should guarantee practical payment usability in everyday government, including cash access and acceptance where law protects it, legible public-payment channels, and inclusive collection design; metropolitan and regional institutions should coordinate shared payment touchpoints where commuting, service markets, and public agencies cross borders; nations should own legal tender, central bank money, payment-system oversight, public-payment rails, consumer protection, anti-fraud baselines, and resilience; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in message standards, cross-border interoperability, remittance quality, and data-friction reduction rather than pretending that local service design or national monetary legitimacy can be outsourced.
- `544-delegated-public-functions-contractors-concessions-nonprofits-and-platforms-cannot-be-constitutional-escape-hatches.md` — An ideal polity may delegate bounded execution to contractors, concessionaires, nonprofit operators, co-operatives, or digital platforms when doing so is genuinely useful, but it should never outsource the state’s continuing duties to set rights-respecting rules, preserve public capacity, keep money and risk legible, maintain records and remedies, guarantee continuity, and retake control when delegation fails; public obligations should follow the public function rather than disappearing into private legal form.
- `610-accountability-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-scrutiny-audit-disclosure-complaints-review-and-no-government-by-jurisdictional-gap.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **accountability home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, and administrative one: its own scrutiny forum, named records-and-disclosure duties, internal control and audit proportionate to risk, external audit and integrity jurisdiction, complaint and review routes that ordinary people can actually find, and explicit accountability for operators and contractors so the territory is not really governed in the gaps between municipalities, agencies, and the state.
- `619-contract-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-procurement-franchising-change-control-exit-capacity-and-no-government-by-concession-patchwork.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **contract home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, service, planning, capital, and regulatory one: a visible buyer-or-commissioner function, explicit make-buy-franchise tests, lawful procurement and concession routes, disciplined contract and change control, published performance and amendment trails, real handback and step-in capacity, and no territorial government by concession patchwork.
- `713-delegation-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-principal-lane-reserved-powers-operator-chains-step-in-rights-and-no-public-duty-by-outsourced-wrapper.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, and amendment discipline for a field, it should also publish one narrow **delegation packet** saying which slice of the field is still constitutionally owned by the public lane, which execution work may be delegated to public bodies, contractors, concessionaires, nonprofits, co-operatives, or platforms, what powers remain non-delegable, what contract-management and records capacity the principal must retain, what step-in and handback rights keep continuity real, and what review route prevents public duty from disappearing into an outsourced wrapper.
