- `752-government-formation-and-removal-by-scope-micro-local-recall-municipal-manager-confidence-metro-investiture-parliamentary-default-constructive-no-confidence-fixed-terms-and-no-dual-democratic-command.md` — Ideal governments should choose formation and removal rules that create **one legible confidence chain** at each scope — recallable stewards for micro-local bodies, elected-council plus removable manager or mayoral executive in municipalities, explicit investiture and termination rules for metropolitan or regional governments with real power, parliamentary or assembly-confidence default for most large multi-party states, and fixed-term presidential exceptions only where the system can safely absorb dual mandates without chronic collision.
- `755-constitutional-referendum-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-amendment-classes-double-majorities-question-clarity-balanced-information-and-no-plebiscitary-shortcuts.md` — A constitutional referendum should not be treated as a universal cleansing ritual; ideal governments should use it when a constitution genuinely requires **direct constituent ratification** or when a change is foundational enough to justify a people-level decision, and even then only with clear lawful questions, balanced information, explicit downstream effects, and double-legitimacy rules where territorial bargains are at stake.
- `793-maintenance-calendars-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-benchmark-refresh-stress-drill-cadence-trigger-overrides-public-registries-and-no-constitutional-care-by-sporadic-panic.md` — The archive should pair its ideal-government answer key, benchmark cards, stress cards, and scope-audit triggers with one compact **maintenance-calendar rule** for each scope — fixed benchmark refreshes, typed drill cadence, trigger-based overrides, publication and follow-up duties, and explicit closure or rescoping lanes — so multilevel constitutions are maintained as routine public infrastructure rather than rediscovered only during reform waves or crisis embarrassment.
- `803-close-out-verification-and-reopen-rules-for-scope-governance-repair-ledgers-mid-term-checks-field-revisit-residual-risk-and-no-closure-by-self-certification.md` — The archive should pair its finding-register and management-response notes with one compact **close-out and verification grammar**: **every material scope repair item should face a typed follow-up review that tests closure proof against live conditions, declares residual risk, decides close / continue / reopen / rescope, and names the next verification clock, so corrective-action ledgers do not turn into self-closing spreadsheets or polite fiction**.
- `813-legitimacy-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-delegated-councils-principal-owned-backbones-double-key-authorities-directly-elected-tiers-and-no-heavy-power-by-convenience-composition.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, it should also be able to say **what legitimacy chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should be run by delegated elected principals with no hidden hard powers, shared-service backbones should remain clearly owned by the member governments whose duties they support, bounded functional authorities should carry an elected anchor plus explicit double-key gates for major debt, rule, boundary, or remit changes, and general-purpose territorial tiers should normally rest on directly elected chambers with their own scrutiny and executive responsibility rather than on convenience boards pretending to carry full constitutional weight.
- `815-administrative-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-host-secretariats-principal-owned-backbones-chartered-operators-records-homes-and-no-heavy-power-by-borrowed-bureaucracy.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, and **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what administrative chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should use small secretariats with no hidden command over member administrations, shared-service backbones should keep declared principals, employer-of-record rules, records homes, and service agreements, bounded functional authorities should have chartered operating cores with explicit staffing, asset, procurement, and incident-command authority, and general-purpose territorial tiers should normally own their own civil-service, records, and operating spine rather than ruling through borrowed host bureaucracy.
- `816-oversight-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-member-scrutiny-external-audit-ombuds-routes-judicial-review-and-no-heavy-power-by-self-marking.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **who owns it**, **how money moves through it**, and **where its operating spine lives**, it should also be able to say **what oversight chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should remain mainly reviewable through the member governments that delegate into them, shared-service backbones should preserve visible principal-side scrutiny plus independent audit and complaint routes, bounded functional authorities should carry named external audit, maladministration review, legality or regulatory checks, and judicial remedy proportionate to their power, and general-purpose territorial tiers should own a full public oversight constitution rather than marking themselves through internal committees alone.
- `819-boundary-and-membership-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-accession-gates-territory-rules-amendment-thickness-exit-protocols-dissolution-paths-and-no-map-by-one-way-ratchet.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, and **what information chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should use open and reversible participation with no hidden territorial claim, shared-service backbones should declare member classes, accession formulas, notice periods, and unwind rules, bounded functional authorities should use chartered territories plus staged accession and constrained exit, and general-purpose territorial tiers should rely on statutory boundary change with public consultation, transition machinery, and no map by one-way ratchet.
- `820-decision-rule-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-ordinary-majorities-qualified-majorities-unanimity-reserves-deadlock-breakers-and-no-heavy-power-by-procedural-veto.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, **what information chain belongs to it**, and **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what decision-rule chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should seek consensus for advisory work and require visible member ratification for anything binding, shared-service backbones should use ordinary-majority operating rules with reserved supermajority or member-ratification gates for portfolio, burden, and liability shifts, bounded functional authorities should use public standing orders with ordinary-majority defaults plus qualified-majority or double-key gates for tariffs, debt, land, remit, and boundary changes, and general-purpose territorial tiers should govern by ordinary democratic majorities with narrowly cabined supermajority reserves and explicit deadlock routes rather than by permanent veto geography.
- `821-dispute-resolution-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-negotiation-ladders-mediation-expert-determination-jurisdiction-maps-continuity-orders-and-no-heavy-power-by-hostage-dispute.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, **what information chain belongs to it**, **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**, and **what decision-rule chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what dispute-resolution chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should rely on recorded negotiation and visible member-side escalation, shared-service backbones should use negotiation-first ladders with mediation, technical determination, continuity protection, and public-law endpoints, bounded functional authorities should publish jurisdiction maps and interim continuity orders, and general-purpose territorial tiers should rely on ordinary justice and constitutional routes rather than permanent bargaining by hostage dispute.
- `822-asset-and-liability-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-member-owned-infrastructure-ring-fenced-balance-sheets-handback-maps-contingent-obligations-and-no-heavy-power-by-orphaned-balance-sheet.md` — When the archive has already established that a cross-boundary problem is real, chosen the honest form, and said who governs, pays, operates, votes, and hears disputes, it should still require one compact **asset-and-liability chain**: thin connectors should own almost nothing beyond trivial co-ordination tools; shared-service backbones should keep political title with the principals unless a clearly bounded common vehicle is justified; bounded functional authorities may hold and steward system-critical assets and named liabilities inside a ring-fenced public balance sheet; and general-purpose territorial tiers should carry visible asset, debt, reserve, and handback constitutions rather than hiding real sovereignty in host property, off-book obligations, or exit chaos.
- `825-regime-form-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-steward-assemblies-municipal-administration-metropolitan-mandates-regional-parliamentarism-national-confidence-and-global-narrow-waists.md` — The archive should answer the question **what regime form should govern at each scope?** with a scale-matched default set rather than one constitutional idol: assembly-and-stewardship at micro-local scale, elected local democracy plus professional administration in municipalities, directly legitimated metropolitan government for real urban systems, assembly-confidence regional government where a region genuinely carries platform functions, parliamentary or assembly-confidence national government unless a strong case for dual-mandate presidentialism is proved, bounded plurilateral unions built around shared-rule institutions rather than cloned statehood, and globally a narrow-waist charter order rather than a world state.
- `826-mandate-source-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-assembly-voice-council-confidence-metro-public-mandates-regional-investiture-national-confidence-and-treaty-delegation.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should governing authority at each scope get its mandate?** with scale-matched defaults rather than a direct-election fetish: assembly voice and recallable stewardship at micro-local scale, elected councils as the primary democratic source in municipalities, whole-territory public mandates for metropolitan governments that can bind a real urban system, assembly-invested regional government where a region genuinely carries platform functions, parliamentary or assembly-confidence national government as the default source of executive authority, and treaty- or charter-derived delegation with bounded parliamentary and public complements for plurilateral and global bodies.
- `829-selection-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-open-local-voice-proportional-councils-metro-wide-elections-federal-shared-rule-and-delegated-global-seats.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should offices and chambers at each scope actually be chosen?** with scope-matched selection defaults rather than one ballot fetish: open assemblies, simple ward contests, recallable delegates, and rotation where the unit is genuinely face-to-face; proportional or semi-proportional municipal councils plus merit administration where everyday city government begins; whole-territory metropolitan elections where metro power is real; regional and national lower chambers chosen by proportional rules strong enough to reflect plural publics, with territorial second chambers only where shared rule is real; and continental or global bodies chosen mainly through treaty delegation, indirect parliamentary composition, and merit-based secretariat appointment rather than fake world-state plebiscites.
- `830-decision-rule-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-majorities-municipal-ordinary-rules-federal-double-keys-and-no-fake-global-unanimity.md` — The archive should answer the question **what internal decision rule should usually govern at each scope once the body is real?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one voting fetish: **micro-local institutions should seek rough consensus but fall back cheaply to ordinary majority; municipalities, metropolitan governments, and most regional and national lower chambers should decide ordinary business by ordinary majority with reserved supermajorities for constitutional, territorial, debt, or rights-sensitive thresholds; shared-rule chambers may justify double keys where constituent units are genuinely co-authors of the settlement; and continental or global bodies should treat consensus as a discipline of accommodation, not a veto constitution, reserving unanimity only for narrow membership-, treaty-, or sovereignty-touching classes**.
- `831-fiscal-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-tiny-commons-municipal-own-source-metro-shares-regional-equalization-national-solidarity-and-treaty-dues.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should each scope ordinarily be financed?** with scale-matched fiscal defaults rather than one treasury fetish: micro-local bodies should live on tiny discretionary funds, member contributions, and visible small grants rather than debt or payroll empires; municipalities should be the first level with meaningful own-source revenue, rule-bound transfers, ordinary operating reserves, and capital access for durable local assets; metropolitan governments should use assigned revenue shares, formula transfers, and user-charge lanes where systems justify them rather than annual pleas from member municipalities; regional and provincial governments should combine own revenues, shared taxes, equalization, and platform-scale capital budgets; national government should carry the broad tax base, macro-stabilization, and solidarity machinery; and continental or global bodies should usually rely on treaty dues, assessed contributions, and tightly bounded common finance rather than counterfeit world taxation or donor-whim constitutions.
- `832-oversight-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-witness-municipal-scrutiny-metro-audit-national-watchdogs-and-treaty-review.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should each scope ordinarily be scrutinized and corrected once it has real public authority?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one watchdog fetish: **micro-local bodies should rely mainly on open meetings, visible records, rotation, and cheap escalation rather than a miniature oversight state; municipalities should be the first level with a full public oversight kit of chamber scrutiny, independent external audit, complaint or ombuds routes, disclosure, and ordinary legality review; metropolitan and regional governments should own equally real audit and redress lanes rather than borrowing them permanently from a host city or ministry; national government should carry the fullest fourth-branch and court-backed oversight constitution; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound but still face visible member scrutiny, independent audit and evaluation, complaint and ethics channels, and published review cycles rather than secretariat self-marking**.
- `833-coercion-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-witness-municipal-civil-enforcement-regional-police-platforms-national-force-monopoly-and-treaty-bound-restraint.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should coercive and enforcement power ordinarily live at each scope?** with scale-matched restraint rather than one badge fetish: **micro-local bodies should default to witness, de-escalation, and referral rather than general coercive authority; municipalities should be the first ordinary home of civil enforcement, inspections, nuisance abatement, and everyday public-order administration under ordinary law; metropolitan governments should hold only those bounded cross-boundary enforcement and emergency-coordination powers that shared systems actually require; regional or provincial governments may honestly house large territorial police, emergency, and regulatory platforms where the constitutional order truly assigns them; national government should carry the thickest monopoly over criminal law, armed force, borders, and exceptional emergency concentration under the strongest rights and review discipline; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound, relying mainly on inspection, reporting, sanctions, certification, and tightly authorized operations rather than ambient upper-state police sovereignty**.
- `836-participation-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-assembly-municipal-dockets-metro-territorial-hearings-national-petition-ladders-and-treaty-observers.md` — If the archive already knows **what government should exist at each scope**, **how it is chosen**, **how it is financed**, **how it is scrutinized**, **where force lives**, **where records live**, and **what emergency lane fits it**, it should also know **how public voice honestly re-enters that government at each scale**: direct and reachable assembly voice at micro-local scale; petitions, hearings, consultations, bounded participatory-budget lanes, and occasional deliberative mini-publics at municipal scale; territory-wide participation homes for metropolitan and regional bodies that govern real shared systems; parliamentary hearing, petition, consultation, and rare constitution-level referendum lanes at national scale; and structured observer, submission, hearing, and stakeholder-participation routes for continental and global bodies rather than fake world-plebiscitary theater.

## elections

- `490-representation-by-scope-neighborhood-voice-metro-election-federal-shared-rule-and-deliberative-complement.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not clone one representation formula at every scale: it should use close, participatory voice where place knowledge is richest, directly elected councils for city and metro systems, population-based representation for common citizenship, territorial shared-rule chambers where constituent units need a federal voice, and representative deliberative mini-publics as a complement for hard cross-cutting questions.
- `500-political-competition-by-scope-civic-lists-durable-parties-public-finance-spending-discipline-and-no-incumbency-self-dealing.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should make political competition open enough for renewal and structured enough for governability: local elections should allow civic lists, independents, and low-friction entry where that fits; larger scales need durable parties that aggregate interests across territory and time; and public finance, spending discipline, timely disclosure, equal treatment, and anti-incumbency rules should keep wealth and state machinery from becoming the real ballot language.
- `552-electoral-administration-by-scope-local-voter-service-municipal-operations-regional-tabulation-national-standards-and-no-government-by-partisan-referee.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat electoral administration as a permanent, professional, and politically impartial public function: keep voter-facing service and polling logistics close enough to work, size counting and tabulation to real operational catchments, reserve core rulemaking and national certification architecture to a permanent central authority bounded by law, route disputes quickly to competent review bodies, and never let the government of the day become the referee of its own election.
- `566-electoral-systems-by-scope-direct-local-voice-municipal-proportionality-metropolitan-legitimacy-regional-balancing-national-pr-and-federal-shared-rule.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not force one electoral formula onto every scale: use direct and low-barrier democracy where the unit is genuinely small and stewardship-heavy, prefer proportional or semi-proportional council elections for municipalities and metropolitan governments that must aggregate durable diversity, fit executive election rules to the actual executive model, reserve territorial second chambers for real shared rule rather than decorative bicameralism, and keep continental and global bodies grounded mainly in treaty delegation plus bounded participatory and parliamentary complements rather than pretending every problem is solved by copying a national ballot upward.
- `599-local-and-regional-assembly-scrutiny-rights-agenda-power-questions-committee-capacity-and-no-majoritarian-blackout.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the **scrutiny rights of local and regional assemblies as constitutional operating equipment rather than as optional etiquette**: councils and assemblies should control the budgetary and rulemaking core, all members should have enforceable rights to meetings, agendas, questions, information, and proportionate committee work, opposition and minority blocs should be able to scrutinise without begging the executive for oxygen, and executive accountability should be structured so local democracy cannot be reduced to periodic elections plus majority blackout.
- `607-democratic-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-indirect-councils-double-legitimacy-direct-election-and-no-metropolitan-rule-by-proxy.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, the honest constitutional question is not whether it needs democracy but **which democratic home fits the power**: keep indirect representation for narrow and bounded co-ordination, use double-legitimacy designs where both people and component governments must visibly count, and prefer directly elected territorial government once the body can bind residents through compulsory finance, major debt, cross-sector territorial bargaining, or durable system-shaping authority.
- `626-public-communication-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-canonical-channels-corrections-inclusive-reach-and-no-government-by-press-release-federation.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it should acquire an explicit **public-communication home**: a named official communications function distinct from party or campaign messaging; one canonical set of channels for notices, updates, warnings, and explanations; correction and version trails; multilingual and accessible publication discipline; clear docking between general information and legal notice; and archival capture of official statements so the territory does not govern through host-city press offices, operator fragments, screenshots, and rumor.
- `627-constitutionalization-bundles-for-shared-territorial-power-core-upgrades-supporting-upgrades-and-no-government-by-single-home-fetish.md` — Once co-operation has crossed the threshold into real shared territorial government, an ideal polity should not pretend that one institutional fix — election alone, revenue alone, law alone, map alone, platform alone, or participation alone — makes the arrangement honest; it should constitutionalize in **bundles**, starting with a minimum core of public-law, democratic, fiscal, administrative, and accountability upgrades, then docking territorial, temporal, intergovernmental, and operating bundles as the functions actually governed require.
- `684-shared-regime-secretariat-workforce-constitutions-appointments-merit-geographic-balance-secondments-conduct-separation-and-no-regime-by-patronage.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed secretariat workforce constitution** that separates political head selection from career staffing, makes merit and integrity the paramount recruitment rule, gives geographic balance a visible but bounded place, constrains secondments and related-party hiring, and types conduct, reassignment, discipline, and separation lanes — so the regime is not governed by patronage, donor-owned posts, or borrowed-capacity fog.
- `760-public-appointments-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-merit-vs-political-trust-open-competition-mixed-selection-confirmation-discipline-and-no-office-by-patronage-default.md` — Ideal governments should treat public appointments as a **typed constitutional lane rather than one generic power of disposal**: elected offices should be filled by voters, political-trust offices should be few and plainly political, most administrative and service-delivery posts should be filled through open merit-based recruitment, constitutionally sensitive or independence-bearing offices may justify mixed nominating and confirmation arrangements, and no polity should let patronage, vacancy manipulation, or prestige theatrics become the real appointments constitution.
- `762-official-opposition-and-legislative-minority-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-recognition-scrutiny-rights-agenda-oxygen-committee-chairs-evidence-capacity-and-no-government-by-majority-blackout.md` — Ideal governments should treat the opposition and legislative minority as **constitutional scrutiny equipment rather than a tolerated inconvenience**: they should guarantee recognition, speaking and questioning rights, proportional committee presence, some agenda oxygen, evidence and staffing capacity, and in key oversight domains opposition-led scrutiny, so democratic government remains accountable between elections and does not collapse into rule by majority blackout.
- `763-caretaker-government-and-pre-election-restraint-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-routine-administration-incoming-government-consultation-major-appointments-freeze-emergency-carve-outs-and-no-mandate-stretch-between-verdict-and-handover.md` — Ideal governments should treat dissolution, hung-parliament bargaining, post-election transition, and imminent change of government as **a distinct continuity-with-restraint mode rather than business as usual**: outgoing governments should continue routine administration and urgent protection of the public, but major policy, appointments, contracts, publicity, and irreversible international or fiscal commitments should pause, narrow, or move only after consultation with the likely successor, so no one stretches an expiring mandate through the handover gap.
- `764-political-finance-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-small-donor-pluralism-real-time-disclosure-spending-ceilings-audit-trails-digital-ad-archives-and-no-office-by-money-primary.md` — Ideal governments should treat political finance as **a bounded democratic input rather than a private market for public power**: parties and candidates should be able to raise and spend enough to compete, but large-donor dependency, opaque third-party spending, cash fog, and untraceable digital advertising should be constrained through donation rules, proportionate public funding, timely disclosure, auditable accounts, independent oversight, and enforceable ceilings where they fit, so office is not functionally auctioned to whoever can finance political attention most aggressively.
- `798-reference-classes-and-comparator-cohorts-for-ideal-governments-by-scope-morphology-matched-peers-functional-territories-capacity-bands-and-no-benchmark-by-postcard.md` — The archive should compare real governments-by-scope against the ideal stack through small, declared **comparator cohorts** built from the right **scope type, morphology, functional territory, legal vocation, and capacity band**, so benchmark work stays like-with-like instead of drifting into prestige case selection, capital-city halo, and false analogies between unlike institutions.
- `805-sampling-frames-and-case-selection-discipline-for-scope-assessments-risk-bands-ordinary-and-failed-routes-negative-cases-and-no-benchmark-by-showcase-tour.md` — The archive should pair its assessment-mission and tracer-route notes with one compact **sampling-frame grammar**: **every serious scope review should declare which sites, records, routes, stakeholders, and time slices are in frame, which are being sampled representatively or purposively, what is excluded, and what claims the chosen sample can honestly support, so benchmark work cannot drift into prestige tours, complaint-only anecdote, or constitutional overclaim from a thin showcase set**.
- `826-mandate-source-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-assembly-voice-council-confidence-metro-public-mandates-regional-investiture-national-confidence-and-treaty-delegation.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should governing authority at each scope get its mandate?** with scale-matched defaults rather than a direct-election fetish: assembly voice and recallable stewardship at micro-local scale, elected councils as the primary democratic source in municipalities, whole-territory public mandates for metropolitan governments that can bind a real urban system, assembly-invested regional government where a region genuinely carries platform functions, parliamentary or assembly-confidence national government as the default source of executive authority, and treaty- or charter-derived delegation with bounded parliamentary and public complements for plurilateral and global bodies.
- `829-selection-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-open-local-voice-proportional-councils-metro-wide-elections-federal-shared-rule-and-delegated-global-seats.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should offices and chambers at each scope actually be chosen?** with scope-matched selection defaults rather than one ballot fetish: open assemblies, simple ward contests, recallable delegates, and rotation where the unit is genuinely face-to-face; proportional or semi-proportional municipal councils plus merit administration where everyday city government begins; whole-territory metropolitan elections where metro power is real; regional and national lower chambers chosen by proportional rules strong enough to reflect plural publics, with territorial second chambers only where shared rule is real; and continental or global bodies chosen mainly through treaty delegation, indirect parliamentary composition, and merit-based secretariat appointment rather than fake world-state plebiscites.

## end-of-life-governance

- `527-end-of-life-and-death-care-by-scope-local-accompaniment-municipal-death-administration-regional-palliative-capacity-national-rights-and-global-pain-relief.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat dying, death care, and bereavement as governed phases of civic life rather than hospital leftovers: households, friends, and community institutions can accompany the dying and mourn the dead but should not be left alone to navigate pain, paperwork, and impossible choices; municipalities should make death registration, burial or cremation access, bereavement navigation, and culturally plural local practice legible and reachable; regional bodies should coordinate palliative-care networks, hospice and specialist capacity, coronial or medical-examiner functions, and referral pathways that outrun one city; nations should guarantee consent law, advance directives, surrogate decision rules, equitable palliative access, medicine availability, and vital-registration baselines; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in essential pain-relief access, rights norms, and knowledge exchange rather than pretending to legislate every intimate end-of-life question for the whole world.
- `595-territorial-reorganization-incorporation-mergers-splits-status-change-and-no-map-surgery-by-managerial-fiat.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the creation, merger, split, annexation, abolition, and status change of territorial authorities as constitutional surgery rather than managerial tidying, so map reform remains lawful, consultative, alternatives-tested, continuity-safe, and reviewable instead of becoming a shortcut around self-government.
- `745-tombstone-consolidation-and-register-absorption-packets-for-retired-government-bodies-scopes-and-shells-directory-merge-alias-preservation-correction-chain-retention-and-no-disappearance-by-tidying.md` — Once the archive can create a tombstone (`741`), reroute it (`742`), correct it (`743`), and steward it (`744`), it should also keep one compact **tombstone-consolidation and register-absorption packet**: one bounded proof object for folding a standalone dead-page surface into a broader historical register, catalogue, or directory without losing discoverability, correction history, or the plain statement that the old authority is dead, so the polity does not mistake tidier information architecture for permission to erase institutional memory.
- `799-sunset-renewal-graduation-and-burial-rules-for-temporary-scope-arrangements-bridges-pilots-derogations-special-measures-and-no-shadow-constitution-by-serial-extension.md` — Whenever a polity uses a **temporary scope arrangement** — bridge body, host authority, pilot, derogation, emergency measure, temporary exemption, special administrator, or other exceptional workaround — the archive should require one compact **sunset / renewal / graduation rule**: **declare the default end state at the start, time-limit the arrangement, raise the proof burden on every renewal, force legitimacy and finance upgrades before any “temporary” body becomes ordinary government, and archive the ending publicly so shadow constitutions cannot survive by serial extension**.

## entity-registry-governance

- `516-markets-and-company-power-by-scope-local-entry-metro-space-national-antitrust-and-fair-global-rules.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern markets by keeping entry barriers, permits, public procurement access, and everyday consumer signal detection close to local life; using metropolitan and regional institutions to manage commercial geography, logistics, and market systems that cross municipal borders; reserving competition law, merger control, company law, securities rules, labour and consumer floors, and strategic industrial discipline to the nation; and using the global layer for trade predictability, anti-cartel cooperation, tax-base protection, and narrow common rules that prevent regulatory arbitrage without constitutionalizing corporate power above democracy.
- `570-legal-entity-business-and-beneficial-ownership-registries-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-entry-desks-regional-coordination-national-public-truth-and-no-government-by-paper-shell.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat organizational identity as constitutional infrastructure rather than clerical residue: communities can help witness real economic and associational life, municipalities or counties should usually provide the reachable entry desk for ordinary business-facing registrations and permits, regional or state layers should coordinate where federal structure or market geography requires it, national or constitutional-state law should own the authoritative registry of legal persons and the rules for unique identifiers, lifecycle events, disclosure, and strike-off, beneficial ownership should be held through a public authority or tightly governed equivalent with rapid lawful access and strong update discipline, and continental or global bodies should provide interoperability rails rather than pretending there can be one sovereign company register for the world.
- `595-territorial-reorganization-incorporation-mergers-splits-status-change-and-no-map-surgery-by-managerial-fiat.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the creation, merger, split, annexation, abolition, and status change of territorial authorities as constitutional surgery rather than managerial tidying, so map reform remains lawful, consultative, alternatives-tested, continuity-safe, and reviewable instead of becoming a shortcut around self-government.
- `625-temporal-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-pilot-clocks-review-amendment-succession-and-no-government-by-immortal-pilot.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it should stop living in indefinite provisional status and acquire an explicit temporal home: a declared start basis, time-bounded pilot and transition rules where experimentation is still honest, published review clocks, visible renewal and amendment routes, sunset for temporary derogations, and lawful succession or dissolution rules so the polity does not govern for decades as an “interim” arrangement that nobody ever formally chose to keep.
- `763-caretaker-government-and-pre-election-restraint-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-routine-administration-incoming-government-consultation-major-appointments-freeze-emergency-carve-outs-and-no-mandate-stretch-between-verdict-and-handover.md` — Ideal governments should treat dissolution, hung-parliament bargaining, post-election transition, and imminent change of government as **a distinct continuity-with-restraint mode rather than business as usual**: outgoing governments should continue routine administration and urgent protection of the public, but major policy, appointments, contracts, publicity, and irreversible international or fiscal commitments should pause, narrow, or move only after consultation with the likely successor, so no one stretches an expiring mandate through the handover gap.
- `819-boundary-and-membership-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-accession-gates-territory-rules-amendment-thickness-exit-protocols-dissolution-paths-and-no-map-by-one-way-ratchet.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, and **what information chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should use open and reversible participation with no hidden territorial claim, shared-service backbones should declare member classes, accession formulas, notice periods, and unwind rules, bounded functional authorities should use chartered territories plus staged accession and constrained exit, and general-purpose territorial tiers should rely on statutory boundary change with public consultation, transition machinery, and no map by one-way ratchet.
- `828-mandate-exit-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-recall-municipal-dismissal-confidence-loss-bounded-dissolution-and-treaty-lapse.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should governing mandates end when they fail, expire early, or lose their public basis?** with scope-matched exit defaults rather than one romantic removal myth: simple recall or replacement for tiny steward bodies, council-centered dismissal and tightly bounded mayoral removal at municipal scale, explicit confidence-loss and successor grammar for metropolitan and regional governments with real power, bounded parliamentary exit and dissolution rules for most national governments, and fixed reauthorization, for-cause removal, or treaty-lapse rules for plurilateral and global bodies that must never drift into ambient permanence.

## evaluation

- `419-production-monitoring-fed-by-complaints-appeals-and-user-feedback.md` — A public automated system is not adequately monitored if it only watches internal metrics. **Complaints, appeals, operator reports, and affected-user feedback** should be treated as first-class operational telemetry and folded into the system’s monitoring, evaluation, and review loop.
- `420-drift-budgets-rollback-paths-and-decommission-thresholds.md` — Public automation should not merely be monitored; it should come with **predefined thresholds for rollback, deactivation, or retirement**. A system that drifts past its risk tolerance should face a governed response path, including fallback operation and, where necessary, decommissioning.
- `432-adversarial-testing-diverse-red-teams-and-contextual-impact-evaluation.md` — Before and during consequential public deployment, AI systems should face a plural evidence stack: adversarial testing, diverse red-teaming, baseline comparison, impact evaluation in context, and renewed evaluation whenever the intervention or setting materially changes.
- `434-override-telemetry-escalation-queues-and-second-look-sampling.md` — Human oversight is not real unless overrides, disagreements, and stop decisions are counted, reviewed, and turned into operating changes instead of disappearing as private friction.
- `437-subgroup-floor-metrics-public-harm-registries-and-thresholds.md` — Public AI systems should not pass on aggregate accuracy alone: they need **subgroup floor metrics**, visible harm registries, and predefined thresholds that trigger mitigation, fallback, or suspension when particular groups are carrying disproportionate risk.
- `440-determination-registers-waiver-ledgers-and-expiring-deviations.md` — Whenever a public AI team decides that a use case falls outside a stricter risk category, or waives a baseline safeguard, that choice should become a **numbered determination record** with scope, justification, evidence, owner, expiry, and a public-facing summary.
- `443-version-pinned-baselines-approved-change-windows-and-rollback.md` — A public AI service should run from a **named approved baseline** — model version, prompt or policy layer, retrieval corpus, thresholds, integrations, and dependencies — and every material change should move through a documented change window with rollback-ready evidence.
- `481-ephemeral-working-aids-decisional-capture-thresholds-and-no-shadow-dossiers.md` — Consequential public-AI operations should clearly separate ephemeral drafts, scratchpads, convenience copies, and personal working aids from authority-bearing records, but once those aids are circulated, relied on, or add unique decisional substance, they must either be captured into the governed record or barred from carrying decision weight.
- `482-queue-dwell-honesty-service-clocks-and-anti-starvation-escalation.md` — Rights-bearing requests, reviews, appeals, exceptions, and incident items should expose when their clock started, what service window or expectation applies, whether they are merely queued or actively worked, what is blocking progress, and how escalation happens when dwell exceeds thresholds, so “under review” cannot launder starvation.
- `488-scope-typed-governance-stack-block-municipality-metro-region-nation-and-planet.md` — An ideal government is not one uniform sovereign repeated at different sizes, but a scope-typed stack in which each level is optimized for the kinds of problems it can actually see, coordinate, and correct: block for stewardship, municipality for place, metro for networks, region for landscapes and major systems, nation for rights and redistribution, and global bodies for commons, peace, and shared baselines.
- `495-crisis-federalism-threshold-escalation-rule-of-law-temporariness-and-handback-clocks.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should handle crises through threshold-based escalation from the lowest competent level upward, with reserve capacity and coordination available at higher tiers, global notification and commons machinery where cross-border harms exist, and emergency powers kept lawful, necessary, proportionate, temporary, and visibly handed back once ordinary authority can govern again.
- `502-public-safety-by-scope-prevention-first-local-legitimacy-metro-serious-crime-coordination-and-rights-locked-cooperation.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat public safety as a scale-matched civic function rather than a single armed hierarchy: neighborhoods and municipalities should lead on prevention, trust, and visible order; metropolitan and regional bodies should coordinate spillover systems and serious-crime patterns; nations should set rights, training, and investigative baselines; and international police cooperation should stay narrow, ordinary-law, human-rights-bound, and never become a back door for political policing.
- `505-land-and-housing-by-scope-secure-tenure-municipal-place-making-metro-housing-markets-regional-landscapes-and-national-fairness.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat housing and land as a scale-matched constitutional domain: micro-local institutions steward shared places and surface need; municipalities handle parcels, streets, permits, and neighborhood upgrading; metropolitan bodies govern the real housing market and fair-share growth; regions protect landscapes, basins, and food land; nations guarantee rights, anti-segregation floors, and housing finance; and global institutions supply rights baselines, data, and crisis support rather than pretending to zone the planet.
- `507-membership-and-movement-by-scope-local-inclusion-national-citizenship-regional-mobility-and-global-protection.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should split membership and movement cleanly by scale: local governments make residence workable and non-exclusionary in daily life; national governments control citizenship, ordinary admission rules, and status determination under law; regional bodies can widen lawful mobility and burden-sharing where states consent; and global institutions should enforce refugee, anti-statelessness, and human-rights baselines so border control never becomes a permission slip for rightlessness.
- `511-climate-by-scope-local-adaptation-metropolitan-form-regional-resilience-national-transition-and-global-carbon-limits.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern climate by splitting powers according to where they actually bite: neighborhoods and local institutions surface risk and build resilience in daily life; municipalities shape buildings, land use, local mobility, heat, flooding, and service continuity; metropolitan and regional bodies govern commutes, airsheds, catchments, and strategic adaptation systems that cross municipal borders; nations set binding transition rules, carbon and industrial policy, just-transition finance, and national adaptation plans; and the global layer sets temperature and reporting baselines, climate-finance duties, and narrow coordination rules rather than pretending to run every place-based transition itself.
- `515-digital-public-infrastructure-by-scope-local-access-city-service-design-national-rails-and-global-open-standards.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern digital public infrastructure by keeping assisted access, trust-building, and service usability close to people; letting municipalities and metropolitan institutions integrate place-based services and local data uses under strong law; reserving identity, payments, base registries, secure data exchange, notifications, cybersecurity baselines, and universal-access duties to the nation; and keeping the global layer focused on open technical standards and narrow identifier coordination rather than allowing either platform monopolies or a fantasy world digital state to swallow public governance.
- `524-children-and-youth-by-scope-local-belonging-municipal-voice-regional-opportunity-national-guarantees-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern childhood and youth as a full citizenship-building architecture rather than a sentimental side issue: families, peers, schools, and neighborhood institutions should make belonging and safety real; municipalities should build child-friendly streets, services, and participation channels; regional bodies should coordinate transport, child protection pathways, specialist services, and opportunity systems that outrun one town; nations should guarantee rights, income floors, education and care baselines, and fair transitions to adulthood; and the global layer should protect child-rights norms, anti-exploitation baselines, and cross-border solidarity without becoming a world parent.
- `527-end-of-life-and-death-care-by-scope-local-accompaniment-municipal-death-administration-regional-palliative-capacity-national-rights-and-global-pain-relief.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat dying, death care, and bereavement as governed phases of civic life rather than hospital leftovers: households, friends, and community institutions can accompany the dying and mourn the dead but should not be left alone to navigate pain, paperwork, and impossible choices; municipalities should make death registration, burial or cremation access, bereavement navigation, and culturally plural local practice legible and reachable; regional bodies should coordinate palliative-care networks, hospice and specialist capacity, coronial or medical-examiner functions, and referral pathways that outrun one city; nations should guarantee consent law, advance directives, surrogate decision rules, equitable palliative access, medicine availability, and vital-registration baselines; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in essential pain-relief access, rights norms, and knowledge exchange rather than pretending to legislate every intimate end-of-life question for the whole world.
- `528-freedom-of-conscience-and-religion-by-scope-local-coexistence-municipal-neutrality-regional-fairness-national-rights-and-global-protection.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat freedom of conscience, religion, and belief as plural civic infrastructure rather than a privilege of dominant traditions or a project of militant homogenization: households, associations, and communities should be free to form, change, practice, criticize, or refuse belief without coercion; municipalities should keep ordinary civic life neutral and usable through fair permits, equal access, cemetery and calendar accommodation, and non-discriminatory service interfaces; regional bodies should coordinate fairness across hospitals, prisons, schools, and other institutions whose catchments outrun one city; nations should guarantee legal personality, anti-discrimination law, equal citizenship, education and service neutrality, hate-crime and incitement baselines, and rights-safe rules for conscientious objection; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in rights norms, persecution response, and anti-incitement principles rather than trying to govern theology from afar.
- `535-transport-and-logistics-by-scope-local-streets-metro-transit-regional-corridors-national-networks-and-global-interoperability.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat transport as a lived access system and a strategic circulation system at the same time: neighbourhoods and households can surface danger, exclusion, curb conflict, and last-mile need but should not be left to self-organize mobility; municipalities should govern streets, sidewalks, cycling, bus priority, curb use, traffic calming, road safety, and visible access to daily destinations; metropolitan authorities should own mass transit integration, fare systems, freight interfaces, and land-use coordination across one labour and housing market; regional institutions should govern intercity corridors, ports, inland waterways, airports, and resilience across the geography through which people and goods actually move; nations should own network finance, safety baselines, decarbonization strategy, essential-service guarantees, and major modal balance; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in aviation and maritime rules, cross-border interoperability, and fair technical standards rather than pretending one city can regulate the skies or the sea lanes.
- `538-money-and-payments-by-scope-local-cash-access-municipal-acceptance-national-public-money-and-global-interoperability.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat money and payments as constitutional infrastructure: households and neighbourhood institutions can surface exclusion, fraud, outage, and cash-access failures but should not mint rival monies for ordinary public life; municipalities should guarantee practical payment usability in everyday government, including cash access and acceptance where law protects it, legible public-payment channels, and inclusive collection design; metropolitan and regional institutions should coordinate shared payment touchpoints where commuting, service markets, and public agencies cross borders; nations should own legal tender, central bank money, payment-system oversight, public-payment rails, consumer protection, anti-fraud baselines, and resilience; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in message standards, cross-border interoperability, remittance quality, and data-friction reduction rather than pretending that local service design or national monetary legitimacy can be outsourced.
- `563-public-procurement-institutions-and-review-by-scope-local-needs-regional-shared-buying-national-rules-independent-challenges-and-no-government-by-emergency-sole-source-fog.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat public procurement as a governed public institution rather than a clerical back office: keep need definition, user-facing specification, and day-to-day contract management close to the service; use metropolitan, county, provincial, state, or other regional shared-buying bodies where market structure, scarce expertise, or repeated categories make pooling sensible; reserve national government for the procurement code, standard documents, core e-procurement rails, integrity controls, supplier-access baselines, independent complaint review design, and open-contracting discipline; keep the global layer narrow in interoperable standards, anti-rigging and anti-corruption cooperation, and fair cross-border conditions of competition; and never let emergency exemptions, framework sprawl, or vendor dependence turn public spending into shadow executive power.
- `583-subnational-distress-administrative-supervision-special-measures-handback-clocks-and-no-silent-recentralization.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **intervention in failing local or regional government as a lawful last-resort ladder**: ordinary supervision should be legality-bound and proportionate, support and co-production should come before takeover, financial distress and service collapse should trigger explicit temporary special measures only under published legal thresholds, essential services and rights routes must remain protected throughout, and every intervention should carry a reviewable restoration-and-handback path so rescue does not harden into permanent tutelage.
- `590-multilevel-impact-packets-subsidiarity-territorial-effects-rural-proofing-and-no-lawmaking-by-placeless-abstraction.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should require any higher-tier law, regulation, spending program, or platform reform that materially affects lower-tier powers, finances, administrative burden, or territorial outcomes to ship with a **published multilevel impact packet** — a compact subsidiarity, proportionality, territorial-effects, implementation, and consultation record — so central action is argued openly rather than smuggled through placeless abstraction.
- `606-when-co-operation-becomes-government-thresholds-for-constitutionalizing-shared-territorial-power-and-no-metropolitan-rule-by-consortium.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should let municipalities and regions co-operate freely for shared capacity and service delivery, but once a joint body starts making repeated cross-boundary trade-offs across several sectors, raising compulsory money, issuing debt, binding land use or major infrastructure choices, or functioning as the real political center of a territory, it should be constitutionalized as honest metropolitan or regional government rather than left as a consortium, summit, or quango stack.
- `614-knowledge-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-observatories-territorial-indicators-basemaps-scenario-capacity-and-no-government-by-fragmented-spreadsheets.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **knowledge home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, and participatory one: a territorially coherent observatory, common basemaps and boundary files, a published indicator set at the scale actually being governed, lawful data-sharing and evaluation capacity, open methods and release discipline, and visible routes from evidence into plans and budgets — so the shared tier stops governing through municipal spreadsheet fragments, ministry leftovers, vendor dashboards, and dueling numbers.
- `627-constitutionalization-bundles-for-shared-territorial-power-core-upgrades-supporting-upgrades-and-no-government-by-single-home-fetish.md` — Once co-operation has crossed the threshold into real shared territorial government, an ideal polity should not pretend that one institutional fix — election alone, revenue alone, law alone, map alone, platform alone, or participation alone — makes the arrangement honest; it should constitutionalize in **bundles**, starting with a minimum core of public-law, democratic, fiscal, administrative, and accountability upgrades, then docking territorial, temporal, intergovernmental, and operating bundles as the functions actually governed require.
- `632-scope-audit-triggers-review-packets-evaluation-lanes-and-no-constitutional-sleepwalk.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should keep a standing **scope audit registry** that uses territorial-impact, fiscal, democratic, and operational tripwires to trigger a typed **review packet** whenever real responsibility drifts away from the nominal map, so repair begins from evidence and laddered choice rather than from crisis improvisation or silent constitutional sleepwalk.
- `646-scope-severability-fallback-baselines-partial-invalidity-and-no-whole-stack-collapse-by-contamination.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat a materially stack-altering package as **severable where honest**, preserving only those parts that can still be described as lawful, coherent, and democratically ownable on their own terms, with one visible fallback baseline and one public explanation of what survives, what is stayed, and what must be rebuilt, so a single defect neither launders the whole package nor needlessly detonates the lawful remainder.
- `662-global-institution-toolkit-by-problem-class-assemblies-secretariats-scientific-panels-registries-inspection-compliance-funds-and-no-world-state-monoculture.md` — The ideal global layer should be built from a **small toolkit of treaty-bound institutional forms matched to problem class** rather than from one fantasy model of world government: use assemblies and councils for norm-setting, secretariats and focal-point networks for continuous coordination, scientific panels for shared factual baselines, registries and reporting systems for comparability, inspection or verification where cheating matters, dispute and compliance lanes where interpretation recurs, and dedicated funds where solidarity is required — while refusing both fake world-state domesticity and empty declarations with no operating spine.
- `663-cross-border-integration-ladders-information-sharing-minimum-standards-mutual-recognition-common-enforcement-budget-tools-and-no-union-by-slogan.md` — Ideal continental or plurilateral governance should climb an explicit **integration ladder** — information exchange, benchmarking, minimum standards, mutual recognition, shared operational rails, pooled enforcement, common financing, and only then deeper legislative or fiscal union where truly necessary — so polities can co-govern real spillovers without pretending every problem requires the same depth of union or drifting by slogan into competence creep.
- `669-shared-regime-entry-ladders-observers-signatories-provisional-application-accession-admission-thresholds-depositaries-entry-into-force-and-no-membership-by-affiliation-claim.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed participation ladder** that distinguishes observer, applicant, signatory, provisional applier, party/member, and deeper-module participant — with actor eligibility, admission body, deposited instrument, effective date, rights bundle, and reviewable public status — so the public can tell who is merely near a regime and who is actually bound.
- `685-shared-regime-procurement-constitutions-competition-thresholds-exceptions-award-records-protest-debarment-and-no-regime-by-sole-source-habit.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed procurement constitution** that separates planning, solicitation methods, competition defaults, threshold rules, emergency and sole-source exceptions, award records, debriefing, complaint or protest lanes, vendor-sanctions logic, contract-change control, and exit capacity — so the regime is not governed by incumbent vendors, emergency habit, or off-book buyer discretion.
- `686-shared-regime-administrative-justice-constitutions-ethics-ombuds-investigations-management-evaluation-tribunals-and-no-secretariat-by-untestable-discipline.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed administrative-justice constitution** that separates confidential advice, ombuds or informal resolution, protected disclosure, investigations, interim protection, management review, disciplinary decision, independent tribunal review, and public jurisprudence memory — so the secretariat is not governed by rumor, retaliation fear, or untestable disciplinary power.
- `696-shared-regime-evaluation-and-learning-constitutions-workplans-independence-management-response-recommendation-tracking-after-action-review-and-no-regime-by-report-shelf.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed evaluation-and-learning constitution** that separates workplan setting, commissioning, evaluator independence, evaluation from audit or monitoring, management response, recommendation tracking, public release, and structured learning loops such as after-action review — so institutional learning does not decay into report shelfware, recommendation theater, or “lessons learned” with no decision route.
- `697-shared-regime-strategic-planning-and-results-constitutions-general-programmes-programme-budgets-theories-of-change-baselines-targets-reviews-and-no-mission-by-project-pile.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed strategic-planning-and-results constitution** that separates long-horizon strategy, medium-term programme budgets, theories of change, outcome and output ladders, indicator and baseline rules, target-setting, reprogramming, and mid-cycle review — so the institution does not drift into mission by project pile, target theater, dashboard government, or budget without strategy.
- `709-challenge-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-entry-routes-complaints-petitions-second-look-lanes-feedback-duties-and-no-public-voice-by-consultation-theater.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, and an evidence packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **challenge packet** naming who may raise what kind of challenge, through which front door, with what triage into complaint, petition, appeal, ombuds, whistleblowing, or regulatory lanes, on what clocks, with what feedback and anti-retaliation duties, so the field can be corrected by the governed instead of merely observed by them.
- `723-review-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-reconsideration-appeal-remand-interim-relief-finality-and-no-government-by-remedy-maze.md` — Once the archive has challenge, decision, notice, and effect packets for a field, it should also publish one narrow **review packet** saying which second-look lanes exist, which acts must pass through reconsideration before appeal and which may go straight outward, who hears each route, what record and standard of review apply, what interim relief or stay is available, what remand or substitution powers exist, and when finality blocks endless reopening — so the field does not decay into government by remedy maze, sponsor-friendly reconsideration, or hidden no-review zones.
- `726-default-function-routing-table-for-ideal-governments-everyday-place-shared-systems-guarantor-duties-compact-unions-and-treaty-narrow-waists.md` — The archive should keep one compact **default routing table** for common public functions: route witness, stewardship, and micro-commons to micro-local units; ordinary daily place government to municipalities; shared urban systems to metropolitan government or narrow utilities; basin, hospital, university, corridor, and ecological platforms to regions or typed functional authorities; equal citizenship, redistribution, macro-stability, and constitutional settlement to nations; bounded cross-border markets, mobility, and corridors to compact unions; and genuinely planetary peace, alerting, interoperability, and commons baselines to treaty-bound global narrow waists — while forcing mixed fields to declare lead scope, support scopes, fiscal logic, and upgrade tests instead of choosing a level from scratch every time.
- `771-public-policy-evaluation-and-management-response-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-workplans-independence-publication-response-ledgers-reopen-triggers-and-no-learning-by-unanswered-recommendation.md` — Ideal governments should treat public-policy evaluation as **a standing learning-and-accountability lane rather than a report genre**: significant policies, programmes, and reforms should be selected through visible workplans and triggers, evaluated with enough independence and methodological fit to say what is working and for whom, answered through time-bound management responses, tracked through public recommendation ledgers, and reopened where implementation stalls or the policy context materially changes, so learning is not reduced to ceremonial “lessons learned” prose with no decision route.
- `772-ombuds-and-maladministration-redress-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-independent-complaint-entry-own-motion-investigation-recommendation-powers-systemic-reporting-and-no-rights-by-complaint-maze.md` — Ideal governments should treat the ombuds lane as **an independent, low-friction, non-court redress and learning system for maladministration**: people should be able to complain without prohibitive cost or procedural sophistication, the institution should be able to investigate administrative unfairness and service failure, make recommendations, report systemically, and route cases onward where harder remedies are needed, so everyday state error does not force the public to choose between silence, media scandal, and full litigation.
- `773-administrative-appeal-and-tribunal-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-reasons-file-access-internal-review-suspensive-relief-merits-vs-legality-review-and-no-rights-by-one-shot-decision.md` — Ideal governments should treat administrative appeals and tribunals as **the ordinary second-look constitution of the state**: when public authorities make decisions that affect rights, status, money, permits, benefits, penalties, or obligations, people should receive reasons, access to the relevant file, a prompt internal reconsideration or equivalent first review where appropriate, and then an independent appeal or tribunal lane with powers proportionate to the stakes, so administrative authority does not become a one-shot command enforced mainly by cost, speed, and user exhaustion.
- `787-language-interpretation-plain-language-and-accessible-format-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-comprehension-duty-translation-thresholds-and-no-rights-by-unreadable-procedure.md` — Ideal governments should require that **administrative procedure be intelligible to the people it governs**: binding notices, adverse cases, required actions, deadlines, hearing opportunities, and remedies should be communicated in **plain language, understandable form, and accessible modes**, with **interpretation, translation, and disability accommodation triggered by stakes and necessity** rather than treated as optional courtesy.
- `791-benchmark-cards-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-vocation-fit-kit-floors-fiscal-congruence-review-lanes-tripwires-and-no-admiration-without-scoring.md` — The archive should pair its canonical scope matrix and answer-key notes with one compact **benchmark-card format** for each scope — vocation fit, minimum complete kit, fiscal and capability congruence, spillover or solidarity fit, review and remedy integrity, participation and scrutiny proportionality, and named upgrade or handback tripwires — so real constitutions, reform proposals, and case studies can be compared tersely against the ideal stack without reopening the whole theory.
- `792-stress-test-and-drill-cards-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-essential-service-continuity-command-legibility-fiscal-buffers-rights-discipline-rescoping-signals-and-no-paper-constitution-by-calm-weather.md` — The archive should pair its ideal-government answer key and benchmark cards with one compact **stress-test and drill-card format** for each scope — essential-service continuity, command and escalation legibility, reserve and surge discipline, intergovernmental handoff integrity, legality and rights restraint under pressure, public communication, and recovery or handback triggers — so governments are judged not only by their steady-state design but by whether they remain honest under flood, blackout, outbreak, fiscal shock, cyber disruption, or constitutional strain.
- `793-maintenance-calendars-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-benchmark-refresh-stress-drill-cadence-trigger-overrides-public-registries-and-no-constitutional-care-by-sporadic-panic.md` — The archive should pair its ideal-government answer key, benchmark cards, stress cards, and scope-audit triggers with one compact **maintenance-calendar rule** for each scope — fixed benchmark refreshes, typed drill cadence, trigger-based overrides, publication and follow-up duties, and explicit closure or rescoping lanes — so multilevel constitutions are maintained as routine public infrastructure rather than rediscovered only during reform waves or crisis embarrassment.
- `795-public-proof-packs-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-benchmark-publication-stress-summaries-maintenance-ledgers-transition-boards-and-no-constitutional-claim-without-outward-evidence.md` — The archive should pair its answer-key, benchmark, stress-test, maintenance, and upgrade-path notes with one compact **public proof-pack rule** for each scope: **publish the minimum outward evidence that lets residents, auditors, legislatures, journalists, courts, and peer polities verify what the arrangement is, how it scored, what failed under stress, what is due next, and where any transition actually stands**.
- `796-intervention-ladders-for-failing-governments-of-each-scope-support-first-proportional-supervision-special-measures-handback-clocks-and-no-permanent-emergency-custody.md` — When a government-by-scope arrangement keeps failing its benchmark, stress, maintenance, or proof duties, the archive should not jump straight from diagnosis to permanent takeover. It should use one compact **intervention ladder**: **support first, escalate by law and proportionality, separate own-competence supervision from delegated-task control, keep any special measures temporary and reviewable, and pair every intervention with a handback or formal rescoping test so rescue does not harden into quiet permanent custody**.
- `797-contestability-ladders-for-scope-governance-benchmark-objections-trigger-appeals-intervention-review-handback-denials-and-no-constitutional-maintenance-by-self-marking.md` — The archive should pair its answer-key, benchmark, stress-test, maintenance, upgrade-path, public-proof, and intervention notes with one compact **contestability ladder**: **benchmark classifications, trigger openings or closures, stress findings used for redesign, intervention orders, renewals, handback denials, and other stack-shaping judgments should all carry typed standing, reasons, interim-relief logic, and final independent review, so governments do not maintain the constitutional stack by marking their own homework and calling the result settled**.
- `798-reference-classes-and-comparator-cohorts-for-ideal-governments-by-scope-morphology-matched-peers-functional-territories-capacity-bands-and-no-benchmark-by-postcard.md` — The archive should compare real governments-by-scope against the ideal stack through small, declared **comparator cohorts** built from the right **scope type, morphology, functional territory, legal vocation, and capacity band**, so benchmark work stays like-with-like instead of drifting into prestige case selection, capital-city halo, and false analogies between unlike institutions.
- `800-assessment-missions-for-ideal-governments-by-scope-self-assessment-desk-review-site-visits-public-hearings-evidence-rooms-management-response-and-no-benchmark-by-questionnaire-alone.md` — The archive should pair its answer-key, benchmark, stress-test, maintenance, proof-pack, contestability, comparator, and temporary-object notes with one compact **assessment-mission grammar**: **every serious scope judgment should declare its review method, combine self-assessment with desk review, site or field verification, stakeholder hearings, contradiction logging, and a reasoned management-response path, so governments are not benchmarked by questionnaire alone or by prestige-site theater instead of evidence**.
- `801-finding-registers-for-scope-assessments-lane-specific-scores-confidence-classes-severity-clocks-contradiction-residue-and-no-constitutional-verdict-by-blended-number.md` — The archive should pair its answer-key, benchmark, assessment-mission, proof-pack, and contestability notes with one compact **finding-register grammar**: **every serious scope review should express its result lane by lane, state confidence and severity separately, preserve unresolved contradiction residue, allow no-score where proof is thin, and attach next-action clocks, so constitutional judgments are not collapsed into one blended number or one breezy headline verdict**.
- `805-sampling-frames-and-case-selection-discipline-for-scope-assessments-risk-bands-ordinary-and-failed-routes-negative-cases-and-no-benchmark-by-showcase-tour.md` — The archive should pair its assessment-mission and tracer-route notes with one compact **sampling-frame grammar**: **every serious scope review should declare which sites, records, routes, stakeholders, and time slices are in frame, which are being sampled representatively or purposively, what is excluded, and what claims the chosen sample can honestly support, so benchmark work cannot drift into prestige tours, complaint-only anecdote, or constitutional overclaim from a thin showcase set**.
- `806-evidence-registers-and-provenance-chains-for-scope-assessments-exhibit-ids-source-typing-redaction-ledgers-finding-links-and-no-verdict-by-orphaned-exhibit.md` — The archive should pair its assessment-mission, sampling, tracer-route, finding-register, and close-out notes with one compact **evidence-register grammar**: **every serious scope review should keep a stable exhibit register that says what each evidence object is, where it came from, what version or date it belongs to, what was redacted or withheld, which finding it supports or contradicts, and how later reviewers can reuse it, so constitutional judgments are not built from orphaned exhibits, floating screenshots, or unverifiable quotations**.
- `808-calibration-packs-moderation-loops-and-precedent-banks-for-scope-assessments-score-anchors-difficult-case-conferences-documented-departures-and-no-benchmark-by-reviewer-mood.md` — The archive should pair its benchmark, mission, evidence-register, and mission-integrity notes with one compact **review-calibration grammar**: **every serious scope assessment should keep a small calibration pack with lane-specific score anchors, worked examples, threshold splits, precedent notes, moderation checkpoints, and documented departures, so that different review teams can reach comparably disciplined judgments without collapsing everything into one blended score or one charismatic reviewer’s mood**.
- `809-research-frontier-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-settled-defaults-live-thresholds-morphology-uncertainty-fiscal-floor-tests-legitimacy-triggers-and-no-false-precision-by-constitutional-confidence-theater.md` — The archive should now separate **settled default doctrine** from **live research questions**: it can state with high confidence the vocation, minimum kit, and anti-cosplay limit of each scope, but it should keep threshold questions — when a functional city truly needs metro democracy, when sparse territories need county-style pooling, when a region is a real platform rather than decorative duplication, how much fiscal congruence is enough, when intervention should trigger, and how thick upper-tier institutions may become — inside one compact research frontier rather than pretending the whole stack is equally settled.
- `810-threshold-dossiers-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-metro-triggers-county-pooling-regional-platform-proof-fiscal-floors-legitimacy-thickness-and-no-tier-thickening-by-anecdote.md` — When the archive reaches a **live threshold question** rather than a settled scope doctrine question, it should require one compact **threshold dossier**: a declared threshold claim, the right territory and comparator cohort, a small set of named evidence lanes, visible contradiction residue, and a provisional confidence statement, so judgments such as **when metro democracy is now required, when sparse territories need pooled county-scale service backbones, when a region is a real platform, or when a lower tier is fiscally non-hollow** are made by typed evidence rather than by population fetish, prestige case imitation, or crisis anecdote.
- `811-scope-verdict-packets-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-settled-holdings-frontier-thresholds-benchmark-findings-repair-routes-public-proof-and-no-applied-judgment-by-scattered-cross-reference.md` — When the archive uses its ideal-governments-by-scope stack on a **real polity, proposal, or case study**, it should emit one compact **scope verdict packet** that bundles the settled scope holding, any live threshold holdings, the benchmark finding, material stress or maintenance modifiers, the active repair or intervention path, and the public-proof class — so later applied judgments stay portable, comparable, and compact instead of dissolving into essay recap or a trail of scattered note citations.
