- `807-assessment-team-independence-and-conflict-discipline-for-scope-reviews-recusal-rosters-secondment-firebreaks-host-picked-experts-donor-pathways-and-no-constitutional-judgment-by-interested-mission.md` — The archive should pair its assessment-mission, evidence-register, contestability, and close-out notes with one compact **mission-integrity grammar**: **every serious scope review should declare who is judging, who is only informing, what interests and funding pathways each reviewer carries, what firebreaks apply to secondees and host-nominated specialists, when recusal is mandatory, and how outsiders can challenge the composition of the team before findings harden into the live constitution, so the archive does not mistake expertise, proximity, or funding convenience for independence**.
- `808-calibration-packs-moderation-loops-and-precedent-banks-for-scope-assessments-score-anchors-difficult-case-conferences-documented-departures-and-no-benchmark-by-reviewer-mood.md` — The archive should pair its benchmark, mission, evidence-register, and mission-integrity notes with one compact **review-calibration grammar**: **every serious scope assessment should keep a small calibration pack with lane-specific score anchors, worked examples, threshold splits, precedent notes, moderation checkpoints, and documented departures, so that different review teams can reach comparably disciplined judgments without collapsing everything into one blended score or one charismatic reviewer’s mood**.
- `809-research-frontier-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-settled-defaults-live-thresholds-morphology-uncertainty-fiscal-floor-tests-legitimacy-triggers-and-no-false-precision-by-constitutional-confidence-theater.md` — The archive should now separate **settled default doctrine** from **live research questions**: it can state with high confidence the vocation, minimum kit, and anti-cosplay limit of each scope, but it should keep threshold questions — when a functional city truly needs metro democracy, when sparse territories need county-style pooling, when a region is a real platform rather than decorative duplication, how much fiscal congruence is enough, when intervention should trigger, and how thick upper-tier institutions may become — inside one compact research frontier rather than pretending the whole stack is equally settled.
- `810-threshold-dossiers-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-metro-triggers-county-pooling-regional-platform-proof-fiscal-floors-legitimacy-thickness-and-no-tier-thickening-by-anecdote.md` — When the archive reaches a **live threshold question** rather than a settled scope doctrine question, it should require one compact **threshold dossier**: a declared threshold claim, the right territory and comparator cohort, a small set of named evidence lanes, visible contradiction residue, and a provisional confidence statement, so judgments such as **when metro democracy is now required, when sparse territories need pooled county-scale service backbones, when a region is a real platform, or when a lower tier is fiscally non-hollow** are made by typed evidence rather than by population fetish, prestige case imitation, or crisis anecdote.
- `811-scope-verdict-packets-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-settled-holdings-frontier-thresholds-benchmark-findings-repair-routes-public-proof-and-no-applied-judgment-by-scattered-cross-reference.md` — When the archive uses its ideal-governments-by-scope stack on a **real polity, proposal, or case study**, it should emit one compact **scope verdict packet** that bundles the settled scope holding, any live threshold holdings, the benchmark finding, material stress or maintenance modifiers, the active repair or intervention path, and the public-proof class — so later applied judgments stay portable, comparable, and compact instead of dissolving into essay recap or a trail of scattered note citations.
- `815-administrative-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-host-secretariats-principal-owned-backbones-chartered-operators-records-homes-and-no-heavy-power-by-borrowed-bureaucracy.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, and **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what administrative chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should use small secretariats with no hidden command over member administrations, shared-service backbones should keep declared principals, employer-of-record rules, records homes, and service agreements, bounded functional authorities should have chartered operating cores with explicit staffing, asset, procurement, and incident-command authority, and general-purpose territorial tiers should normally own their own civil-service, records, and operating spine rather than ruling through borrowed host bureaucracy.
- `818-information-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-shared-facts-observatories-record-homes-official-statistics-links-publication-calendars-and-no-heavy-power-by-private-dashboard.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, and **what participation chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what information chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should use open shared-indicator rooms and light observatories, shared-service backbones should keep principal-readable service telemetry plus declared case and record routes, bounded functional authorities should keep authoritative operational data homes with method notes and publication calendars, and general-purpose territorial tiers should carry a fuller public-knowledge constitution rather than governing through host-held or vendor-held dashboards.
- `821-dispute-resolution-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-negotiation-ladders-mediation-expert-determination-jurisdiction-maps-continuity-orders-and-no-heavy-power-by-hostage-dispute.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, **what information chain belongs to it**, **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**, and **what decision-rule chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what dispute-resolution chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should rely on recorded negotiation and visible member-side escalation, shared-service backbones should use negotiation-first ladders with mediation, technical determination, continuity protection, and public-law endpoints, bounded functional authorities should publish jurisdiction maps and interim continuity orders, and general-purpose territorial tiers should rely on ordinary justice and constitutional routes rather than permanent bargaining by hostage dispute.
- `832-oversight-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-witness-municipal-scrutiny-metro-audit-national-watchdogs-and-treaty-review.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should each scope ordinarily be scrutinized and corrected once it has real public authority?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one watchdog fetish: **micro-local bodies should rely mainly on open meetings, visible records, rotation, and cheap escalation rather than a miniature oversight state; municipalities should be the first level with a full public oversight kit of chamber scrutiny, independent external audit, complaint or ombuds routes, disclosure, and ordinary legality review; metropolitan and regional governments should own equally real audit and redress lanes rather than borrowing them permanently from a host city or ministry; national government should carry the fullest fourth-branch and court-backed oversight constitution; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound but still face visible member scrutiny, independent audit and evaluation, complaint and ethics channels, and published review cycles rather than secretariat self-marking**.
- `834-information-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-ledgers-municipal-record-homes-metro-observatories-national-statistics-and-treaty-registries.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should authoritative public facts, records, and decision visibility ordinarily live at each scope?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one dashboard fetish: **micro-local bodies should keep simple minutes, noticeboards, steward ledgers, and escalation logs rather than miniature data states; municipalities should be the first level with a full public information constitution of clerks or record stewards, open meeting packets, service and permit records, publication calendars, and reusable public data; metropolitan and regional governments should own their own observatories, geospatial baselines, and cross-boundary performance records rather than parasitic dependence on a host city or ministry; national government should carry the thickest official-statistics, gazette, archive, and interoperability spine; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound but still maintain comparability standards, registries, alerting channels, and shared reporting rather than private dashboards or counterfeit world omniscience**.
- `835-emergency-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-readiness-municipal-incident-command-regional-civil-protection-national-derogation-discipline-and-treaty-alerting.md` — The archive should answer the question **what emergency and exception grammar should ordinarily fit each scope?** with scale-matched escalation rather than one panic state fetish: **micro-local bodies should default to readiness, warning, mutual aid, and witness rather than emergency sovereignty; municipalities should be the first ordinary home of incident command, continuity, sheltering, and short-horizon emergency operations under ordinary law; metropolitan governments should carry shared-system disruption management where the functional city is one risk field; regional or provincial governments may honestly house civil-protection, wildfire, flood, logistics, and mutual-aid platforms where those risks are territorially real; national government should hold the thickest declaration, derogation, reserve, and exceptional coordination powers under legislative renewal, judicial review, and strict handback discipline; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound, specializing in alerting, coordination, standards, pooled assistance, and tightly authorized collective action rather than becoming ambient permanent emergency government**.
- `836-participation-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-assembly-municipal-dockets-metro-territorial-hearings-national-petition-ladders-and-treaty-observers.md` — If the archive already knows **what government should exist at each scope**, **how it is chosen**, **how it is financed**, **how it is scrutinized**, **where force lives**, **where records live**, and **what emergency lane fits it**, it should also know **how public voice honestly re-enters that government at each scale**: direct and reachable assembly voice at micro-local scale; petitions, hearings, consultations, bounded participatory-budget lanes, and occasional deliberative mini-publics at municipal scale; territory-wide participation homes for metropolitan and regional bodies that govern real shared systems; parliamentary hearing, petition, consultation, and rare constitution-level referendum lanes at national scale; and structured observer, submission, hearing, and stakeholder-participation routes for continental and global bodies rather than fake world-plebiscitary theater.
- `837-adjudication-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-pre-legal-entry-municipal-administrative-justice-regional-ordinary-courts-national-apex-review-and-treaty-tribunals.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should adjudication itself honestly live at each scope?** with scale-matched defaults rather than court fetish or courthouse minimalism: **micro-local bodies should offer witness, record, mediation, and easy entry into law rather than pretending to be sovereign courts; municipalities should be the first scale with a legible administrative-justice front door for ordinary daily disputes, but not the last word on legality against themselves; metropolitan and regional governments with real cross-boundary power should have equally real ordinary-court, tribunal, or legality-review homes rather than sending people on a host-city treasure hunt; national government should carry the apex and constitutional-review layer that secures rights, uniform due-process floors, and competence settlement across the stack; and continental or global bodies should use treaty-bound courts and tribunals only where the mandate is genuinely real, without pretending to be either a world judiciary of everything or a diplomacy-only zone immune from law**.

## extractive-governance

- `496-civil-service-by-scope-stewardship-without-patronage-municipal-professionalism-metro-capacity-and-constitutional-merit-cores.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not use one staffing model at every scale: it should pair light, recallable stewardship at the micro-local level with professional merit administration where continuity and technical competence matter, give metropolitan and regional bodies their own real operating capacity when they wield real powers, protect a constitutional core civil service against spoils and purge cycles, and keep plurilateral and global secretariats thin, expert, and mandate-bound.
- `517-public-revenue-and-taxation-by-scope-local-own-source-taxes-metropolitan-base-sharing-national-progressivity-and-global-anti-evasion-floors.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should fund government by keeping visible own-source revenues tied to place and service at the local level; using metropolitan and regional revenue-sharing where commuters, land values, logistics, or extractive burdens cross borders; reserving progressive income taxation, broad consumption taxes, social insurance contributions, debt management, and equalizing transfers to the nation; and using the global layer for narrow anti-evasion, information-exchange, and minimum-tax rules that stop mobile capital from hollowing out democratic finance.
- `529-indigenous-peoples-and-self-government-by-scope-community-authority-municipal-consent-regional-co-governance-national-plurinational-constitutionalism-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat Indigenous peoples as peoples and governing authorities rather than as cultural stakeholders inside someone else’s map: Indigenous communities and nations should retain authority over identity, membership, internal institutions, culture, and many matters of everyday law according to their own traditions and evolving consent; municipalities should share space, services, permits, and practical coexistence through negotiated respect rather than zoning override or paternal inclusion; regional bodies should co-govern watersheds, forests, transport, health, education, and other shared systems whose real catchments outrun one settlement; nations should constitutionally recognize Indigenous peoples, lands, treaties, restitution claims, fiscal powers, and free, prior and informed consent rather than forcing all authority through a unitary citizenship mold; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in rights norms, anti-extractive scrutiny, and cross-border Indigenous solidarity rather than pretending a world body can govern each people’s internal life.
- `534-extractive-resources-by-scope-local-consent-regional-cumulative-impacts-national-public-rents-and-global-just-transition-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat subsoil wealth as a temporary public endowment rather than a permanent license for frontier sacrifice: affected communities and Indigenous peoples should hold real consent, monitoring, grievance, and benefit-sharing power close to the site; regional bodies should govern cumulative impacts on water, housing, health, roads, labour markets, tailings, and emergency corridors across the wider extraction zone; nations should own licensing architecture, contract disclosure, beneficial-ownership rules, royalties, sovereign wealth or stabilization policy, closure liability, anti-corruption enforcement, and diversification strategy; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in transparency standards, trade and due-diligence rules, conflict prevention, and just-transition principles rather than letting a scramble for critical minerals recreate colonial extraction under green branding.
- `570-legal-entity-business-and-beneficial-ownership-registries-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-entry-desks-regional-coordination-national-public-truth-and-no-government-by-paper-shell.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat organizational identity as constitutional infrastructure rather than clerical residue: communities can help witness real economic and associational life, municipalities or counties should usually provide the reachable entry desk for ordinary business-facing registrations and permits, regional or state layers should coordinate where federal structure or market geography requires it, national or constitutional-state law should own the authoritative registry of legal persons and the rules for unique identifiers, lifecycle events, disclosure, and strike-off, beneficial ownership should be held through a public authority or tightly governed equivalent with rapid lawful access and strong update discipline, and continental or global bodies should provide interoperability rails rather than pretending there can be one sovereign company register for the world.

## finance-governance

- `485-effective-state-resolution-correction-graphs-and-no-authority-by-feed-order.md` — When consequential public-AI notices, status updates, corrections, withdrawals, and superseding records accumulate over time, the institution should compute and publish one deterministic effective current state from explicit lineage links, and should treat forks or unresolved ambiguity as incidents rather than letting feed order, CMS recency, or whichever copy looks newest decide authority.
- `514-justice-by-scope-local-resolution-city-legal-aid-regional-courts-national-codes-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern justice by keeping low-stakes dispute resolution, legal help, and problem sensing close to daily life; sizing trial and appellate institutions to real catchments rather than arbitrary municipal lines; reserving criminal codes, procedural guarantees, judicial independence, prosecution architecture, and equal access floors to the nation; and treating the global layer as a narrow guarantor of rights, cooperation, and last-resort review rather than as a substitute domestic judiciary.
- `538-money-and-payments-by-scope-local-cash-access-municipal-acceptance-national-public-money-and-global-interoperability.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat money and payments as constitutional infrastructure: households and neighbourhood institutions can surface exclusion, fraud, outage, and cash-access failures but should not mint rival monies for ordinary public life; municipalities should guarantee practical payment usability in everyday government, including cash access and acceptance where law protects it, legible public-payment channels, and inclusive collection design; metropolitan and regional institutions should coordinate shared payment touchpoints where commuting, service markets, and public agencies cross borders; nations should own legal tender, central bank money, payment-system oversight, public-payment rails, consumer protection, anti-fraud baselines, and resilience; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in message standards, cross-border interoperability, remittance quality, and data-friction reduction rather than pretending that local service design or national monetary legitimacy can be outsourced.
- `539-banking-credit-and-financial-stability-by-scope-local-relationship-lending-regional-development-finance-national-prudential-oversight-and-global-backstops.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat banking and credit as a public-risk-bearing capability rather than a private allocation game: households, workers, firms, and local institutions can surface credit exclusion, predatory products, and place-specific capital starvation but should not be left to self-insure against systemic finance; municipalities can convene local credit intelligence, public banking interfaces, and anti-exclusion measures but should not act as miniature prudential sovereigns; regional institutions should govern development banks, housing and infrastructure finance platforms, and sectoral transition tools where production systems and catchments are wider than one city; nations should own licensing, prudential supervision, macroprudential policy, deposit insurance, resolution, lender-of-last-resort functions, and the constitutional line between utility banking and speculative risk; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in supervisory standards, cross-border resolution cooperation, correspondent-finance continuity, and anti-arbitrage floors rather than pretending world technocracy can substitute for domestic democratic control.
- `572-standards-metrology-testing-accreditation-and-conformity-assessment-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-inspection-regional-labs-national-quality-infrastructure-and-no-government-by-unverified-measurement.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **standards, metrology, testing, accreditation, and conformity assessment** as a **constitutional measurement layer**: keep user witnessing, complaint, and local inspection close to communities and municipalities; pool expensive laboratories, calibration, and specialist technical capacity at regional scale where fragmentation would waste money or degrade competence; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the quality-infrastructure core — measurement units, national metrology, accreditation, legal metrology, standard-setting mandates, and recognition rules — and use continental and global layers for equivalence, interoperability, and trade discipline rather than for a fantasy of one world product ministry.
- `671-shared-regime-representation-ladders-credentials-chief-delegates-alternates-observers-speaking-rights-committee-access-and-no-state-voice-by-self-appointment.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed representation ladder** that separates party or member status from delegate credentials, chief delegates from alternates and advisers, participants from observers, and speaking rights from voting rights — with accrediting authority, challenge lane, substitution rules, public roster, and functional-independence protections — so no one can conjure state or member voice by badge, donor access, press credential, or self-appointment.
- `677-shared-regime-external-participation-constitutions-accreditation-observer-categories-submissions-hearings-transparency-registers-and-no-public-power-by-lanyard.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed external-participation constitution** that separates membership from observer or accredited-participant status, standing accreditation from session registration, document access from floor rights, written submissions from negotiation rights, and consultation from decision power — so public authority does not drift toward whoever got a badge, a side-room invitation, or a privileged mailing list.
- `686-shared-regime-administrative-justice-constitutions-ethics-ombuds-investigations-management-evaluation-tribunals-and-no-secretariat-by-untestable-discipline.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed administrative-justice constitution** that separates confidential advice, ombuds or informal resolution, protected disclosure, investigations, interim protection, management review, disciplinary decision, independent tribunal review, and public jurisprudence memory — so the secretariat is not governed by rumor, retaliation fear, or untestable disciplinary power.
- `808-calibration-packs-moderation-loops-and-precedent-banks-for-scope-assessments-score-anchors-difficult-case-conferences-documented-departures-and-no-benchmark-by-reviewer-mood.md` — The archive should pair its benchmark, mission, evidence-register, and mission-integrity notes with one compact **review-calibration grammar**: **every serious scope assessment should keep a small calibration pack with lane-specific score anchors, worked examples, threshold splits, precedent notes, moderation checkpoints, and documented departures, so that different review teams can reach comparably disciplined judgments without collapsing everything into one blended score or one charismatic reviewer’s mood**.
- `821-dispute-resolution-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-negotiation-ladders-mediation-expert-determination-jurisdiction-maps-continuity-orders-and-no-heavy-power-by-hostage-dispute.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, **what information chain belongs to it**, **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**, and **what decision-rule chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what dispute-resolution chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should rely on recorded negotiation and visible member-side escalation, shared-service backbones should use negotiation-first ladders with mediation, technical determination, continuity protection, and public-law endpoints, bounded functional authorities should publish jurisdiction maps and interim continuity orders, and general-purpose territorial tiers should rely on ordinary justice and constitutional routes rather than permanent bargaining by hostage dispute.

## fiscal-governance

- `419-production-monitoring-fed-by-complaints-appeals-and-user-feedback.md` — A public automated system is not adequately monitored if it only watches internal metrics. **Complaints, appeals, operator reports, and affected-user feedback** should be treated as first-class operational telemetry and folded into the system’s monitoring, evaluation, and review loop.
- `489-fiscal-equalization-universal-floors-and-no-postcode-lottery.md` — Decentralization is only legitimate when paired with upper-tier equalization and universal social floors, so local self-government can shape place without turning basic rights, public goods, and life chances into a lottery of inherited tax base.
- `492-competence-conflict-routing-intergovernmental-arbitration-and-no-settlement-by-fiscal-blackmail.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should route intergovernmental disputes through declared consultation, mediation, and final legal-arbitral decision rather than through improvisation, prestige contests, or fund-withholding coercion, so conflicts over powers, duties, and money are settled by rules that preserve both common government and lower-tier self-rule.
- `497-public-knowledge-by-scope-local-records-metro-observatories-independent-statistics-audit-and-open-science.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should build a scale-matched public knowledge stack: durable local records and meeting visibility close to the ground, municipal and metropolitan observatories for place-based systems, independent national statistics and audit institutions for common facts and fiscal truth, and international scientific and reporting networks for cross-border harms, with methods and evidence as open as safety and privacy allow.
- `498-constitutional-change-by-scope-local-charters-double-majorities-constituent-consent-and-no-silent-recentralization.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should be adaptable without being easy to hijack: routine institutional adjustment should happen through ordinary law or local charters where appropriate, but changes to the territorial bargain, rights architecture, or division of powers should require heightened procedures, constituent-unit consent where federal balance is affected, and fair consultation or referendum only on constitutionally grounded terms, with no unilateral recentralization by ordinary statute, fiscal leverage, or emergency drift.
- `516-markets-and-company-power-by-scope-local-entry-metro-space-national-antitrust-and-fair-global-rules.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern markets by keeping entry barriers, permits, public procurement access, and everyday consumer signal detection close to local life; using metropolitan and regional institutions to manage commercial geography, logistics, and market systems that cross municipal borders; reserving competition law, merger control, company law, securities rules, labour and consumer floors, and strategic industrial discipline to the nation; and using the global layer for trade predictability, anti-cartel cooperation, tax-base protection, and narrow common rules that prevent regulatory arbitrage without constitutionalizing corporate power above democracy.
- `517-public-revenue-and-taxation-by-scope-local-own-source-taxes-metropolitan-base-sharing-national-progressivity-and-global-anti-evasion-floors.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should fund government by keeping visible own-source revenues tied to place and service at the local level; using metropolitan and regional revenue-sharing where commuters, land values, logistics, or extractive burdens cross borders; reserving progressive income taxation, broad consumption taxes, social insurance contributions, debt management, and equalizing transfers to the nation; and using the global layer for narrow anti-evasion, information-exchange, and minimum-tax rules that stop mobile capital from hollowing out democratic finance.
- `529-indigenous-peoples-and-self-government-by-scope-community-authority-municipal-consent-regional-co-governance-national-plurinational-constitutionalism-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat Indigenous peoples as peoples and governing authorities rather than as cultural stakeholders inside someone else’s map: Indigenous communities and nations should retain authority over identity, membership, internal institutions, culture, and many matters of everyday law according to their own traditions and evolving consent; municipalities should share space, services, permits, and practical coexistence through negotiated respect rather than zoning override or paternal inclusion; regional bodies should co-govern watersheds, forests, transport, health, education, and other shared systems whose real catchments outrun one settlement; nations should constitutionally recognize Indigenous peoples, lands, treaties, restitution claims, fiscal powers, and free, prior and informed consent rather than forcing all authority through a unitary citizenship mold; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in rights norms, anti-extractive scrutiny, and cross-border Indigenous solidarity rather than pretending a world body can govern each people’s internal life.
- `531-rural-remote-and-peripheral-places-by-scope-local-agency-intermunicipal-service-backbones-regional-catchments-national-territorial-solidarity-and-global-learning.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat rural, remote, island, mountain, and other peripheral places not as residual territories waiting to shrink quietly but as legitimate political communities with distinct distance, sparsity, ecology, and production constraints: local institutions should set priorities, steward place knowledge, and surface service failure early; intermunicipal compacts should provide the shared administrative and service backbones that low-density places often need to remain capable; regional bodies should govern labour markets, referral systems, transport, watershed and land-use spillovers, and adaptation systems that cross many small jurisdictions; nations should guarantee territorial solidarity through fiscal equalization, connectivity, service floors, fair resource revenue, and public employment and investment rules that do not punish distance; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in fair trade, climate and connectivity support, and shared learning rather than imposing metro-centric metrics on every place.
- `540-trade-customs-and-border-procedures-by-scope-local-port-interfaces-regional-gateways-national-trade-policy-and-global-rules.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat trade governance as both a rules system and a border operations system: households, workers, firms, and local communities can surface chokepoints, corruption, hazardous shipments, and the lived burden of gateways but should not each define external trade law; municipalities should govern port-adjacent land use, truck conflict, inspection-site interfaces, market transparency, and emergency support for traders without becoming fragmented customs sovereignties; regional institutions should coordinate corridors, dry ports, airports, inland terminals, and gateway ecosystems across the geography through which goods actually move; nations should own tariff schedules, trade agreements, customs law, single-window architecture, revenue collection, sanctions and strategic controls, and the constitutional balance between openness, security, labour, and environment; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in trade rules, customs standards, interoperable data models, and facilitation norms rather than pretending that one city or one ministry can govern cross-border exchange alone.
- `545-regulators-inspections-and-enforcement-role-clarity-risk-based-proportionality-due-process-and-no-government-by-shakedown.md` — An ideal polity should treat regulators and inspectorates as bounded public-law institutions whose job is to reduce real harm, preserve fair conditions, and keep essential systems trustworthy; give them clear missions, enough independence to resist improper influence, enough accountability to remain public servants, risk-based and proportionate enforcement tools, visible appeal routes, and budgets not addicted to penalties; and never let licensing, inspection, or fines become a substitute tax system, a patronage machine, or a theatre of arbitrary power.
- `546-public-enterprises-and-state-owned-enterprises-explicit-rationales-separated-roles-hard-budget-constraints-and-open-books.md` — An ideal polity may own and operate enterprises where public ownership is genuinely justified — for natural monopolies, essential network infrastructure, strategic resilience, mission-critical finance, or other clearly stated public purposes — but it should publish why it owns them, separate ownership from regulation and policy-making, state public-service obligations explicitly, compensate them transparently, impose hard budget constraints, keep boards and books professional and visible, and review the portfolio often enough that public enterprise does not become a hiding place for patronage, off-balance-sheet debt, or anti-competitive favoritism.
- `547-budgeting-treasury-and-public-accounts-credible-ceilings-legislative-authority-one-treasury-and-no-government-by-fund-fog.md` — An ideal polity should turn public money into a lawful cycle of strategy, appropriation, controlled execution, and audited account: set clear fiscal objectives and medium-term ceilings, present one comprehensive budget rather than a maze of side funds, give the legislature real time and analytic capacity to approve totals and appropriations, execute through a unified treasury, chart of accounts, commitment controls, and cash planning, publish in-year reports and year-end financial statements, disclose fiscal risks honestly, and route audit findings back into correction so the state cannot govern through supplementary fog, arrears, or off-budget improvisation.
- `567-public-borrowing-and-debt-by-scope-no-neighborhood-debt-municipal-capital-discipline-metro-infrastructure-national-stabilization-and-no-government-by-hidden-guarantees.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat borrowing as a scale-matched constitutional power rather than a general permission slip: micro-local bodies should usually not borrow at all, municipalities and regions should borrow mainly for long-lived capital under hard disclosure and restructuring rules, national governments should own macro-stabilization and sovereign debt management openly rather than laundering risk through off-book vehicles, and continental or global borrowing should remain narrow, charter-bound, and formula-backed instead of pretending a thin treaty body is already a full fiscal state.
- `581-mandate-finance-congruence-unfunded-mandates-vertical-fiscal-imbalance-and-no-decentralization-by-fiscal-theater.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **mandate-finance congruence** as constitutional law rather than budget etiquette: no level of government should be assigned a durable public function unless the same settlement also names the revenue basket, transfer formula, equalization rule, borrowing limits, and capability backstop that make the function actually dischargeable; delegated tasks must come with commensurate resources, local self-government must include at least some real own-source fiscal room, and upward rescue must be visible and reviewable rather than leaving decentralization to degrade into blame-shifting.
- `583-subnational-distress-administrative-supervision-special-measures-handback-clocks-and-no-silent-recentralization.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **intervention in failing local or regional government as a lawful last-resort ladder**: ordinary supervision should be legality-bound and proportionate, support and co-production should come before takeover, financial distress and service collapse should trigger explicit temporary special measures only under published legal thresholds, essential services and rights routes must remain protected throughout, and every intervention should carry a reviewable restoration-and-handback path so rescue does not harden into permanent tutelage.
- `585-conditional-grants-matching-funds-competitive-programs-and-no-government-by-grant-maze.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **intergovernmental grants as constitutional instruments rather than administrative weather**: ordinary local discretion and equal citizenship should rest mainly on own-source revenue plus predictable general and equalization transfers; earmarked, matching, performance, capital, or competitive grants should be reserved for narrow cases where rights floors, spillovers, transition priorities, or shared investment genuinely justify them; co-financing duties should scale to fiscal capacity; application, reporting, and audit rules should be harmonized and limited; and no higher tier should be allowed to govern municipalities, metros, or regions mainly by forcing them to live inside a permanent grant maze.
- `586-function-transfer-packs-staff-assets-records-contracts-liabilities-and-no-reassignment-by-legal-text-alone.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **any transfer of a public function across levels of government as a full transfer pack rather than a sentence in a law**: whenever a competence moves, the same settlement should also name the effective date, service standard, staff lane, asset and lease inventory, contract and procurement treatment, records and data custody, ongoing-case handoff, fiscal lane, liability rule, transition authority, dispute route, and review clock, so that decentralisation or recentralisation cannot occur by moving the headline power while leaving the receiving government to inherit an empty shell.
- `596-special-purpose-authorities-utility-districts-metro-agencies-and-no-government-by-quango-sprawl.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should use special-purpose authorities only as tightly bounded tools for real network, basin, corridor, or technical-governance problems, so shared systems can be run at the right scale without letting single-purpose bodies metastasize into a shadow constitution of opaque boards, off-budget debt, and blame-proof government.
- `606-when-co-operation-becomes-government-thresholds-for-constitutionalizing-shared-territorial-power-and-no-metropolitan-rule-by-consortium.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should let municipalities and regions co-operate freely for shared capacity and service delivery, but once a joint body starts making repeated cross-boundary trade-offs across several sectors, raising compulsory money, issuing debt, binding land use or major infrastructure choices, or functioning as the real political center of a territory, it should be constitutionalized as honest metropolitan or regional government rather than left as a consortium, summit, or quango stack.
- `607-democratic-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-indirect-councils-double-legitimacy-direct-election-and-no-metropolitan-rule-by-proxy.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, the honest constitutional question is not whether it needs democracy but **which democratic home fits the power**: keep indirect representation for narrow and bounded co-ordination, use double-legitimacy designs where both people and component governments must visibly count, and prefer directly elected territorial government once the body can bind residents through compulsory finance, major debt, cross-sector territorial bargaining, or durable system-shaping authority.
- `608-fiscal-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-own-source-revenue-predictable-equalization-capital-discipline-and-no-metropolitan-government-by-begging-bowl.md` — Once shared territorial power has become real metropolitan or regional government, the polity should give it an honest fiscal constitution: responsibilities commensurate with resources, a visible base of own or rule-based shared revenue, diversified and buoyant funding, equalization that protects weaker places without destroying discretion, grants used for clear national or supralocal purposes rather than everyday dependence, and borrowing bounded mainly to capital investment rather than operational drift.
- `609-administrative-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-own-executive-own-staff-records-treasury-planning-core-and-no-government-by-secondment-maze.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **administrative home** as well as a democratic and fiscal one: a legally visible executive center, its own staff and records, a durable core for planning/finance/procurement/legal/data work, interoperable but non-subordinate interfaces with component governments and the state, and enough administrative continuity that the territory is not really governed through borrowed personnel, rotating mayoral bandwidth, consultants, or agency shrubbery.
- `610-accountability-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-scrutiny-audit-disclosure-complaints-review-and-no-government-by-jurisdictional-gap.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **accountability home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, and administrative one: its own scrutiny forum, named records-and-disclosure duties, internal control and audit proportionate to risk, external audit and integrity jurisdiction, complaint and review routes that ordinary people can actually find, and explicit accountability for operators and contractors so the territory is not really governed in the gaps between municipalities, agencies, and the state.
- `612-intergovernmental-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-standing-consultation-compacts-dispute-lanes-and-no-government-by-ad-hoc-summit.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **intergovernmental home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, and public-law one: a standing place in state decision-making, lawful consultation routes, regular bargaining forums, explicit compact and co-financing lanes, visible conflict-escalation and dispute rules, and no territorial government by occasional summit, ministry favour, or host-city mediation.
- `613-participatory-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-petitions-hearings-mini-publics-territorial-notice-and-no-metropolitan-participation-by-postcode.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **participatory home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, and intergovernmental one: territory-wide notice, petition and question routes, public hearings and consultations, bounded co-prioritisation and participatory-budget lanes where suitable, representative deliberative processes for complex trade-offs, and visible response duties — so residents can influence the shared tier directly rather than relying on borrowed municipal channels, host-city publicity, or consultation theatre.
- `614-knowledge-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-observatories-territorial-indicators-basemaps-scenario-capacity-and-no-government-by-fragmented-spreadsheets.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **knowledge home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, and participatory one: a territorially coherent observatory, common basemaps and boundary files, a published indicator set at the scale actually being governed, lawful data-sharing and evaluation capacity, open methods and release discipline, and visible routes from evidence into plans and budgets — so the shared tier stops governing through municipal spreadsheet fragments, ministry leftovers, vendor dashboards, and dueling numbers.
- `615-service-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-service-authorities-operator-chains-commissioning-continuity-and-no-government-by-memorandum-network.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **service home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, and knowledge one: a visible split among authority, operator, and regulator; a named territorial service map showing what stays local and what becomes shared; lawful commissioning, franchising, or direct-operation routes where system services are real; service standards, continuity duties, and fallback rules that survive contracts and politics; and clear public entry and complaint handoffs — so the territory stops being governed through memoranda, host-city favors, improvised consortia, and operator clubs.
- `616-planning-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-territorial-plans-plan-hierarchies-conformity-and-no-government-by-vision-deck.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **planning home** as well as democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, and service ones: a territorial planning authority with a real public plan, a declared hierarchy with municipal and state plans, visible conformity or compatibility rules, infrastructure-and-land-use coupling, amendment and review clocks, and no territorial government by advisory strategy deck.
- `617-capital-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-multi-year-pipelines-asset-stewardship-lifecycle-discipline-and-no-government-by-project-list.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **capital home** as well as democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, service, and planning ones: a visible multi-year capital programme, declared prioritisation and appraisal rules, asset-condition and maintenance stewardship, explicit funding-versus-financing discipline, and no territorial government by project list.
- `618-regulatory-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-licensing-permits-standards-inspection-enforcement-and-no-government-by-operator-rulebook.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **regulatory home** as well as democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, service, planning, and capital ones: a visible territorial rulebook, named licensing and permitting lanes where risk demands them, a clear separation among rule-maker, regulator, operator, and reviewer, proportionate inspection and enforcement, and no government by operator rulebook.
- `619-contract-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-procurement-franchising-change-control-exit-capacity-and-no-government-by-concession-patchwork.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **contract home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, service, planning, capital, and regulatory one: a visible buyer-or-commissioner function, explicit make-buy-franchise tests, lawful procurement and concession routes, disciplined contract and change control, published performance and amendment trails, real handback and step-in capacity, and no territorial government by concession patchwork.
- `623-redress-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-complaints-hearings-appeals-ombuds-and-no-government-by-jurisdiction-hunt.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **redress home** as well as democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, service, planning, capital, regulatory, contract, workforce, digital-operating, and emergency ones: one visible territorial path for complaint, reconsideration, hearing, appeal, ombuds, and judicial review, with reasons, clocks, and no government by jurisdiction hunt.
- `627-constitutionalization-bundles-for-shared-territorial-power-core-upgrades-supporting-upgrades-and-no-government-by-single-home-fetish.md` — Once co-operation has crossed the threshold into real shared territorial government, an ideal polity should not pretend that one institutional fix — election alone, revenue alone, law alone, map alone, platform alone, or participation alone — makes the arrangement honest; it should constitutionalize in **bundles**, starting with a minimum core of public-law, democratic, fiscal, administrative, and accountability upgrades, then docking territorial, temporal, intergovernmental, and operating bundles as the functions actually governed require.
- `630-rescoping-authority-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-administration-by-law-constitutional-bargains-by-consent-and-no-jurisdictional-rewire-by-executive-deal.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat **moving a function between scopes as a graded constitutional act**: ordinary implementation detail may be adjusted through ordinary law inside fixed competences, sectoral reallocations among existing tiers should travel through public legislation with consultation and impact proof, any move that alters the protected bargain of local or regional self-government should require the higher law and consent route appropriate to that bargain, and no executive compact, grant condition, crisis summit, or managerial workaround should be allowed to rewire who really governs what.
- `632-scope-audit-triggers-review-packets-evaluation-lanes-and-no-constitutional-sleepwalk.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should keep a standing **scope audit registry** that uses territorial-impact, fiscal, democratic, and operational tripwires to trigger a typed **review packet** whenever real responsibility drifts away from the nominal map, so repair begins from evidence and laddered choice rather than from crisis improvisation or silent constitutional sleepwalk.
- `648-scope-functional-equivalence-rules-anti-circumvention-tests-and-no-stack-change-by-relabeling.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should classify **materially stack-altering moves by their real effect rather than by their chosen label**: if a grant condition, procurement framework, software default, model contract, coordination protocol, “pilot”, guidance note, or emergency instruction functionally reallocates who decides, who must comply, who pays, who may object, or which tier now governs in practice, it should travel through the same packet, opinion, override, register, and review lanes as any openly named scope change.
- `657-scope-successor-accountability-legacy-acts-liabilities-records-and-no-blame-laundering-by-rescoping.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat **future competence, predecessor accountability, successor service continuity, records custody, litigation defence, and fiscal liability as separate questions that must each be typed explicitly whenever a function moves**, so rescoping cannot become a way to enjoy new power while laundering blame for old acts, omissions, debts, broken files, or unremedied harms.
- `660-canonical-government-matrix-by-scope-legislature-executive-civil-service-fiscal-base-review-participation-and-no-full-stack-rewrite-for-every-tier.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should reuse one **canonical scope matrix** rather than reinventing every tier from scratch: micro-local units for witness and stewardship, municipalities for ordinary place government, metropolitan authorities for functional urban systems, regions for major territorial platforms and shared rule, nations for equal citizenship and redistribution, continental bodies for bounded cross-border compacts, and global institutions for treaty-bound peace, commons, alerting, and interoperability — each with a scope-matched decision forum, executive spine, civil-service density, fiscal base, review lane, and participation channel.
- `663-cross-border-integration-ladders-information-sharing-minimum-standards-mutual-recognition-common-enforcement-budget-tools-and-no-union-by-slogan.md` — Ideal continental or plurilateral governance should climb an explicit **integration ladder** — information exchange, benchmarking, minimum standards, mutual recognition, shared operational rails, pooled enforcement, common financing, and only then deeper legislative or fiscal union where truly necessary — so polities can co-govern real spillovers without pretending every problem requires the same depth of union or drifting by slogan into competence creep.
- `687-shared-regime-privileges-and-immunities-constitutions-functional-independence-jurisdiction-tax-customs-inviolability-waiver-and-no-sovereignty-cosplay.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed privileges-and-immunities authority map** that separates juridical personality, inviolability, immunity from legal process, archives and communications protection, fiscal and customs facilities, visa and entry support, category-specific treatment for representatives and officials, waiver authority, and abuse-control lanes — so institutional independence is protected without decaying into sovereignty cosplay, perk inflation, or unreviewable impunity.
- `695-shared-regime-enterprise-risk-and-internal-control-constitutions-risk-appetite-owners-registers-control-testing-exceptions-assurance-maps-and-no-governance-by-unknown-exposure.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed enterprise-risk-and-internal-control constitution** that separates risk appetite, risk taxonomy, owner assignment, principal-risk review, key-control design, control testing, exception handling, assurance mapping, and governing-body reporting — so operational exposure does not disappear into unknown exposure, stale registers, control folklore, or audit surprise government.
- `700-minimum-design-packet-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-archetype-vocation-boundary-kit-fiscal-proof-exception-ladder-upgrade-triggers-and-no-essay-length-restatement.md` — Any later archive note that claims what the ideal government at a given scope should be should default to one small **design packet** — name the scope archetype, state the vocation, define the boundary logic, specify the minimum complete kit, show the fiscal and capability proof, declare any exception ladder, and list upgrade or reversibility triggers — so the archive can compare designs, merge revisions, and stay compact without re-arguing the whole multilevel constitution every time.
- `701-adjudication-matrix-for-competing-ideal-governments-of-the-same-function-packet-comparison-dominance-tests-reversible-tie-breaks-and-no-scope-choice-by-ideology-alone.md` — When the archive faces several plausible claims about which scope should govern the same function, it should compare the rival **design packets** through one compact adjudication matrix — vocation fit, boundary honesty, minimum kit completeness, fiscal and capability proof, spillover handling, solidarity and rights-floor fit, democratic proportionality, reversibility, and machinery cost — so the archive can choose or bracket the better packet without collapsing into ideology, naming habit, or essay-length restatement.
- `703-interface-packets-for-lane-typed-government-stacks-lead-lanes-handoffs-shared-facts-escalation-clocks-and-no-governance-by-glue-folklore.md` — Once the archive has split a composite field into lane-sized scope packets, it should also publish one **interface packet** for the resulting typed stack: name the lead for each lane, the handoff triggers between lanes, the shared facts and records that must travel, the timing and escalation rules, the fiscal and liability crosswalks, and the public route map, so distributed government does not collapse back into blame circulation, duplicate work, or quiet recentralization by whoever controls the glue.
- `706-repair-packets-for-recurrently-failing-government-fields-after-action-conversion-root-cause-ownership-funding-lanes-closure-proof-and-no-government-by-permanent-recovery-mode.md` — Lane-typed government fields that repeatedly re-enter **degraded, emergency, or recovery modes** should publish a typed **repair packet** that converts after-action learning into owned structural change — clearly separating quick corrective action from deeper fiscal, staffing, capital, digital, legal, or boundary repair — with recurrence triggers, service-floor protection, closure proof, and escalation when “temporary recovery” is becoming the field’s real constitution.
- `707-sunset-packets-for-obsolete-government-lanes-bodies-and-temporary-machinery-review-triggers-successor-homes-residue-registers-closure-proof-and-no-immortal-institutions-by-inherited-backlog.md` — Once a field has repair packets, it should also publish one **sunset packet** whenever review shows that a lane, body, or temporary governance machine no longer deserves to exist in live form — naming the trigger, the successor home or true extinction rule, the rights and service floors that still bind during wind-down, the residue register for cases, contracts, assets, staff, records, data, debt, and public-facing channels, the closure proof, and the reactivation rule — so obsolete institutions do not stay alive merely because they still have backlog, leases, websites, or logos.
- `714-fiscal-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-operating-base-equalization-spine-reserves-capital-lanes-and-no-government-by-grant-fog.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, and delegation rules for a field, it should also publish one narrow **fiscal packet** saying what recurring operating base actually funds the field, which lane holds budget and treasury authority, what equalization or solidarity rule corrects uneven burdens, what reserve and contingency ladder keeps shocks from becoming constitutional panic, what capital and debt lane is lawful, and what grants may supplement but not substitute for an honest money constitution.
- `715-capability-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-employer-lane-merit-floor-training-ladders-surge-rosters-and-no-government-by-borrowed-payroll.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, and a fiscal packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **capability packet** saying which lane is the employer of record and capability steward, what minimum in-house core the field must retain, what merit and qualification floor applies, what training and profession ladders sustain scarce skills, what secondment and surge rules are allowed, and what vacancy or churn triggers open repair or redesign — so the field does not rely on borrowed payroll, consultant memory, or permanent emergency staffing to remain governmental at all.
- `716-information-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-canonical-case-home-access-model-sharing-boundaries-retention-clocks-and-no-government-by-portal-shell.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, and a capability packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **information packet** saying where the field’s canonical case and record homes live, which surface is the system of record and which are only presentation or intake layers, what role-and-access model governs staff and delegates, what sharing boundaries and information agreements apply, what retention/export/handback rules preserve public memory, and what recovery path keeps the field governable when platforms, vendors, or host systems fail — so the field does not become government by portal shell, spreadsheet relay, or vendor-admin shadow.
- `717-asset-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-estate-fleet-equipment-condition-discipline-handback-and-no-government-by-orphan-assets.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, and an information packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **asset packet** saying which lane owns and stewards the field’s estate, fleet, equipment, depots, labs, stores, and critical spares; who holds custody, maintenance, calibration, and replacement duty; what condition and resilience floor applies; what lease, host-site, or operator dependencies exist; and what handback rule survives exit or transfer — so the field does not decay into government by orphan assets, lease camouflage, or maintenance exile.
- `718-service-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-whole-service-front-doors-route-classes-service-floors-continuity-and-no-government-by-front-door-scatter.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, an information packet, and an asset packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **service packet** saying what outcome the field’s service actually promises, which lane owns that promise, what front doors and route classes the public may use, what clocks and service floors bind, how channels and operators compose into one whole service, and what continuity and fallback rules survive overload, outage, provider failure, or redesign — so the field does not decay into government by front-door scatter, route roulette, or service-standard theater.
- `726-default-function-routing-table-for-ideal-governments-everyday-place-shared-systems-guarantor-duties-compact-unions-and-treaty-narrow-waists.md` — The archive should keep one compact **default routing table** for common public functions: route witness, stewardship, and micro-commons to micro-local units; ordinary daily place government to municipalities; shared urban systems to metropolitan government or narrow utilities; basin, hospital, university, corridor, and ecological platforms to regions or typed functional authorities; equal citizenship, redistribution, macro-stability, and constitutional settlement to nations; bounded cross-border markets, mobility, and corridors to compact unions; and genuinely planetary peace, alerting, interoperability, and commons baselines to treaty-bound global narrow waists — while forcing mixed fields to declare lead scope, support scopes, fiscal logic, and upgrade tests instead of choosing a level from scratch every time.
- `728-sideways-authority-packets-for-ideal-governments-bounded-remit-footprint-logic-board-fiscal-lane-review-clocks-and-no-functional-wrapper-without-constitutional-kit.md` — When the archive routes a function **sideways** into a bounded functional authority rather than into an ordinary territorial tier, it should default to one compact **sideways-authority packet** naming the real system footprint, the exact remit and exclusions, the principal public lane that still owns the wider constitutional bargain, the legitimacy and fiscal model, the review and participation routes, and the upgrade-or-exit triggers — so basins, corridors, grids, ports, referral networks, and similar in-between institutions stay governable without pretending to be full territorial governments or dissolving into quango fog.
- `737-release-packets-for-ideal-government-neutral-custody-full-partial-and-phased-release-receiver-readiness-residual-safeguards-and-no-custody-exit-by-impatience.md` — Once the archive has a temporary neutral-custody packet (`736`), it should also keep one compact **custody-release packet** for the moment named surfaces leave custody and re-enter ordinary government: classify the release type, prove receiver readiness surface by surface, preserve case and record lineage, state what safeguards remain temporarily in force, and refuse to end custody merely because a deadline, press statement, or impatient principal wants the appearance of settlement.
- `758-delegated-legislation-and-executive-rulemaking-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-framework-statutes-purposes-scope-time-limits-scrutiny-publication-and-no-government-by-decree-laundering.md` — Ideal governments should treat delegated legislation as a **bounded implementation instrument rather than a spare legislature**: primary law should carry the main political choices, delegations should state purposes, subject matter, scope, and when needed time limits, parliaments should retain real scrutiny power, the public should be able to see and challenge what is made in their name, and executive rulemaking should never become a laundering route for major constitutional, fiscal, rights, or territorial change.
- `763-caretaker-government-and-pre-election-restraint-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-routine-administration-incoming-government-consultation-major-appointments-freeze-emergency-carve-outs-and-no-mandate-stretch-between-verdict-and-handover.md` — Ideal governments should treat dissolution, hung-parliament bargaining, post-election transition, and imminent change of government as **a distinct continuity-with-restraint mode rather than business as usual**: outgoing governments should continue routine administration and urgent protection of the public, but major policy, appointments, contracts, publicity, and irreversible international or fiscal commitments should pause, narrow, or move only after consultation with the likely successor, so no one stretches an expiring mandate through the handover gap.
- `791-benchmark-cards-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-vocation-fit-kit-floors-fiscal-congruence-review-lanes-tripwires-and-no-admiration-without-scoring.md` — The archive should pair its canonical scope matrix and answer-key notes with one compact **benchmark-card format** for each scope — vocation fit, minimum complete kit, fiscal and capability congruence, spillover or solidarity fit, review and remedy integrity, participation and scrutiny proportionality, and named upgrade or handback tripwires — so real constitutions, reform proposals, and case studies can be compared tersely against the ideal stack without reopening the whole theory.
- `792-stress-test-and-drill-cards-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-essential-service-continuity-command-legibility-fiscal-buffers-rights-discipline-rescoping-signals-and-no-paper-constitution-by-calm-weather.md` — The archive should pair its ideal-government answer key and benchmark cards with one compact **stress-test and drill-card format** for each scope — essential-service continuity, command and escalation legibility, reserve and surge discipline, intergovernmental handoff integrity, legality and rights restraint under pressure, public communication, and recovery or handback triggers — so governments are judged not only by their steady-state design but by whether they remain honest under flood, blackout, outbreak, fiscal shock, cyber disruption, or constitutional strain.
- `794-sequenced-upgrade-paths-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-first-honest-steps-bridge-arrangements-cutover-gates-and-no-full-stack-redesign-by-manifesto.md` — When a real polity is far from the archive’s ideal scope stack, reform should move through a sequenced upgrade path: **make the current arrangement honest first, repair the minimum complete kit and fiscal congruence next, constitutionalise any bridge institutions that are already exercising real power, transfer functions only with continuity proof, and attempt deeper territorial or constitutional redesign only after the operating spine is real**.
- `809-research-frontier-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-settled-defaults-live-thresholds-morphology-uncertainty-fiscal-floor-tests-legitimacy-triggers-and-no-false-precision-by-constitutional-confidence-theater.md` — The archive should now separate **settled default doctrine** from **live research questions**: it can state with high confidence the vocation, minimum kit, and anti-cosplay limit of each scope, but it should keep threshold questions — when a functional city truly needs metro democracy, when sparse territories need county-style pooling, when a region is a real platform rather than decorative duplication, how much fiscal congruence is enough, when intervention should trigger, and how thick upper-tier institutions may become — inside one compact research frontier rather than pretending the whole stack is equally settled.
- `810-threshold-dossiers-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-metro-triggers-county-pooling-regional-platform-proof-fiscal-floors-legitimacy-thickness-and-no-tier-thickening-by-anecdote.md` — When the archive reaches a **live threshold question** rather than a settled scope doctrine question, it should require one compact **threshold dossier**: a declared threshold claim, the right territory and comparator cohort, a small set of named evidence lanes, visible contradiction residue, and a provisional confidence statement, so judgments such as **when metro democracy is now required, when sparse territories need pooled county-scale service backbones, when a region is a real platform, or when a lower tier is fiscally non-hollow** are made by typed evidence rather than by population fetish, prestige case imitation, or crisis anecdote.
- `812-institutional-form-choice-ladders-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-thin-connectors-shared-service-backbones-bounded-authorities-general-purpose-tiers-and-no-new-tier-by-spillover-alone.md` — When the archive has already established that a cross-boundary problem is real, it should choose institutional form through one compact **choice ladder**: use a **thin connector** when alignment and information-sharing are enough; a **shared-service backbone** when capacity pooling is the real need; a **bounded functional authority** when one system needs continuous cross-boundary operations or asset stewardship; and a **general-purpose elected tier** only when recurring distributive, land-use, borrowing, coercive, or multi-sector balancing powers make thinner forms constitutionally dishonest.
- `813-legitimacy-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-delegated-councils-principal-owned-backbones-double-key-authorities-directly-elected-tiers-and-no-heavy-power-by-convenience-composition.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, it should also be able to say **what legitimacy chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should be run by delegated elected principals with no hidden hard powers, shared-service backbones should remain clearly owned by the member governments whose duties they support, bounded functional authorities should carry an elected anchor plus explicit double-key gates for major debt, rule, boundary, or remit changes, and general-purpose territorial tiers should normally rest on directly elected chambers with their own scrutiny and executive responsibility rather than on convenience boards pretending to carry full constitutional weight.
- `814-fiscal-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-dues-and-service-payments-assigned-revenues-equalization-keys-capital-lanes-and-no-heavy-power-by-shadow-treasury.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary form is honest** and **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what fiscal chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should live on modest dues and project-preparation money with no disguised distributive budget, shared-service backbones should run on principal-owned service payments and declared cost-sharing plus reserve rules, bounded functional authorities should use assigned revenues, user charges, or rule-bound transfers matched to their narrow charter with explicit capital discipline, and general-purpose territorial tiers should have a public budget constitution with own-source or rule-bound shared revenues, equalization, and visible borrowing limits rather than living by discretionary grants, annual pleas, or off-book vehicles.
- `815-administrative-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-host-secretariats-principal-owned-backbones-chartered-operators-records-homes-and-no-heavy-power-by-borrowed-bureaucracy.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, and **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what administrative chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should use small secretariats with no hidden command over member administrations, shared-service backbones should keep declared principals, employer-of-record rules, records homes, and service agreements, bounded functional authorities should have chartered operating cores with explicit staffing, asset, procurement, and incident-command authority, and general-purpose territorial tiers should normally own their own civil-service, records, and operating spine rather than ruling through borrowed host bureaucracy.
- `817-participation-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-open-dockets-hearings-user-councils-deliberative-mini-publics-response-ledgers-and-no-heavy-power-by-consultation-theater.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **who owns it**, **how money moves through it**, **where its operating spine lives**, and **where scrutiny and redress live**, it should also be able to say **what participation chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should publish open dockets and simple input windows rather than staging fake popular mandates, shared-service backbones should run structured user and accessibility input without pretending pooled operations are a substitute for elected politics, bounded functional authorities should carry recurring hearings and response duties plus deliberative methods where long-horizon tradeoffs justify them, and general-purpose territorial tiers should own a full participation constitution rather than borrowing legitimacy from consultation theater.
- `818-information-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-shared-facts-observatories-record-homes-official-statistics-links-publication-calendars-and-no-heavy-power-by-private-dashboard.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, and **what participation chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what information chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should use open shared-indicator rooms and light observatories, shared-service backbones should keep principal-readable service telemetry plus declared case and record routes, bounded functional authorities should keep authoritative operational data homes with method notes and publication calendars, and general-purpose territorial tiers should carry a fuller public-knowledge constitution rather than governing through host-held or vendor-held dashboards.
- `819-boundary-and-membership-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-accession-gates-territory-rules-amendment-thickness-exit-protocols-dissolution-paths-and-no-map-by-one-way-ratchet.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, and **what information chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should use open and reversible participation with no hidden territorial claim, shared-service backbones should declare member classes, accession formulas, notice periods, and unwind rules, bounded functional authorities should use chartered territories plus staged accession and constrained exit, and general-purpose territorial tiers should rely on statutory boundary change with public consultation, transition machinery, and no map by one-way ratchet.
