- `820-decision-rule-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-ordinary-majorities-qualified-majorities-unanimity-reserves-deadlock-breakers-and-no-heavy-power-by-procedural-veto.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, **what information chain belongs to it**, and **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what decision-rule chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should seek consensus for advisory work and require visible member ratification for anything binding, shared-service backbones should use ordinary-majority operating rules with reserved supermajority or member-ratification gates for portfolio, burden, and liability shifts, bounded functional authorities should use public standing orders with ordinary-majority defaults plus qualified-majority or double-key gates for tariffs, debt, land, remit, and boundary changes, and general-purpose territorial tiers should govern by ordinary democratic majorities with narrowly cabined supermajority reserves and explicit deadlock routes rather than by permanent veto geography.
- `821-dispute-resolution-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-negotiation-ladders-mediation-expert-determination-jurisdiction-maps-continuity-orders-and-no-heavy-power-by-hostage-dispute.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, **what information chain belongs to it**, **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**, and **what decision-rule chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what dispute-resolution chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should rely on recorded negotiation and visible member-side escalation, shared-service backbones should use negotiation-first ladders with mediation, technical determination, continuity protection, and public-law endpoints, bounded functional authorities should publish jurisdiction maps and interim continuity orders, and general-purpose territorial tiers should rely on ordinary justice and constitutional routes rather than permanent bargaining by hostage dispute.
- `822-asset-and-liability-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-member-owned-infrastructure-ring-fenced-balance-sheets-handback-maps-contingent-obligations-and-no-heavy-power-by-orphaned-balance-sheet.md` — When the archive has already established that a cross-boundary problem is real, chosen the honest form, and said who governs, pays, operates, votes, and hears disputes, it should still require one compact **asset-and-liability chain**: thin connectors should own almost nothing beyond trivial co-ordination tools; shared-service backbones should keep political title with the principals unless a clearly bounded common vehicle is justified; bounded functional authorities may hold and steward system-critical assets and named liabilities inside a ring-fenced public balance sheet; and general-purpose territorial tiers should carry visible asset, debt, reserve, and handback constitutions rather than hiding real sovereignty in host property, off-book obligations, or exit chaos.
- `830-decision-rule-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-majorities-municipal-ordinary-rules-federal-double-keys-and-no-fake-global-unanimity.md` — The archive should answer the question **what internal decision rule should usually govern at each scope once the body is real?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one voting fetish: **micro-local institutions should seek rough consensus but fall back cheaply to ordinary majority; municipalities, metropolitan governments, and most regional and national lower chambers should decide ordinary business by ordinary majority with reserved supermajorities for constitutional, territorial, debt, or rights-sensitive thresholds; shared-rule chambers may justify double keys where constituent units are genuinely co-authors of the settlement; and continental or global bodies should treat consensus as a discipline of accommodation, not a veto constitution, reserving unanimity only for narrow membership-, treaty-, or sovereignty-touching classes**.
- `831-fiscal-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-tiny-commons-municipal-own-source-metro-shares-regional-equalization-national-solidarity-and-treaty-dues.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should each scope ordinarily be financed?** with scale-matched fiscal defaults rather than one treasury fetish: micro-local bodies should live on tiny discretionary funds, member contributions, and visible small grants rather than debt or payroll empires; municipalities should be the first level with meaningful own-source revenue, rule-bound transfers, ordinary operating reserves, and capital access for durable local assets; metropolitan governments should use assigned revenue shares, formula transfers, and user-charge lanes where systems justify them rather than annual pleas from member municipalities; regional and provincial governments should combine own revenues, shared taxes, equalization, and platform-scale capital budgets; national government should carry the broad tax base, macro-stabilization, and solidarity machinery; and continental or global bodies should usually rely on treaty dues, assessed contributions, and tightly bounded common finance rather than counterfeit world taxation or donor-whim constitutions.
- `832-oversight-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-witness-municipal-scrutiny-metro-audit-national-watchdogs-and-treaty-review.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should each scope ordinarily be scrutinized and corrected once it has real public authority?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one watchdog fetish: **micro-local bodies should rely mainly on open meetings, visible records, rotation, and cheap escalation rather than a miniature oversight state; municipalities should be the first level with a full public oversight kit of chamber scrutiny, independent external audit, complaint or ombuds routes, disclosure, and ordinary legality review; metropolitan and regional governments should own equally real audit and redress lanes rather than borrowing them permanently from a host city or ministry; national government should carry the fullest fourth-branch and court-backed oversight constitution; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound but still face visible member scrutiny, independent audit and evaluation, complaint and ethics channels, and published review cycles rather than secretariat self-marking**.

## food-governance

- `505-land-and-housing-by-scope-secure-tenure-municipal-place-making-metro-housing-markets-regional-landscapes-and-national-fairness.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat housing and land as a scale-matched constitutional domain: micro-local institutions steward shared places and surface need; municipalities handle parcels, streets, permits, and neighborhood upgrading; metropolitan bodies govern the real housing market and fair-share growth; regions protect landscapes, basins, and food land; nations guarantee rights, anti-segregation floors, and housing finance; and global institutions supply rights baselines, data, and crisis support rather than pretending to zone the planet.
- `513-food-systems-by-scope-local-access-regional-foodsheds-national-guarantees-and-fair-global-rules.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern food as a rights-bearing system rather than as a commodity silo: neighborhoods and local institutions surface hunger, diet, and access failures; municipalities shape markets, meals, land-use interfaces, waste reduction, and emergency food continuity; regional institutions govern foodsheds, logistics, processing, watershed and disease spillovers, and some fisheries or farming systems; nations guarantee the right to food, farm and labour law, food safety, social protection, strategic reserves, and coherent agrifood policy; and global institutions should coordinate standards, evidence, and crisis solidarity without subordinating food security to opaque trade power.
- `532-water-and-sanitation-by-scope-local-access-municipal-stormwater-basin-governance-national-rights-and-transboundary-cooperation.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat water as both a daily service and a shared ecological system: households, farms, and neighbourhood institutions can surface failures, conserve, and steward local sources but should not be left to absorb utility risk alone; municipalities should guarantee drinking water, sanitation, stormwater, leak response, and ordinary public-space water safety; basin or regional authorities should govern aquifers, rivers, drought, flood, wastewater spillovers, and allocation conflicts at the hydrological scale that actually exists; nations should guarantee the human rights to water and sanitation, finance universal access, regulate quality, affordability, extraction, and public-health protection, and prevent postcode hydrology from becoming lower citizenship; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in transboundary waters, comparable standards, early warning, and upstream-downstream cooperation rather than pretending one local utility can solve a shared basin.
- `536-oceans-coasts-and-fisheries-by-scope-local-stewardship-regional-seascapes-national-jurisdiction-and-global-high-seas-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the ocean as both a lived coast and a shared planetary system: coastal communities, ports, and small-scale fishers should hold real stewardship, monitoring, harbour, and livelihood voice close to place; regional or sea-basin institutions should govern migratory stocks, coastal erosion, estuaries, shipping spillovers, marine protected networks, and cumulative seascape impacts at the ecological scale that actually exists; coastal states should own marine spatial planning within their jurisdiction, fisheries law, labour and safety enforcement, port-state control, public marine science, and fair distribution of marine rents; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in the law of the sea, high-seas biodiversity, shipping pollution, seabed restraint, and shared fish-stock rules rather than letting coastal nationalism or flag-of-convenience arbitrage hollow out the ocean commons.

## gender-governance

- `523-gender-equality-and-bodily-autonomy-by-scope-local-safety-municipal-access-regional-referral-national-equality-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat gender equality and bodily autonomy as constitutional infrastructure rather than a private lifestyle dispute: households, schools, clinics, workplaces, and neighborhoods should surface risk and practice non-domination; municipalities should make prevention, safe mobility, childcare links, crisis help, and sexual-and-reproductive-health access actually reachable; regional bodies should coordinate specialist referral, shelters, forensic capacity, and hospital catchments that outrun one city; nations should guarantee equal legal status, anti-violence law, labour and care equality, and bodily-autonomy rights; and the global layer should keep a narrow but serious role in rights norms, cross-border accountability, evidence, and anti-backsliding solidarity.

## health-governance

- `506-health-by-scope-primary-care-regional-capacity-national-risk-pools-and-global-alerts.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat health as a layered public good: neighborhoods and municipalities support prevention and the social conditions of health; community-facing systems deliver primary care as close as feasible to daily life; regions run hospital, laboratory, ambulance, and surge platforms; nations guarantee universal coverage, workforce strategy, medicines policy, and equitable finance; and global institutions coordinate alerts, standards, and outbreak response without pretending to administer ordinary care everywhere.
- `523-gender-equality-and-bodily-autonomy-by-scope-local-safety-municipal-access-regional-referral-national-equality-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat gender equality and bodily autonomy as constitutional infrastructure rather than a private lifestyle dispute: households, schools, clinics, workplaces, and neighborhoods should surface risk and practice non-domination; municipalities should make prevention, safe mobility, childcare links, crisis help, and sexual-and-reproductive-health access actually reachable; regional bodies should coordinate specialist referral, shelters, forensic capacity, and hospital catchments that outrun one city; nations should guarantee equal legal status, anti-violence law, labour and care equality, and bodily-autonomy rights; and the global layer should keep a narrow but serious role in rights norms, cross-border accountability, evidence, and anti-backsliding solidarity.
- `527-end-of-life-and-death-care-by-scope-local-accompaniment-municipal-death-administration-regional-palliative-capacity-national-rights-and-global-pain-relief.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat dying, death care, and bereavement as governed phases of civic life rather than hospital leftovers: households, friends, and community institutions can accompany the dying and mourn the dead but should not be left alone to navigate pain, paperwork, and impossible choices; municipalities should make death registration, burial or cremation access, bereavement navigation, and culturally plural local practice legible and reachable; regional bodies should coordinate palliative-care networks, hospice and specialist capacity, coronial or medical-examiner functions, and referral pathways that outrun one city; nations should guarantee consent law, advance directives, surrogate decision rules, equitable palliative access, medicine availability, and vital-registration baselines; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in essential pain-relief access, rights norms, and knowledge exchange rather than pretending to legislate every intimate end-of-life question for the whole world.
- `528-freedom-of-conscience-and-religion-by-scope-local-coexistence-municipal-neutrality-regional-fairness-national-rights-and-global-protection.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat freedom of conscience, religion, and belief as plural civic infrastructure rather than a privilege of dominant traditions or a project of militant homogenization: households, associations, and communities should be free to form, change, practice, criticize, or refuse belief without coercion; municipalities should keep ordinary civic life neutral and usable through fair permits, equal access, cemetery and calendar accommodation, and non-discriminatory service interfaces; regional bodies should coordinate fairness across hospitals, prisons, schools, and other institutions whose catchments outrun one city; nations should guarantee legal personality, anti-discrimination law, equal citizenship, education and service neutrality, hate-crime and incitement baselines, and rights-safe rules for conscientious objection; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in rights norms, persecution response, and anti-incitement principles rather than trying to govern theology from afar.
- `529-indigenous-peoples-and-self-government-by-scope-community-authority-municipal-consent-regional-co-governance-national-plurinational-constitutionalism-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat Indigenous peoples as peoples and governing authorities rather than as cultural stakeholders inside someone else’s map: Indigenous communities and nations should retain authority over identity, membership, internal institutions, culture, and many matters of everyday law according to their own traditions and evolving consent; municipalities should share space, services, permits, and practical coexistence through negotiated respect rather than zoning override or paternal inclusion; regional bodies should co-govern watersheds, forests, transport, health, education, and other shared systems whose real catchments outrun one settlement; nations should constitutionally recognize Indigenous peoples, lands, treaties, restitution claims, fiscal powers, and free, prior and informed consent rather than forcing all authority through a unitary citizenship mold; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in rights norms, anti-extractive scrutiny, and cross-border Indigenous solidarity rather than pretending a world body can govern each people’s internal life.
- `530-language-and-linguistic-pluralism-by-scope-local-use-municipal-service-access-regional-language-ecologies-national-rights-and-global-support.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat language as civic infrastructure rather than as a badge of dominance or a private burden of translation: households, associations, and communities should be free to use, transmit, revive, and change their languages in everyday life; municipalities should make frontline services, signage, interpretation, naming, and basic public interfaces actually usable in the languages that structure local life; regional bodies should sustain language ecologies that outrun one town through media, teacher pipelines, courts, hospitals, universities, and cultural institutions; nations should define official-language settlements, guarantee minority and Indigenous language rights, fund multilingual education and translation capacity, and prevent language-based exclusion from citizenship, justice, or public work; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in language-rights norms, endangered-language support, digital standards, and shared linguistic infrastructure rather than trying to impose one administrative tongue on humanity.
- `532-water-and-sanitation-by-scope-local-access-municipal-stormwater-basin-governance-national-rights-and-transboundary-cooperation.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat water as both a daily service and a shared ecological system: households, farms, and neighbourhood institutions can surface failures, conserve, and steward local sources but should not be left to absorb utility risk alone; municipalities should guarantee drinking water, sanitation, stormwater, leak response, and ordinary public-space water safety; basin or regional authorities should govern aquifers, rivers, drought, flood, wastewater spillovers, and allocation conflicts at the hydrological scale that actually exists; nations should guarantee the human rights to water and sanitation, finance universal access, regulate quality, affordability, extraction, and public-health protection, and prevent postcode hydrology from becoming lower citizenship; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in transboundary waters, comparable standards, early warning, and upstream-downstream cooperation rather than pretending one local utility can solve a shared basin.
- `534-extractive-resources-by-scope-local-consent-regional-cumulative-impacts-national-public-rents-and-global-just-transition-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat subsoil wealth as a temporary public endowment rather than a permanent license for frontier sacrifice: affected communities and Indigenous peoples should hold real consent, monitoring, grievance, and benefit-sharing power close to the site; regional bodies should govern cumulative impacts on water, housing, health, roads, labour markets, tailings, and emergency corridors across the wider extraction zone; nations should own licensing architecture, contract disclosure, beneficial-ownership rules, royalties, sovereign wealth or stabilization policy, closure liability, anti-corruption enforcement, and diversification strategy; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in transparency standards, trade and due-diligence rules, conflict prevention, and just-transition principles rather than letting a scramble for critical minerals recreate colonial extraction under green branding.
- `557-detention-corrections-and-reentry-by-scope-local-contact-and-release-links-regional-custody-probation-national-rights-floors-and-no-government-by-warehousing.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **detention, corrections, and reentry** as a **strictly limited, rights-bound, reintegration-oriented part of justice** rather than as a hidden warehousing system: keep local roles focused on family contact, service continuity, diversion support, and release preparation rather than long-term cage sovereignty; use metropolitan or regional institutions for most remand custody, prisons, probation, parole, health continuity, and professionally managed inspectionable facilities; reserve national government for penal law, decarceration incentives, independent monitoring, and non-negotiable humane-treatment floors; and never allow **jails, prisons, or release systems to become opaque human storage insulated from courts, health systems, and society**.
- `562-civil-registration-vital-statistics-and-legal-identity-institutions-by-scope-local-event-capture-municipal-service-access-regional-backstops-national-trust-frameworks-and-no-government-by-documentary-erasure.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat civil registration, vital statistics, and legal identity as a linked but non-collapsed public infrastructure: keep event notification and ordinary registration close to births, deaths, marriages, divorces, and residence reality; make municipal or county-level offices, health interfaces, and mobile service routes the ordinary access layer; use regional or provincial backstops where geography, federalism, or sparse settlement require them; reserve national government for the legal-status framework, secure and privacy-bounded identity trust architecture, interoperability rules, consular extension, and systemwide statistics coordination; and never let personhood, kinship, or access to basic rights depend on surviving a hostile documentary maze.
- `572-standards-metrology-testing-accreditation-and-conformity-assessment-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-inspection-regional-labs-national-quality-infrastructure-and-no-government-by-unverified-measurement.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **standards, metrology, testing, accreditation, and conformity assessment** as a **constitutional measurement layer**: keep user witnessing, complaint, and local inspection close to communities and municipalities; pool expensive laboratories, calibration, and specialist technical capacity at regional scale where fragmentation would waste money or degrade competence; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the quality-infrastructure core — measurement units, national metrology, accreditation, legal metrology, standard-setting mandates, and recognition rules — and use continental and global layers for equivalence, interoperability, and trade discipline rather than for a fantasy of one world product ministry.
- `602-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-steward-cells-municipal-general-government-metropolitan-systems-democracy-regional-territorial-platforms-national-guarantor-states-continental-compacts-and-global-treaty-narrow-waists.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should give each scope a distinct governing vocation and a minimum complete kit: micro-local units as visible stewardship and signal cells; municipalities as the first full general-purpose governments of ordinary life; metropolitan governments as democratically legitimated operators of shared urban systems; regional, provincial, or state governments as territorial-platform governments for landscapes, hospitals, grids, universities, and shared rule; nations as guarantor states for equal citizenship, redistribution, macro-stability, and constitutional settlement; continental bodies as bounded compact governments for cross-border mobility, markets, and infrastructures; and global institutions as treaty-bound narrow waists for peace, commons, alerting, and standards rather than as a fake world domestic state.
- `726-default-function-routing-table-for-ideal-governments-everyday-place-shared-systems-guarantor-duties-compact-unions-and-treaty-narrow-waists.md` — The archive should keep one compact **default routing table** for common public functions: route witness, stewardship, and micro-commons to micro-local units; ordinary daily place government to municipalities; shared urban systems to metropolitan government or narrow utilities; basin, hospital, university, corridor, and ecological platforms to regions or typed functional authorities; equal citizenship, redistribution, macro-stability, and constitutional settlement to nations; bounded cross-border markets, mobility, and corridors to compact unions; and genuinely planetary peace, alerting, interoperability, and commons baselines to treaty-bound global narrow waists — while forcing mixed fields to declare lead scope, support scopes, fiscal logic, and upgrade tests instead of choosing a level from scratch every time.
- `744-tombstone-stewardship-and-health-check-packets-for-retired-government-bodies-scopes-and-shells-named-maintainer-link-probes-stewardship-transfer-and-no-orphaned-memory-surfaces.md` — Once the archive can create a tombstone (`741`), reroute it when successors drift (`742`), and correct it when the dead-page story is materially wrong (`743`), it should also keep one compact **tombstone stewardship and health-check packet**: one light maintenance object naming who keeps the dead page, redirects, alias map, record-home links, archive-home links, and legacy-question lane reachable and accurate over time, how failures are classified and escalated, and how stewardship itself is rehomed when institutions change again, so memorial objects do not decay into **orphaned memory surfaces**.
- `766-lobbying-transparency-and-revolving-door-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-registers-meeting-logs-gift-rules-cooling-off-advice-lanes-and-no-policy-by-invisible-influence.md` — Ideal governments should treat lobbying and influence as **a legitimate democratic input that becomes dangerous when it is invisible, unequal, or privately entangled with officeholding**: they should disclose who seeks to influence whom, on whose behalf, about what, through which channels, under which gift and hospitality rules, and with what pre- and post-public-employment constraints, so policy is not quietly written by invisible influence.
- `792-stress-test-and-drill-cards-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-essential-service-continuity-command-legibility-fiscal-buffers-rights-discipline-rescoping-signals-and-no-paper-constitution-by-calm-weather.md` — The archive should pair its ideal-government answer key and benchmark cards with one compact **stress-test and drill-card format** for each scope — essential-service continuity, command and escalation legibility, reserve and surge discipline, intergovernmental handoff integrity, legality and rights restraint under pressure, public communication, and recovery or handback triggers — so governments are judged not only by their steady-state design but by whether they remain honest under flood, blackout, outbreak, fiscal shock, cyber disruption, or constitutional strain.

## housing-governance

- `415-phase-labeled-public-automation-lifecycles.md` — Public automated systems should never drift through hidden stages. They should carry an explicit **lifecycle phase label** — such as pre-deployment, beta or pilot, production, paused, or retired — with different evidence, visibility, and approval requirements at each phase.
- `435-role-specific-ai-literacy-runbooks-and-rehearsal-drills.md` — AI literacy in public institutions should be role-specific and operational: staff need current runbooks, escalation paths, and rehearsal drills for the failures they are expected to catch, not just generic awareness that AI exists.
- `451-canonical-disclosure-heads-frozen-citation-tips-and-stale-copy-warnings.md` — If consequential public-AI disclosures exist in multiple versions, mirrors, excerpts, or derived summaries, the institution should publish one canonical current head, preserve citation-frozen heads for historical reference, and visibly warn when a stale or branched copy is no longer authority-bearing.
- `476-cross-surface-capability-parity-declared-limits-and-continuity-handoffs.md` — Consequential public-AI systems should preserve the same core capability classes across their major surfaces—or declare exact limits and continuity-preserving handoffs—so web, mobile, kiosk, PDF, API, assisted-digital, and operator projections do not quietly tell different governance stories.
- `485-effective-state-resolution-correction-graphs-and-no-authority-by-feed-order.md` — When consequential public-AI notices, status updates, corrections, withdrawals, and superseding records accumulate over time, the institution should compute and publish one deterministic effective current state from explicit lineage links, and should treat forks or unresolved ambiguity as incidents rather than letting feed order, CMS recency, or whichever copy looks newest decide authority.
- `488-scope-typed-governance-stack-block-municipality-metro-region-nation-and-planet.md` — An ideal government is not one uniform sovereign repeated at different sizes, but a scope-typed stack in which each level is optimized for the kinds of problems it can actually see, coordinate, and correct: block for stewardship, municipality for place, metro for networks, region for landscapes and major systems, nation for rights and redistribution, and global bodies for commons, peace, and shared baselines.
- `491-adaptive-boundaries-functional-geographies-prior-consultation-and-no-frozen-maps.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat boundaries as governed instruments rather than sacred relics: review them when functional geographies drift, consult affected communities before changing them, prefer overlap or joint authority where clean redrawing is impossible, and never let inherited lines quietly dictate today’s housing markets, watersheds, or service systems.
- `501-public-sphere-by-scope-community-media-public-service-independence-ownership-transparency-and-civic-information-commons.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat a plural information order as constitutional infrastructure: community and local media should have legal room and sustainable support, public service media should be editorially independent and publicly accountable rather than government-controlled, media ownership and state support should be transparent, and digital distribution rules should protect access to diverse public-interest information instead of quietly collapsing the public sphere into either oligarchy or platform dependence.
- `505-land-and-housing-by-scope-secure-tenure-municipal-place-making-metro-housing-markets-regional-landscapes-and-national-fairness.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat housing and land as a scale-matched constitutional domain: micro-local institutions steward shared places and surface need; municipalities handle parcels, streets, permits, and neighborhood upgrading; metropolitan bodies govern the real housing market and fair-share growth; regions protect landscapes, basins, and food land; nations guarantee rights, anti-segregation floors, and housing finance; and global institutions supply rights baselines, data, and crisis support rather than pretending to zone the planet.
- `511-climate-by-scope-local-adaptation-metropolitan-form-regional-resilience-national-transition-and-global-carbon-limits.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern climate by splitting powers according to where they actually bite: neighborhoods and local institutions surface risk and build resilience in daily life; municipalities shape buildings, land use, local mobility, heat, flooding, and service continuity; metropolitan and regional bodies govern commutes, airsheds, catchments, and strategic adaptation systems that cross municipal borders; nations set binding transition rules, carbon and industrial policy, just-transition finance, and national adaptation plans; and the global layer sets temperature and reporting baselines, climate-finance duties, and narrow coordination rules rather than pretending to run every place-based transition itself.
- `512-biodiversity-by-scope-local-stewardship-municipal-ecology-regional-landscapes-national-law-and-global-commons.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern biodiversity as a whole-territory constitutional question rather than as a parks afterthought: local and Indigenous or community institutions steward place-based knowledge and care; municipalities integrate biodiversity into everyday land-use, water, and public-space decisions; regional and basin scales govern corridors, landscapes, seascapes, and cumulative extraction pressures; nations set conservation law, restoration duties, species protection, finance, and national biodiversity strategies; and global institutions define common goals, migratory-species and commons rules, and accountability frameworks without pretending to micromanage each ecosystem from abroad.
- `513-food-systems-by-scope-local-access-regional-foodsheds-national-guarantees-and-fair-global-rules.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern food as a rights-bearing system rather than as a commodity silo: neighborhoods and local institutions surface hunger, diet, and access failures; municipalities shape markets, meals, land-use interfaces, waste reduction, and emergency food continuity; regional institutions govern foodsheds, logistics, processing, watershed and disease spillovers, and some fisheries or farming systems; nations guarantee the right to food, farm and labour law, food safety, social protection, strategic reserves, and coherent agrifood policy; and global institutions should coordinate standards, evidence, and crisis solidarity without subordinating food security to opaque trade power.
- `517-public-revenue-and-taxation-by-scope-local-own-source-taxes-metropolitan-base-sharing-national-progressivity-and-global-anti-evasion-floors.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should fund government by keeping visible own-source revenues tied to place and service at the local level; using metropolitan and regional revenue-sharing where commuters, land values, logistics, or extractive burdens cross borders; reserving progressive income taxation, broad consumption taxes, social insurance contributions, debt management, and equalizing transfers to the nation; and using the global layer for narrow anti-evasion, information-exchange, and minimum-tax rules that stop mobile capital from hollowing out democratic finance.
- `521-disability-and-accessibility-by-scope-local-barrier-removal-municipal-universal-design-regional-supports-national-rights-and-global-standards.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern disability through rights, accessibility, and support rather than pity, segregation, or medical gatekeeping: neighborhoods and local institutions should surface barriers and support ordinary inclusion; municipalities should make streets, transit, schools, public information, housing interfaces, and service counters accessible by design; regional bodies should coordinate specialized mobility, communication, personal-assistance, safeguarding, and referral systems that cross local borders; nations should guarantee equal legal capacity, anti-discrimination law, benefits, assistive-technology coverage, and enforceable accessibility obligations; and the global layer should maintain disability-rights norms, interoperable standards, and humanitarian inclusion rather than leaving disability to domestic discretion.
- `522-culture-and-heritage-by-scope-local-belonging-municipal-institutions-regional-ecologies-national-pluralism-and-global-commons.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern culture as a rights-bearing public good rather than propaganda, luxury, or folklore storage: neighborhoods and communities keep living practices, memory, and language-use close to life; municipalities should sustain libraries, museums, venues, festivals, archives, arts education links, public space, and fair local cultural access; regional bodies should support linguistic and heritage ecologies, touring circuits, landscape-scale memory, and cultural production systems that outrun one city; nations should guarantee cultural rights, artistic freedom, public support, restitution and heritage law, and plural national institutions without imposing one official culture; and the global layer should protect humanity’s shared heritage, support cultural diversity, and coordinate anti-trafficking and cooperation without becoming a world ministry of taste.
- `523-gender-equality-and-bodily-autonomy-by-scope-local-safety-municipal-access-regional-referral-national-equality-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat gender equality and bodily autonomy as constitutional infrastructure rather than a private lifestyle dispute: households, schools, clinics, workplaces, and neighborhoods should surface risk and practice non-domination; municipalities should make prevention, safe mobility, childcare links, crisis help, and sexual-and-reproductive-health access actually reachable; regional bodies should coordinate specialist referral, shelters, forensic capacity, and hospital catchments that outrun one city; nations should guarantee equal legal status, anti-violence law, labour and care equality, and bodily-autonomy rights; and the global layer should keep a narrow but serious role in rights norms, cross-border accountability, evidence, and anti-backsliding solidarity.
- `524-children-and-youth-by-scope-local-belonging-municipal-voice-regional-opportunity-national-guarantees-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern childhood and youth as a full citizenship-building architecture rather than a sentimental side issue: families, peers, schools, and neighborhood institutions should make belonging and safety real; municipalities should build child-friendly streets, services, and participation channels; regional bodies should coordinate transport, child protection pathways, specialist services, and opportunity systems that outrun one town; nations should guarantee rights, income floors, education and care baselines, and fair transitions to adulthood; and the global layer should protect child-rights norms, anti-exploitation baselines, and cross-border solidarity without becoming a world parent.
- `526-older-persons-and-ageing-by-scope-local-belonging-municipal-age-friendly-design-regional-supports-national-income-security-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat longer life as a civic achievement rather than a private burden: households, kin, and neighbors can offer reciprocity but should not become the hidden welfare state; municipalities should make everyday life age-friendly through reachable services, barrier removal, social infrastructure, and usable local navigation; regional bodies should coordinate specialist geriatrics, abuse response, mobility and housing transitions, and care pathways that outrun one municipality; nations should guarantee income security, anti-age-discrimination law, retirement and work rules, legal-capacity safeguards, and equal access to core supports; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in human-rights norms, anti-ageism, portable learning, and knowledge exchange rather than pretending there can be a world pension ministry.
- `529-indigenous-peoples-and-self-government-by-scope-community-authority-municipal-consent-regional-co-governance-national-plurinational-constitutionalism-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat Indigenous peoples as peoples and governing authorities rather than as cultural stakeholders inside someone else’s map: Indigenous communities and nations should retain authority over identity, membership, internal institutions, culture, and many matters of everyday law according to their own traditions and evolving consent; municipalities should share space, services, permits, and practical coexistence through negotiated respect rather than zoning override or paternal inclusion; regional bodies should co-govern watersheds, forests, transport, health, education, and other shared systems whose real catchments outrun one settlement; nations should constitutionally recognize Indigenous peoples, lands, treaties, restitution claims, fiscal powers, and free, prior and informed consent rather than forcing all authority through a unitary citizenship mold; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in rights norms, anti-extractive scrutiny, and cross-border Indigenous solidarity rather than pretending a world body can govern each people’s internal life.
- `531-rural-remote-and-peripheral-places-by-scope-local-agency-intermunicipal-service-backbones-regional-catchments-national-territorial-solidarity-and-global-learning.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat rural, remote, island, mountain, and other peripheral places not as residual territories waiting to shrink quietly but as legitimate political communities with distinct distance, sparsity, ecology, and production constraints: local institutions should set priorities, steward place knowledge, and surface service failure early; intermunicipal compacts should provide the shared administrative and service backbones that low-density places often need to remain capable; regional bodies should govern labour markets, referral systems, transport, watershed and land-use spillovers, and adaptation systems that cross many small jurisdictions; nations should guarantee territorial solidarity through fiscal equalization, connectivity, service floors, fair resource revenue, and public employment and investment rules that do not punish distance; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in fair trade, climate and connectivity support, and shared learning rather than imposing metro-centric metrics on every place.
- `534-extractive-resources-by-scope-local-consent-regional-cumulative-impacts-national-public-rents-and-global-just-transition-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat subsoil wealth as a temporary public endowment rather than a permanent license for frontier sacrifice: affected communities and Indigenous peoples should hold real consent, monitoring, grievance, and benefit-sharing power close to the site; regional bodies should govern cumulative impacts on water, housing, health, roads, labour markets, tailings, and emergency corridors across the wider extraction zone; nations should own licensing architecture, contract disclosure, beneficial-ownership rules, royalties, sovereign wealth or stabilization policy, closure liability, anti-corruption enforcement, and diversification strategy; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in transparency standards, trade and due-diligence rules, conflict prevention, and just-transition principles rather than letting a scramble for critical minerals recreate colonial extraction under green branding.
- `535-transport-and-logistics-by-scope-local-streets-metro-transit-regional-corridors-national-networks-and-global-interoperability.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat transport as a lived access system and a strategic circulation system at the same time: neighbourhoods and households can surface danger, exclusion, curb conflict, and last-mile need but should not be left to self-organize mobility; municipalities should govern streets, sidewalks, cycling, bus priority, curb use, traffic calming, road safety, and visible access to daily destinations; metropolitan authorities should own mass transit integration, fare systems, freight interfaces, and land-use coordination across one labour and housing market; regional institutions should govern intercity corridors, ports, inland waterways, airports, and resilience across the geography through which people and goods actually move; nations should own network finance, safety baselines, decarbonization strategy, essential-service guarantees, and major modal balance; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in aviation and maritime rules, cross-border interoperability, and fair technical standards rather than pretending one city can regulate the skies or the sea lanes.
- `536-oceans-coasts-and-fisheries-by-scope-local-stewardship-regional-seascapes-national-jurisdiction-and-global-high-seas-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the ocean as both a lived coast and a shared planetary system: coastal communities, ports, and small-scale fishers should hold real stewardship, monitoring, harbour, and livelihood voice close to place; regional or sea-basin institutions should govern migratory stocks, coastal erosion, estuaries, shipping spillovers, marine protected networks, and cumulative seascape impacts at the ecological scale that actually exists; coastal states should own marine spatial planning within their jurisdiction, fisheries law, labour and safety enforcement, port-state control, public marine science, and fair distribution of marine rents; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in the law of the sea, high-seas biodiversity, shipping pollution, seabed restraint, and shared fish-stock rules rather than letting coastal nationalism or flag-of-convenience arbitrage hollow out the ocean commons.
- `537-outer-space-and-orbital-commons-by-scope-local-hosting-regional-spaceports-national-authorization-and-global-sustainability-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat outer space as a global commons of use rather than a frontier of silent enclosure: local communities should hold real say over launch sites, tracking stations, astronomy impacts, land use, emergency planning, and public benefit where space infrastructure touches the ground; regional institutions should coordinate spaceport corridors, environmental review, disaster interfaces, and research ecosystems where activities spill across jurisdictions; nations should authorize and continuously supervise national activities in space, register objects, govern liability, spectrum and orbital use discipline, public research, procurement, and security constraints, and prevent private launch markets from becoming lightly regulated sovereignty proxies; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in non-appropriation, peaceful use, registration, debris mitigation, conjunction information-sharing, and long-term sustainability rather than letting orbit become an unmanaged congestion market.
- `539-banking-credit-and-financial-stability-by-scope-local-relationship-lending-regional-development-finance-national-prudential-oversight-and-global-backstops.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat banking and credit as a public-risk-bearing capability rather than a private allocation game: households, workers, firms, and local institutions can surface credit exclusion, predatory products, and place-specific capital starvation but should not be left to self-insure against systemic finance; municipalities can convene local credit intelligence, public banking interfaces, and anti-exclusion measures but should not act as miniature prudential sovereigns; regional institutions should govern development banks, housing and infrastructure finance platforms, and sectoral transition tools where production systems and catchments are wider than one city; nations should own licensing, prudential supervision, macroprudential policy, deposit insurance, resolution, lender-of-last-resort functions, and the constitutional line between utility banking and speculative risk; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in supervisory standards, cross-border resolution cooperation, correspondent-finance continuity, and anti-arbitrage floors rather than pretending world technocracy can substitute for domestic democratic control.
- `540-trade-customs-and-border-procedures-by-scope-local-port-interfaces-regional-gateways-national-trade-policy-and-global-rules.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat trade governance as both a rules system and a border operations system: households, workers, firms, and local communities can surface chokepoints, corruption, hazardous shipments, and the lived burden of gateways but should not each define external trade law; municipalities should govern port-adjacent land use, truck conflict, inspection-site interfaces, market transparency, and emergency support for traders without becoming fragmented customs sovereignties; regional institutions should coordinate corridors, dry ports, airports, inland terminals, and gateway ecosystems across the geography through which goods actually move; nations should own tariff schedules, trade agreements, customs law, single-window architecture, revenue collection, sanctions and strategic controls, and the constitutional balance between openness, security, labour, and environment; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in trade rules, customs standards, interoperable data models, and facilitation norms rather than pretending that one city or one ministry can govern cross-border exchange alone.
- `541-government-by-scope-micro-local-stewardship-municipal-professionalism-metropolitan-democracy-regional-capacity-national-guarantees-and-global-narrow-waists.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not ask every scale to be the same kind of government: micro-local units should be light stewardship and signal institutions, municipalities should be general-purpose democratic governments with professional administration, metropolitan governments should be directly legitimated coordinators of shared urban systems, regional governments should carry landscape and major-service capacity, national governments should guarantee equal citizenship, redistribution, macro-stability, and constitutional rights, and global bodies should remain narrow, treaty-bound organs for peace, commons, alerting, and interoperability rather than aspiring to one undifferentiated world state.
- `543-special-purpose-authorities-and-arms-length-bodies-narrow-remits-hard-charters-open-books-and-sunset-review.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should use special-purpose authorities, public corporations, and arm’s-length bodies only where a bounded cross-municipal or regional function — such as transit, utilities, watershed management, market regulation, or other impartial technical tasks — genuinely requires them; give them narrow remits, hard-law charters, published financing, public accountability, and periodic review; and never let them become shadow governments, patronage shelters, or constitutional escape hatches.
- `546-public-enterprises-and-state-owned-enterprises-explicit-rationales-separated-roles-hard-budget-constraints-and-open-books.md` — An ideal polity may own and operate enterprises where public ownership is genuinely justified — for natural monopolies, essential network infrastructure, strategic resilience, mission-critical finance, or other clearly stated public purposes — but it should publish why it owns them, separate ownership from regulation and policy-making, state public-service obligations explicitly, compensate them transparently, impose hard budget constraints, keep boards and books professional and visible, and review the portfolio often enough that public enterprise does not become a hiding place for patronage, off-balance-sheet debt, or anti-competitive favoritism.
- `557-detention-corrections-and-reentry-by-scope-local-contact-and-release-links-regional-custody-probation-national-rights-floors-and-no-government-by-warehousing.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **detention, corrections, and reentry** as a **strictly limited, rights-bound, reintegration-oriented part of justice** rather than as a hidden warehousing system: keep local roles focused on family contact, service continuity, diversion support, and release preparation rather than long-term cage sovereignty; use metropolitan or regional institutions for most remand custody, prisons, probation, parole, health continuity, and professionally managed inspectionable facilities; reserve national government for penal law, decarceration incentives, independent monitoring, and non-negotiable humane-treatment floors; and never allow **jails, prisons, or release systems to become opaque human storage insulated from courts, health systems, and society**.
- `558-public-defense-and-legal-aid-by-scope-local-entry-municipal-navigation-regional-provider-capacity-national-independence-and-no-justice-by-unaffordable-counsel.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **public defense and legal aid** as a **core constitutional capacity for equal justice** rather than as charity or courthouse aftercare: keep first contact, rights information, and navigable entry close to daily life; use metropolitan, county, provincial, state, or other regional institutions for most ordinary defender offices, provider networks, and specialist capacity; reserve national government for the right itself, independent legal-aid authority design, fair funding, quality floors, and territorial equalization; and never allow **freedom, family life, housing, status, or civil survival to depend on whether a person can privately purchase counsel on short notice**.
- `568-land-administration-and-cadastre-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-parcel-service-regional-coordination-national-tenure-rules-and-no-government-by-documentary-dispossession.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat land administration as a scale-matched constitutional infrastructure rather than a clerical property office: community and customary institutions should help witness real people-to-land relationships, municipal or county offices should be the ordinary parcel-service front door, metropolitan or regional layers should pool cadastre and geospatial coordination where fragmentation would break the map, national or constitutional-state law should own tenure forms, identifiers, interoperability, and register integrity, and continental or global bodies should provide standards and support rather than pretending a world cadastre exists.
- `569-addresses-place-names-and-administrative-geography-by-scope-community-legibility-municipal-address-authority-regional-coherence-national-reference-frames-and-no-government-by-phantom-location.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat addresses, place names, and administrative geography as constitutional infrastructure rather than clerical leftovers: communities should help surface real local names and hard-to-map places, municipalities or counties should usually be the ordinary authority for street naming and address maintenance, metropolitan or regional layers should keep cross-boundary location systems coherent where daily life and service networks spill across borders, national institutions should own the authoritative reference frame for identifiers, geocoding, administrative units, and interoperability, and continental or global bodies should provide standards rather than pretending there can be one sovereign address book for the world.
- `580-asymmetric-decentralization-special-status-territories-and-no-one-size-fits-all-stack.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **asymmetry** as a disciplined constitutional tool rather than as a taboo or a patronage trick: keep a clear default stack for ordinary places, but allow differentiated powers, institutions, and finance for metropolitan areas, capital districts, islands, remote regions, indigenous or plurinational territories, and other genuinely exceptional geographies when functional scale, capacity, history, identity, remoteness, or constitutional settlement justify it; pair that flexibility with equal-rights floors, transparent criteria, published finance rules, review clocks, and routes into and out of special status; and reject both one-size-fits-all map worship and ad hoc dealmaking that turns territorial difference into permanent favoritism.
- `591-concurrent-competences-lead-lane-typing-paramountcy-defaults-and-no-government-by-overlap-fog.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **concurrent or shared competences as a typed constitutional settlement rather than as a vague admission that “everyone is involved”**: where more than one level must legitimately act in the same field, the law should split the field into visible lanes — such as rights floors, finance, planning, delivery, inspection, data, and remedy — assign a lead level for each lane, state what happens on conflict, preserve lower-tier headroom where that is the point of the arrangement, and publish a coordination rulebook so citizens are not forced to infer government structure from a pile of overlapping claims.
- `602-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-steward-cells-municipal-general-government-metropolitan-systems-democracy-regional-territorial-platforms-national-guarantor-states-continental-compacts-and-global-treaty-narrow-waists.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should give each scope a distinct governing vocation and a minimum complete kit: micro-local units as visible stewardship and signal cells; municipalities as the first full general-purpose governments of ordinary life; metropolitan governments as democratically legitimated operators of shared urban systems; regional, provincial, or state governments as territorial-platform governments for landscapes, hospitals, grids, universities, and shared rule; nations as guarantor states for equal citizenship, redistribution, macro-stability, and constitutional settlement; continental bodies as bounded compact governments for cross-border mobility, markets, and infrastructures; and global institutions as treaty-bound narrow waists for peace, commons, alerting, and standards rather than as a fake world domestic state.
- `606-when-co-operation-becomes-government-thresholds-for-constitutionalizing-shared-territorial-power-and-no-metropolitan-rule-by-consortium.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should let municipalities and regions co-operate freely for shared capacity and service delivery, but once a joint body starts making repeated cross-boundary trade-offs across several sectors, raising compulsory money, issuing debt, binding land use or major infrastructure choices, or functioning as the real political center of a territory, it should be constitutionalized as honest metropolitan or regional government rather than left as a consortium, summit, or quango stack.
- `614-knowledge-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-observatories-territorial-indicators-basemaps-scenario-capacity-and-no-government-by-fragmented-spreadsheets.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **knowledge home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, and participatory one: a territorially coherent observatory, common basemaps and boundary files, a published indicator set at the scale actually being governed, lawful data-sharing and evaluation capacity, open methods and release discipline, and visible routes from evidence into plans and budgets — so the shared tier stops governing through municipal spreadsheet fragments, ministry leftovers, vendor dashboards, and dueling numbers.
- `616-planning-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-territorial-plans-plan-hierarchies-conformity-and-no-government-by-vision-deck.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **planning home** as well as democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, and service ones: a territorial planning authority with a real public plan, a declared hierarchy with municipal and state plans, visible conformity or compatibility rules, infrastructure-and-land-use coupling, amendment and review clocks, and no territorial government by advisory strategy deck.
- `640-post-launch-scope-observability-variance-ledgers-rollback-lanes-and-no-stack-change-by-runtime-custom.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat materially stack-altering reforms as **actively observable after go-live**, with one linked post-launch variance ledger, short review clocks, named correction and rollback lanes, and explicit closure criteria, so the lived operation of budgets, staff, systems, supervision, and remedies cannot quietly become a different constitutional settlement by runtime custom.
- `643-scope-reactivation-certificates-dormancy-fresh-clearance-and-no-constitutional-necromancy.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require one public **scope-reactivation certificate** before any materially stack-bearing authority, exception lane, shared body, or supervisory hold returns from retirement, dormancy, suspension, or expiry: old text, old systems, old habits, and old crisis muscle memory should not make public power live again without fresh legality, current rights checks, updated scope classification, and a visible register change.
- `646-scope-severability-fallback-baselines-partial-invalidity-and-no-whole-stack-collapse-by-contamination.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat a materially stack-altering package as **severable where honest**, preserving only those parts that can still be described as lawful, coherent, and democratically ownable on their own terms, with one visible fallback baseline and one public explanation of what survives, what is stayed, and what must be rebuilt, so a single defect neither launders the whole package nor needlessly detonates the lawful remainder.
- `664-obligation-and-funding-formulas-by-problem-class-capacity-to-pay-equalization-polluter-pays-beneficiary-pays-risk-solidarity-and-no-one-formula-federalism.md` — Ideal multilevel and global governance should match each shared obligation to the right **apportionment rule** — capacity to pay for common institutions, equalization for rights floors, polluter-pays for harm control, beneficiary-pays for optional service gains, risk-based pooling for insurance and emergency reserves, and differentiated duties where histories and capabilities materially differ — so solidarity is explicit and reviewable rather than smuggled through arbitrary shares, annual bargaining, or one formula pasted across every tier and problem.
- `665-external-commitment-landing-paths-signature-ratification-transposition-direct-effect-operational-owners-and-no-treaty-by-press-release.md` — Cross-border and global commitments should not stop at signature or ratification: an honest polity should show the full **landing path** from external commitment to domestic legal effect, operational owners, budgeting, reporting, review, and subnational fit, so treaty participation does not masquerade as implementation.
- `667-differentiated-commitments-in-shared-regimes-reservations-opt-outs-derogations-transition-periods-territorial-application-review-clocks-and-no-uniformity-by-false-claim.md` — Shared regimes should maintain a **typed differentiation register** that distinguishes reservations, interpretive declarations, opt-outs, temporary derogations, transition periods, territorial applications, and enhanced-cooperation rings — with legal basis, scope, duration, review clock, and accession or withdrawal path — so a regime can use lawful variable geometry without lying that every member carries the same obligation.
- `668-shared-regime-change-ladders-review-conferences-amendments-protocols-annex-updates-tacit-acceptance-version-registers-and-no-regime-rewrite-by-secretariat-faq.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed change ladder** that distinguishes political guidance, interpretive guidance, implementing decisions, annex or technical updates, formal amendments, optional protocols, and refounding texts — each with its own adoption body, consent rule, objection or non-acceptance lane, entry-into-force logic, version register, and domestic landing path — so the regime can evolve without either paralysis or quiet constitutional rewrite by circular, dashboard, or FAQ.
- `689-shared-regime-territorial-presence-constitutions-headquarters-regional-offices-country-offices-liaison-posts-service-hubs-host-instruments-review-clocks-and-no-regime-by-landlord-permission.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed territorial-presence constitution** that separates headquarters, regional offices, country offices, liaison posts, service hubs, hosted outposts, and temporary mission footprints — with a named host instrument, mandate fit, reporting line, support package, review clock, and closure path for each — so institutional presence stays functional and reviewable instead of hardening into landlord permission, prestige geography, or office sprawl by habit.
- `702-unbundling-mixed-function-claims-before-scope-choice-lane-split-first-packet-second-rivalry-third-and-no-one-tier-answer-to-a-composite-field.md` — Before the archive decides which scope should ideally govern a field, it should first test whether the field is really a **composite bundle of different lanes with different scale logics**; if so, it should split the field into lane-sized claims, build packets for those lanes, and run rivalry only on the pieces that remain genuinely contested, rather than forcing one total jurisdictional answer onto a mixed-function question.
- `706-repair-packets-for-recurrently-failing-government-fields-after-action-conversion-root-cause-ownership-funding-lanes-closure-proof-and-no-government-by-permanent-recovery-mode.md` — Lane-typed government fields that repeatedly re-enter **degraded, emergency, or recovery modes** should publish a typed **repair packet** that converts after-action learning into owned structural change — clearly separating quick corrective action from deeper fiscal, staffing, capital, digital, legal, or boundary repair — with recurrence triggers, service-floor protection, closure proof, and escalation when “temporary recovery” is becoming the field’s real constitution.
- `725-ideal-governance-stack-from-block-to-planet-territorial-tiers-functional-authorities-compact-unions-and-no-empty-tier-fetish.md` — An ideal governance stack from block to planet is not a neat ladder of identical states but a mixed constitutional order: micro-local bodies for witness and stewardship, municipalities for ordinary place government, metropolitan and regional tiers where urban systems or territorial platforms are real, nations for equal citizenship and solidarity, continental compacts for recurrent cross-border problems, global institutions for peace, alerting, commons, and interoperability, and bounded functional authorities in between whenever a watershed, corridor, grid, basin, port, or referral network plainly outruns ordinary administrative geography.
- `746-historical-register-rehousing-and-cross-catalog-migration-packets-for-absorbed-tombstones-register-home-change-stable-entry-identifiers-alias-continuity-and-no-disappearance-by-replatforming.md` — Once the archive can absorb standalone tombstones into grouped historical registers (`745`), it should also keep one compact **historical-register rehousing and cross-catalog migration packet**: one bounded proof object for moving absorbed dead-object entries from one register, catalogue, directory, or memorial platform to another without losing individually addressable identity, alias coverage, correction lineage, or the plain statement that the authority is dead, so the polity does not mistake platform migration for permission to break historical lookup.
- `759-independent-institutions-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-referee-functions-bounded-mandates-appointment-discipline-budget-protection-review-lanes-and-no-fourth-branch-sprawl.md` — Ideal governments should create independent institutions only where a function genuinely requires **credible distance from day-to-day political command**—as referee, guardian, watchdog, or integrity backstop—and should then give that institution a bounded mandate, protected but not blank-cheque resources, multi-actor appointment and removal discipline, transparent duties, reviewable powers, and a constitutional place that prevents both ministerial capture and fourth-branch sprawl.
- `777-execution-of-administrative-and-judicial-decisions-against-public-authorities-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-compliance-clocks-budget-home-escalation-and-no-judgment-by-non-execution.md` — Ideal governments should treat **execution of administrative and judicial decisions against public authorities** as part of the rule-of-law core rather than as post-judgment housekeeping: when a ministry, municipality, agency, regulator, police body, prison authority, benefits office, land registrar, or treasury loses, the system should have clear compliance clocks, named responsible officials, budget and payment homes, interest and penalty rules, supervisory escalation, and user-visible follow-up so the state cannot turn delay, fragmentation, or lack-of-funds claims into a second victory after losing on the merits.
- `779-interim-relief-and-urgent-public-law-protection-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-stays-preservation-orders-irreparable-harm-clocks-and-no-rights-by-fait-accompli.md` — Ideal governments should treat **interim relief as ordinary rule-of-law protection against irreversible harm and fait accompli rather than as exotic emergency indulgence**: public-law systems should offer typed stays, preservation orders, temporary mandatory measures, rapid hearing lanes, and in especially irreversible domains default suspensive effect, so review remains capable of protecting rights before demolition, removal, disclosure, eviction, exclusion, or other irreversible state action has already done its work.
- `794-sequenced-upgrade-paths-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-first-honest-steps-bridge-arrangements-cutover-gates-and-no-full-stack-redesign-by-manifesto.md` — When a real polity is far from the archive’s ideal scope stack, reform should move through a sequenced upgrade path: **make the current arrangement honest first, repair the minimum complete kit and fiscal congruence next, constitutionalise any bridge institutions that are already exercising real power, transfer functions only with continuity proof, and attempt deeper territorial or constitutional redesign only after the operating spine is real**.
- `808-calibration-packs-moderation-loops-and-precedent-banks-for-scope-assessments-score-anchors-difficult-case-conferences-documented-departures-and-no-benchmark-by-reviewer-mood.md` — The archive should pair its benchmark, mission, evidence-register, and mission-integrity notes with one compact **review-calibration grammar**: **every serious scope assessment should keep a small calibration pack with lane-specific score anchors, worked examples, threshold splits, precedent notes, moderation checkpoints, and documented departures, so that different review teams can reach comparably disciplined judgments without collapsing everything into one blended score or one charismatic reviewer’s mood**.
- `812-institutional-form-choice-ladders-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-thin-connectors-shared-service-backbones-bounded-authorities-general-purpose-tiers-and-no-new-tier-by-spillover-alone.md` — When the archive has already established that a cross-boundary problem is real, it should choose institutional form through one compact **choice ladder**: use a **thin connector** when alignment and information-sharing are enough; a **shared-service backbone** when capacity pooling is the real need; a **bounded functional authority** when one system needs continuous cross-boundary operations or asset stewardship; and a **general-purpose elected tier** only when recurring distributive, land-use, borrowing, coercive, or multi-sector balancing powers make thinner forms constitutionally dishonest.
- `820-decision-rule-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-ordinary-majorities-qualified-majorities-unanimity-reserves-deadlock-breakers-and-no-heavy-power-by-procedural-veto.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, **what information chain belongs to it**, and **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what decision-rule chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should seek consensus for advisory work and require visible member ratification for anything binding, shared-service backbones should use ordinary-majority operating rules with reserved supermajority or member-ratification gates for portfolio, burden, and liability shifts, bounded functional authorities should use public standing orders with ordinary-majority defaults plus qualified-majority or double-key gates for tariffs, debt, land, remit, and boundary changes, and general-purpose territorial tiers should govern by ordinary democratic majorities with narrowly cabined supermajority reserves and explicit deadlock routes rather than by permanent veto geography.
- `835-emergency-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-readiness-municipal-incident-command-regional-civil-protection-national-derogation-discipline-and-treaty-alerting.md` — The archive should answer the question **what emergency and exception grammar should ordinarily fit each scope?** with scale-matched escalation rather than one panic state fetish: **micro-local bodies should default to readiness, warning, mutual aid, and witness rather than emergency sovereignty; municipalities should be the first ordinary home of incident command, continuity, sheltering, and short-horizon emergency operations under ordinary law; metropolitan governments should carry shared-system disruption management where the functional city is one risk field; regional or provincial governments may honestly house civil-protection, wildfire, flood, logistics, and mutual-aid platforms where those risks are territorially real; national government should hold the thickest declaration, derogation, reserve, and exceptional coordination powers under legislative renewal, judicial review, and strict handback discipline; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound, specializing in alerting, coordination, standards, pooled assistance, and tightly authorized collective action rather than becoming ambient permanent emergency government**.
- `839-amendment-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-bylaws-municipal-charters-metro-double-keys-federal-entrenchment-and-treaty-ratification.md` — The archive should usually prefer different amendment grammars by scale: **micro-local rules should change publicly and cheaply; municipalities through charter or organic-law procedures with real community consultation for boundary or status change; metropolitan and regional governments through double-key amendment where shared systems or constituent bargains are real; national constitutions through heightened but repairable procedures with territorial participation for settlement-class changes; and continental or global regimes through explicit treaty amendment and ratification rather than executive side deals, secretariat drift, or permanent provisionalism**.
- `840-preemption-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-headroom-metro-primacy-federal-bargain-locks-national-floors-and-treaty-bounded-override.md` — The archive should usually prefer different override grammars by scale: **micro-local bodies should remain subject to municipal law and charter while keeping visible voice lanes; municipalities should enjoy broad headroom above common floors unless preemption is explicit, proportionate, and reviewable; metropolitan governments should hold named primacy inside real shared urban systems; regional governments should keep constitutionally real autonomy except where the federal bargain openly assigns paramount power elsewhere; national governments may impose rights floors, solidarity rules, and interoperability baselines but should face a higher burden before using ceilings or field occupation; and continental or global bodies should override only through explicit treaty commitments rather than ambient upper-tier drift**.

## human-rights-governance

- `521-disability-and-accessibility-by-scope-local-barrier-removal-municipal-universal-design-regional-supports-national-rights-and-global-standards.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern disability through rights, accessibility, and support rather than pity, segregation, or medical gatekeeping: neighborhoods and local institutions should surface barriers and support ordinary inclusion; municipalities should make streets, transit, schools, public information, housing interfaces, and service counters accessible by design; regional bodies should coordinate specialized mobility, communication, personal-assistance, safeguarding, and referral systems that cross local borders; nations should guarantee equal legal capacity, anti-discrimination law, benefits, assistive-technology coverage, and enforceable accessibility obligations; and the global layer should maintain disability-rights norms, interoperable standards, and humanitarian inclusion rather than leaving disability to domestic discretion.
- `528-freedom-of-conscience-and-religion-by-scope-local-coexistence-municipal-neutrality-regional-fairness-national-rights-and-global-protection.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat freedom of conscience, religion, and belief as plural civic infrastructure rather than a privilege of dominant traditions or a project of militant homogenization: households, associations, and communities should be free to form, change, practice, criticize, or refuse belief without coercion; municipalities should keep ordinary civic life neutral and usable through fair permits, equal access, cemetery and calendar accommodation, and non-discriminatory service interfaces; regional bodies should coordinate fairness across hospitals, prisons, schools, and other institutions whose catchments outrun one city; nations should guarantee legal personality, anti-discrimination law, equal citizenship, education and service neutrality, hate-crime and incitement baselines, and rights-safe rules for conscientious objection; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in rights norms, persecution response, and anti-incitement principles rather than trying to govern theology from afar.
