- `526-older-persons-and-ageing-by-scope-local-belonging-municipal-age-friendly-design-regional-supports-national-income-security-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat longer life as a civic achievement rather than a private burden: households, kin, and neighbors can offer reciprocity but should not become the hidden welfare state; municipalities should make everyday life age-friendly through reachable services, barrier removal, social infrastructure, and usable local navigation; regional bodies should coordinate specialist geriatrics, abuse response, mobility and housing transitions, and care pathways that outrun one municipality; nations should guarantee income security, anti-age-discrimination law, retirement and work rules, legal-capacity safeguards, and equal access to core supports; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in human-rights norms, anti-ageism, portable learning, and knowledge exchange rather than pretending there can be a world pension ministry.
- `531-rural-remote-and-peripheral-places-by-scope-local-agency-intermunicipal-service-backbones-regional-catchments-national-territorial-solidarity-and-global-learning.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat rural, remote, island, mountain, and other peripheral places not as residual territories waiting to shrink quietly but as legitimate political communities with distinct distance, sparsity, ecology, and production constraints: local institutions should set priorities, steward place knowledge, and surface service failure early; intermunicipal compacts should provide the shared administrative and service backbones that low-density places often need to remain capable; regional bodies should govern labour markets, referral systems, transport, watershed and land-use spillovers, and adaptation systems that cross many small jurisdictions; nations should guarantee territorial solidarity through fiscal equalization, connectivity, service floors, fair resource revenue, and public employment and investment rules that do not punish distance; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in fair trade, climate and connectivity support, and shared learning rather than imposing metro-centric metrics on every place.
- `533-waste-and-materials-by-scope-local-collection-regional-recovery-national-producer-responsibility-and-global-hazard-controls.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat waste as failed material design rather than municipal fate: households, shops, workplaces, and neighbourhood institutions can sort, return, repair, and surface illegal dumping but should not carry the whole burden of circularity; municipalities should guarantee clean streets, universal collection, public-space litter control, reuse access points, and safe everyday interfaces with residents; regional bodies should run the real recovery geography of transfer stations, composting, remanufacturing, recycling markets, and final disposal capacity that usually outruns one city; nations should shift cost and design responsibility upstream through product standards, extended producer responsibility, deposit and take-back systems, right-to-repair rules, public procurement, data reporting, and labour protections; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in hazardous-waste controls, waste-trade rules, and common floor disciplines that prevent one country’s circular rhetoric from becoming another country’s toxic burden.
- `534-extractive-resources-by-scope-local-consent-regional-cumulative-impacts-national-public-rents-and-global-just-transition-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat subsoil wealth as a temporary public endowment rather than a permanent license for frontier sacrifice: affected communities and Indigenous peoples should hold real consent, monitoring, grievance, and benefit-sharing power close to the site; regional bodies should govern cumulative impacts on water, housing, health, roads, labour markets, tailings, and emergency corridors across the wider extraction zone; nations should own licensing architecture, contract disclosure, beneficial-ownership rules, royalties, sovereign wealth or stabilization policy, closure liability, anti-corruption enforcement, and diversification strategy; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in transparency standards, trade and due-diligence rules, conflict prevention, and just-transition principles rather than letting a scramble for critical minerals recreate colonial extraction under green branding.
- `535-transport-and-logistics-by-scope-local-streets-metro-transit-regional-corridors-national-networks-and-global-interoperability.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat transport as a lived access system and a strategic circulation system at the same time: neighbourhoods and households can surface danger, exclusion, curb conflict, and last-mile need but should not be left to self-organize mobility; municipalities should govern streets, sidewalks, cycling, bus priority, curb use, traffic calming, road safety, and visible access to daily destinations; metropolitan authorities should own mass transit integration, fare systems, freight interfaces, and land-use coordination across one labour and housing market; regional institutions should govern intercity corridors, ports, inland waterways, airports, and resilience across the geography through which people and goods actually move; nations should own network finance, safety baselines, decarbonization strategy, essential-service guarantees, and major modal balance; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in aviation and maritime rules, cross-border interoperability, and fair technical standards rather than pretending one city can regulate the skies or the sea lanes.
- `536-oceans-coasts-and-fisheries-by-scope-local-stewardship-regional-seascapes-national-jurisdiction-and-global-high-seas-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the ocean as both a lived coast and a shared planetary system: coastal communities, ports, and small-scale fishers should hold real stewardship, monitoring, harbour, and livelihood voice close to place; regional or sea-basin institutions should govern migratory stocks, coastal erosion, estuaries, shipping spillovers, marine protected networks, and cumulative seascape impacts at the ecological scale that actually exists; coastal states should own marine spatial planning within their jurisdiction, fisheries law, labour and safety enforcement, port-state control, public marine science, and fair distribution of marine rents; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in the law of the sea, high-seas biodiversity, shipping pollution, seabed restraint, and shared fish-stock rules rather than letting coastal nationalism or flag-of-convenience arbitrage hollow out the ocean commons.
- `539-banking-credit-and-financial-stability-by-scope-local-relationship-lending-regional-development-finance-national-prudential-oversight-and-global-backstops.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat banking and credit as a public-risk-bearing capability rather than a private allocation game: households, workers, firms, and local institutions can surface credit exclusion, predatory products, and place-specific capital starvation but should not be left to self-insure against systemic finance; municipalities can convene local credit intelligence, public banking interfaces, and anti-exclusion measures but should not act as miniature prudential sovereigns; regional institutions should govern development banks, housing and infrastructure finance platforms, and sectoral transition tools where production systems and catchments are wider than one city; nations should own licensing, prudential supervision, macroprudential policy, deposit insurance, resolution, lender-of-last-resort functions, and the constitutional line between utility banking and speculative risk; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in supervisory standards, cross-border resolution cooperation, correspondent-finance continuity, and anti-arbitrage floors rather than pretending world technocracy can substitute for domestic democratic control.
- `540-trade-customs-and-border-procedures-by-scope-local-port-interfaces-regional-gateways-national-trade-policy-and-global-rules.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat trade governance as both a rules system and a border operations system: households, workers, firms, and local communities can surface chokepoints, corruption, hazardous shipments, and the lived burden of gateways but should not each define external trade law; municipalities should govern port-adjacent land use, truck conflict, inspection-site interfaces, market transparency, and emergency support for traders without becoming fragmented customs sovereignties; regional institutions should coordinate corridors, dry ports, airports, inland terminals, and gateway ecosystems across the geography through which goods actually move; nations should own tariff schedules, trade agreements, customs law, single-window architecture, revenue collection, sanctions and strategic controls, and the constitutional balance between openness, security, labour, and environment; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in trade rules, customs standards, interoperable data models, and facilitation norms rather than pretending that one city or one ministry can govern cross-border exchange alone.
- `545-regulators-inspections-and-enforcement-role-clarity-risk-based-proportionality-due-process-and-no-government-by-shakedown.md` — An ideal polity should treat regulators and inspectorates as bounded public-law institutions whose job is to reduce real harm, preserve fair conditions, and keep essential systems trustworthy; give them clear missions, enough independence to resist improper influence, enough accountability to remain public servants, risk-based and proportionate enforcement tools, visible appeal routes, and budgets not addicted to penalties; and never let licensing, inspection, or fines become a substitute tax system, a patronage machine, or a theatre of arbitrary power.
- `549-civil-service-and-public-workforce-merit-neutrality-capability-fair-pay-and-no-government-by-patronage.md` — An ideal government should build a professional public workforce that is mostly recruited and promoted on merit, protected against undue political interference yet accountable for lawful performance, paid and trained well enough to attract and retain capability, open to worker voice and fair discipline, and clearly separated from the small political layer that is entitled to choose direction but not to colonize the state.
- `572-standards-metrology-testing-accreditation-and-conformity-assessment-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-inspection-regional-labs-national-quality-infrastructure-and-no-government-by-unverified-measurement.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **standards, metrology, testing, accreditation, and conformity assessment** as a **constitutional measurement layer**: keep user witnessing, complaint, and local inspection close to communities and municipalities; pool expensive laboratories, calibration, and specialist technical capacity at regional scale where fragmentation would waste money or degrade competence; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the quality-infrastructure core — measurement units, national metrology, accreditation, legal metrology, standard-setting mandates, and recognition rules — and use continental and global layers for equivalence, interoperability, and trade discipline rather than for a fantasy of one world product ministry.
- `598-conditions-of-office-for-local-elected-representatives-free-mandate-fair-compensation-lawful-removal-and-no-self-government-by-attrition.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the **conditions of office of local elected representatives as a constitutional operating condition**: councillors, mayors, and other directly elected local officeholders should be able to exercise a free mandate with adequate compensation, time compatibility, facilities, training, narrow law-set incompatibilities, and strong protection against arbitrary suspension, trustee substitution, or intimidation — so local self-government is not hollowed out by unpaid exhaustion, factional starvation, or discretionary removal.
- `620-workforce-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-employer-status-recruitment-training-labor-relations-and-no-government-by-borrowed-payroll.md` — Real metropolitan or regional government needs its own **employer constitution**: a named employer of record, merit-based staffing and progression, explicit pay and labor-relations rules, bounded reliance on secondment, visible workforce metrics, and a transition path out of borrowed payroll.
- `643-scope-reactivation-certificates-dormancy-fresh-clearance-and-no-constitutional-necromancy.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require one public **scope-reactivation certificate** before any materially stack-bearing authority, exception lane, shared body, or supervisory hold returns from retirement, dormancy, suspension, or expiry: old text, old systems, old habits, and old crisis muscle memory should not make public power live again without fresh legality, current rights checks, updated scope classification, and a visible register change.
- `666-compliance-ladders-for-shared-regimes-reporting-peer-review-inspection-dispute-settlement-remediation-suspension-and-no-treaty-by-voluntary-vibes.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **graduated compliance ladder** matched to the problem class — from reporting and peer review through technical verification, corrective action, dispute settlement, and where necessary suspension or other consequence — so co-operation does not depend on vibes and enforcement does not jump straight from silence to punishment.
- `670-shared-regime-exit-ladders-denunciation-withdrawal-suspension-expulsion-savings-clauses-wind-down-duties-and-no-perpetual-membership-fiction.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed exit ladder** that distinguishes withdrawal or denunciation, temporary suspension, lawful expulsion where the constituting text allows it, module exit, territorial rollback, and post-exit survival clauses — with trigger, notice lane, decision body, effective date, pending-case rule, continuing liabilities, record duties, and re-entry path — so participation can end without pretending either that membership is irrevocable or that exit erases prior obligations.
- `698-shared-regime-implementing-partner-and-pass-through-constitutions-due-diligence-workplans-cash-transfer-assurance-suspension-closeout-and-no-mission-by-subaward-fog.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed implementing-partner-and-pass-through constitution** that separates partner eligibility, due diligence, engagement risk, workplans, funding modality, milestone and expenditure reporting, assurance activity, corrective action, suspension, and closeout — so delivery through external partners does not dissolve into subaward fog, unreviewed dependency, or mission by pass-through habit.
- `766-lobbying-transparency-and-revolving-door-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-registers-meeting-logs-gift-rules-cooling-off-advice-lanes-and-no-policy-by-invisible-influence.md` — Ideal governments should treat lobbying and influence as **a legitimate democratic input that becomes dangerous when it is invisible, unequal, or privately entangled with officeholding**: they should disclose who seeks to influence whom, on whose behalf, about what, through which channels, under which gift and hospitality rules, and with what pre- and post-public-employment constraints, so policy is not quietly written by invisible influence.

## land-administration-governance

- `568-land-administration-and-cadastre-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-parcel-service-regional-coordination-national-tenure-rules-and-no-government-by-documentary-dispossession.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat land administration as a scale-matched constitutional infrastructure rather than a clerical property office: community and customary institutions should help witness real people-to-land relationships, municipal or county offices should be the ordinary parcel-service front door, metropolitan or regional layers should pool cadastre and geospatial coordination where fragmentation would break the map, national or constitutional-state law should own tenure forms, identifiers, interoperability, and register integrity, and continental or global bodies should provide standards and support rather than pretending a world cadastre exists.

## language-governance

- `522-culture-and-heritage-by-scope-local-belonging-municipal-institutions-regional-ecologies-national-pluralism-and-global-commons.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern culture as a rights-bearing public good rather than propaganda, luxury, or folklore storage: neighborhoods and communities keep living practices, memory, and language-use close to life; municipalities should sustain libraries, museums, venues, festivals, archives, arts education links, public space, and fair local cultural access; regional bodies should support linguistic and heritage ecologies, touring circuits, landscape-scale memory, and cultural production systems that outrun one city; nations should guarantee cultural rights, artistic freedom, public support, restitution and heritage law, and plural national institutions without imposing one official culture; and the global layer should protect humanity’s shared heritage, support cultural diversity, and coordinate anti-trafficking and cooperation without becoming a world ministry of taste.
- `530-language-and-linguistic-pluralism-by-scope-local-use-municipal-service-access-regional-language-ecologies-national-rights-and-global-support.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat language as civic infrastructure rather than as a badge of dominance or a private burden of translation: households, associations, and communities should be free to use, transmit, revive, and change their languages in everyday life; municipalities should make frontline services, signage, interpretation, naming, and basic public interfaces actually usable in the languages that structure local life; regional bodies should sustain language ecologies that outrun one town through media, teacher pipelines, courts, hospitals, universities, and cultural institutions; nations should define official-language settlements, guarantee minority and Indigenous language rights, fund multilingual education and translation capacity, and prevent language-based exclusion from citizenship, justice, or public work; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in language-rights norms, endangered-language support, digital standards, and shared linguistic infrastructure rather than trying to impose one administrative tongue on humanity.
- `550-judiciaries-by-scope-neighborhood-entry-regional-trial-courts-national-apex-review-and-global-rights-backstops.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should keep justice entry and informal problem-sensing close to daily life, organize ordinary first-instance and specialized courts at the smallest catchment that can sustain independence and competence, reserve apex review, constitutional interpretation, judicial-appointment safeguards, and equality before the law to the national level, and treat supranational or global courts as narrow rights and treaty backstops rather than as substitutes for a functioning domestic judiciary.
- `577-public-service-delivery-one-stop-shops-and-assisted-digital-access-by-scope-community-navigation-municipal-front-counters-regional-shared-service-centers-national-service-standards-and-no-government-by-channel-maze.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **public service delivery** as the **constitutional execution layer** of government: keep trusted navigation, assisted digital help, and ordinary human contact close to communities and municipalities; pool shared service centers, call centers, translation, queue balancing, and specialist case support above fragmented local jurisdictions where scale adds competence; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for service standards, life-event integration, channel parity, common status semantics, and the core rails that let services feel like one government rather than a pile of agencies; and keep continental or global roles narrow enough to support cross-border information, procedures, assistance, and evidence exchange without becoming a world ministry of customer service.
- `626-public-communication-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-canonical-channels-corrections-inclusive-reach-and-no-government-by-press-release-federation.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it should acquire an explicit **public-communication home**: a named official communications function distinct from party or campaign messaging; one canonical set of channels for notices, updates, warnings, and explanations; correction and version trails; multilingual and accessible publication discipline; clear docking between general information and legal notice; and archival capture of official statements so the territory does not govern through host-city press offices, operator fragments, screenshots, and rumor.
- `662-global-institution-toolkit-by-problem-class-assemblies-secretariats-scientific-panels-registries-inspection-compliance-funds-and-no-world-state-monoculture.md` — The ideal global layer should be built from a **small toolkit of treaty-bound institutional forms matched to problem class** rather than from one fantasy model of world government: use assemblies and councils for norm-setting, secretariats and focal-point networks for continuous coordination, scientific panels for shared factual baselines, registries and reporting systems for comparability, inspection or verification where cheating matters, dispute and compliance lanes where interpretation recurs, and dedicated funds where solidarity is required — while refusing both fake world-state domesticity and empty declarations with no operating spine.
- `679-shared-regime-interpretation-constitutions-authentic-texts-ordinary-meaning-context-object-purpose-authoritative-interpretations-guidance-and-no-binding-law-by-helpdesk.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed interpretation constitution** that separates authentic text, ordinary interpretation, subsequent agreement or practice, member-adopted authoritative interpretation, adjudicative clarification, and secretariat guidance — so legal meaning does not drift between frozen literalism and quiet rulemaking by FAQ.
- `680-shared-regime-jurisprudence-memory-and-consistency-holdings-digests-departure-reasons-advisory-opinions-and-no-random-walk-governance.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed jurisprudence-memory constitution** that separates binding force, persuasive reasoning, holdings, summaries, digests, advisory opinions, and departure rules — so interpretation develops through visible continuity rather than random walk, citation theater, or stealth precedent.
- `682-shared-regime-language-and-text-discipline-official-working-languages-translation-interpretation-authentic-texts-terminology-control-and-no-law-by-convenience-copy.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed language-and-text constitution** that separates official languages, working languages, authentic texts, translated texts, interpretation duties, terminology control, and convenience copies — so legal meaning does not drift toward whichever language, rendering, or summary is easiest for insiders to circulate.
- `724-guidance-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-rule-hierarchy-interpretive-notes-precedent-digests-reliance-boundaries-and-no-binding-law-by-helpdesk.md` — Once the archive has amendment, service, case, decision, notice, effect, and review packets for a field, it should also publish one narrow **guidance packet** saying which texts actually bind, which guidance products merely explain, who may issue or clear each class, what reliance they support, how they are versioned and superseded, when repeated answers must be promoted into public guidance, and when a claimed interpretation must be routed out to amendment, decision, or review — so the field does not decay into binding law by helpdesk, secret manual, or stale portal copy.
- `782-administrative-guidance-circulars-and-soft-law-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-publicity-legal-status-clarity-consultable-updates-and-no-hidden-law-by-guidance.md` — Ideal governments should treat **administrative guidance, circulars, manuals, FAQs, enforcement policies, and advisory opinions as a compliance-support and interpretation layer rather than as a covert lawmaking lane**: guidance should be typed by legal status, publicly accessible when it matters to outsiders, consistent with enacted law, versioned and dated, consultable when it materially reshapes burdens, and reviewable when it hardens into de facto law.
- `787-language-interpretation-plain-language-and-accessible-format-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-comprehension-duty-translation-thresholds-and-no-rights-by-unreadable-procedure.md` — Ideal governments should require that **administrative procedure be intelligible to the people it governs**: binding notices, adverse cases, required actions, deadlines, hearing opportunities, and remedies should be communicated in **plain language, understandable form, and accessible modes**, with **interpretation, translation, and disability accommodation triggered by stakes and necessity** rather than treated as optional courtesy.

## legislature-governance

- `490-representation-by-scope-neighborhood-voice-metro-election-federal-shared-rule-and-deliberative-complement.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not clone one representation formula at every scale: it should use close, participatory voice where place knowledge is richest, directly elected councils for city and metro systems, population-based representation for common citizenship, territorial shared-rule chambers where constituent units need a federal voice, and representative deliberative mini-publics as a complement for hard cross-cutting questions.
- `503-intelligence-by-scope-no-local-secret-police-judicial-authorization-minimization-and-multi-key-oversight.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should keep intelligence and surveillance narrowly scoped to genuine national-security functions under public law, forbid local secret-police formation and routine law-enforcement drift, require prior independent authorization and minimization for intrusive measures, and place the whole system under layered executive, legislative, judicial, privacy, and redress oversight so secrecy never matures into ungoverned power.
- `504-defense-by-scope-civilian-control-civil-defense-no-subnational-war-machines-and-narrow-waist-collective-security.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should place war-making and armed defense at the national level under democratic civilian control and legislative budget authority, give subnational governments civil-defense and resilience roles without autonomous war machines, keep the military distinct from routine domestic order, and rely on treaty-bound regional alliances and a narrow global collective-security layer for external peace and aggression response rather than romanticizing either total sovereignty or world-state militarism.
- `529-indigenous-peoples-and-self-government-by-scope-community-authority-municipal-consent-regional-co-governance-national-plurinational-constitutionalism-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat Indigenous peoples as peoples and governing authorities rather than as cultural stakeholders inside someone else’s map: Indigenous communities and nations should retain authority over identity, membership, internal institutions, culture, and many matters of everyday law according to their own traditions and evolving consent; municipalities should share space, services, permits, and practical coexistence through negotiated respect rather than zoning override or paternal inclusion; regional bodies should co-govern watersheds, forests, transport, health, education, and other shared systems whose real catchments outrun one settlement; nations should constitutionally recognize Indigenous peoples, lands, treaties, restitution claims, fiscal powers, and free, prior and informed consent rather than forcing all authority through a unitary citizenship mold; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in rights norms, anti-extractive scrutiny, and cross-border Indigenous solidarity rather than pretending a world body can govern each people’s internal life.
- `547-budgeting-treasury-and-public-accounts-credible-ceilings-legislative-authority-one-treasury-and-no-government-by-fund-fog.md` — An ideal polity should turn public money into a lawful cycle of strategy, appropriation, controlled execution, and audited account: set clear fiscal objectives and medium-term ceilings, present one comprehensive budget rather than a maze of side funds, give the legislature real time and analytic capacity to approve totals and appropriations, execute through a unified treasury, chart of accounts, commitment controls, and cash planning, publish in-year reports and year-end financial statements, disclose fiscal risks honestly, and route audit findings back into correction so the state cannot govern through supplementary fog, arrears, or off-budget improvisation.
- `548-legislatures-by-scope-neighborhood-assemblies-municipal-councils-metro-chambers-federal-shared-rule-and-no-government-by-decree.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should fit its legislative institutions to scale: use direct assemblies and recallable delegates for micro-local stewardship, elected municipal and metropolitan councils where visible services and shared systems need contestable public rulemaking, regional and federal chambers where territory and shared rule must be represented, and national parliaments strong enough to legislate, budget, scrutinize, and police delegated law rather than surrendering government to executives, party cartels, or decree.
- `553-supreme-audit-institutions-and-external-public-audit-by-scope-local-books-regional-state-audit-national-independence-and-no-government-by-self-audit.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should keep bookkeeping, internal control, and managerial accountability inside every public body, but place **external audit** in institutions independent of the auditee: make local books and records unavoidable, size municipal and state/provincial external audit to real government tiers and catchments, give the national supreme audit institution constitutional standing, access, budget, and publication rights, require legislatures and executives to follow up publicly, and never let the government audit itself in secret and call that accountability.
- `566-electoral-systems-by-scope-direct-local-voice-municipal-proportionality-metropolitan-legitimacy-regional-balancing-national-pr-and-federal-shared-rule.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not force one electoral formula onto every scale: use direct and low-barrier democracy where the unit is genuinely small and stewardship-heavy, prefer proportional or semi-proportional council elections for municipalities and metropolitan governments that must aggregate durable diversity, fit executive election rules to the actual executive model, reserve territorial second chambers for real shared rule rather than decorative bicameralism, and keep continental and global bodies grounded mainly in treaty delegation plus bounded participatory and parliamentary complements rather than pretending every problem is solved by copying a national ballot upward.
- `571-public-records-archives-and-official-publications-by-scope-community-memory-municipal-record-discipline-regional-repositories-national-gazettes-and-no-government-by-disappearing-state.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **public records, archives, and official publication** as a **constitutional memory layer**: keep firsthand witnessing, local minutes, notice, and records help close to communities and municipalities; pool preservation, repository, and disaster-recovery capacity at regional scale where fragmentation would otherwise erase public memory; reserve national or constitutional-state law for records duties, transfer rules, authentic promulgation, and archival independence; and use continental and global layers for interoperability, documentary-heritage protection, and common access norms rather than for a fantasy of one world archive sovereign.
- `578-open-data-and-public-information-reuse-by-scope-community-scrutiny-municipal-publishing-regional-aggregation-national-standards-and-no-government-by-pdf-fog.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **open data and public-information reuse** as the **constitutional public-reuse layer** of government: keep community scrutiny, correction demand, and context close to the people and places described by the data; require municipalities and frontline bodies to publish routine local information in genuinely reusable ways rather than as decorative PDF dumps; pool regional aggregation, comparison, and cross-boundary publication where fragmented local release would make the public blind to shared systems; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the legal framework on reuse, licensing, metadata, machine-readable publication, privacy and confidentiality boundaries, high-value dataset rules, and catalog standards; and keep continental or global roles narrow enough to support interoperable metadata, cross-border discovery, and common high-value publication patterns without becoming one world data ministry.
- `590-multilevel-impact-packets-subsidiarity-territorial-effects-rural-proofing-and-no-lawmaking-by-placeless-abstraction.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should require any higher-tier law, regulation, spending program, or platform reform that materially affects lower-tier powers, finances, administrative burden, or territorial outcomes to ship with a **published multilevel impact packet** — a compact subsidiarity, proportionality, territorial-effects, implementation, and consultation record — so central action is argued openly rather than smuggled through placeless abstraction.
- `592-local-ordinance-power-bylaws-framework-laws-review-lanes-and-no-self-government-by-administration-only.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should give **general-purpose local governments** a real but bounded **local ordinance / by-law power** within framework law — enough to make binding local rules on genuinely local matters, subject to legality review, rights floors, and explicit upper-tier reservations — so self-government does not collapse into mere administration of other people’s rules.
- `599-local-and-regional-assembly-scrutiny-rights-agenda-power-questions-committee-capacity-and-no-majoritarian-blackout.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the **scrutiny rights of local and regional assemblies as constitutional operating equipment rather than as optional etiquette**: councils and assemblies should control the budgetary and rulemaking core, all members should have enforceable rights to meetings, agendas, questions, information, and proportionate committee work, opposition and minority blocs should be able to scrutinise without begging the executive for oxygen, and executive accountability should be structured so local democracy cannot be reduced to periodic elections plus majority blackout.
- `600-organizational-autonomy-internal-administrative-structures-standing-orders-and-no-self-government-by-template-lock.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **organizational autonomy inside local and regional government as part of self-government itself**: higher-tier law may set democratic floors, rights safeguards, and role boundaries, but local and regional authorities should retain broad discretion to choose their internal administrative structures, committee maps, standing orders, subordinate units, and service-delivery arrangements so they can adapt institutions to local needs instead of governing through template lock from above.
- `601-publicity-of-local-deliberation-open-meetings-agenda-notice-closed-session-limits-and-no-government-by-chamber-obscurity.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **the publicity of local and regional deliberation as a constitutional operating condition rather than as optional etiquette**: plenary meetings and decision-shaping committees should be open by default, agendas and core papers should be published with usable notice, closed sessions should be narrow and reasoned, minutes and vote records should remain durable and searchable, and open meetings should complement rather than substitute for broader participatory methods so self-government does not retreat into chamber obscurity.
- `610-accountability-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-scrutiny-audit-disclosure-complaints-review-and-no-government-by-jurisdictional-gap.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **accountability home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, and administrative one: its own scrutiny forum, named records-and-disclosure duties, internal control and audit proportionate to risk, external audit and integrity jurisdiction, complaint and review routes that ordinary people can actually find, and explicit accountability for operators and contractors so the territory is not really governed in the gaps between municipalities, agencies, and the state.
- `630-rescoping-authority-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-administration-by-law-constitutional-bargains-by-consent-and-no-jurisdictional-rewire-by-executive-deal.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat **moving a function between scopes as a graded constitutional act**: ordinary implementation detail may be adjusted through ordinary law inside fixed competences, sectoral reallocations among existing tiers should travel through public legislation with consultation and impact proof, any move that alters the protected bargain of local or regional self-government should require the higher law and consent route appropriate to that bargain, and no executive compact, grant condition, crisis summit, or managerial workaround should be allowed to rewire who really governs what.
- `660-canonical-government-matrix-by-scope-legislature-executive-civil-service-fiscal-base-review-participation-and-no-full-stack-rewrite-for-every-tier.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should reuse one **canonical scope matrix** rather than reinventing every tier from scratch: micro-local units for witness and stewardship, municipalities for ordinary place government, metropolitan authorities for functional urban systems, regions for major territorial platforms and shared rule, nations for equal citizenship and redistribution, continental bodies for bounded cross-border compacts, and global institutions for treaty-bound peace, commons, alerting, and interoperability — each with a scope-matched decision forum, executive spine, civil-service density, fiscal base, review lane, and participation channel.
- `663-cross-border-integration-ladders-information-sharing-minimum-standards-mutual-recognition-common-enforcement-budget-tools-and-no-union-by-slogan.md` — Ideal continental or plurilateral governance should climb an explicit **integration ladder** — information exchange, benchmarking, minimum standards, mutual recognition, shared operational rails, pooled enforcement, common financing, and only then deeper legislative or fiscal union where truly necessary — so polities can co-govern real spillovers without pretending every problem requires the same depth of union or drifting by slogan into competence creep.
- `671-shared-regime-representation-ladders-credentials-chief-delegates-alternates-observers-speaking-rights-committee-access-and-no-state-voice-by-self-appointment.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed representation ladder** that separates party or member status from delegate credentials, chief delegates from alternates and advisers, participants from observers, and speaking rights from voting rights — with accrediting authority, challenge lane, substitution rules, public roster, and functional-independence protections — so no one can conjure state or member voice by badge, donor access, press credential, or self-appointment.
- `674-shared-regime-records-and-publicity-public-private-sessions-document-registers-meeting-records-vote-records-authentic-texts-corrections-and-no-governance-by-missing-papertrail.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed documentary constitution** that separates session publicity, agenda and paper circulation, official document registers, meeting-record formats, vote records, authentic texts, correction notices, and retention or access rules — so public authority does not vanish into missing minutes, unofficial drafts, or document folklore.
- `676-shared-regime-subsidiary-body-constitutions-committees-working-groups-expert-panels-terms-of-reference-report-back-sunset-and-no-shadow-regime-by-working-party.md` — Shared regimes should create **subsidiary bodies through explicit delegation instruments** that name mandate, composition, officer rules, procedure inheritance, publication and records rules, report-back duty, review or sunset, and non-delegable matters — so committees and working parties do not become permanent shadow constitutions.
- `681-shared-regime-session-constitutions-regular-special-emergency-extraordinary-virtual-hybrid-adjournment-recess-and-no-government-by-permanent-session.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed session constitution in their rules of procedure** that separates regular, special, emergency, resumed, adjourned, recessed, virtual, and hybrid sittings — so convening power, urgency, quorum, agenda compression, and temporary meeting modalities do not quietly become a shadow amendment power.
- `711-oversight-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-audit-inspection-ombuds-parliamentary-scrutiny-follow-up-ledgers-and-no-self-certification-by-the-same-office.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, an evidence packet, a challenge packet, and a participation packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **oversight packet** naming which independent bodies outside the live control plane may inspect which questions, on what triggers and calendars, with what access powers, response duties, and follow-up ledger, so the field is not left certifying itself by the same office that designed, funded, or operated it.
- `712-amendment-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-change-classes-ratification-ladders-version-ledgers-drift-logs-and-no-field-redesign-by-memo.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, an evidence packet, challenge and participation packets, and an oversight packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **amendment packet** naming which changes are merely tuning and which are constitutional, who may propose them, what participation and scrutiny gates apply, what ratification ladder adopts them, when they take effect, and what version ledger plus drift log keeps the field from being redesigned by memo, queue custom, temporary exception, or software default.
- `752-government-formation-and-removal-by-scope-micro-local-recall-municipal-manager-confidence-metro-investiture-parliamentary-default-constructive-no-confidence-fixed-terms-and-no-dual-democratic-command.md` — Ideal governments should choose formation and removal rules that create **one legible confidence chain** at each scope — recallable stewards for micro-local bodies, elected-council plus removable manager or mayoral executive in municipalities, explicit investiture and termination rules for metropolitan or regional governments with real power, parliamentary or assembly-confidence default for most large multi-party states, and fixed-term presidential exceptions only where the system can safely absorb dual mandates without chronic collision.
- `753-upper-chamber-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-territorial-shared-rule-bounded-veto-domains-asymmetric-bargains-suspensive-delay-and-no-duplicate-bicameralism.md` — An upper chamber should exist only when it performs a **real shared-rule, territorial-protection, or bounded revising function** that a single chamber cannot credibly carry; otherwise ideal governments should prefer unicameralism, strong committee review, or at most a weak suspensive chamber over prestigious duplication.
- `757-emergency-powers-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-ordinary-law-first-temporal-limits-legislative-renewal-judicial-review-and-no-shadow-constitution-by-crisis.md` — Ideal governments should treat constitutional emergency powers as a **last-resort continuity instrument rather than an alternative operating system**: ordinary law should carry as much crisis response as possible, exceptional powers should be legally typed, temporary, and reviewable, legislative renewal should be real rather than ceremonial, courts should remain open enough to test necessity and proportionality, and no emergency should be allowed to harden into a shadow constitution.
- `758-delegated-legislation-and-executive-rulemaking-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-framework-statutes-purposes-scope-time-limits-scrutiny-publication-and-no-government-by-decree-laundering.md` — Ideal governments should treat delegated legislation as a **bounded implementation instrument rather than a spare legislature**: primary law should carry the main political choices, delegations should state purposes, subject matter, scope, and when needed time limits, parliaments should retain real scrutiny power, the public should be able to see and challenge what is made in their name, and executive rulemaking should never become a laundering route for major constitutional, fiscal, rights, or territorial change.
- `762-official-opposition-and-legislative-minority-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-recognition-scrutiny-rights-agenda-oxygen-committee-chairs-evidence-capacity-and-no-government-by-majority-blackout.md` — Ideal governments should treat the opposition and legislative minority as **constitutional scrutiny equipment rather than a tolerated inconvenience**: they should guarantee recognition, speaking and questioning rights, proportional committee presence, some agenda oxygen, evidence and staffing capacity, and in key oversight domains opposition-led scrutiny, so democratic government remains accountable between elections and does not collapse into rule by majority blackout.
- `763-caretaker-government-and-pre-election-restraint-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-routine-administration-incoming-government-consultation-major-appointments-freeze-emergency-carve-outs-and-no-mandate-stretch-between-verdict-and-handover.md` — Ideal governments should treat dissolution, hung-parliament bargaining, post-election transition, and imminent change of government as **a distinct continuity-with-restraint mode rather than business as usual**: outgoing governments should continue routine administration and urgent protection of the public, but major policy, appointments, contracts, publicity, and irreversible international or fiscal commitments should pause, narrow, or move only after consultation with the likely successor, so no one stretches an expiring mandate through the handover gap.
- `769-supreme-audit-and-public-accounts-follow-up-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-independence-open-reports-opposition-chaired-hearings-implementation-ledgers-and-no-accountability-by-unread-audit.md` — Ideal governments should treat supreme audit and legislative follow-up as **a standing ex post accountability engine rather than a publication ritual**: an independent external auditor should be able to choose and conduct audits within its lawful mandate, access records, publish findings, and report to the public and legislature, while a public-accounts or equivalent committee should hold hearings, require executive responses, track implementation, and distinguish correction from repetition, so audit does not end as an unread PDF or ceremonial annual hearing.
- `782-administrative-guidance-circulars-and-soft-law-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-publicity-legal-status-clarity-consultable-updates-and-no-hidden-law-by-guidance.md` — Ideal governments should treat **administrative guidance, circulars, manuals, FAQs, enforcement policies, and advisory opinions as a compliance-support and interpretation layer rather than as a covert lawmaking lane**: guidance should be typed by legal status, publicly accessible when it matters to outsiders, consistent with enacted law, versioned and dated, consultable when it materially reshapes burdens, and reviewable when it hardens into de facto law.
- `791-benchmark-cards-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-vocation-fit-kit-floors-fiscal-congruence-review-lanes-tripwires-and-no-admiration-without-scoring.md` — The archive should pair its canonical scope matrix and answer-key notes with one compact **benchmark-card format** for each scope — vocation fit, minimum complete kit, fiscal and capability congruence, spillover or solidarity fit, review and remedy integrity, participation and scrutiny proportionality, and named upgrade or handback tripwires — so real constitutions, reform proposals, and case studies can be compared tersely against the ideal stack without reopening the whole theory.
- `795-public-proof-packs-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-benchmark-publication-stress-summaries-maintenance-ledgers-transition-boards-and-no-constitutional-claim-without-outward-evidence.md` — The archive should pair its answer-key, benchmark, stress-test, maintenance, and upgrade-path notes with one compact **public proof-pack rule** for each scope: **publish the minimum outward evidence that lets residents, auditors, legislatures, journalists, courts, and peer polities verify what the arrangement is, how it scored, what failed under stress, what is due next, and where any transition actually stands**.
- `813-legitimacy-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-delegated-councils-principal-owned-backbones-double-key-authorities-directly-elected-tiers-and-no-heavy-power-by-convenience-composition.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, it should also be able to say **what legitimacy chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should be run by delegated elected principals with no hidden hard powers, shared-service backbones should remain clearly owned by the member governments whose duties they support, bounded functional authorities should carry an elected anchor plus explicit double-key gates for major debt, rule, boundary, or remit changes, and general-purpose territorial tiers should normally rest on directly elected chambers with their own scrutiny and executive responsibility rather than on convenience boards pretending to carry full constitutional weight.
- `816-oversight-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-member-scrutiny-external-audit-ombuds-routes-judicial-review-and-no-heavy-power-by-self-marking.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **who owns it**, **how money moves through it**, and **where its operating spine lives**, it should also be able to say **what oversight chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should remain mainly reviewable through the member governments that delegate into them, shared-service backbones should preserve visible principal-side scrutiny plus independent audit and complaint routes, bounded functional authorities should carry named external audit, maladministration review, legality or regulatory checks, and judicial remedy proportionate to their power, and general-purpose territorial tiers should own a full public oversight constitution rather than marking themselves through internal committees alone.
- `817-participation-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-open-dockets-hearings-user-councils-deliberative-mini-publics-response-ledgers-and-no-heavy-power-by-consultation-theater.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **who owns it**, **how money moves through it**, **where its operating spine lives**, and **where scrutiny and redress live**, it should also be able to say **what participation chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should publish open dockets and simple input windows rather than staging fake popular mandates, shared-service backbones should run structured user and accessibility input without pretending pooled operations are a substitute for elected politics, bounded functional authorities should carry recurring hearings and response duties plus deliberative methods where long-horizon tradeoffs justify them, and general-purpose territorial tiers should own a full participation constitution rather than borrowing legitimacy from consultation theater.
- `820-decision-rule-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-ordinary-majorities-qualified-majorities-unanimity-reserves-deadlock-breakers-and-no-heavy-power-by-procedural-veto.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, **what information chain belongs to it**, and **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what decision-rule chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should seek consensus for advisory work and require visible member ratification for anything binding, shared-service backbones should use ordinary-majority operating rules with reserved supermajority or member-ratification gates for portfolio, burden, and liability shifts, bounded functional authorities should use public standing orders with ordinary-majority defaults plus qualified-majority or double-key gates for tariffs, debt, land, remit, and boundary changes, and general-purpose territorial tiers should govern by ordinary democratic majorities with narrowly cabined supermajority reserves and explicit deadlock routes rather than by permanent veto geography.
- `825-regime-form-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-steward-assemblies-municipal-administration-metropolitan-mandates-regional-parliamentarism-national-confidence-and-global-narrow-waists.md` — The archive should answer the question **what regime form should govern at each scope?** with a scale-matched default set rather than one constitutional idol: assembly-and-stewardship at micro-local scale, elected local democracy plus professional administration in municipalities, directly legitimated metropolitan government for real urban systems, assembly-confidence regional government where a region genuinely carries platform functions, parliamentary or assembly-confidence national government unless a strong case for dual-mandate presidentialism is proved, bounded plurilateral unions built around shared-rule institutions rather than cloned statehood, and globally a narrow-waist charter order rather than a world state.
- `826-mandate-source-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-assembly-voice-council-confidence-metro-public-mandates-regional-investiture-national-confidence-and-treaty-delegation.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should governing authority at each scope get its mandate?** with scale-matched defaults rather than a direct-election fetish: assembly voice and recallable stewardship at micro-local scale, elected councils as the primary democratic source in municipalities, whole-territory public mandates for metropolitan governments that can bind a real urban system, assembly-invested regional government where a region genuinely carries platform functions, parliamentary or assembly-confidence national government as the default source of executive authority, and treaty- or charter-derived delegation with bounded parliamentary and public complements for plurilateral and global bodies.
- `828-mandate-exit-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-recall-municipal-dismissal-confidence-loss-bounded-dissolution-and-treaty-lapse.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should governing mandates end when they fail, expire early, or lose their public basis?** with scope-matched exit defaults rather than one romantic removal myth: simple recall or replacement for tiny steward bodies, council-centered dismissal and tightly bounded mayoral removal at municipal scale, explicit confidence-loss and successor grammar for metropolitan and regional governments with real power, bounded parliamentary exit and dissolution rules for most national governments, and fixed reauthorization, for-cause removal, or treaty-lapse rules for plurilateral and global bodies that must never drift into ambient permanence.
- `829-selection-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-open-local-voice-proportional-councils-metro-wide-elections-federal-shared-rule-and-delegated-global-seats.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should offices and chambers at each scope actually be chosen?** with scope-matched selection defaults rather than one ballot fetish: open assemblies, simple ward contests, recallable delegates, and rotation where the unit is genuinely face-to-face; proportional or semi-proportional municipal councils plus merit administration where everyday city government begins; whole-territory metropolitan elections where metro power is real; regional and national lower chambers chosen by proportional rules strong enough to reflect plural publics, with territorial second chambers only where shared rule is real; and continental or global bodies chosen mainly through treaty delegation, indirect parliamentary composition, and merit-based secretariat appointment rather than fake world-state plebiscites.
- `830-decision-rule-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-majorities-municipal-ordinary-rules-federal-double-keys-and-no-fake-global-unanimity.md` — The archive should answer the question **what internal decision rule should usually govern at each scope once the body is real?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one voting fetish: **micro-local institutions should seek rough consensus but fall back cheaply to ordinary majority; municipalities, metropolitan governments, and most regional and national lower chambers should decide ordinary business by ordinary majority with reserved supermajorities for constitutional, territorial, debt, or rights-sensitive thresholds; shared-rule chambers may justify double keys where constituent units are genuinely co-authors of the settlement; and continental or global bodies should treat consensus as a discipline of accommodation, not a veto constitution, reserving unanimity only for narrow membership-, treaty-, or sovereignty-touching classes**.
- `832-oversight-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-witness-municipal-scrutiny-metro-audit-national-watchdogs-and-treaty-review.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should each scope ordinarily be scrutinized and corrected once it has real public authority?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one watchdog fetish: **micro-local bodies should rely mainly on open meetings, visible records, rotation, and cheap escalation rather than a miniature oversight state; municipalities should be the first level with a full public oversight kit of chamber scrutiny, independent external audit, complaint or ombuds routes, disclosure, and ordinary legality review; metropolitan and regional governments should own equally real audit and redress lanes rather than borrowing them permanently from a host city or ministry; national government should carry the fullest fourth-branch and court-backed oversight constitution; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound but still face visible member scrutiny, independent audit and evaluation, complaint and ethics channels, and published review cycles rather than secretariat self-marking**.
- `834-information-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-ledgers-municipal-record-homes-metro-observatories-national-statistics-and-treaty-registries.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should authoritative public facts, records, and decision visibility ordinarily live at each scope?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one dashboard fetish: **micro-local bodies should keep simple minutes, noticeboards, steward ledgers, and escalation logs rather than miniature data states; municipalities should be the first level with a full public information constitution of clerks or record stewards, open meeting packets, service and permit records, publication calendars, and reusable public data; metropolitan and regional governments should own their own observatories, geospatial baselines, and cross-boundary performance records rather than parasitic dependence on a host city or ministry; national government should carry the thickest official-statistics, gazette, archive, and interoperability spine; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound but still maintain comparability standards, registries, alerting channels, and shared reporting rather than private dashboards or counterfeit world omniscience**.
- `835-emergency-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-readiness-municipal-incident-command-regional-civil-protection-national-derogation-discipline-and-treaty-alerting.md` — The archive should answer the question **what emergency and exception grammar should ordinarily fit each scope?** with scale-matched escalation rather than one panic state fetish: **micro-local bodies should default to readiness, warning, mutual aid, and witness rather than emergency sovereignty; municipalities should be the first ordinary home of incident command, continuity, sheltering, and short-horizon emergency operations under ordinary law; metropolitan governments should carry shared-system disruption management where the functional city is one risk field; regional or provincial governments may honestly house civil-protection, wildfire, flood, logistics, and mutual-aid platforms where those risks are territorially real; national government should hold the thickest declaration, derogation, reserve, and exceptional coordination powers under legislative renewal, judicial review, and strict handback discipline; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound, specializing in alerting, coordination, standards, pooled assistance, and tightly authorized collective action rather than becoming ambient permanent emergency government**.
- `836-participation-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-assembly-municipal-dockets-metro-territorial-hearings-national-petition-ladders-and-treaty-observers.md` — If the archive already knows **what government should exist at each scope**, **how it is chosen**, **how it is financed**, **how it is scrutinized**, **where force lives**, **where records live**, and **what emergency lane fits it**, it should also know **how public voice honestly re-enters that government at each scale**: direct and reachable assembly voice at micro-local scale; petitions, hearings, consultations, bounded participatory-budget lanes, and occasional deliberative mini-publics at municipal scale; territory-wide participation homes for metropolitan and regional bodies that govern real shared systems; parliamentary hearing, petition, consultation, and rare constitution-level referendum lanes at national scale; and structured observer, submission, hearing, and stakeholder-participation routes for continental and global bodies rather than fake world-plebiscitary theater.
- `839-amendment-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-bylaws-municipal-charters-metro-double-keys-federal-entrenchment-and-treaty-ratification.md` — The archive should usually prefer different amendment grammars by scale: **micro-local rules should change publicly and cheaply; municipalities through charter or organic-law procedures with real community consultation for boundary or status change; metropolitan and regional governments through double-key amendment where shared systems or constituent bargains are real; national constitutions through heightened but repairable procedures with territorial participation for settlement-class changes; and continental or global regimes through explicit treaty amendment and ratification rather than executive side deals, secretariat drift, or permanent provisionalism**.

## lifecycle

- `414-federated-launch-rehearsals-before-shared-go-live.md` — Before a shared public digital system becomes mandatory or widely relied upon, its operators should run **federated launch rehearsals**: structured peer-to-peer testing under realistic conditions, with public lessons and explicit launch gates.
- `415-phase-labeled-public-automation-lifecycles.md` — Public automated systems should never drift through hidden stages. They should carry an explicit **lifecycle phase label** — such as pre-deployment, beta or pilot, production, paused, or retired — with different evidence, visibility, and approval requirements at each phase.
- `417-retest-after-material-change-and-periodic-reapproval.md` — Evidence for a public automated system expires. When the system, its data, its oversight practice, or its context changes in a material way, it should be **retested and reapproved**; even without a trigger event, high-impact systems should face a periodic reapproval clock.
- `418-bounded-beta-and-parallel-run-gates-before-consequential-use.md` — Public automated systems should not jump from lab confidence to civic dependence. Before a system becomes consequential in live operations, it should pass through a **bounded beta or parallel-run gate** with explicit scope limits, learning goals, fallback arrangements, and a named decision about whether it is actually ready for live reliance.
- `537-outer-space-and-orbital-commons-by-scope-local-hosting-regional-spaceports-national-authorization-and-global-sustainability-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat outer space as a global commons of use rather than a frontier of silent enclosure: local communities should hold real say over launch sites, tracking stations, astronomy impacts, land use, emergency planning, and public benefit where space infrastructure touches the ground; regional institutions should coordinate spaceport corridors, environmental review, disaster interfaces, and research ecosystems where activities spill across jurisdictions; nations should authorize and continuously supervise national activities in space, register objects, govern liability, spectrum and orbital use discipline, public research, procurement, and security constraints, and prevent private launch markets from becoming lightly regulated sovereignty proxies; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in non-appropriation, peaceful use, registration, debris mitigation, conjunction information-sharing, and long-term sustainability rather than letting orbit become an unmanaged congestion market.
- `570-legal-entity-business-and-beneficial-ownership-registries-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-entry-desks-regional-coordination-national-public-truth-and-no-government-by-paper-shell.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat organizational identity as constitutional infrastructure rather than clerical residue: communities can help witness real economic and associational life, municipalities or counties should usually provide the reachable entry desk for ordinary business-facing registrations and permits, regional or state layers should coordinate where federal structure or market geography requires it, national or constitutional-state law should own the authoritative registry of legal persons and the rules for unique identifiers, lifecycle events, disclosure, and strike-off, beneficial ownership should be held through a public authority or tightly governed equivalent with rapid lawful access and strong update discipline, and continental or global bodies should provide interoperability rails rather than pretending there can be one sovereign company register for the world.
- `617-capital-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-multi-year-pipelines-asset-stewardship-lifecycle-discipline-and-no-government-by-project-list.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **capital home** as well as democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, service, and planning ones: a visible multi-year capital programme, declared prioritisation and appraisal rules, asset-condition and maintenance stewardship, explicit funding-versus-financing discipline, and no territorial government by project list.
- `625-temporal-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-pilot-clocks-review-amendment-succession-and-no-government-by-immortal-pilot.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it should stop living in indefinite provisional status and acquire an explicit temporal home: a declared start basis, time-bounded pilot and transition rules where experimentation is still honest, published review clocks, visible renewal and amendment routes, sunset for temporary derogations, and lawful succession or dissolution rules so the polity does not govern for decades as an “interim” arrangement that nobody ever formally chose to keep.
- `640-post-launch-scope-observability-variance-ledgers-rollback-lanes-and-no-stack-change-by-runtime-custom.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat materially stack-altering reforms as **actively observable after go-live**, with one linked post-launch variance ledger, short review clocks, named correction and rollback lanes, and explicit closure criteria, so the lived operation of budgets, staff, systems, supervision, and remedies cannot quietly become a different constitutional settlement by runtime custom.
- `644-scope-nullity-rules-void-voidable-cure-freeze-lanes-and-no-constitutional-laundering-by-fait-accompli.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should distinguish **void**, **voidable**, and **curable** defects in materially stack-altering acts, and should require one public **scope-nullity ruling** or equivalent settlement object when a reform skipped the required scope lane: illegality should not ripen into constitutional fact merely because budgets spent, portals launched, or officials kept operating.
- `648-scope-functional-equivalence-rules-anti-circumvention-tests-and-no-stack-change-by-relabeling.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should classify **materially stack-altering moves by their real effect rather than by their chosen label**: if a grant condition, procurement framework, software default, model contract, coordination protocol, “pilot”, guidance note, or emergency instruction functionally reallocates who decides, who must comply, who pays, who may object, or which tier now governs in practice, it should travel through the same packet, opinion, override, register, and review lanes as any openly named scope change.
- `799-sunset-renewal-graduation-and-burial-rules-for-temporary-scope-arrangements-bridges-pilots-derogations-special-measures-and-no-shadow-constitution-by-serial-extension.md` — Whenever a polity uses a **temporary scope arrangement** — bridge body, host authority, pilot, derogation, emergency measure, temporary exemption, special administrator, or other exceptional workaround — the archive should require one compact **sunset / renewal / graduation rule**: **declare the default end state at the start, time-limit the arrangement, raise the proof burden on every renewal, force legitimacy and finance upgrades before any “temporary” body becomes ordinary government, and archive the ending publicly so shadow constitutions cannot survive by serial extension**.

## market-governance

- `516-markets-and-company-power-by-scope-local-entry-metro-space-national-antitrust-and-fair-global-rules.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern markets by keeping entry barriers, permits, public procurement access, and everyday consumer signal detection close to local life; using metropolitan and regional institutions to manage commercial geography, logistics, and market systems that cross municipal borders; reserving competition law, merger control, company law, securities rules, labour and consumer floors, and strategic industrial discipline to the nation; and using the global layer for trade predictability, anti-cartel cooperation, tax-base protection, and narrow common rules that prevent regulatory arbitrage without constitutionalizing corporate power above democracy.
- `538-money-and-payments-by-scope-local-cash-access-municipal-acceptance-national-public-money-and-global-interoperability.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat money and payments as constitutional infrastructure: households and neighbourhood institutions can surface exclusion, fraud, outage, and cash-access failures but should not mint rival monies for ordinary public life; municipalities should guarantee practical payment usability in everyday government, including cash access and acceptance where law protects it, legible public-payment channels, and inclusive collection design; metropolitan and regional institutions should coordinate shared payment touchpoints where commuting, service markets, and public agencies cross borders; nations should own legal tender, central bank money, payment-system oversight, public-payment rails, consumer protection, anti-fraud baselines, and resilience; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in message standards, cross-border interoperability, remittance quality, and data-friction reduction rather than pretending that local service design or national monetary legitimacy can be outsourced.
- `540-trade-customs-and-border-procedures-by-scope-local-port-interfaces-regional-gateways-national-trade-policy-and-global-rules.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat trade governance as both a rules system and a border operations system: households, workers, firms, and local communities can surface chokepoints, corruption, hazardous shipments, and the lived burden of gateways but should not each define external trade law; municipalities should govern port-adjacent land use, truck conflict, inspection-site interfaces, market transparency, and emergency support for traders without becoming fragmented customs sovereignties; regional institutions should coordinate corridors, dry ports, airports, inland terminals, and gateway ecosystems across the geography through which goods actually move; nations should own tariff schedules, trade agreements, customs law, single-window architecture, revenue collection, sanctions and strategic controls, and the constitutional balance between openness, security, labour, and environment; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in trade rules, customs standards, interoperable data models, and facilitation norms rather than pretending that one city or one ministry can govern cross-border exchange alone.
- `548-legislatures-by-scope-neighborhood-assemblies-municipal-councils-metro-chambers-federal-shared-rule-and-no-government-by-decree.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should fit its legislative institutions to scale: use direct assemblies and recallable delegates for micro-local stewardship, elected municipal and metropolitan councils where visible services and shared systems need contestable public rulemaking, regional and federal chambers where territory and shared rule must be represented, and national parliaments strong enough to legislate, budget, scrutinize, and police delegated law rather than surrendering government to executives, party cartels, or decree.

## materials-governance

- `431-data-provenance-chains-and-ai-ready-dataset-declarations.md` — Public-sector AI should maintain a provenance chain for every consequential dataset and publish a compact dataset declaration that names source, collection method, transformations, representativeness limits, legal basis, sharing constraints, and reuse conditions.
- `533-waste-and-materials-by-scope-local-collection-regional-recovery-national-producer-responsibility-and-global-hazard-controls.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat waste as failed material design rather than municipal fate: households, shops, workplaces, and neighbourhood institutions can sort, return, repair, and surface illegal dumping but should not carry the whole burden of circularity; municipalities should guarantee clean streets, universal collection, public-space litter control, reuse access points, and safe everyday interfaces with residents; regional bodies should run the real recovery geography of transfer stations, composting, remanufacturing, recycling markets, and final disposal capacity that usually outruns one city; nations should shift cost and design responsibility upstream through product standards, extended producer responsibility, deposit and take-back systems, right-to-repair rules, public procurement, data reporting, and labour protections; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in hazardous-waste controls, waste-trade rules, and common floor disciplines that prevent one country’s circular rhetoric from becoming another country’s toxic burden.
- `578-open-data-and-public-information-reuse-by-scope-community-scrutiny-municipal-publishing-regional-aggregation-national-standards-and-no-government-by-pdf-fog.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **open data and public-information reuse** as the **constitutional public-reuse layer** of government: keep community scrutiny, correction demand, and context close to the people and places described by the data; require municipalities and frontline bodies to publish routine local information in genuinely reusable ways rather than as decorative PDF dumps; pool regional aggregation, comparison, and cross-boundary publication where fragmented local release would make the public blind to shared systems; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the legal framework on reuse, licensing, metadata, machine-readable publication, privacy and confidentiality boundaries, high-value dataset rules, and catalog standards; and keep continental or global roles narrow enough to support interoperable metadata, cross-border discovery, and common high-value publication patterns without becoming one world data ministry.
