- `536-oceans-coasts-and-fisheries-by-scope-local-stewardship-regional-seascapes-national-jurisdiction-and-global-high-seas-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the ocean as both a lived coast and a shared planetary system: coastal communities, ports, and small-scale fishers should hold real stewardship, monitoring, harbour, and livelihood voice close to place; regional or sea-basin institutions should govern migratory stocks, coastal erosion, estuaries, shipping spillovers, marine protected networks, and cumulative seascape impacts at the ecological scale that actually exists; coastal states should own marine spatial planning within their jurisdiction, fisheries law, labour and safety enforcement, port-state control, public marine science, and fair distribution of marine rents; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in the law of the sea, high-seas biodiversity, shipping pollution, seabed restraint, and shared fish-stock rules rather than letting coastal nationalism or flag-of-convenience arbitrage hollow out the ocean commons.
- `537-outer-space-and-orbital-commons-by-scope-local-hosting-regional-spaceports-national-authorization-and-global-sustainability-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat outer space as a global commons of use rather than a frontier of silent enclosure: local communities should hold real say over launch sites, tracking stations, astronomy impacts, land use, emergency planning, and public benefit where space infrastructure touches the ground; regional institutions should coordinate spaceport corridors, environmental review, disaster interfaces, and research ecosystems where activities spill across jurisdictions; nations should authorize and continuously supervise national activities in space, register objects, govern liability, spectrum and orbital use discipline, public research, procurement, and security constraints, and prevent private launch markets from becoming lightly regulated sovereignty proxies; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in non-appropriation, peaceful use, registration, debris mitigation, conjunction information-sharing, and long-term sustainability rather than letting orbit become an unmanaged congestion market.
- `538-money-and-payments-by-scope-local-cash-access-municipal-acceptance-national-public-money-and-global-interoperability.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat money and payments as constitutional infrastructure: households and neighbourhood institutions can surface exclusion, fraud, outage, and cash-access failures but should not mint rival monies for ordinary public life; municipalities should guarantee practical payment usability in everyday government, including cash access and acceptance where law protects it, legible public-payment channels, and inclusive collection design; metropolitan and regional institutions should coordinate shared payment touchpoints where commuting, service markets, and public agencies cross borders; nations should own legal tender, central bank money, payment-system oversight, public-payment rails, consumer protection, anti-fraud baselines, and resilience; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in message standards, cross-border interoperability, remittance quality, and data-friction reduction rather than pretending that local service design or national monetary legitimacy can be outsourced.
- `539-banking-credit-and-financial-stability-by-scope-local-relationship-lending-regional-development-finance-national-prudential-oversight-and-global-backstops.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat banking and credit as a public-risk-bearing capability rather than a private allocation game: households, workers, firms, and local institutions can surface credit exclusion, predatory products, and place-specific capital starvation but should not be left to self-insure against systemic finance; municipalities can convene local credit intelligence, public banking interfaces, and anti-exclusion measures but should not act as miniature prudential sovereigns; regional institutions should govern development banks, housing and infrastructure finance platforms, and sectoral transition tools where production systems and catchments are wider than one city; nations should own licensing, prudential supervision, macroprudential policy, deposit insurance, resolution, lender-of-last-resort functions, and the constitutional line between utility banking and speculative risk; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in supervisory standards, cross-border resolution cooperation, correspondent-finance continuity, and anti-arbitrage floors rather than pretending world technocracy can substitute for domestic democratic control.
- `540-trade-customs-and-border-procedures-by-scope-local-port-interfaces-regional-gateways-national-trade-policy-and-global-rules.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat trade governance as both a rules system and a border operations system: households, workers, firms, and local communities can surface chokepoints, corruption, hazardous shipments, and the lived burden of gateways but should not each define external trade law; municipalities should govern port-adjacent land use, truck conflict, inspection-site interfaces, market transparency, and emergency support for traders without becoming fragmented customs sovereignties; regional institutions should coordinate corridors, dry ports, airports, inland terminals, and gateway ecosystems across the geography through which goods actually move; nations should own tariff schedules, trade agreements, customs law, single-window architecture, revenue collection, sanctions and strategic controls, and the constitutional balance between openness, security, labour, and environment; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in trade rules, customs standards, interoperable data models, and facilitation norms rather than pretending that one city or one ministry can govern cross-border exchange alone.
- `541-government-by-scope-micro-local-stewardship-municipal-professionalism-metropolitan-democracy-regional-capacity-national-guarantees-and-global-narrow-waists.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not ask every scale to be the same kind of government: micro-local units should be light stewardship and signal institutions, municipalities should be general-purpose democratic governments with professional administration, metropolitan governments should be directly legitimated coordinators of shared urban systems, regional governments should carry landscape and major-service capacity, national governments should guarantee equal citizenship, redistribution, macro-stability, and constitutional rights, and global bodies should remain narrow, treaty-bound organs for peace, commons, alerting, and interoperability rather than aspiring to one undifferentiated world state.
- `542-intergovernmental-machinery-lawful-councils-compacts-formula-finance-and-no-government-by-summit.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern the spaces **between** levels through lawful intergovernmental machinery—standing councils, mandatory consultation, rule-bound compacts, formula finance, shared operational forums, and independent dispute routes—so coordination is continuous, reviewable, and bounded rather than a contest of press conferences, emergency bargaining, and grant blackmail.
- `543-special-purpose-authorities-and-arms-length-bodies-narrow-remits-hard-charters-open-books-and-sunset-review.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should use special-purpose authorities, public corporations, and arm’s-length bodies only where a bounded cross-municipal or regional function — such as transit, utilities, watershed management, market regulation, or other impartial technical tasks — genuinely requires them; give them narrow remits, hard-law charters, published financing, public accountability, and periodic review; and never let them become shadow governments, patronage shelters, or constitutional escape hatches.
- `548-legislatures-by-scope-neighborhood-assemblies-municipal-councils-metro-chambers-federal-shared-rule-and-no-government-by-decree.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should fit its legislative institutions to scale: use direct assemblies and recallable delegates for micro-local stewardship, elected municipal and metropolitan councils where visible services and shared systems need contestable public rulemaking, regional and federal chambers where territory and shared rule must be represented, and national parliaments strong enough to legislate, budget, scrutinize, and police delegated law rather than surrendering government to executives, party cartels, or decree.
- `550-judiciaries-by-scope-neighborhood-entry-regional-trial-courts-national-apex-review-and-global-rights-backstops.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should keep justice entry and informal problem-sensing close to daily life, organize ordinary first-instance and specialized courts at the smallest catchment that can sustain independence and competence, reserve apex review, constitutional interpretation, judicial-appointment safeguards, and equality before the law to the national level, and treat supranational or global courts as narrow rights and treaty backstops rather than as substitutes for a functioning domestic judiciary.
- `551-public-prosecution-by-scope-local-diversion-regional-ordinary-charging-national-integrity-cases-and-no-government-by-prosecutor.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should keep prosecution lawful, impartial, and scale-matched: use community-near intake and diversion for ordinary low-level harm, size ordinary charging offices to regional or metropolitan court catchments large enough for competence and independence, reserve national prosecutors for public-corruption, state-integrity, and interjurisdictional serious crime, and keep cross-border prosecutorial cooperation narrow, reviewable, and rights-bound so neither local vendetta nor central spectacle can govern by charge.
- `552-electoral-administration-by-scope-local-voter-service-municipal-operations-regional-tabulation-national-standards-and-no-government-by-partisan-referee.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat electoral administration as a permanent, professional, and politically impartial public function: keep voter-facing service and polling logistics close enough to work, size counting and tabulation to real operational catchments, reserve core rulemaking and national certification architecture to a permanent central authority bounded by law, route disputes quickly to competent review bodies, and never let the government of the day become the referee of its own election.
- `553-supreme-audit-institutions-and-external-public-audit-by-scope-local-books-regional-state-audit-national-independence-and-no-government-by-self-audit.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should keep bookkeeping, internal control, and managerial accountability inside every public body, but place **external audit** in institutions independent of the auditee: make local books and records unavoidable, size municipal and state/provincial external audit to real government tiers and catchments, give the national supreme audit institution constitutional standing, access, budget, and publication rights, require legislatures and executives to follow up publicly, and never let the government audit itself in secret and call that accountability.
- `554-ombuds-institutions-by-scope-frontline-complaint-entry-municipal-redress-regional-coordination-national-independence-and-no-government-by-unanswered-grievance.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the **ombuds institution** as part of the constitutional remedy stack, not as a decorative ethics mascot: make complaint entry free, simple, and reachable close to everyday life; use municipal or regional ombuds capacity where public-service density and constitutional autonomy justify it; give the national ombuds institution a firm legal basis, real independence, own-initiative powers, publication rights, and escalation routes; coordinate multiple general and specialised ombuds bodies so people do not fall into a referral maze; and never let ordinary maladministration harden into **government by unanswered grievance**.
- `555-independent-human-rights-and-equality-institutions-by-scope-local-access-regional-reach-national-paris-principles-cores-and-no-government-by-self-certified-rights-compliance.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **independent human rights and equality institutions** as part of the constitutional checking system rather than as decorative values offices: keep rights access and discrimination complaint entry close to ordinary life, use regional or state-level bodies where territorial scale and constitutional structure justify them, anchor a broad, pluralist, independent national human rights institution in strong law, give equality bodies real investigatory and assistance powers, coordinate specialised monitors across the rights ecosystem, and never let governments drift into **self-certified rights compliance**.
- `556-police-services-by-scope-neighborhood-legibility-municipal-or-county-operations-metropolitan-serious-crime-bureaus-national-standards-and-no-police-self-investigation.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **police services** as a **civilian, rights-bound, externally answerable public service** rather than as a self-defining armed caste: keep neighborhood contact and ordinary response close enough to communities to stay legible, size police organizations and custody/investigation support large enough to resist tiny-jurisdiction capture, push serious-crime, forensic, and cross-border investigation to metropolitan or regional institutions, reserve national government for legal floors, training, anti-corruption and narrow specialist support, and never allow **police self-investigation** or militarized political policing to masquerade as democratic order.
- `557-detention-corrections-and-reentry-by-scope-local-contact-and-release-links-regional-custody-probation-national-rights-floors-and-no-government-by-warehousing.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **detention, corrections, and reentry** as a **strictly limited, rights-bound, reintegration-oriented part of justice** rather than as a hidden warehousing system: keep local roles focused on family contact, service continuity, diversion support, and release preparation rather than long-term cage sovereignty; use metropolitan or regional institutions for most remand custody, prisons, probation, parole, health continuity, and professionally managed inspectionable facilities; reserve national government for penal law, decarceration incentives, independent monitoring, and non-negotiable humane-treatment floors; and never allow **jails, prisons, or release systems to become opaque human storage insulated from courts, health systems, and society**.
- `558-public-defense-and-legal-aid-by-scope-local-entry-municipal-navigation-regional-provider-capacity-national-independence-and-no-justice-by-unaffordable-counsel.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **public defense and legal aid** as a **core constitutional capacity for equal justice** rather than as charity or courthouse aftercare: keep first contact, rights information, and navigable entry close to daily life; use metropolitan, county, provincial, state, or other regional institutions for most ordinary defender offices, provider networks, and specialist capacity; reserve national government for the right itself, independent legal-aid authority design, fair funding, quality floors, and territorial equalization; and never allow **freedom, family life, housing, status, or civil survival to depend on whether a person can privately purchase counsel on short notice**.
- `559-access-to-information-and-data-protection-institutions-by-scope-local-records-help-municipal-disclosure-discipline-regional-casework-national-independence-and-no-government-by-secrecy-or-panopticon.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **access-to-information and data-protection institutions** as a **paired constitutional circuit for democratic legibility and personal autonomy**: keep records help, routine request handling, and privacy-aware service design close to agencies and municipalities; use metropolitan, provincial, state, or other regional commissioners for much ordinary appeals and complaint casework where scale permits; reserve national government for the rights themselves, commissioner independence, common standards, difficult cross-sector investigations, and cross-border coordination; and never allow the same line ministries that benefit from secrecy or mass data collection to act as the final judges of openness and privacy.
- `560-official-statistics-and-census-institutions-by-scope-local-administrative-data-discipline-regional-capacity-national-independence-and-no-government-by-partisan-numbers.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **official statistics and census institutions** as a **constitutional public-facts system**: keep administrative-data quality, respondent support, and local enumeration logistics close to where people and records actually are; use provincial, state, regional, or other intermediate statistical institutions where territorial scale or federal structure justifies durable subject-matter capacity; reserve national government for the legal guarantees of professional independence, statistical confidentiality, census authority, coordination of the national statistical system, common methods and classifications, and public release calendars; and never allow the government of the day to decide the country’s facts by press office, police apparatus, or ministry convenience.
- `561-districting-and-boundary-commissions-by-scope-local-polling-areas-municipal-wards-regional-mapmaking-national-equal-suffrage-rules-and-no-government-by-incumbent-cartography.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat districting and seat allocation as a periodic, law-bound integrity function: keep polling-area maintenance close to real voter-service geography, place most ward and constituency mapmaking in independent local or regional boundary bodies sized to the polity they serve, reserve national government for equal-suffrage rules, census-to-seat apportionment, protected exceptions, and judicially reviewable backstops, and never let incumbents quietly draw the map that chooses their next electorate.
- `562-civil-registration-vital-statistics-and-legal-identity-institutions-by-scope-local-event-capture-municipal-service-access-regional-backstops-national-trust-frameworks-and-no-government-by-documentary-erasure.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat civil registration, vital statistics, and legal identity as a linked but non-collapsed public infrastructure: keep event notification and ordinary registration close to births, deaths, marriages, divorces, and residence reality; make municipal or county-level offices, health interfaces, and mobile service routes the ordinary access layer; use regional or provincial backstops where geography, federalism, or sparse settlement require them; reserve national government for the legal-status framework, secure and privacy-bounded identity trust architecture, interoperability rules, consular extension, and systemwide statistics coordination; and never let personhood, kinship, or access to basic rights depend on surviving a hostile documentary maze.
- `563-public-procurement-institutions-and-review-by-scope-local-needs-regional-shared-buying-national-rules-independent-challenges-and-no-government-by-emergency-sole-source-fog.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat public procurement as a governed public institution rather than a clerical back office: keep need definition, user-facing specification, and day-to-day contract management close to the service; use metropolitan, county, provincial, state, or other regional shared-buying bodies where market structure, scarce expertise, or repeated categories make pooling sensible; reserve national government for the procurement code, standard documents, core e-procurement rails, integrity controls, supplier-access baselines, independent complaint review design, and open-contracting discipline; keep the global layer narrow in interoperable standards, anti-rigging and anti-corruption cooperation, and fair cross-border conditions of competition; and never let emergency exemptions, framework sprawl, or vendor dependence turn public spending into shadow executive power.
- `564-anti-corruption-bodies-and-integrity-commissions-by-scope-local-routing-regional-case-development-national-specialization-and-no-government-by-heroic-commission.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not rely on one heroic anti-corruption commission: keep local complaint intake, disclosure routing, whistleblower handoff, and ordinary integrity advice close enough to be usable; place regional or state-level investigative and inspection capacity where corruption markets, procurement webs, and patronage chains cross municipalities or where tiny jurisdictions are too captured to investigate themselves; reserve national government for the preventive architecture required by law, high-level and cross-regional corruption, asset-declaration verification, beneficial-ownership tracing, international cooperation, and strategy coordination; keep the global layer narrow in standards, peer review, and transnational case support; and never let anti-corruption institutions become either decorative ethics theater or unreviewable prosecutor-states.
- `565-ideal-constitutional-kits-by-scope-neighborhood-voice-municipal-councils-metropolitan-democracy-regional-federal-capacity-national-solidarity-continental-compacts-and-global-narrow-waists.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat each scope as needing a **complete but scale-matched constitutional kit** — decision forum, executive administration, finance, oversight, and participation — with neighborhood institutions optimized for voice and upkeep, municipalities for general-purpose place governance, metropolitan bodies for shared urban systems, regions for major territorial platforms and shared rule, nations for rights and solidarity, continental bodies for bounded cooperation, and global institutions for mandate-bound coordination of peace, commons, alerting, and common standards.
- `566-electoral-systems-by-scope-direct-local-voice-municipal-proportionality-metropolitan-legitimacy-regional-balancing-national-pr-and-federal-shared-rule.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not force one electoral formula onto every scale: use direct and low-barrier democracy where the unit is genuinely small and stewardship-heavy, prefer proportional or semi-proportional council elections for municipalities and metropolitan governments that must aggregate durable diversity, fit executive election rules to the actual executive model, reserve territorial second chambers for real shared rule rather than decorative bicameralism, and keep continental and global bodies grounded mainly in treaty delegation plus bounded participatory and parliamentary complements rather than pretending every problem is solved by copying a national ballot upward.
- `567-public-borrowing-and-debt-by-scope-no-neighborhood-debt-municipal-capital-discipline-metro-infrastructure-national-stabilization-and-no-government-by-hidden-guarantees.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat borrowing as a scale-matched constitutional power rather than a general permission slip: micro-local bodies should usually not borrow at all, municipalities and regions should borrow mainly for long-lived capital under hard disclosure and restructuring rules, national governments should own macro-stabilization and sovereign debt management openly rather than laundering risk through off-book vehicles, and continental or global borrowing should remain narrow, charter-bound, and formula-backed instead of pretending a thin treaty body is already a full fiscal state.
- `568-land-administration-and-cadastre-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-parcel-service-regional-coordination-national-tenure-rules-and-no-government-by-documentary-dispossession.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat land administration as a scale-matched constitutional infrastructure rather than a clerical property office: community and customary institutions should help witness real people-to-land relationships, municipal or county offices should be the ordinary parcel-service front door, metropolitan or regional layers should pool cadastre and geospatial coordination where fragmentation would break the map, national or constitutional-state law should own tenure forms, identifiers, interoperability, and register integrity, and continental or global bodies should provide standards and support rather than pretending a world cadastre exists.
- `569-addresses-place-names-and-administrative-geography-by-scope-community-legibility-municipal-address-authority-regional-coherence-national-reference-frames-and-no-government-by-phantom-location.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat addresses, place names, and administrative geography as constitutional infrastructure rather than clerical leftovers: communities should help surface real local names and hard-to-map places, municipalities or counties should usually be the ordinary authority for street naming and address maintenance, metropolitan or regional layers should keep cross-boundary location systems coherent where daily life and service networks spill across borders, national institutions should own the authoritative reference frame for identifiers, geocoding, administrative units, and interoperability, and continental or global bodies should provide standards rather than pretending there can be one sovereign address book for the world.
- `570-legal-entity-business-and-beneficial-ownership-registries-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-entry-desks-regional-coordination-national-public-truth-and-no-government-by-paper-shell.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat organizational identity as constitutional infrastructure rather than clerical residue: communities can help witness real economic and associational life, municipalities or counties should usually provide the reachable entry desk for ordinary business-facing registrations and permits, regional or state layers should coordinate where federal structure or market geography requires it, national or constitutional-state law should own the authoritative registry of legal persons and the rules for unique identifiers, lifecycle events, disclosure, and strike-off, beneficial ownership should be held through a public authority or tightly governed equivalent with rapid lawful access and strong update discipline, and continental or global bodies should provide interoperability rails rather than pretending there can be one sovereign company register for the world.
- `571-public-records-archives-and-official-publications-by-scope-community-memory-municipal-record-discipline-regional-repositories-national-gazettes-and-no-government-by-disappearing-state.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **public records, archives, and official publication** as a **constitutional memory layer**: keep firsthand witnessing, local minutes, notice, and records help close to communities and municipalities; pool preservation, repository, and disaster-recovery capacity at regional scale where fragmentation would otherwise erase public memory; reserve national or constitutional-state law for records duties, transfer rules, authentic promulgation, and archival independence; and use continental and global layers for interoperability, documentary-heritage protection, and common access norms rather than for a fantasy of one world archive sovereign.
- `572-standards-metrology-testing-accreditation-and-conformity-assessment-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-inspection-regional-labs-national-quality-infrastructure-and-no-government-by-unverified-measurement.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **standards, metrology, testing, accreditation, and conformity assessment** as a **constitutional measurement layer**: keep user witnessing, complaint, and local inspection close to communities and municipalities; pool expensive laboratories, calibration, and specialist technical capacity at regional scale where fragmentation would waste money or degrade competence; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the quality-infrastructure core — measurement units, national metrology, accreditation, legal metrology, standard-setting mandates, and recognition rules — and use continental and global layers for equivalence, interoperability, and trade discipline rather than for a fantasy of one world product ministry.
- `573-administrative-procedure-permits-and-licenses-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-front-doors-regional-technical-review-national-procedure-codes-and-no-government-by-permit-maze.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **administrative procedure, permits, and licenses** as the **constitutional authorization layer** of government: keep lived fact-finding, pre-application help, and ordinary place-based intake close to communities and municipalities; pool specialist review and cross-boundary technical assessment regionally where risks or spillovers justify it; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the core procedural guarantees, common clocks, appeal architecture, and recognition rules that make the whole system legible; and use continental and global layers for interoperability, evidence exchange, and mutual recognition rather than for a fantasy of one world permit desk.
- `574-electronic-identification-signatures-seals-and-document-authentication-by-scope-community-attestation-municipal-enrollment-regional-federation-national-trust-frameworks-and-no-government-by-unverifiable-file.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **electronic identification, trust services, signatures, seals, time-stamps, and document authentication** as the **constitutional trust layer** of government: keep assisted enrollment, local fact correction, and ordinary witnessing close to people and firms; allow municipal and other frontline offices to serve as practical entry points into proofing and service use; pool federation and shared technical operations where subnational scale genuinely adds capacity; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the legal trust framework, assurance levels, authoritative source linkage, trusted lists, revocation discipline, and long-term verifiability of state acts; and use continental and global layers for standards, narrow recognition, and document authentication across borders rather than for a fantasy of one world identity stack.
- `575-official-notice-service-and-proof-of-delivery-by-scope-community-contact-municipal-address-for-service-regional-coordination-national-effect-rules-and-no-government-by-presumed-receipt.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **official notice, service of documents, proof of delivery, and legally significant receipt** as the **constitutional contact layer** of government: keep contact correction, local explanation, and assisted receipt close to people and firms; use municipalities and other frontline offices as ordinary points for address-for-service maintenance and help; pool specialist field service and hard-to-reach delivery work where subnational scale adds competence; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the rules that determine when notice counts, when clocks start, what proof suffices, and how failed delivery affects legal effect; and use continental and global layers for narrow treaty-bound cross-border service rather than for a fantasy of one world notification stack.
- `576-base-registries-identifiers-reference-data-and-interoperability-by-scope-community-error-surfacing-municipal-data-stewardship-regional-brokers-national-authoritative-sources-and-no-government-by-contradictory-copies.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **base registries, identifiers, reference data, and interoperability** as the **constitutional integration layer** of government: keep error surfacing, assisted correction, and local fact challenge close to people and firms; use municipalities and other frontline bodies as disciplined stewards and consumers of authoritative data rather than rival sovereign databases; pool interconnection, exchange infrastructure, and semantic support above fragmented local jurisdictions where scale adds competence; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for designating authoritative sources, assigning identifier rules, governing access, and maintaining shared code lists and metadata; and keep continental or global roles narrow enough to support cross-border evidence exchange, schemas, and semantic alignment without becoming a world master database.
- `577-public-service-delivery-one-stop-shops-and-assisted-digital-access-by-scope-community-navigation-municipal-front-counters-regional-shared-service-centers-national-service-standards-and-no-government-by-channel-maze.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **public service delivery** as the **constitutional execution layer** of government: keep trusted navigation, assisted digital help, and ordinary human contact close to communities and municipalities; pool shared service centers, call centers, translation, queue balancing, and specialist case support above fragmented local jurisdictions where scale adds competence; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for service standards, life-event integration, channel parity, common status semantics, and the core rails that let services feel like one government rather than a pile of agencies; and keep continental or global roles narrow enough to support cross-border information, procedures, assistance, and evidence exchange without becoming a world ministry of customer service.
- `578-open-data-and-public-information-reuse-by-scope-community-scrutiny-municipal-publishing-regional-aggregation-national-standards-and-no-government-by-pdf-fog.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **open data and public-information reuse** as the **constitutional public-reuse layer** of government: keep community scrutiny, correction demand, and context close to the people and places described by the data; require municipalities and frontline bodies to publish routine local information in genuinely reusable ways rather than as decorative PDF dumps; pool regional aggregation, comparison, and cross-boundary publication where fragmented local release would make the public blind to shared systems; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the legal framework on reuse, licensing, metadata, machine-readable publication, privacy and confidentiality boundaries, high-value dataset rules, and catalog standards; and keep continental or global roles narrow enough to support interoperable metadata, cross-border discovery, and common high-value publication patterns without becoming one world data ministry.
- `579-scope-allocation-by-level-intimacy-spillovers-coercion-solidarity-infrastructure-commons-and-no-government-by-level-confusion.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should allocate functions by a compact **scope-allocation grammar** rather than by inherited prestige or map inertia: keep voice, stewardship, and context-heavy discretion as close to people as possible; shift authority upward when spillovers outrun local borders, when network infrastructures require shared operation, when equal-rights floors and due-process guarantees require stronger uniformity, when risk-pooling and redistribution need a wider base, and when cross-border commons or security problems cannot be solved domestically; and treat continental and global layers as **narrow-waist coordination regimes** for shared problems rather than as imitation nation-states.
- `580-asymmetric-decentralization-special-status-territories-and-no-one-size-fits-all-stack.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **asymmetry** as a disciplined constitutional tool rather than as a taboo or a patronage trick: keep a clear default stack for ordinary places, but allow differentiated powers, institutions, and finance for metropolitan areas, capital districts, islands, remote regions, indigenous or plurinational territories, and other genuinely exceptional geographies when functional scale, capacity, history, identity, remoteness, or constitutional settlement justify it; pair that flexibility with equal-rights floors, transparent criteria, published finance rules, review clocks, and routes into and out of special status; and reject both one-size-fits-all map worship and ad hoc dealmaking that turns territorial difference into permanent favoritism.
- `581-mandate-finance-congruence-unfunded-mandates-vertical-fiscal-imbalance-and-no-decentralization-by-fiscal-theater.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **mandate-finance congruence** as constitutional law rather than budget etiquette: no level of government should be assigned a durable public function unless the same settlement also names the revenue basket, transfer formula, equalization rule, borrowing limits, and capability backstop that make the function actually dischargeable; delegated tasks must come with commensurate resources, local self-government must include at least some real own-source fiscal room, and upward rescue must be visible and reviewable rather than leaving decentralization to degrade into blame-shifting.
- `582-capability-congruence-minimum-viable-jurisdiction-intermunicipal-backstops-and-no-subsidiarity-by-fiction.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should pair subsidiarity with **capability congruence**: public functions should sit at the closest level that can actually staff, finance, procure, supervise, and lawfully discharge them; when small jurisdictions cannot sustain that floor on their own, the constitution should prefer **intermunicipal shared-service backbones, regional technical corps, explicit fallback lanes, and only then carefully justified consolidation** rather than pretending every map unit is a fully capable government.
- `583-subnational-distress-administrative-supervision-special-measures-handback-clocks-and-no-silent-recentralization.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **intervention in failing local or regional government as a lawful last-resort ladder**: ordinary supervision should be legality-bound and proportionate, support and co-production should come before takeover, financial distress and service collapse should trigger explicit temporary special measures only under published legal thresholds, essential services and rights routes must remain protected throughout, and every intervention should carry a reviewable restoration-and-handback path so rescue does not harden into permanent tutelage.
- `584-common-floors-local-headroom-explicit-preemption-rules-and-no-silent-override-by-upper-tier-convenience.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **preemption and override as explicit constitutional instruments rather than as ambient higher-tier privilege**: upper levels may set rights floors, solidarity guarantees, interoperability rules, and protections against genuine cross-border harms, but they should leave subnational governments real room to go further or adapt locally unless a law clearly names the conflict, states the protected interest, consults affected governments, provides transition and finance where duties are displaced, and subjects any ceiling preemption or field occupation to review rather than letting uniformity spread by habit.
- `585-conditional-grants-matching-funds-competitive-programs-and-no-government-by-grant-maze.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **intergovernmental grants as constitutional instruments rather than administrative weather**: ordinary local discretion and equal citizenship should rest mainly on own-source revenue plus predictable general and equalization transfers; earmarked, matching, performance, capital, or competitive grants should be reserved for narrow cases where rights floors, spillovers, transition priorities, or shared investment genuinely justify them; co-financing duties should scale to fiscal capacity; application, reporting, and audit rules should be harmonized and limited; and no higher tier should be allowed to govern municipalities, metros, or regions mainly by forcing them to live inside a permanent grant maze.
- `586-function-transfer-packs-staff-assets-records-contracts-liabilities-and-no-reassignment-by-legal-text-alone.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **any transfer of a public function across levels of government as a full transfer pack rather than a sentence in a law**: whenever a competence moves, the same settlement should also name the effective date, service standard, staff lane, asset and lease inventory, contract and procurement treatment, records and data custody, ongoing-case handoff, fiscal lane, liability rule, transition authority, dispute route, and review clock, so that decentralisation or recentralisation cannot occur by moving the headline power while leaving the receiving government to inherit an empty shell.
- `587-deconcentrated-state-administration-prefects-field-offices-and-no-shadow-local-government.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should use **deconcentrated state administration** only for the territorial presence of the common state — co-ordination of national services, lawful supervision of delegated tasks, emergency interface, and field execution of genuinely national functions — while keeping democratic **local and regional self-government** institutionally distinct, so prefects, governors, or line-ministry field offices do not become unelected substitute governments for places that actually need elected voice.
- `588-delegated-state-tasks-local-discretion-agent-status-funding-and-no-mixed-accountability-blur.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should use **delegated state tasks** only for bounded functions that remain owned by a higher tier but require territorial execution through local or regional governments, and it should write those delegations as explicit public compacts that name the task, the discretion band, the instruction and supervision route, the funding rule, and the remedy path, so lower tiers do not become underfunded agents of the center while still being blamed as if they were governing in their own right.
- `589-general-competence-home-rule-local-charters-municipal-initiative-and-no-government-by-ultra-vires-fragment.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should give its **general-purpose local governments** a clear **general competence / home-rule footing** — the right, within law, to act on matters of local public concern unless those matters are expressly reserved elsewhere — so municipalities do not need a fresh positive legal warrant for every practical problem, and so local democracy governs by visible political responsibility rather than by ultra vires scavenger hunts.
- `590-multilevel-impact-packets-subsidiarity-territorial-effects-rural-proofing-and-no-lawmaking-by-placeless-abstraction.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should require any higher-tier law, regulation, spending program, or platform reform that materially affects lower-tier powers, finances, administrative burden, or territorial outcomes to ship with a **published multilevel impact packet** — a compact subsidiarity, proportionality, territorial-effects, implementation, and consultation record — so central action is argued openly rather than smuggled through placeless abstraction.
- `591-concurrent-competences-lead-lane-typing-paramountcy-defaults-and-no-government-by-overlap-fog.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **concurrent or shared competences as a typed constitutional settlement rather than as a vague admission that “everyone is involved”**: where more than one level must legitimately act in the same field, the law should split the field into visible lanes — such as rights floors, finance, planning, delivery, inspection, data, and remedy — assign a lead level for each lane, state what happens on conflict, preserve lower-tier headroom where that is the point of the arrangement, and publish a coordination rulebook so citizens are not forced to infer government structure from a pile of overlapping claims.
- `592-local-ordinance-power-bylaws-framework-laws-review-lanes-and-no-self-government-by-administration-only.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should give **general-purpose local governments** a real but bounded **local ordinance / by-law power** within framework law — enough to make binding local rules on genuinely local matters, subject to legality review, rights floors, and explicit upper-tier reservations — so self-government does not collapse into mere administration of other people’s rules.
- `593-local-self-government-judicial-remedy-constitutional-standing-interim-relief-and-no-autonomy-without-recourse.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should guarantee **local and regional governments** a real **right of recourse to judicial remedy** — including standing against executive interference, a route to constitutional review where laws themselves wound self-government, and timely interim relief against irreversible harm — so autonomy is defended by law rather than left to negotiation, prestige, or endurance.
- `594-local-authority-associations-consortia-transfrontier-co-operation-and-no-self-government-in-isolation.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the right of local authorities to co-operate, form delivery consortia, join representative associations, and work with counterparts across borders as part of self-government itself, so municipalities and regions can pool capacity, defend common interests, and solve cross-boundary problems without being reduced to isolated administrative fragments.
- `595-territorial-reorganization-incorporation-mergers-splits-status-change-and-no-map-surgery-by-managerial-fiat.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the creation, merger, split, annexation, abolition, and status change of territorial authorities as constitutional surgery rather than managerial tidying, so map reform remains lawful, consultative, alternatives-tested, continuity-safe, and reviewable instead of becoming a shortcut around self-government.
- `596-special-purpose-authorities-utility-districts-metro-agencies-and-no-government-by-quango-sprawl.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should use special-purpose authorities only as tightly bounded tools for real network, basin, corridor, or technical-governance problems, so shared systems can be run at the right scale without letting single-purpose bodies metastasize into a shadow constitution of opaque boards, off-budget debt, and blame-proof government.
- `597-local-participation-rights-petitions-initiatives-referendums-deliberative-mini-publics-and-no-direct-democracy-by-ambush.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **participation in local and regional affairs as a bounded constitutional layer of self-government**: people should have low-friction rights to petition, place issues on the agenda, join structured consultations, take part in participatory budgeting and civic monitoring where appropriate, and in some cases trigger or vote in referendums — but each channel should have a clear legal purpose, a visible response duty, and strong protections against capture, rights injury, and plebiscitary short-circuiting of representative government.
- `599-local-and-regional-assembly-scrutiny-rights-agenda-power-questions-committee-capacity-and-no-majoritarian-blackout.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the **scrutiny rights of local and regional assemblies as constitutional operating equipment rather than as optional etiquette**: councils and assemblies should control the budgetary and rulemaking core, all members should have enforceable rights to meetings, agendas, questions, information, and proportionate committee work, opposition and minority blocs should be able to scrutinise without begging the executive for oxygen, and executive accountability should be structured so local democracy cannot be reduced to periodic elections plus majority blackout.
- `600-organizational-autonomy-internal-administrative-structures-standing-orders-and-no-self-government-by-template-lock.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **organizational autonomy inside local and regional government as part of self-government itself**: higher-tier law may set democratic floors, rights safeguards, and role boundaries, but local and regional authorities should retain broad discretion to choose their internal administrative structures, committee maps, standing orders, subordinate units, and service-delivery arrangements so they can adapt institutions to local needs instead of governing through template lock from above.
- `601-publicity-of-local-deliberation-open-meetings-agenda-notice-closed-session-limits-and-no-government-by-chamber-obscurity.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **the publicity of local and regional deliberation as a constitutional operating condition rather than as optional etiquette**: plenary meetings and decision-shaping committees should be open by default, agendas and core papers should be published with usable notice, closed sessions should be narrow and reasoned, minutes and vote records should remain durable and searchable, and open meetings should complement rather than substitute for broader participatory methods so self-government does not retreat into chamber obscurity.
- `602-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-steward-cells-municipal-general-government-metropolitan-systems-democracy-regional-territorial-platforms-national-guarantor-states-continental-compacts-and-global-treaty-narrow-waists.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should give each scope a distinct governing vocation and a minimum complete kit: micro-local units as visible stewardship and signal cells; municipalities as the first full general-purpose governments of ordinary life; metropolitan governments as democratically legitimated operators of shared urban systems; regional, provincial, or state governments as territorial-platform governments for landscapes, hospitals, grids, universities, and shared rule; nations as guarantor states for equal citizenship, redistribution, macro-stability, and constitutional settlement; continental bodies as bounded compact governments for cross-border mobility, markets, and infrastructures; and global institutions as treaty-bound narrow waists for peace, commons, alerting, and standards rather than as a fake world domestic state.
- `603-order-of-operations-for-ideal-multilevel-government-vocation-assignment-kits-connectors-asymmetry-and-no-reform-by-layer-shopping.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should be designed in a disciplined order: start from the class of problems and the real geography they inhabit, assign responsibilities by explicit scope tests, fit each chosen level with a minimum complete institutional kit, bind that kit to finance and capability, add coordination/review/equalization connectors, and only then allow principled asymmetry and transfer rules; reject reforms that start by picking a favored level first and inventing reasons afterward.
- `604-diagnosing-scope-misfit-overbuild-underbuild-duplicate-chains-orphan-functions-and-no-government-by-institutional-furniture.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should **periodically diagnose scope misfit** rather than merely inherit its jurisdictional stack: detect overbuilt levels, underbuilt levels, duplicate chains, orphan functions, paper metros or paper regions, false localism, and false centralism by testing whether each public problem has a real governing vocation, a visible lead for each lane of work, a minimum complete institutional kit, matched money and capability, and lawful connectors and review paths.
- `605-repair-ladders-for-multilevel-government-lane-fixes-connectors-kit-completion-cooperation-territorial-upgrades-map-surgery-and-no-reform-by-single-instrument.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should repair scope misfit through an ordered ladder: diagnose the exact pathology first, then clarify lanes, add missing connectors, complete the minimum institutional kit at the live tier, use intermunicipal or intergovernmental cooperation where scale outruns unit size, create or strengthen narrow special-purpose machinery only where a real functional geography demands it, upgrade to an honest metropolitan or regional tier when shared politics and multi-sector system governance are unavoidable, and reach for mergers, splits, or boundary surgery only after lighter repairs have been tested, consulted, and continuity-proofed.
- `606-when-co-operation-becomes-government-thresholds-for-constitutionalizing-shared-territorial-power-and-no-metropolitan-rule-by-consortium.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should let municipalities and regions co-operate freely for shared capacity and service delivery, but once a joint body starts making repeated cross-boundary trade-offs across several sectors, raising compulsory money, issuing debt, binding land use or major infrastructure choices, or functioning as the real political center of a territory, it should be constitutionalized as honest metropolitan or regional government rather than left as a consortium, summit, or quango stack.
- `607-democratic-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-indirect-councils-double-legitimacy-direct-election-and-no-metropolitan-rule-by-proxy.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, the honest constitutional question is not whether it needs democracy but **which democratic home fits the power**: keep indirect representation for narrow and bounded co-ordination, use double-legitimacy designs where both people and component governments must visibly count, and prefer directly elected territorial government once the body can bind residents through compulsory finance, major debt, cross-sector territorial bargaining, or durable system-shaping authority.
- `608-fiscal-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-own-source-revenue-predictable-equalization-capital-discipline-and-no-metropolitan-government-by-begging-bowl.md` — Once shared territorial power has become real metropolitan or regional government, the polity should give it an honest fiscal constitution: responsibilities commensurate with resources, a visible base of own or rule-based shared revenue, diversified and buoyant funding, equalization that protects weaker places without destroying discretion, grants used for clear national or supralocal purposes rather than everyday dependence, and borrowing bounded mainly to capital investment rather than operational drift.
- `609-administrative-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-own-executive-own-staff-records-treasury-planning-core-and-no-government-by-secondment-maze.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **administrative home** as well as a democratic and fiscal one: a legally visible executive center, its own staff and records, a durable core for planning/finance/procurement/legal/data work, interoperable but non-subordinate interfaces with component governments and the state, and enough administrative continuity that the territory is not really governed through borrowed personnel, rotating mayoral bandwidth, consultants, or agency shrubbery.
- `610-accountability-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-scrutiny-audit-disclosure-complaints-review-and-no-government-by-jurisdictional-gap.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **accountability home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, and administrative one: its own scrutiny forum, named records-and-disclosure duties, internal control and audit proportionate to risk, external audit and integrity jurisdiction, complaint and review routes that ordinary people can actually find, and explicit accountability for operators and contractors so the territory is not really governed in the gaps between municipalities, agencies, and the state.
- `611-public-law-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-legal-personality-named-competences-rulemaking-and-no-government-by-interlocal-contract.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should allow municipalities and regions to cooperate by agreement for bounded shared tasks, but once a metropolitan or regional body is doing real territorial government it should have an honest public-law home: legal personality, a named territorial basis, competences prescribed by constitution or statute, a proportionate rulemaking lane, clear relations with member governments and the state, and no government by interlocal contract.
- `612-intergovernmental-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-standing-consultation-compacts-dispute-lanes-and-no-government-by-ad-hoc-summit.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **intergovernmental home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, and public-law one: a standing place in state decision-making, lawful consultation routes, regular bargaining forums, explicit compact and co-financing lanes, visible conflict-escalation and dispute rules, and no territorial government by occasional summit, ministry favour, or host-city mediation.
- `613-participatory-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-petitions-hearings-mini-publics-territorial-notice-and-no-metropolitan-participation-by-postcode.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **participatory home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, and intergovernmental one: territory-wide notice, petition and question routes, public hearings and consultations, bounded co-prioritisation and participatory-budget lanes where suitable, representative deliberative processes for complex trade-offs, and visible response duties — so residents can influence the shared tier directly rather than relying on borrowed municipal channels, host-city publicity, or consultation theatre.
- `614-knowledge-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-observatories-territorial-indicators-basemaps-scenario-capacity-and-no-government-by-fragmented-spreadsheets.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **knowledge home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, and participatory one: a territorially coherent observatory, common basemaps and boundary files, a published indicator set at the scale actually being governed, lawful data-sharing and evaluation capacity, open methods and release discipline, and visible routes from evidence into plans and budgets — so the shared tier stops governing through municipal spreadsheet fragments, ministry leftovers, vendor dashboards, and dueling numbers.
- `615-service-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-service-authorities-operator-chains-commissioning-continuity-and-no-government-by-memorandum-network.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **service home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, and knowledge one: a visible split among authority, operator, and regulator; a named territorial service map showing what stays local and what becomes shared; lawful commissioning, franchising, or direct-operation routes where system services are real; service standards, continuity duties, and fallback rules that survive contracts and politics; and clear public entry and complaint handoffs — so the territory stops being governed through memoranda, host-city favors, improvised consortia, and operator clubs.
- `616-planning-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-territorial-plans-plan-hierarchies-conformity-and-no-government-by-vision-deck.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **planning home** as well as democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, and service ones: a territorial planning authority with a real public plan, a declared hierarchy with municipal and state plans, visible conformity or compatibility rules, infrastructure-and-land-use coupling, amendment and review clocks, and no territorial government by advisory strategy deck.
- `617-capital-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-multi-year-pipelines-asset-stewardship-lifecycle-discipline-and-no-government-by-project-list.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **capital home** as well as democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, service, and planning ones: a visible multi-year capital programme, declared prioritisation and appraisal rules, asset-condition and maintenance stewardship, explicit funding-versus-financing discipline, and no territorial government by project list.
- `618-regulatory-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-licensing-permits-standards-inspection-enforcement-and-no-government-by-operator-rulebook.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **regulatory home** as well as democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, service, planning, and capital ones: a visible territorial rulebook, named licensing and permitting lanes where risk demands them, a clear separation among rule-maker, regulator, operator, and reviewer, proportionate inspection and enforcement, and no government by operator rulebook.
- `619-contract-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-procurement-franchising-change-control-exit-capacity-and-no-government-by-concession-patchwork.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **contract home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, service, planning, capital, and regulatory one: a visible buyer-or-commissioner function, explicit make-buy-franchise tests, lawful procurement and concession routes, disciplined contract and change control, published performance and amendment trails, real handback and step-in capacity, and no territorial government by concession patchwork.
- `620-workforce-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-employer-status-recruitment-training-labor-relations-and-no-government-by-borrowed-payroll.md` — Real metropolitan or regional government needs its own **employer constitution**: a named employer of record, merit-based staffing and progression, explicit pay and labor-relations rules, bounded reliance on secondment, visible workforce metrics, and a transition path out of borrowed payroll.
- `621-digital-operating-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-case-systems-identity-access-release-discipline-and-no-government-by-portal-shell.md` — Real metropolitan or regional government needs its own **digital operating constitution**: a named digital authority, canonical case/workflow and records systems, explicit identity-and-access rules, bounded interoperable exchange, release and incident discipline, continuity safeguards, and channel parity — not government by portal shell.
- `622-emergency-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-emergency-operations-continuity-mutual-aid-recovery-and-no-government-by-crisis-summit.md` — Real metropolitan or regional government needs its own **emergency constitution**: a named territorial emergency authority, an all-hazards risk picture, predefined escalation and mutual-aid rules, continuity of government and essential services, exercised communication and warning routes, recovery and handback discipline, and bounded extraordinary powers — not government by crisis summit.
- `623-redress-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-complaints-hearings-appeals-ombuds-and-no-government-by-jurisdiction-hunt.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **redress home** as well as democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, service, planning, capital, regulatory, contract, workforce, digital-operating, and emergency ones: one visible territorial path for complaint, reconsideration, hearing, appeal, ombuds, and judicial review, with reasons, clocks, and no government by jurisdiction hunt.
- `624-territorial-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-boundaries-membership-accession-exit-review-and-no-government-by-opt-in-map.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it should stop living on voluntary membership residue, project geography, or host-city convenience and instead acquire an explicit territorial home: a publicly declared boundary, named member units, clear rules for accession, exit, annexation or detachment, periodic but not perpetual review, and one authoritative map that matches the powers, money, plans, and obligations the territory actually carries.
- `625-temporal-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-pilot-clocks-review-amendment-succession-and-no-government-by-immortal-pilot.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it should stop living in indefinite provisional status and acquire an explicit temporal home: a declared start basis, time-bounded pilot and transition rules where experimentation is still honest, published review clocks, visible renewal and amendment routes, sunset for temporary derogations, and lawful succession or dissolution rules so the polity does not govern for decades as an “interim” arrangement that nobody ever formally chose to keep.
- `626-public-communication-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-canonical-channels-corrections-inclusive-reach-and-no-government-by-press-release-federation.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it should acquire an explicit **public-communication home**: a named official communications function distinct from party or campaign messaging; one canonical set of channels for notices, updates, warnings, and explanations; correction and version trails; multilingual and accessible publication discipline; clear docking between general information and legal notice; and archival capture of official statements so the territory does not govern through host-city press offices, operator fragments, screenshots, and rumor.
- `627-constitutionalization-bundles-for-shared-territorial-power-core-upgrades-supporting-upgrades-and-no-government-by-single-home-fetish.md` — Once co-operation has crossed the threshold into real shared territorial government, an ideal polity should not pretend that one institutional fix — election alone, revenue alone, law alone, map alone, platform alone, or participation alone — makes the arrangement honest; it should constitutionalize in **bundles**, starting with a minimum core of public-law, democratic, fiscal, administrative, and accountability upgrades, then docking territorial, temporal, intergovernmental, and operating bundles as the functions actually governed require.
- `628-honesty-tests-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-vocation-complete-kits-constitutional-upgrade-and-no-jurisdictional-cosplay.md` — An ideal government at any scope is not defined by prestige, inherited labels, or institutional symmetry, but by an honest fit among governing vocation, territorial reality, democratic legitimacy, administrative capacity, money, review routes, and upgrade triggers: micro-local units should stay signal-rich and light; municipalities should be the first full governments of ordinary life; metropolitan and regional tiers should harden once shared territorial power is real; nations should guarantee equal citizenship, solidarity, and constitutional order without swallowing the stack; and continental and global bodies should remain competence-bounded compact and treaty narrow waists rather than drifting into jurisdictional cosplay.
- `629-default-presumptions-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-first-for-ordinary-place-system-tiers-by-proof-guarantor-layers-by-duty-and-no-scope-without-burden-of-proof.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should not treat scope assignment as a blank slate every time; it should carry default constitutional presumptions: micro-local institutions presumptively hold stewardship, signal, and civic-entry functions, municipalities ordinary-place government, metropolitan and regional tiers only the functions that truly live in shared systems or territorial platforms, nations the guarantor duties of equal citizenship and solidarity, and continental or global bodies only explicitly named cross-border necessities under bounded compact or treaty forms.
- `630-rescoping-authority-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-administration-by-law-constitutional-bargains-by-consent-and-no-jurisdictional-rewire-by-executive-deal.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat **moving a function between scopes as a graded constitutional act**: ordinary implementation detail may be adjusted through ordinary law inside fixed competences, sectoral reallocations among existing tiers should travel through public legislation with consultation and impact proof, any move that alters the protected bargain of local or regional self-government should require the higher law and consent route appropriate to that bargain, and no executive compact, grant condition, crisis summit, or managerial workaround should be allowed to rewire who really governs what.
- `631-reversibility-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-handback-clocks-fresh-proof-return-lanes-and-no-one-way-recentralization-ratchet.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat exceptional upward concentration, distress takeover, emergency command, grant-conditioned control, and other scope shifts as **expiring claims rather than one-way ratchets**: the level that temporarily takes more power should carry a visible handback clock, a fresh-proof burden if it wants to keep the power, a capability-repair plan for the lower tier, a lawful return lane for money/staff/records/discretion, and a public explanation for any permanent reallocation.
- `638-clear-statement-rules-for-scope-change-interpretive-backstops-and-no-rescoping-by-ambiguity.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should adopt one public **clear-statement rule for scope change**: ambiguous statutes, grants, budgets, guidance, compacts, or software defaults should not be interpreted as materially reallocating protected competences, narrowing local or regional discretion, or creating durable new stack relations unless the instrument says so explicitly and travels with the linked scope packet, opinion, and override path where required.
- `645-scope-standstill-defaults-suspensory-effect-interim-relief-and-no-stack-change-by-racing-the-clock.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should give timely, credible challenges to materially stack-altering acts a visible **scope-standstill** or equally fast **interim-relief lane**, so the live constitutional stack cannot be rewritten simply because deployment moved faster than review.
- `646-scope-severability-fallback-baselines-partial-invalidity-and-no-whole-stack-collapse-by-contamination.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat a materially stack-altering package as **severable where honest**, preserving only those parts that can still be described as lawful, coherent, and democratically ownable on their own terms, with one visible fallback baseline and one public explanation of what survives, what is stayed, and what must be rebuilt, so a single defect neither launders the whole package nor needlessly detonates the lawful remainder.
- `648-scope-functional-equivalence-rules-anti-circumvention-tests-and-no-stack-change-by-relabeling.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should classify **materially stack-altering moves by their real effect rather than by their chosen label**: if a grant condition, procurement framework, software default, model contract, coordination protocol, “pilot”, guidance note, or emergency instruction functionally reallocates who decides, who must comply, who pays, who may object, or which tier now governs in practice, it should travel through the same packet, opinion, override, register, and review lanes as any openly named scope change.
- `652-scope-desuetude-limits-abandonment-fictions-and-no-stack-change-by-atrophy.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should not let **non-use, weak use, under-enforcement, dormancy, or degraded capacity** silently extinguish protected competence: materially stack-bearing authority may require review, repair, reactivation, or even lawful reassignment, but it should not be treated as lost merely because it was not exercised often, boldly, or recently enough.
- `655-scope-retroactivity-limits-future-only-defaults-curative-acts-and-no-stack-change-by-backdating.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat **materially stack-altering acts as future-facing by default**: if a sponsor wants retroactive effect, retroactive validation, or a backdated effective date, it should have to travel through an unusually narrow, explicit, legally justified lane with preserved **review routes**, **judicial remedy**, and clear **legal authority** rather than letting the stack change by historical rewrite.
- `656-scope-transition-rules-for-pending-matters-cutover-queues-file-transfer-and-no-stack-change-by-midstream-grab.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require every **materially stack-altering act** to carry explicit transition rules for pending applications, permits, investigations, appeals, contracts, liabilities, records, and service queues — with named cutover dates, forum rules, file-transfer duties, and clock-preservation — so old matters do not silently jump sovereigns, stall in limbo, or get re-decided by midstream grab.
- `658-scope-evidentiary-continuity-record-provenance-and-no-proof-laundering-by-migration.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require every **materially stack-altering reform** to preserve **evidentiary continuity** across record transfer, system migration, redaction, archival cutover, and platform replacement — with stable identifiers, provenance metadata, chain-of-custody, transformation logs, and certified retrieval routes — so responsibility can still be proven after a function moves and rescoping cannot dissolve proof through administrative or technical migration.
- `660-canonical-government-matrix-by-scope-legislature-executive-civil-service-fiscal-base-review-participation-and-no-full-stack-rewrite-for-every-tier.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should reuse one **canonical scope matrix** rather than reinventing every tier from scratch: micro-local units for witness and stewardship, municipalities for ordinary place government, metropolitan authorities for functional urban systems, regions for major territorial platforms and shared rule, nations for equal citizenship and redistribution, continental bodies for bounded cross-border compacts, and global institutions for treaty-bound peace, commons, alerting, and interoperability — each with a scope-matched decision forum, executive spine, civil-service density, fiscal base, review lane, and participation channel.
- `661-collapsed-stack-rules-for-microstates-city-states-fused-tiers-shared-capacity-and-no-full-ladder-cosplay.md` — When a polity is too small, too urban-concentrated, too remote, or too capacity-constrained to sustain the full municipal–regional–national ladder as separate apparatuses, the ideal answer is not ceremonial duplication but **honest scope collapse**: fuse tiers openly where necessary, preserve functional separation inside the fused institutions, keep neighborhood and municipal voice where lived place still matters, pool specialist capacity through explicit shared-service or treaty arrangements, and refuse both fake federal pageantry and centralized one-office government.
- `662-global-institution-toolkit-by-problem-class-assemblies-secretariats-scientific-panels-registries-inspection-compliance-funds-and-no-world-state-monoculture.md` — The ideal global layer should be built from a **small toolkit of treaty-bound institutional forms matched to problem class** rather than from one fantasy model of world government: use assemblies and councils for norm-setting, secretariats and focal-point networks for continuous coordination, scientific panels for shared factual baselines, registries and reporting systems for comparability, inspection or verification where cheating matters, dispute and compliance lanes where interpretation recurs, and dedicated funds where solidarity is required — while refusing both fake world-state domesticity and empty declarations with no operating spine.
- `663-cross-border-integration-ladders-information-sharing-minimum-standards-mutual-recognition-common-enforcement-budget-tools-and-no-union-by-slogan.md` — Ideal continental or plurilateral governance should climb an explicit **integration ladder** — information exchange, benchmarking, minimum standards, mutual recognition, shared operational rails, pooled enforcement, common financing, and only then deeper legislative or fiscal union where truly necessary — so polities can co-govern real spillovers without pretending every problem requires the same depth of union or drifting by slogan into competence creep.
- `664-obligation-and-funding-formulas-by-problem-class-capacity-to-pay-equalization-polluter-pays-beneficiary-pays-risk-solidarity-and-no-one-formula-federalism.md` — Ideal multilevel and global governance should match each shared obligation to the right **apportionment rule** — capacity to pay for common institutions, equalization for rights floors, polluter-pays for harm control, beneficiary-pays for optional service gains, risk-based pooling for insurance and emergency reserves, and differentiated duties where histories and capabilities materially differ — so solidarity is explicit and reviewable rather than smuggled through arbitrary shares, annual bargaining, or one formula pasted across every tier and problem.
- `665-external-commitment-landing-paths-signature-ratification-transposition-direct-effect-operational-owners-and-no-treaty-by-press-release.md` — Cross-border and global commitments should not stop at signature or ratification: an honest polity should show the full **landing path** from external commitment to domestic legal effect, operational owners, budgeting, reporting, review, and subnational fit, so treaty participation does not masquerade as implementation.
- `674-shared-regime-records-and-publicity-public-private-sessions-document-registers-meeting-records-vote-records-authentic-texts-corrections-and-no-governance-by-missing-papertrail.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed documentary constitution** that separates session publicity, agenda and paper circulation, official document registers, meeting-record formats, vote records, authentic texts, correction notices, and retention or access rules — so public authority does not vanish into missing minutes, unofficial drafts, or document folklore.
