- `677-shared-regime-external-participation-constitutions-accreditation-observer-categories-submissions-hearings-transparency-registers-and-no-public-power-by-lanyard.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed external-participation constitution** that separates membership from observer or accredited-participant status, standing accreditation from session registration, document access from floor rights, written submissions from negotiation rights, and consultation from decision power — so public authority does not drift toward whoever got a badge, a side-room invitation, or a privileged mailing list.
- `684-shared-regime-secretariat-workforce-constitutions-appointments-merit-geographic-balance-secondments-conduct-separation-and-no-regime-by-patronage.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed secretariat workforce constitution** that separates political head selection from career staffing, makes merit and integrity the paramount recruitment rule, gives geographic balance a visible but bounded place, constrains secondments and related-party hiring, and types conduct, reassignment, discipline, and separation lanes — so the regime is not governed by patronage, donor-owned posts, or borrowed-capacity fog.
- `689-shared-regime-territorial-presence-constitutions-headquarters-regional-offices-country-offices-liaison-posts-service-hubs-host-instruments-review-clocks-and-no-regime-by-landlord-permission.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed territorial-presence constitution** that separates headquarters, regional offices, country offices, liaison posts, service hubs, hosted outposts, and temporary mission footprints — with a named host instrument, mandate fit, reporting line, support package, review clock, and closure path for each — so institutional presence stays functional and reviewable instead of hardening into landlord permission, prestige geography, or office sprawl by habit.
- `690-shared-regime-field-security-and-continuity-constitutions-designated-officials-risk-tiers-clearance-crisis-cells-stockpiles-evacuation-and-no-presence-by-hope.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed field security-and-continuity constitution** that separates risk assessment, travel and deployment clearance, duty-station roles, premises security, crisis management cells, incident logging, logistics and stockpiles, evacuation or hibernation choices, and continuity of records and core services — so territorial presence is sustained by visible duty-of-care and continuity architecture rather than by courage theater, local improvisation, or hope.
- `692-shared-regime-digital-and-cyber-operating-constitutions-system-owners-identity-and-access-admin-tiers-change-windows-incident-response-vulnerability-disclosure-backups-recovery-vendor-lanes-and-no-secretariat-by-shared-password.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed digital-and-cyber operating constitution** that separates system ownership, identity and access, privileged administration, change and release control, incident response, vulnerability disclosure, vendor and cloud access, backup and restoration, recovery targets, and degraded-mode continuity — so the regime is not actually run through shared passwords, orphan systems, incident backlog, or recovery theater.
- `694-shared-regime-statistics-and-indicator-constitutions-designation-methodology-metadata-revisions-quality-assurance-release-calendars-and-no-governance-by-number-theater.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed statistics-and-indicator constitution** that separates designated official series from exploratory analytics, indicator ownership from political sponsorship, methodology from messaging, metadata from headline numbers, revisions from corrections, and release discipline from communications convenience — so evidence does not decay into number theater, indicator shopping, or policy-by-dashboard without professional standards.
- `699-scope-spine-for-ideal-governments-seven-default-tiers-label-to-vocation-crosswalks-two-exception-ladders-and-no-new-tier-theory-every-time.md` — The archive should treat ideal government from micro-local to global as one reusable **scope spine** — micro-local witness-and-stewardship units, municipalities as the first complete governments of ordinary life, metropolitan bodies for shared urban systems, regions for territorial platforms and shared rule, nations as guarantor states, continental bodies as bounded compacts, and global institutions as treaty narrow waists — while mapping ambiguous labels like county, district, province, state, and union back to those archetypes and using collapsed-stack and shared-regime exception ladders where the default seven do not fit.
- `700-minimum-design-packet-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-archetype-vocation-boundary-kit-fiscal-proof-exception-ladder-upgrade-triggers-and-no-essay-length-restatement.md` — Any later archive note that claims what the ideal government at a given scope should be should default to one small **design packet** — name the scope archetype, state the vocation, define the boundary logic, specify the minimum complete kit, show the fiscal and capability proof, declare any exception ladder, and list upgrade or reversibility triggers — so the archive can compare designs, merge revisions, and stay compact without re-arguing the whole multilevel constitution every time.
- `701-adjudication-matrix-for-competing-ideal-governments-of-the-same-function-packet-comparison-dominance-tests-reversible-tie-breaks-and-no-scope-choice-by-ideology-alone.md` — When the archive faces several plausible claims about which scope should govern the same function, it should compare the rival **design packets** through one compact adjudication matrix — vocation fit, boundary honesty, minimum kit completeness, fiscal and capability proof, spillover handling, solidarity and rights-floor fit, democratic proportionality, reversibility, and machinery cost — so the archive can choose or bracket the better packet without collapsing into ideology, naming habit, or essay-length restatement.
- `702-unbundling-mixed-function-claims-before-scope-choice-lane-split-first-packet-second-rivalry-third-and-no-one-tier-answer-to-a-composite-field.md` — Before the archive decides which scope should ideally govern a field, it should first test whether the field is really a **composite bundle of different lanes with different scale logics**; if so, it should split the field into lane-sized claims, build packets for those lanes, and run rivalry only on the pieces that remain genuinely contested, rather than forcing one total jurisdictional answer onto a mixed-function question.
- `703-interface-packets-for-lane-typed-government-stacks-lead-lanes-handoffs-shared-facts-escalation-clocks-and-no-governance-by-glue-folklore.md` — Once the archive has split a composite field into lane-sized scope packets, it should also publish one **interface packet** for the resulting typed stack: name the lead for each lane, the handoff triggers between lanes, the shared facts and records that must travel, the timing and escalation rules, the fiscal and liability crosswalks, and the public route map, so distributed government does not collapse back into blame circulation, duplicate work, or quiet recentralization by whoever controls the glue.
- `704-control-plane-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-priorities-common-ledger-exception-queues-and-no-hidden-center-by-coordination.md` — Once the archive has split a field into lane-sized governments and published the seam rules between them, it should also publish one narrow **control-plane packet** for the field as a whole — naming the common goals, rights floors, shared metrics, review rhythm, exception queue, budget and capacity crosswalk, and upgrade triggers — so the stack can be steered and inspected as one public system without quietly inventing an undeclared super-tier that governs by coordination alone.
- `705-mode-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-normal-degraded-emergency-recovery-handback-clocks-and-no-permanent-government-by-exception.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, and a field control plane, it should also publish one **mode packet** for the field — naming normal, degraded, emergency, and recovery operation, the triggers for entering each mode, what powers and duties change, what rights and service floors remain non-negotiable, and what handback clock returns the stack to ordinary routing — so a stressed system does not quietly adopt emergency pathways as its permanent constitution.
- `706-repair-packets-for-recurrently-failing-government-fields-after-action-conversion-root-cause-ownership-funding-lanes-closure-proof-and-no-government-by-permanent-recovery-mode.md` — Lane-typed government fields that repeatedly re-enter **degraded, emergency, or recovery modes** should publish a typed **repair packet** that converts after-action learning into owned structural change — clearly separating quick corrective action from deeper fiscal, staffing, capital, digital, legal, or boundary repair — with recurrence triggers, service-floor protection, closure proof, and escalation when “temporary recovery” is becoming the field’s real constitution.
- `707-sunset-packets-for-obsolete-government-lanes-bodies-and-temporary-machinery-review-triggers-successor-homes-residue-registers-closure-proof-and-no-immortal-institutions-by-inherited-backlog.md` — Once a field has repair packets, it should also publish one **sunset packet** whenever review shows that a lane, body, or temporary governance machine no longer deserves to exist in live form — naming the trigger, the successor home or true extinction rule, the rights and service floors that still bind during wind-down, the residue register for cases, contracts, assets, staff, records, data, debt, and public-facing channels, the closure proof, and the reactivation rule — so obsolete institutions do not stay alive merely because they still have backlog, leases, websites, or logos.
- `708-evidence-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-shared-indicators-trigger-maps-blind-spot-registers-assurance-rhythm-and-no-government-by-dashboard-vibes.md` — Lane-typed government fields should publish one compact **evidence packet** that names the shared indicators, signal owners, trigger map, blind-spot register, and assurance rhythm used to judge the field — so control planes, mode shifts, repair packets, and sunset reviews run on explicit evidence with known gaps rather than on anecdotes, heroic operator memory, or dashboard theater.
- `709-challenge-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-entry-routes-complaints-petitions-second-look-lanes-feedback-duties-and-no-public-voice-by-consultation-theater.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, and an evidence packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **challenge packet** naming who may raise what kind of challenge, through which front door, with what triage into complaint, petition, appeal, ombuds, whistleblowing, or regulatory lanes, on what clocks, with what feedback and anti-retaliation duties, so the field can be corrected by the governed instead of merely observed by them.
- `710-participation-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-agenda-windows-method-fit-inclusion-duties-response-ledgers-and-no-public-input-by-one-off-hearing.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, an evidence packet, and a challenge packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **participation packet** naming which design and priority questions are open to public participation, at which policy-cycle phase, by which method, with which inclusion and response duties, so public input shapes the field before harm, drift, or redesign battles are forced into the complaint system.
- `711-oversight-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-audit-inspection-ombuds-parliamentary-scrutiny-follow-up-ledgers-and-no-self-certification-by-the-same-office.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, an evidence packet, a challenge packet, and a participation packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **oversight packet** naming which independent bodies outside the live control plane may inspect which questions, on what triggers and calendars, with what access powers, response duties, and follow-up ledger, so the field is not left certifying itself by the same office that designed, funded, or operated it.
- `712-amendment-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-change-classes-ratification-ladders-version-ledgers-drift-logs-and-no-field-redesign-by-memo.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, an evidence packet, challenge and participation packets, and an oversight packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **amendment packet** naming which changes are merely tuning and which are constitutional, who may propose them, what participation and scrutiny gates apply, what ratification ladder adopts them, when they take effect, and what version ledger plus drift log keeps the field from being redesigned by memo, queue custom, temporary exception, or software default.
- `713-delegation-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-principal-lane-reserved-powers-operator-chains-step-in-rights-and-no-public-duty-by-outsourced-wrapper.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, and amendment discipline for a field, it should also publish one narrow **delegation packet** saying which slice of the field is still constitutionally owned by the public lane, which execution work may be delegated to public bodies, contractors, concessionaires, nonprofits, co-operatives, or platforms, what powers remain non-delegable, what contract-management and records capacity the principal must retain, what step-in and handback rights keep continuity real, and what review route prevents public duty from disappearing into an outsourced wrapper.
- `714-fiscal-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-operating-base-equalization-spine-reserves-capital-lanes-and-no-government-by-grant-fog.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, and delegation rules for a field, it should also publish one narrow **fiscal packet** saying what recurring operating base actually funds the field, which lane holds budget and treasury authority, what equalization or solidarity rule corrects uneven burdens, what reserve and contingency ladder keeps shocks from becoming constitutional panic, what capital and debt lane is lawful, and what grants may supplement but not substitute for an honest money constitution.
- `715-capability-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-employer-lane-merit-floor-training-ladders-surge-rosters-and-no-government-by-borrowed-payroll.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, and a fiscal packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **capability packet** saying which lane is the employer of record and capability steward, what minimum in-house core the field must retain, what merit and qualification floor applies, what training and profession ladders sustain scarce skills, what secondment and surge rules are allowed, and what vacancy or churn triggers open repair or redesign — so the field does not rely on borrowed payroll, consultant memory, or permanent emergency staffing to remain governmental at all.
- `716-information-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-canonical-case-home-access-model-sharing-boundaries-retention-clocks-and-no-government-by-portal-shell.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, and a capability packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **information packet** saying where the field’s canonical case and record homes live, which surface is the system of record and which are only presentation or intake layers, what role-and-access model governs staff and delegates, what sharing boundaries and information agreements apply, what retention/export/handback rules preserve public memory, and what recovery path keeps the field governable when platforms, vendors, or host systems fail — so the field does not become government by portal shell, spreadsheet relay, or vendor-admin shadow.
- `717-asset-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-estate-fleet-equipment-condition-discipline-handback-and-no-government-by-orphan-assets.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, and an information packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **asset packet** saying which lane owns and stewards the field’s estate, fleet, equipment, depots, labs, stores, and critical spares; who holds custody, maintenance, calibration, and replacement duty; what condition and resilience floor applies; what lease, host-site, or operator dependencies exist; and what handback rule survives exit or transfer — so the field does not decay into government by orphan assets, lease camouflage, or maintenance exile.
- `718-service-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-whole-service-front-doors-route-classes-service-floors-continuity-and-no-government-by-front-door-scatter.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, an information packet, and an asset packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **service packet** saying what outcome the field’s service actually promises, which lane owns that promise, what front doors and route classes the public may use, what clocks and service floors bind, how channels and operators compose into one whole service, and what continuity and fallback rules survive overload, outage, provider failure, or redesign — so the field does not decay into government by front-door scatter, route roulette, or service-standard theater.
- `719-case-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-intake-triage-state-model-lineage-notice-duty-and-no-government-by-unofficial-casework.md` — Once the archive has a service packet for a lane-typed government field, it should also publish one narrow **case packet** saying what unit of work counts as a case, how a matter becomes one, what intake and triage rules apply before and after acknowledgement, which visible states and clocks bind, what lineage and notice duties survive pause, transfer, merge, withdrawal, supersession, or reopen, and where the authoritative status truth lives — so the field does not decay into government by unofficial casework, invisible queues, or closure by folklore.
- `720-decision-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-determination-class-reason-giving-effectivity-appeal-linkage-and-no-government-by-outcome-letter-alone.md` — Once the archive has service and case packets for a lane-typed government field, it should also publish one narrow **decision packet** saying what counts as a consequential determination, which decision classes exist, who may make and sign them, what minimum findings, reasons, legal basis, conditions, effect dates, implementation duties, and review links must travel with them, and how correction, withdrawal, supersession, and reconsideration preserve lineage — so the field does not decay into government by outcome letter alone, silent conditions, or appeal clocks detached from the act they challenge.
- `723-review-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-reconsideration-appeal-remand-interim-relief-finality-and-no-government-by-remedy-maze.md` — Once the archive has challenge, decision, notice, and effect packets for a field, it should also publish one narrow **review packet** saying which second-look lanes exist, which acts must pass through reconsideration before appeal and which may go straight outward, who hears each route, what record and standard of review apply, what interim relief or stay is available, what remand or substitution powers exist, and when finality blocks endless reopening — so the field does not decay into government by remedy maze, sponsor-friendly reconsideration, or hidden no-review zones.
- `725-ideal-governance-stack-from-block-to-planet-territorial-tiers-functional-authorities-compact-unions-and-no-empty-tier-fetish.md` — An ideal governance stack from block to planet is not a neat ladder of identical states but a mixed constitutional order: micro-local bodies for witness and stewardship, municipalities for ordinary place government, metropolitan and regional tiers where urban systems or territorial platforms are real, nations for equal citizenship and solidarity, continental compacts for recurrent cross-border problems, global institutions for peace, alerting, commons, and interoperability, and bounded functional authorities in between whenever a watershed, corridor, grid, basin, port, or referral network plainly outruns ordinary administrative geography.
- `726-default-function-routing-table-for-ideal-governments-everyday-place-shared-systems-guarantor-duties-compact-unions-and-treaty-narrow-waists.md` — The archive should keep one compact **default routing table** for common public functions: route witness, stewardship, and micro-commons to micro-local units; ordinary daily place government to municipalities; shared urban systems to metropolitan government or narrow utilities; basin, hospital, university, corridor, and ecological platforms to regions or typed functional authorities; equal citizenship, redistribution, macro-stability, and constitutional settlement to nations; bounded cross-border markets, mobility, and corridors to compact unions; and genuinely planetary peace, alerting, interoperability, and commons baselines to treaty-bound global narrow waists — while forcing mixed fields to declare lead scope, support scopes, fiscal logic, and upgrade tests instead of choosing a level from scratch every time.
- `727-routing-override-triad-for-ideal-governments-downward-intimacy-upward-guarantees-sideways-functional-authorities-and-no-scope-choice-by-prestige.md` — Once the archive has a default routing table for common public functions, departures from that default should occur only through one explicit override triad: **downward** when intimacy, place variance, or rapid correction dominates; **upward** when rights floors, solidarity, macro-risk, security, or interoperability dominates; and **sideways** into a bounded functional authority when the real system footprint mismatches ordinary civic territory.
- `728-sideways-authority-packets-for-ideal-governments-bounded-remit-footprint-logic-board-fiscal-lane-review-clocks-and-no-functional-wrapper-without-constitutional-kit.md` — When the archive routes a function **sideways** into a bounded functional authority rather than into an ordinary territorial tier, it should default to one compact **sideways-authority packet** naming the real system footprint, the exact remit and exclusions, the principal public lane that still owns the wider constitutional bargain, the legitimacy and fiscal model, the review and participation routes, and the upgrade-or-exit triggers — so basins, corridors, grids, ports, referral networks, and similar in-between institutions stay governable without pretending to be full territorial governments or dissolving into quango fog.
- `729-ratification-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-proof-weights-consent-ladders-double-legitimacy-and-no-function-move-by-wrong-organ.md` — Once the archive has a default routing table (`726`), an override grammar (`727`), and a minimum sideways-authority packet (`728`), it should also keep one compact **ratification packet** for materially moving a function across scopes, especially where protected local or regional self-government, delegated tasks, boundary effects, or treaty-bound compact obligations are in play: classify the move by constitutional depth, scale the proof burden accordingly, require assent from the organs and publics whose protected bargain is being touched, and refuse any rescoping by executive convenience, grant coercion, software default, or after-the-fact folklore.
- `730-continuity-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-staff-budget-records-cases-contracts-assets-cutover-and-no-ratification-by-theory-alone.md` — Once the archive has a default routing table (`726`), an override grammar (`727`), a sideways-authority packet (`728`), and a ratification packet for moving functions across scopes (`729`), it should also keep one compact **continuity packet** for the move itself: no scope shift is constitutionally honest until the polity can show who employs the people, holds the money, owns the contracts, keeps the files, answers the live cases, preserves the review routes, and runs the cutover without dropping rights, services, or accountability.
- `731-cutover-witness-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-effective-state-old-holder-new-holder-exception-ledger-and-no-transfer-by-folklore.md` — Once the archive has a continuity packet for scope shifts (`730`), it should also keep one compact **cutover witness packet** for the handoff moment itself: every materially consequential move across scopes should leave behind one contemporaneous public-and-reviewable witness saying what changed, when it changed, which holder lost authority, which holder gained authority, what remained transitional, which queues, records, contracts, and budgets were still in flight, which exceptions stayed live, and what fallback path still existed — so later review does not have to reconstruct the transfer from rumor, screenshots, or contradictory portal residue.
- `732-transitional-hosting-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-host-of-record-command-boundaries-forwarding-duties-expiry-clocks-and-no-sovereignty-by-borrowed-runtime.md` — Once the archive has a continuity packet (`730`) and a cutover witness packet (`731`), it should also keep one compact **transitional hosting packet** for the awkward but common period when legal authority has moved while some systems, staff, channels, or operational substrate are still being hosted by the predecessor or a third party: every such bridge should name the principal public holder, the temporary host, the exact host-only powers, the forwarding and cure duties, the money and service-floor terms, the evidence and logging boundary, the break-glass path, and the hard expiry or re-clearance clock — so a borrowed runtime never silently becomes the real constitution.
- `733-bridge-closure-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-host-release-channel-retirement-records-signoff-and-no-temporary-forever.md` — Once the archive has a transitional-hosting packet (`732`), it should also require one compact **bridge-closure packet** before anybody may claim the scope shift is operationally complete: classify the closure state, retire or rewire every legacy front door, release host-side powers and keys, freeze and hand over the final evidence package, settle the residual exceptions ledger, and refuse to relabel an unresolved dependency as “complete” merely because the cutover date has passed.
- `734-post-closure-stabilization-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-independent-live-window-rebound-triggers-review-metrics-and-no-independence-by-one-quiet-week.md` — Once the archive has a bridge-closure packet (`733`), it should also require one compact **post-closure stabilization packet** before anybody treats the new holder as independently settled: declare a bounded independent-live window, name the minimum service, control, evidence, and public-route signals that must stay inside floor, classify any rebound toward host-side dependence, and refuse to infer real independence from a brief quiet period.
- `735-rollback-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-failed-stabilization-return-authority-pending-matters-record-lineage-and-no-reversal-by-headline-alone.md` — Once the archive can say how a function should be routed (`726`-`728`), ratified (`729`), kept continuous (`730`), witnessed at cutover (`731`), temporarily hosted (`732`), cleanly closed (`733`), and tested through a bounded independent-live window (`734`), it should also keep one compact **rollback packet** for the case where the successor does not hold: classify the rollback type, name the interim principal and public route, preserve the legal and evidentiary state of pending matters, move money/staff/systems/keys with the reversal rather than by headline alone, and refuse both automatic restoration folklore and disguised permanent recentralization.
- `736-temporary-neutral-custody-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-contested-handoffs-rights-bearing-queues-record-spines-credential-escrow-and-no-settlement-by-possession.md` — Once the archive can say how a function should be routed (`726`-`728`), ratified (`729`), kept continuous (`730`), witnessed at cutover (`731`), temporarily hosted (`732`), cleanly closed (`733`), tested through an independent-live window (`734`), and rolled back when stabilization fails (`735`), it should also keep one compact **temporary neutral-custody packet** for the harder interval where neither old holder nor new holder can honestly be treated as fully settled: appoint a bounded custodian for named control surfaces, preserve the public route and evidentiary spine, freeze or escrow high-risk powers, keep pending matters legible, and refuse to let mere possession of live systems, records, or credentials masquerade as constitutional settlement.
- `739-residual-estate-packets-for-post-custody-government-closeout-shells-claims-record-access-financial-tail-review-clocks-and-no-ghost-state-by-leftover-residue.md` — Once the archive can place named surfaces into temporary neutral custody (`736`), release them out again (`737`), and discharge the custodian itself (`738`), it should also keep one compact **residual-estate packet** for the narrower afterlife that sometimes honestly remains: a typed closeout shell for surviving claims, residual funds, record-access duties, litigation or audit tails, and other bounded obligations, with one public route, one residue ledger, one accountable owner, and one termination proof so a leftover estate does not quietly become a ghost state by residue.
- `740-residual-estate-termination-certificates-for-post-custody-government-closeout-shells-zero-residue-proof-final-routing-and-no-ghost-state-by-never-ending-tail.md` — Once the archive can admit a bounded residual estate after custody discharge (`739`), it should also keep one compact **residual-estate termination certificate** proving when that tail is actually over: zero open residue or explicitly rehomed last fragments, final accounts and closure disclosures, exhausted or lawfully rerouted claims, sealed record and disclosure homes, revoked residual powers, retired public routes, and one durable historical certificate — so a closeout shell cannot linger forever as ghost state by never-ending tail.
- `748-historical-object-boundary-repair-packets-for-retired-government-bodies-scopes-and-shells-split-merge-creator-links-and-no-one-dead-authority-by-cataloguing-accident.md` — Once the archive can absorb tombstones into grouped historical registers (`745`), move those grouped registers across homes (`746`), and restore one absorbed entry back into a standalone memorial surface (`747`), it should also keep one compact **historical-object-boundary-repair packet**: one bounded proof object for the harder case where the memorial object boundary itself turned out to be wrong — one entry actually conflated several distinct dead authorities, or several entries were really one dead authority all along — so the polity can split, merge, or relink historical objects without rewriting closure history, losing aliases, or mistaking successor routing for object identity.
- `749-ideal-governments-by-scope-micro-local-voice-municipal-competence-county-rural-pooling-metropolitan-systems-regional-platforms-national-solidarity-continental-compacts-and-global-narrow-waists.md` — An ideal multi-level order should not ask every scope to impersonate a sovereign state; it should give each scope the **minimum complete governing kit** that matches its real problem class — micro-local voice and upkeep, municipal everyday place government, county or rural pooling where density is low, metropolitan systems democracy where spillovers are urban, regional territorial platforms and shared rule, national rights-and-solidarity government, continental problem-specific compacts, and global treaty narrow waists for peace, planetary commons, and interoperability.
- `750-polity-morphology-archetypes-for-ideal-government-stacks-dense-metro-polycentric-federal-sparse-archipelagic-and-cross-border-overlay-with-no-one-world-default.md` — The archive should stop implying that one ideal government stack fits every country-form: before designing tiers, it should classify the polity’s **morphology** — dense metro-dominant, polycentric unitary, federal or plurinational, sparse and peripheral, archipelagic, or border-interlocked — and then choose the thinnest honest stack for that morphology rather than copying one universal ladder.
- `751-regional-tier-necessity-tests-territorial-platforms-shared-rule-asymmetry-collapse-and-no-map-inheritance-as-constitution.md` — A regional, provincial, state, or similar tier should be treated as **necessary** only when at least one of four conditions is real — a major territorial platform, a federal or plurinational shared-rule bargain, a very large sparse-area catchment, or a durable asymmetry the constitution must recognize — and otherwise the archive should prefer either stronger municipalities, metropolitan government, bounded functional authorities, or honest scope collapse over decorative regionalism.
- `752-government-formation-and-removal-by-scope-micro-local-recall-municipal-manager-confidence-metro-investiture-parliamentary-default-constructive-no-confidence-fixed-terms-and-no-dual-democratic-command.md` — Ideal governments should choose formation and removal rules that create **one legible confidence chain** at each scope — recallable stewards for micro-local bodies, elected-council plus removable manager or mayoral executive in municipalities, explicit investiture and termination rules for metropolitan or regional governments with real power, parliamentary or assembly-confidence default for most large multi-party states, and fixed-term presidential exceptions only where the system can safely absorb dual mandates without chronic collision.
- `754-head-of-state-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-no-separate-crown-below-national-scale-ceremonial-arbiters-collective-headship-reserve-powers-on-rails-and-no-duplicate-democratic-apex.md` — A separate head of state is not a universal ingredient of ideal government; it is justified mainly when a polity needs a **symbolic or arbitral apex distinct from the governing executive**, and where that office is mostly formal it should usually be indirectly chosen, tightly bounded, continuity-safe, and designed not to create a second competing democratic command.
- `763-caretaker-government-and-pre-election-restraint-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-routine-administration-incoming-government-consultation-major-appointments-freeze-emergency-carve-outs-and-no-mandate-stretch-between-verdict-and-handover.md` — Ideal governments should treat dissolution, hung-parliament bargaining, post-election transition, and imminent change of government as **a distinct continuity-with-restraint mode rather than business as usual**: outgoing governments should continue routine administration and urgent protection of the public, but major policy, appointments, contracts, publicity, and irreversible international or fiscal commitments should pause, narrow, or move only after consultation with the likely successor, so no one stretches an expiring mandate through the handover gap.
- `764-political-finance-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-small-donor-pluralism-real-time-disclosure-spending-ceilings-audit-trails-digital-ad-archives-and-no-office-by-money-primary.md` — Ideal governments should treat political finance as **a bounded democratic input rather than a private market for public power**: parties and candidates should be able to raise and spend enough to compete, but large-donor dependency, opaque third-party spending, cash fog, and untraceable digital advertising should be constrained through donation rules, proportionate public funding, timely disclosure, auditable accounts, independent oversight, and enforceable ceilings where they fit, so office is not functionally auctioned to whoever can finance political attention most aggressively.
- `773-administrative-appeal-and-tribunal-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-reasons-file-access-internal-review-suspensive-relief-merits-vs-legality-review-and-no-rights-by-one-shot-decision.md` — Ideal governments should treat administrative appeals and tribunals as **the ordinary second-look constitution of the state**: when public authorities make decisions that affect rights, status, money, permits, benefits, penalties, or obligations, people should receive reasons, access to the relevant file, a prompt internal reconsideration or equivalent first review where appropriate, and then an independent appeal or tribunal lane with powers proportionate to the stakes, so administrative authority does not become a one-shot command enforced mainly by cost, speed, and user exhaustion.
- `777-execution-of-administrative-and-judicial-decisions-against-public-authorities-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-compliance-clocks-budget-home-escalation-and-no-judgment-by-non-execution.md` — Ideal governments should treat **execution of administrative and judicial decisions against public authorities** as part of the rule-of-law core rather than as post-judgment housekeeping: when a ministry, municipality, agency, regulator, police body, prison authority, benefits office, land registrar, or treasury loses, the system should have clear compliance clocks, named responsible officials, budget and payment homes, interest and penalty rules, supervisory escalation, and user-visible follow-up so the state cannot turn delay, fragmentation, or lack-of-funds claims into a second victory after losing on the merits.
- `779-interim-relief-and-urgent-public-law-protection-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-stays-preservation-orders-irreparable-harm-clocks-and-no-rights-by-fait-accompli.md` — Ideal governments should treat **interim relief as ordinary rule-of-law protection against irreversible harm and fait accompli rather than as exotic emergency indulgence**: public-law systems should offer typed stays, preservation orders, temporary mandatory measures, rapid hearing lanes, and in especially irreversible domains default suspensive effect, so review remains capable of protecting rights before demolition, removal, disclosure, eviction, exclusion, or other irreversible state action has already done its work.
- `785-administrative-fact-finding-evidentiary-burden-and-duty-to-assist-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-ex-officio-records-proof-alternatives-and-no-rights-by-impossible-evidence.md` — Ideal governments should allocate **administrative fact-finding and evidentiary burden** honestly: public authorities should investigate material facts, fetch what the state already knows, disclose the adverse case before deciding, assist people through proof obstacles they cannot reasonably clear alone, and never win by impossible-document demands, evidentiary surprise, or burden shifting disguised as procedure.
- `790-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-answer-key-micro-local-voice-municipal-full-kit-metropolitan-democracy-regional-platforms-national-guarantees-continental-compacts-and-global-narrow-waists.md` — The archive should now treat the question **what would the ideal government at each scope be?** as having one default answer-key: **micro-local institutions for voice, witness, and upkeep; municipalities as the first full-spectrum governments of ordinary life; metropolitan governments for shared urban systems; regional or provincial governments for major territorial platforms and shared rule; national government for equal citizenship, solidarity, macro-capacity, and constitutional guarantee; continental bodies for bounded cross-border compacts; and global bodies for narrow treaty-bound coordination of peace, commons, alerting, and interoperability**.
- `791-benchmark-cards-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-vocation-fit-kit-floors-fiscal-congruence-review-lanes-tripwires-and-no-admiration-without-scoring.md` — The archive should pair its canonical scope matrix and answer-key notes with one compact **benchmark-card format** for each scope — vocation fit, minimum complete kit, fiscal and capability congruence, spillover or solidarity fit, review and remedy integrity, participation and scrutiny proportionality, and named upgrade or handback tripwires — so real constitutions, reform proposals, and case studies can be compared tersely against the ideal stack without reopening the whole theory.
- `792-stress-test-and-drill-cards-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-essential-service-continuity-command-legibility-fiscal-buffers-rights-discipline-rescoping-signals-and-no-paper-constitution-by-calm-weather.md` — The archive should pair its ideal-government answer key and benchmark cards with one compact **stress-test and drill-card format** for each scope — essential-service continuity, command and escalation legibility, reserve and surge discipline, intergovernmental handoff integrity, legality and rights restraint under pressure, public communication, and recovery or handback triggers — so governments are judged not only by their steady-state design but by whether they remain honest under flood, blackout, outbreak, fiscal shock, cyber disruption, or constitutional strain.
- `794-sequenced-upgrade-paths-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-first-honest-steps-bridge-arrangements-cutover-gates-and-no-full-stack-redesign-by-manifesto.md` — When a real polity is far from the archive’s ideal scope stack, reform should move through a sequenced upgrade path: **make the current arrangement honest first, repair the minimum complete kit and fiscal congruence next, constitutionalise any bridge institutions that are already exercising real power, transfer functions only with continuity proof, and attempt deeper territorial or constitutional redesign only after the operating spine is real**.
- `796-intervention-ladders-for-failing-governments-of-each-scope-support-first-proportional-supervision-special-measures-handback-clocks-and-no-permanent-emergency-custody.md` — When a government-by-scope arrangement keeps failing its benchmark, stress, maintenance, or proof duties, the archive should not jump straight from diagnosis to permanent takeover. It should use one compact **intervention ladder**: **support first, escalate by law and proportionality, separate own-competence supervision from delegated-task control, keep any special measures temporary and reviewable, and pair every intervention with a handback or formal rescoping test so rescue does not harden into quiet permanent custody**.
- `797-contestability-ladders-for-scope-governance-benchmark-objections-trigger-appeals-intervention-review-handback-denials-and-no-constitutional-maintenance-by-self-marking.md` — The archive should pair its answer-key, benchmark, stress-test, maintenance, upgrade-path, public-proof, and intervention notes with one compact **contestability ladder**: **benchmark classifications, trigger openings or closures, stress findings used for redesign, intervention orders, renewals, handback denials, and other stack-shaping judgments should all carry typed standing, reasons, interim-relief logic, and final independent review, so governments do not maintain the constitutional stack by marking their own homework and calling the result settled**.
- `799-sunset-renewal-graduation-and-burial-rules-for-temporary-scope-arrangements-bridges-pilots-derogations-special-measures-and-no-shadow-constitution-by-serial-extension.md` — Whenever a polity uses a **temporary scope arrangement** — bridge body, host authority, pilot, derogation, emergency measure, temporary exemption, special administrator, or other exceptional workaround — the archive should require one compact **sunset / renewal / graduation rule**: **declare the default end state at the start, time-limit the arrangement, raise the proof burden on every renewal, force legitimacy and finance upgrades before any “temporary” body becomes ordinary government, and archive the ending publicly so shadow constitutions cannot survive by serial extension**.
- `802-management-responses-and-corrective-action-ledgers-for-scope-governance-finding-by-finding-owners-dependencies-budget-closure-proof-and-no-verdict-without-a-repair-docket.md` — The archive should pair its assessment-mission and finding-register notes with one compact **management-response grammar**: **every material scope finding should receive a finding-by-finding response that states acceptance posture, named owner at the right scope, dependency chain, budget and legal posture, delivery clock, closure proof, and escalation rule, so review does not end in literary recommendations, political nodding, or an unowned pile of next steps**.
- `803-close-out-verification-and-reopen-rules-for-scope-governance-repair-ledgers-mid-term-checks-field-revisit-residual-risk-and-no-closure-by-self-certification.md` — The archive should pair its finding-register and management-response notes with one compact **close-out and verification grammar**: **every material scope repair item should face a typed follow-up review that tests closure proof against live conditions, declares residual risk, decides close / continue / reopen / rescope, and names the next verification clock, so corrective-action ledgers do not turn into self-closing spreadsheets or polite fiction**.
- `804-tracer-routes-and-lived-path-verification-for-scope-governance-user-journeys-fund-flows-case-walks-handoff-tests-and-no-constitution-by-org-chart.md` — The archive should pair its assessment-mission, finding-register, management-response, and close-out notes with one compact **tracer-route grammar**: **every serious scope review should follow a small set of real or lawfully simulated paths — case, payment, referral, complaint, permit, incident, data handoff, or handback — across institutions, clocks, and records, so governments are not judged only by statutes, org charts, or curated meetings instead of by the routes people and work actually travel**.
- `808-calibration-packs-moderation-loops-and-precedent-banks-for-scope-assessments-score-anchors-difficult-case-conferences-documented-departures-and-no-benchmark-by-reviewer-mood.md` — The archive should pair its benchmark, mission, evidence-register, and mission-integrity notes with one compact **review-calibration grammar**: **every serious scope assessment should keep a small calibration pack with lane-specific score anchors, worked examples, threshold splits, precedent notes, moderation checkpoints, and documented departures, so that different review teams can reach comparably disciplined judgments without collapsing everything into one blended score or one charismatic reviewer’s mood**.
- `809-research-frontier-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-settled-defaults-live-thresholds-morphology-uncertainty-fiscal-floor-tests-legitimacy-triggers-and-no-false-precision-by-constitutional-confidence-theater.md` — The archive should now separate **settled default doctrine** from **live research questions**: it can state with high confidence the vocation, minimum kit, and anti-cosplay limit of each scope, but it should keep threshold questions — when a functional city truly needs metro democracy, when sparse territories need county-style pooling, when a region is a real platform rather than decorative duplication, how much fiscal congruence is enough, when intervention should trigger, and how thick upper-tier institutions may become — inside one compact research frontier rather than pretending the whole stack is equally settled.
- `810-threshold-dossiers-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-metro-triggers-county-pooling-regional-platform-proof-fiscal-floors-legitimacy-thickness-and-no-tier-thickening-by-anecdote.md` — When the archive reaches a **live threshold question** rather than a settled scope doctrine question, it should require one compact **threshold dossier**: a declared threshold claim, the right territory and comparator cohort, a small set of named evidence lanes, visible contradiction residue, and a provisional confidence statement, so judgments such as **when metro democracy is now required, when sparse territories need pooled county-scale service backbones, when a region is a real platform, or when a lower tier is fiscally non-hollow** are made by typed evidence rather than by population fetish, prestige case imitation, or crisis anecdote.
- `812-institutional-form-choice-ladders-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-thin-connectors-shared-service-backbones-bounded-authorities-general-purpose-tiers-and-no-new-tier-by-spillover-alone.md` — When the archive has already established that a cross-boundary problem is real, it should choose institutional form through one compact **choice ladder**: use a **thin connector** when alignment and information-sharing are enough; a **shared-service backbone** when capacity pooling is the real need; a **bounded functional authority** when one system needs continuous cross-boundary operations or asset stewardship; and a **general-purpose elected tier** only when recurring distributive, land-use, borrowing, coercive, or multi-sector balancing powers make thinner forms constitutionally dishonest.
- `813-legitimacy-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-delegated-councils-principal-owned-backbones-double-key-authorities-directly-elected-tiers-and-no-heavy-power-by-convenience-composition.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, it should also be able to say **what legitimacy chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should be run by delegated elected principals with no hidden hard powers, shared-service backbones should remain clearly owned by the member governments whose duties they support, bounded functional authorities should carry an elected anchor plus explicit double-key gates for major debt, rule, boundary, or remit changes, and general-purpose territorial tiers should normally rest on directly elected chambers with their own scrutiny and executive responsibility rather than on convenience boards pretending to carry full constitutional weight.
- `814-fiscal-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-dues-and-service-payments-assigned-revenues-equalization-keys-capital-lanes-and-no-heavy-power-by-shadow-treasury.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary form is honest** and **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what fiscal chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should live on modest dues and project-preparation money with no disguised distributive budget, shared-service backbones should run on principal-owned service payments and declared cost-sharing plus reserve rules, bounded functional authorities should use assigned revenues, user charges, or rule-bound transfers matched to their narrow charter with explicit capital discipline, and general-purpose territorial tiers should have a public budget constitution with own-source or rule-bound shared revenues, equalization, and visible borrowing limits rather than living by discretionary grants, annual pleas, or off-book vehicles.
- `815-administrative-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-host-secretariats-principal-owned-backbones-chartered-operators-records-homes-and-no-heavy-power-by-borrowed-bureaucracy.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, and **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what administrative chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should use small secretariats with no hidden command over member administrations, shared-service backbones should keep declared principals, employer-of-record rules, records homes, and service agreements, bounded functional authorities should have chartered operating cores with explicit staffing, asset, procurement, and incident-command authority, and general-purpose territorial tiers should normally own their own civil-service, records, and operating spine rather than ruling through borrowed host bureaucracy.
- `816-oversight-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-member-scrutiny-external-audit-ombuds-routes-judicial-review-and-no-heavy-power-by-self-marking.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **who owns it**, **how money moves through it**, and **where its operating spine lives**, it should also be able to say **what oversight chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should remain mainly reviewable through the member governments that delegate into them, shared-service backbones should preserve visible principal-side scrutiny plus independent audit and complaint routes, bounded functional authorities should carry named external audit, maladministration review, legality or regulatory checks, and judicial remedy proportionate to their power, and general-purpose territorial tiers should own a full public oversight constitution rather than marking themselves through internal committees alone.
- `817-participation-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-open-dockets-hearings-user-councils-deliberative-mini-publics-response-ledgers-and-no-heavy-power-by-consultation-theater.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **who owns it**, **how money moves through it**, **where its operating spine lives**, and **where scrutiny and redress live**, it should also be able to say **what participation chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should publish open dockets and simple input windows rather than staging fake popular mandates, shared-service backbones should run structured user and accessibility input without pretending pooled operations are a substitute for elected politics, bounded functional authorities should carry recurring hearings and response duties plus deliberative methods where long-horizon tradeoffs justify them, and general-purpose territorial tiers should own a full participation constitution rather than borrowing legitimacy from consultation theater.
- `818-information-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-shared-facts-observatories-record-homes-official-statistics-links-publication-calendars-and-no-heavy-power-by-private-dashboard.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, and **what participation chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what information chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should use open shared-indicator rooms and light observatories, shared-service backbones should keep principal-readable service telemetry plus declared case and record routes, bounded functional authorities should keep authoritative operational data homes with method notes and publication calendars, and general-purpose territorial tiers should carry a fuller public-knowledge constitution rather than governing through host-held or vendor-held dashboards.
- `819-boundary-and-membership-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-accession-gates-territory-rules-amendment-thickness-exit-protocols-dissolution-paths-and-no-map-by-one-way-ratchet.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, and **what information chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should use open and reversible participation with no hidden territorial claim, shared-service backbones should declare member classes, accession formulas, notice periods, and unwind rules, bounded functional authorities should use chartered territories plus staged accession and constrained exit, and general-purpose territorial tiers should rely on statutory boundary change with public consultation, transition machinery, and no map by one-way ratchet.
- `820-decision-rule-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-ordinary-majorities-qualified-majorities-unanimity-reserves-deadlock-breakers-and-no-heavy-power-by-procedural-veto.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, **what information chain belongs to it**, and **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what decision-rule chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should seek consensus for advisory work and require visible member ratification for anything binding, shared-service backbones should use ordinary-majority operating rules with reserved supermajority or member-ratification gates for portfolio, burden, and liability shifts, bounded functional authorities should use public standing orders with ordinary-majority defaults plus qualified-majority or double-key gates for tariffs, debt, land, remit, and boundary changes, and general-purpose territorial tiers should govern by ordinary democratic majorities with narrowly cabined supermajority reserves and explicit deadlock routes rather than by permanent veto geography.
- `821-dispute-resolution-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-negotiation-ladders-mediation-expert-determination-jurisdiction-maps-continuity-orders-and-no-heavy-power-by-hostage-dispute.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, **what information chain belongs to it**, **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**, and **what decision-rule chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what dispute-resolution chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should rely on recorded negotiation and visible member-side escalation, shared-service backbones should use negotiation-first ladders with mediation, technical determination, continuity protection, and public-law endpoints, bounded functional authorities should publish jurisdiction maps and interim continuity orders, and general-purpose territorial tiers should rely on ordinary justice and constitutional routes rather than permanent bargaining by hostage dispute.
- `822-asset-and-liability-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-member-owned-infrastructure-ring-fenced-balance-sheets-handback-maps-contingent-obligations-and-no-heavy-power-by-orphaned-balance-sheet.md` — When the archive has already established that a cross-boundary problem is real, chosen the honest form, and said who governs, pays, operates, votes, and hears disputes, it should still require one compact **asset-and-liability chain**: thin connectors should own almost nothing beyond trivial co-ordination tools; shared-service backbones should keep political title with the principals unless a clearly bounded common vehicle is justified; bounded functional authorities may hold and steward system-critical assets and named liabilities inside a ring-fenced public balance sheet; and general-purpose territorial tiers should carry visible asset, debt, reserve, and handback constitutions rather than hiding real sovereignty in host property, off-book obligations, or exit chaos.
- `823-contracting-boundary-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-light-support-buying-principal-owned-commissioning-chartered-concessions-change-control-and-no-heavy-power-by-contract-escape-hatch.md` — When the archive has already established that a cross-boundary problem is real, chosen the honest form, and said who governs, pays, operates, votes, hears disputes, owns the assets, and can unwind the map, it should still require one compact **contracting-boundary chain**: thin connectors may buy only light support and must not become hidden commissioners of core public systems; shared-service backbones may buy pooled administrative tools and support services while political title remains visibly with the principals; bounded functional authorities may procure, franchise, or concession the named system they are chartered to govern, but only through a visible commissioner spine, hard change-control, and full public review; and general-purpose territorial tiers may use contracts as delivery instruments without letting procurement, concessions, PPPs, or managed-service deals become constitutional escape hatches for powers that should remain politically owned.
- `824-regulatory-and-enforcement-boundary-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-signal-routing-joined-up-inspections-bounded-permitting-public-sanctions-and-no-heavy-power-by-shared-badge.md` — When the archive has already established that a cross-boundary problem is real, chosen the honest form, and said who governs, pays, operates, votes, publishes, contracts, owns, and can unwind the arrangement, it should still require one compact **regulatory-and-enforcement-boundary chain**: thin connectors may align standards proposals, share risk signals, and route cases but must not issue permits or sanctions in their own name; shared-service backbones may pool intake, inspection support, and specialist process while the political principals retain visible legal title to permissions and coercive acts; bounded functional authorities may license, inspect, direct, and sanction only inside a named public remit with risk-based proportionality, separation from operation, and live review routes; and general-purpose territorial tiers may carry broader permitting and enforcement constitutions without letting host badges, fee addiction, or delegated vendor discipline become hidden sovereignty.
- `825-regime-form-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-steward-assemblies-municipal-administration-metropolitan-mandates-regional-parliamentarism-national-confidence-and-global-narrow-waists.md` — The archive should answer the question **what regime form should govern at each scope?** with a scale-matched default set rather than one constitutional idol: assembly-and-stewardship at micro-local scale, elected local democracy plus professional administration in municipalities, directly legitimated metropolitan government for real urban systems, assembly-confidence regional government where a region genuinely carries platform functions, parliamentary or assembly-confidence national government unless a strong case for dual-mandate presidentialism is proved, bounded plurilateral unions built around shared-rule institutions rather than cloned statehood, and globally a narrow-waist charter order rather than a world state.
- `826-mandate-source-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-assembly-voice-council-confidence-metro-public-mandates-regional-investiture-national-confidence-and-treaty-delegation.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should governing authority at each scope get its mandate?** with scale-matched defaults rather than a direct-election fetish: assembly voice and recallable stewardship at micro-local scale, elected councils as the primary democratic source in municipalities, whole-territory public mandates for metropolitan governments that can bind a real urban system, assembly-invested regional government where a region genuinely carries platform functions, parliamentary or assembly-confidence national government as the default source of executive authority, and treaty- or charter-derived delegation with bounded parliamentary and public complements for plurilateral and global bodies.
- `827-mandate-duration-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-short-local-rotation-municipal-and-metro-stability-national-renewal-windows-and-treaty-review-clocks.md` — The archive should answer the question **how long should governing mandates last at each scope?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one calendar idol: short and recallable mandates for micro-local stewardship, medium terms for municipalities and metropolitan governments that need enough runway to budget and deliver, regional and national renewal windows that are usually long enough to govern but short enough to correct, and plurilateral or global bodies that live on fixed review and reauthorization clocks rather than ambient permanence.
- `828-mandate-exit-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-recall-municipal-dismissal-confidence-loss-bounded-dissolution-and-treaty-lapse.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should governing mandates end when they fail, expire early, or lose their public basis?** with scope-matched exit defaults rather than one romantic removal myth: simple recall or replacement for tiny steward bodies, council-centered dismissal and tightly bounded mayoral removal at municipal scale, explicit confidence-loss and successor grammar for metropolitan and regional governments with real power, bounded parliamentary exit and dissolution rules for most national governments, and fixed reauthorization, for-cause removal, or treaty-lapse rules for plurilateral and global bodies that must never drift into ambient permanence.
- `829-selection-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-open-local-voice-proportional-councils-metro-wide-elections-federal-shared-rule-and-delegated-global-seats.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should offices and chambers at each scope actually be chosen?** with scope-matched selection defaults rather than one ballot fetish: open assemblies, simple ward contests, recallable delegates, and rotation where the unit is genuinely face-to-face; proportional or semi-proportional municipal councils plus merit administration where everyday city government begins; whole-territory metropolitan elections where metro power is real; regional and national lower chambers chosen by proportional rules strong enough to reflect plural publics, with territorial second chambers only where shared rule is real; and continental or global bodies chosen mainly through treaty delegation, indirect parliamentary composition, and merit-based secretariat appointment rather than fake world-state plebiscites.
- `830-decision-rule-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-majorities-municipal-ordinary-rules-federal-double-keys-and-no-fake-global-unanimity.md` — The archive should answer the question **what internal decision rule should usually govern at each scope once the body is real?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one voting fetish: **micro-local institutions should seek rough consensus but fall back cheaply to ordinary majority; municipalities, metropolitan governments, and most regional and national lower chambers should decide ordinary business by ordinary majority with reserved supermajorities for constitutional, territorial, debt, or rights-sensitive thresholds; shared-rule chambers may justify double keys where constituent units are genuinely co-authors of the settlement; and continental or global bodies should treat consensus as a discipline of accommodation, not a veto constitution, reserving unanimity only for narrow membership-, treaty-, or sovereignty-touching classes**.
- `831-fiscal-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-tiny-commons-municipal-own-source-metro-shares-regional-equalization-national-solidarity-and-treaty-dues.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should each scope ordinarily be financed?** with scale-matched fiscal defaults rather than one treasury fetish: micro-local bodies should live on tiny discretionary funds, member contributions, and visible small grants rather than debt or payroll empires; municipalities should be the first level with meaningful own-source revenue, rule-bound transfers, ordinary operating reserves, and capital access for durable local assets; metropolitan governments should use assigned revenue shares, formula transfers, and user-charge lanes where systems justify them rather than annual pleas from member municipalities; regional and provincial governments should combine own revenues, shared taxes, equalization, and platform-scale capital budgets; national government should carry the broad tax base, macro-stabilization, and solidarity machinery; and continental or global bodies should usually rely on treaty dues, assessed contributions, and tightly bounded common finance rather than counterfeit world taxation or donor-whim constitutions.
- `832-oversight-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-witness-municipal-scrutiny-metro-audit-national-watchdogs-and-treaty-review.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should each scope ordinarily be scrutinized and corrected once it has real public authority?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one watchdog fetish: **micro-local bodies should rely mainly on open meetings, visible records, rotation, and cheap escalation rather than a miniature oversight state; municipalities should be the first level with a full public oversight kit of chamber scrutiny, independent external audit, complaint or ombuds routes, disclosure, and ordinary legality review; metropolitan and regional governments should own equally real audit and redress lanes rather than borrowing them permanently from a host city or ministry; national government should carry the fullest fourth-branch and court-backed oversight constitution; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound but still face visible member scrutiny, independent audit and evaluation, complaint and ethics channels, and published review cycles rather than secretariat self-marking**.
- `833-coercion-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-witness-municipal-civil-enforcement-regional-police-platforms-national-force-monopoly-and-treaty-bound-restraint.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should coercive and enforcement power ordinarily live at each scope?** with scale-matched restraint rather than one badge fetish: **micro-local bodies should default to witness, de-escalation, and referral rather than general coercive authority; municipalities should be the first ordinary home of civil enforcement, inspections, nuisance abatement, and everyday public-order administration under ordinary law; metropolitan governments should hold only those bounded cross-boundary enforcement and emergency-coordination powers that shared systems actually require; regional or provincial governments may honestly house large territorial police, emergency, and regulatory platforms where the constitutional order truly assigns them; national government should carry the thickest monopoly over criminal law, armed force, borders, and exceptional emergency concentration under the strongest rights and review discipline; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound, relying mainly on inspection, reporting, sanctions, certification, and tightly authorized operations rather than ambient upper-state police sovereignty**.
- `834-information-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-ledgers-municipal-record-homes-metro-observatories-national-statistics-and-treaty-registries.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should authoritative public facts, records, and decision visibility ordinarily live at each scope?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one dashboard fetish: **micro-local bodies should keep simple minutes, noticeboards, steward ledgers, and escalation logs rather than miniature data states; municipalities should be the first level with a full public information constitution of clerks or record stewards, open meeting packets, service and permit records, publication calendars, and reusable public data; metropolitan and regional governments should own their own observatories, geospatial baselines, and cross-boundary performance records rather than parasitic dependence on a host city or ministry; national government should carry the thickest official-statistics, gazette, archive, and interoperability spine; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound but still maintain comparability standards, registries, alerting channels, and shared reporting rather than private dashboards or counterfeit world omniscience**.
- `835-emergency-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-readiness-municipal-incident-command-regional-civil-protection-national-derogation-discipline-and-treaty-alerting.md` — The archive should answer the question **what emergency and exception grammar should ordinarily fit each scope?** with scale-matched escalation rather than one panic state fetish: **micro-local bodies should default to readiness, warning, mutual aid, and witness rather than emergency sovereignty; municipalities should be the first ordinary home of incident command, continuity, sheltering, and short-horizon emergency operations under ordinary law; metropolitan governments should carry shared-system disruption management where the functional city is one risk field; regional or provincial governments may honestly house civil-protection, wildfire, flood, logistics, and mutual-aid platforms where those risks are territorially real; national government should hold the thickest declaration, derogation, reserve, and exceptional coordination powers under legislative renewal, judicial review, and strict handback discipline; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound, specializing in alerting, coordination, standards, pooled assistance, and tightly authorized collective action rather than becoming ambient permanent emergency government**.
- `836-participation-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-assembly-municipal-dockets-metro-territorial-hearings-national-petition-ladders-and-treaty-observers.md` — If the archive already knows **what government should exist at each scope**, **how it is chosen**, **how it is financed**, **how it is scrutinized**, **where force lives**, **where records live**, and **what emergency lane fits it**, it should also know **how public voice honestly re-enters that government at each scale**: direct and reachable assembly voice at micro-local scale; petitions, hearings, consultations, bounded participatory-budget lanes, and occasional deliberative mini-publics at municipal scale; territory-wide participation homes for metropolitan and regional bodies that govern real shared systems; parliamentary hearing, petition, consultation, and rare constitution-level referendum lanes at national scale; and structured observer, submission, hearing, and stakeholder-participation routes for continental and global bodies rather than fake world-plebiscitary theater.
- `837-adjudication-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-pre-legal-entry-municipal-administrative-justice-regional-ordinary-courts-national-apex-review-and-treaty-tribunals.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should adjudication itself honestly live at each scope?** with scale-matched defaults rather than court fetish or courthouse minimalism: **micro-local bodies should offer witness, record, mediation, and easy entry into law rather than pretending to be sovereign courts; municipalities should be the first scale with a legible administrative-justice front door for ordinary daily disputes, but not the last word on legality against themselves; metropolitan and regional governments with real cross-boundary power should have equally real ordinary-court, tribunal, or legality-review homes rather than sending people on a host-city treasure hunt; national government should carry the apex and constitutional-review layer that secures rights, uniform due-process floors, and competence settlement across the stack; and continental or global bodies should use treaty-bound courts and tribunals only where the mandate is genuinely real, without pretending to be either a world judiciary of everything or a diplomacy-only zone immune from law**.
- `838-guarantee-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-dignity-municipal-nondiscrimination-regional-implementation-national-equal-citizenship-and-treaty-backstops.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should guarantees and rights floors honestly live at each scope?** with scale-matched defaults rather than rights vapor or rights monocentrism: **micro-local institutions should witness harm, include people, and route claims upward rather than pretending to author a tiny bill of rights; municipalities should be the first operational guarantee tier of daily dignity, non-discrimination, accessibility, and reasons-giving in ordinary administration; metropolitan and regional governments with real platform power should carry typed implementation guarantees for the systems they actually govern without fragmenting equal citizenship; national government should hold the thickest enforceable floor of equal citizenship, limitation discipline, due process, and justiciable rights guarantee; and continental or global bodies should function mainly as treaty-bound rights backstops, monitoring, and complaints machinery rather than as counterfeit world guarantor states**.
