- `619-contract-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-procurement-franchising-change-control-exit-capacity-and-no-government-by-concession-patchwork.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **contract home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, service, planning, capital, and regulatory one: a visible buyer-or-commissioner function, explicit make-buy-franchise tests, lawful procurement and concession routes, disciplined contract and change control, published performance and amendment trails, real handback and step-in capacity, and no territorial government by concession patchwork.
- `621-digital-operating-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-case-systems-identity-access-release-discipline-and-no-government-by-portal-shell.md` — Real metropolitan or regional government needs its own **digital operating constitution**: a named digital authority, canonical case/workflow and records systems, explicit identity-and-access rules, bounded interoperable exchange, release and incident discipline, continuity safeguards, and channel parity — not government by portal shell.
- `622-emergency-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-emergency-operations-continuity-mutual-aid-recovery-and-no-government-by-crisis-summit.md` — Real metropolitan or regional government needs its own **emergency constitution**: a named territorial emergency authority, an all-hazards risk picture, predefined escalation and mutual-aid rules, continuity of government and essential services, exercised communication and warning routes, recovery and handback discipline, and bounded extraordinary powers — not government by crisis summit.
- `624-territorial-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-boundaries-membership-accession-exit-review-and-no-government-by-opt-in-map.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it should stop living on voluntary membership residue, project geography, or host-city convenience and instead acquire an explicit territorial home: a publicly declared boundary, named member units, clear rules for accession, exit, annexation or detachment, periodic but not perpetual review, and one authoritative map that matches the powers, money, plans, and obligations the territory actually carries.
- `631-reversibility-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-handback-clocks-fresh-proof-return-lanes-and-no-one-way-recentralization-ratchet.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat exceptional upward concentration, distress takeover, emergency command, grant-conditioned control, and other scope shifts as **expiring claims rather than one-way ratchets**: the level that temporarily takes more power should carry a visible handback clock, a fresh-proof burden if it wants to keep the power, a capability-repair plan for the lower tier, a lawful return lane for money/staff/records/discretion, and a public explanation for any permanent reallocation.
- `648-scope-functional-equivalence-rules-anti-circumvention-tests-and-no-stack-change-by-relabeling.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should classify **materially stack-altering moves by their real effect rather than by their chosen label**: if a grant condition, procurement framework, software default, model contract, coordination protocol, “pilot”, guidance note, or emergency instruction functionally reallocates who decides, who must comply, who pays, who may object, or which tier now governs in practice, it should travel through the same packet, opinion, override, register, and review lanes as any openly named scope change.
- `651-scope-prescription-limits-delay-bars-adverse-possession-and-no-stack-change-by-time-alone.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should not let **mere duration, delayed challenge, or long unlawful exercise** manufacture constitutional title: materially stack-altering arrangements may need continuity management, evidentiary caution, or prospective settlement after long operation, but they should not acquire lawful authority simply because they lasted, were hard to unwind, or went unchallenged for too long.
- `657-scope-successor-accountability-legacy-acts-liabilities-records-and-no-blame-laundering-by-rescoping.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat **future competence, predecessor accountability, successor service continuity, records custody, litigation defence, and fiscal liability as separate questions that must each be typed explicitly whenever a function moves**, so rescoping cannot become a way to enjoy new power while laundering blame for old acts, omissions, debts, broken files, or unremedied harms.
- `658-scope-evidentiary-continuity-record-provenance-and-no-proof-laundering-by-migration.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require every **materially stack-altering reform** to preserve **evidentiary continuity** across record transfer, system migration, redaction, archival cutover, and platform replacement — with stable identifiers, provenance metadata, chain-of-custody, transformation logs, and certified retrieval routes — so responsibility can still be proven after a function moves and rescoping cannot dissolve proof through administrative or technical migration.
- `659-scope-evidentiary-break-presumptions-burden-allocation-and-no-stack-change-by-missing-file.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat any **unrepaired evidentiary break inside a materially stack-altering reform** as a burden-allocation event rather than a neutral accident — keeping the burden on the authority that claims the scope change, continuity, legality, or harmlessness, and refusing to let missing files, broken migration, or lost metadata manufacture constitutional title by opacity.
- `670-shared-regime-exit-ladders-denunciation-withdrawal-suspension-expulsion-savings-clauses-wind-down-duties-and-no-perpetual-membership-fiction.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed exit ladder** that distinguishes withdrawal or denunciation, temporary suspension, lawful expulsion where the constituting text allows it, module exit, territorial rollback, and post-exit survival clauses — with trigger, notice lane, decision body, effective date, pending-case rule, continuing liabilities, record duties, and re-entry path — so participation can end without pretending either that membership is irrevocable or that exit erases prior obligations.
- `680-shared-regime-jurisprudence-memory-and-consistency-holdings-digests-departure-reasons-advisory-opinions-and-no-random-walk-governance.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed jurisprudence-memory constitution** that separates binding force, persuasive reasoning, holdings, summaries, digests, advisory opinions, and departure rules — so interpretation develops through visible continuity rather than random walk, citation theater, or stealth precedent.
- `685-shared-regime-procurement-constitutions-competition-thresholds-exceptions-award-records-protest-debarment-and-no-regime-by-sole-source-habit.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed procurement constitution** that separates planning, solicitation methods, competition defaults, threshold rules, emergency and sole-source exceptions, award records, debriefing, complaint or protest lanes, vendor-sanctions logic, contract-change control, and exit capacity — so the regime is not governed by incumbent vendors, emergency habit, or off-book buyer discretion.
- `688-shared-regime-private-law-claims-constitutions-contracts-torts-procurement-disputes-standing-claims-bodies-arbitration-insurance-and-no-immunity-without-remedy.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed review-and-remedy constitution** for private-law disputes that separates contract claims, procurement complaints, property and personal-injury claims, insurance recovery, amicable settlement, standing claims bodies where needed, arbitration clauses, waiver decisions, and payment authority — so the regime can preserve functional immunity from ordinary local courts without sliding into immunity without remedy.
- `690-shared-regime-field-security-and-continuity-constitutions-designated-officials-risk-tiers-clearance-crisis-cells-stockpiles-evacuation-and-no-presence-by-hope.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed field security-and-continuity constitution** that separates risk assessment, travel and deployment clearance, duty-station roles, premises security, crisis management cells, incident logging, logistics and stockpiles, evacuation or hibernation choices, and continuity of records and core services — so territorial presence is sustained by visible duty-of-care and continuity architecture rather than by courage theater, local improvisation, or hope.
- `692-shared-regime-digital-and-cyber-operating-constitutions-system-owners-identity-and-access-admin-tiers-change-windows-incident-response-vulnerability-disclosure-backups-recovery-vendor-lanes-and-no-secretariat-by-shared-password.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed digital-and-cyber operating constitution** that separates system ownership, identity and access, privileged administration, change and release control, incident response, vulnerability disclosure, vendor and cloud access, backup and restoration, recovery targets, and degraded-mode continuity — so the regime is not actually run through shared passwords, orphan systems, incident backlog, or recovery theater.
- `705-mode-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-normal-degraded-emergency-recovery-handback-clocks-and-no-permanent-government-by-exception.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, and a field control plane, it should also publish one **mode packet** for the field — naming normal, degraded, emergency, and recovery operation, the triggers for entering each mode, what powers and duties change, what rights and service floors remain non-negotiable, and what handback clock returns the stack to ordinary routing — so a stressed system does not quietly adopt emergency pathways as its permanent constitution.
- `713-delegation-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-principal-lane-reserved-powers-operator-chains-step-in-rights-and-no-public-duty-by-outsourced-wrapper.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, and amendment discipline for a field, it should also publish one narrow **delegation packet** saying which slice of the field is still constitutionally owned by the public lane, which execution work may be delegated to public bodies, contractors, concessionaires, nonprofits, co-operatives, or platforms, what powers remain non-delegable, what contract-management and records capacity the principal must retain, what step-in and handback rights keep continuity real, and what review route prevents public duty from disappearing into an outsourced wrapper.
- `716-information-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-canonical-case-home-access-model-sharing-boundaries-retention-clocks-and-no-government-by-portal-shell.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, and a capability packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **information packet** saying where the field’s canonical case and record homes live, which surface is the system of record and which are only presentation or intake layers, what role-and-access model governs staff and delegates, what sharing boundaries and information agreements apply, what retention/export/handback rules preserve public memory, and what recovery path keeps the field governable when platforms, vendors, or host systems fail — so the field does not become government by portal shell, spreadsheet relay, or vendor-admin shadow.
- `717-asset-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-estate-fleet-equipment-condition-discipline-handback-and-no-government-by-orphan-assets.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, and an information packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **asset packet** saying which lane owns and stewards the field’s estate, fleet, equipment, depots, labs, stores, and critical spares; who holds custody, maintenance, calibration, and replacement duty; what condition and resilience floor applies; what lease, host-site, or operator dependencies exist; and what handback rule survives exit or transfer — so the field does not decay into government by orphan assets, lease camouflage, or maintenance exile.
- `718-service-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-whole-service-front-doors-route-classes-service-floors-continuity-and-no-government-by-front-door-scatter.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair and sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, a fiscal packet, a capability packet, an information packet, and an asset packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **service packet** saying what outcome the field’s service actually promises, which lane owns that promise, what front doors and route classes the public may use, what clocks and service floors bind, how channels and operators compose into one whole service, and what continuity and fallback rules survive overload, outage, provider failure, or redesign — so the field does not decay into government by front-door scatter, route roulette, or service-standard theater.
- `721-notice-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-service-rules-proof-models-clock-starts-failed-delivery-and-no-government-by-presumed-receipt.md` — Once a field already has service, case, and decision packets, it should also publish one narrow **notice packet** saying which communications are merely informational, which are consequential official notices, which acts require formal service, what address or notice-home hierarchy governs, which proof model attaches to each lawful channel, when clocks start, how failed delivery is repaired, and what continuity rule survives postal disruption, portal outage, representative change, or cross-border transmission — so the field does not decay into government by presumed receipt, channel ambush, or deadline folklore.
- `728-sideways-authority-packets-for-ideal-governments-bounded-remit-footprint-logic-board-fiscal-lane-review-clocks-and-no-functional-wrapper-without-constitutional-kit.md` — When the archive routes a function **sideways** into a bounded functional authority rather than into an ordinary territorial tier, it should default to one compact **sideways-authority packet** naming the real system footprint, the exact remit and exclusions, the principal public lane that still owns the wider constitutional bargain, the legitimacy and fiscal model, the review and participation routes, and the upgrade-or-exit triggers — so basins, corridors, grids, ports, referral networks, and similar in-between institutions stay governable without pretending to be full territorial governments or dissolving into quango fog.
- `730-continuity-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-staff-budget-records-cases-contracts-assets-cutover-and-no-ratification-by-theory-alone.md` — Once the archive has a default routing table (`726`), an override grammar (`727`), a sideways-authority packet (`728`), and a ratification packet for moving functions across scopes (`729`), it should also keep one compact **continuity packet** for the move itself: no scope shift is constitutionally honest until the polity can show who employs the people, holds the money, owns the contracts, keeps the files, answers the live cases, preserves the review routes, and runs the cutover without dropping rights, services, or accountability.
- `731-cutover-witness-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-effective-state-old-holder-new-holder-exception-ledger-and-no-transfer-by-folklore.md` — Once the archive has a continuity packet for scope shifts (`730`), it should also keep one compact **cutover witness packet** for the handoff moment itself: every materially consequential move across scopes should leave behind one contemporaneous public-and-reviewable witness saying what changed, when it changed, which holder lost authority, which holder gained authority, what remained transitional, which queues, records, contracts, and budgets were still in flight, which exceptions stayed live, and what fallback path still existed — so later review does not have to reconstruct the transfer from rumor, screenshots, or contradictory portal residue.
- `732-transitional-hosting-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-host-of-record-command-boundaries-forwarding-duties-expiry-clocks-and-no-sovereignty-by-borrowed-runtime.md` — Once the archive has a continuity packet (`730`) and a cutover witness packet (`731`), it should also keep one compact **transitional hosting packet** for the awkward but common period when legal authority has moved while some systems, staff, channels, or operational substrate are still being hosted by the predecessor or a third party: every such bridge should name the principal public holder, the temporary host, the exact host-only powers, the forwarding and cure duties, the money and service-floor terms, the evidence and logging boundary, the break-glass path, and the hard expiry or re-clearance clock — so a borrowed runtime never silently becomes the real constitution.
- `736-temporary-neutral-custody-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-contested-handoffs-rights-bearing-queues-record-spines-credential-escrow-and-no-settlement-by-possession.md` — Once the archive can say how a function should be routed (`726`-`728`), ratified (`729`), kept continuous (`730`), witnessed at cutover (`731`), temporarily hosted (`732`), cleanly closed (`733`), tested through an independent-live window (`734`), and rolled back when stabilization fails (`735`), it should also keep one compact **temporary neutral-custody packet** for the harder interval where neither old holder nor new holder can honestly be treated as fully settled: appoint a bounded custodian for named control surfaces, preserve the public route and evidentiary spine, freeze or escrow high-risk powers, keep pending matters legible, and refuse to let mere possession of live systems, records, or credentials masquerade as constitutional settlement.
- `737-release-packets-for-ideal-government-neutral-custody-full-partial-and-phased-release-receiver-readiness-residual-safeguards-and-no-custody-exit-by-impatience.md` — Once the archive has a temporary neutral-custody packet (`736`), it should also keep one compact **custody-release packet** for the moment named surfaces leave custody and re-enter ordinary government: classify the release type, prove receiver readiness surface by surface, preserve case and record lineage, state what safeguards remain temporarily in force, and refuse to end custody merely because a deadline, press statement, or impatient principal wants the appearance of settlement.
- `746-historical-register-rehousing-and-cross-catalog-migration-packets-for-absorbed-tombstones-register-home-change-stable-entry-identifiers-alias-continuity-and-no-disappearance-by-replatforming.md` — Once the archive can absorb standalone tombstones into grouped historical registers (`745`), it should also keep one compact **historical-register rehousing and cross-catalog migration packet**: one bounded proof object for moving absorbed dead-object entries from one register, catalogue, directory, or memorial platform to another without losing individually addressable identity, alias coverage, correction lineage, or the plain statement that the authority is dead, so the polity does not mistake platform migration for permission to break historical lookup.
- `754-head-of-state-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-no-separate-crown-below-national-scale-ceremonial-arbiters-collective-headship-reserve-powers-on-rails-and-no-duplicate-democratic-apex.md` — A separate head of state is not a universal ingredient of ideal government; it is justified mainly when a polity needs a **symbolic or arbitral apex distinct from the governing executive**, and where that office is mostly formal it should usually be indirectly chosen, tightly bounded, continuity-safe, and designed not to create a second competing democratic command.
- `757-emergency-powers-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-ordinary-law-first-temporal-limits-legislative-renewal-judicial-review-and-no-shadow-constitution-by-crisis.md` — Ideal governments should treat constitutional emergency powers as a **last-resort continuity instrument rather than an alternative operating system**: ordinary law should carry as much crisis response as possible, exceptional powers should be legally typed, temporary, and reviewable, legislative renewal should be real rather than ceremonial, courts should remain open enough to test necessity and proportionality, and no emergency should be allowed to harden into a shadow constitution.
- `761-vacancy-and-acting-office-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-succession-order-time-limits-limited-powers-public-reporting-and-no-government-by-permanent-interim.md` — Ideal governments should treat vacancies, succession, holdover service, and acting appointments as **continuity bridges rather than alternate constitutions of rule**: they should publish who succeeds automatically, who may serve temporarily, what powers are narrowed during interim service, how quickly the permanent appointment lane must reopen, and why courts, regulators, watchdogs, ministers, and public-service leadership should never be governed indefinitely by serial temporary placeholders.
- `763-caretaker-government-and-pre-election-restraint-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-routine-administration-incoming-government-consultation-major-appointments-freeze-emergency-carve-outs-and-no-mandate-stretch-between-verdict-and-handover.md` — Ideal governments should treat dissolution, hung-parliament bargaining, post-election transition, and imminent change of government as **a distinct continuity-with-restraint mode rather than business as usual**: outgoing governments should continue routine administration and urgent protection of the public, but major policy, appointments, contracts, publicity, and irreversible international or fiscal commitments should pause, narrow, or move only after consultation with the likely successor, so no one stretches an expiring mandate through the handover gap.
- `788-representation-counsel-nonlawyer-assistance-and-support-person-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-choice-capacity-qualification-confidentiality-and-no-rights-by-solo-navigation.md` — Ideal governments should ensure that **people facing administrative power can choose not to face it alone**: preserve the right to be accompanied, represented, advised, or otherwise assisted; distinguish full legal representation from limited nonlawyer help and ordinary support-person presence; verify authority without turning authorization into obstruction; and type stronger assistance duties where stakes, complexity, disability, language barriers, or vulnerability make solo navigation an unfair fiction.
- `791-benchmark-cards-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-vocation-fit-kit-floors-fiscal-congruence-review-lanes-tripwires-and-no-admiration-without-scoring.md` — The archive should pair its canonical scope matrix and answer-key notes with one compact **benchmark-card format** for each scope — vocation fit, minimum complete kit, fiscal and capability congruence, spillover or solidarity fit, review and remedy integrity, participation and scrutiny proportionality, and named upgrade or handback tripwires — so real constitutions, reform proposals, and case studies can be compared tersely against the ideal stack without reopening the whole theory.
- `792-stress-test-and-drill-cards-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-essential-service-continuity-command-legibility-fiscal-buffers-rights-discipline-rescoping-signals-and-no-paper-constitution-by-calm-weather.md` — The archive should pair its ideal-government answer key and benchmark cards with one compact **stress-test and drill-card format** for each scope — essential-service continuity, command and escalation legibility, reserve and surge discipline, intergovernmental handoff integrity, legality and rights restraint under pressure, public communication, and recovery or handback triggers — so governments are judged not only by their steady-state design but by whether they remain honest under flood, blackout, outbreak, fiscal shock, cyber disruption, or constitutional strain.
- `794-sequenced-upgrade-paths-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-first-honest-steps-bridge-arrangements-cutover-gates-and-no-full-stack-redesign-by-manifesto.md` — When a real polity is far from the archive’s ideal scope stack, reform should move through a sequenced upgrade path: **make the current arrangement honest first, repair the minimum complete kit and fiscal congruence next, constitutionalise any bridge institutions that are already exercising real power, transfer functions only with continuity proof, and attempt deeper territorial or constitutional redesign only after the operating spine is real**.
- `796-intervention-ladders-for-failing-governments-of-each-scope-support-first-proportional-supervision-special-measures-handback-clocks-and-no-permanent-emergency-custody.md` — When a government-by-scope arrangement keeps failing its benchmark, stress, maintenance, or proof duties, the archive should not jump straight from diagnosis to permanent takeover. It should use one compact **intervention ladder**: **support first, escalate by law and proportionality, separate own-competence supervision from delegated-task control, keep any special measures temporary and reviewable, and pair every intervention with a handback or formal rescoping test so rescue does not harden into quiet permanent custody**.
- `797-contestability-ladders-for-scope-governance-benchmark-objections-trigger-appeals-intervention-review-handback-denials-and-no-constitutional-maintenance-by-self-marking.md` — The archive should pair its answer-key, benchmark, stress-test, maintenance, upgrade-path, public-proof, and intervention notes with one compact **contestability ladder**: **benchmark classifications, trigger openings or closures, stress findings used for redesign, intervention orders, renewals, handback denials, and other stack-shaping judgments should all carry typed standing, reasons, interim-relief logic, and final independent review, so governments do not maintain the constitutional stack by marking their own homework and calling the result settled**.
- `804-tracer-routes-and-lived-path-verification-for-scope-governance-user-journeys-fund-flows-case-walks-handoff-tests-and-no-constitution-by-org-chart.md` — The archive should pair its assessment-mission, finding-register, management-response, and close-out notes with one compact **tracer-route grammar**: **every serious scope review should follow a small set of real or lawfully simulated paths — case, payment, referral, complaint, permit, incident, data handoff, or handback — across institutions, clocks, and records, so governments are not judged only by statutes, org charts, or curated meetings instead of by the routes people and work actually travel**.
- `815-administrative-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-host-secretariats-principal-owned-backbones-chartered-operators-records-homes-and-no-heavy-power-by-borrowed-bureaucracy.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, and **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what administrative chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should use small secretariats with no hidden command over member administrations, shared-service backbones should keep declared principals, employer-of-record rules, records homes, and service agreements, bounded functional authorities should have chartered operating cores with explicit staffing, asset, procurement, and incident-command authority, and general-purpose territorial tiers should normally own their own civil-service, records, and operating spine rather than ruling through borrowed host bureaucracy.
- `819-boundary-and-membership-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-accession-gates-territory-rules-amendment-thickness-exit-protocols-dissolution-paths-and-no-map-by-one-way-ratchet.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, and **what information chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should use open and reversible participation with no hidden territorial claim, shared-service backbones should declare member classes, accession formulas, notice periods, and unwind rules, bounded functional authorities should use chartered territories plus staged accession and constrained exit, and general-purpose territorial tiers should rely on statutory boundary change with public consultation, transition machinery, and no map by one-way ratchet.
- `821-dispute-resolution-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-negotiation-ladders-mediation-expert-determination-jurisdiction-maps-continuity-orders-and-no-heavy-power-by-hostage-dispute.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, **what administrative spine belongs to it**, **what oversight chain belongs to it**, **what participation chain belongs to it**, **what information chain belongs to it**, **what boundary-and-membership chain belongs to it**, and **what decision-rule chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what dispute-resolution chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should rely on recorded negotiation and visible member-side escalation, shared-service backbones should use negotiation-first ladders with mediation, technical determination, continuity protection, and public-law endpoints, bounded functional authorities should publish jurisdiction maps and interim continuity orders, and general-purpose territorial tiers should rely on ordinary justice and constitutional routes rather than permanent bargaining by hostage dispute.
- `822-asset-and-liability-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-member-owned-infrastructure-ring-fenced-balance-sheets-handback-maps-contingent-obligations-and-no-heavy-power-by-orphaned-balance-sheet.md` — When the archive has already established that a cross-boundary problem is real, chosen the honest form, and said who governs, pays, operates, votes, and hears disputes, it should still require one compact **asset-and-liability chain**: thin connectors should own almost nothing beyond trivial co-ordination tools; shared-service backbones should keep political title with the principals unless a clearly bounded common vehicle is justified; bounded functional authorities may hold and steward system-critical assets and named liabilities inside a ring-fenced public balance sheet; and general-purpose territorial tiers should carry visible asset, debt, reserve, and handback constitutions rather than hiding real sovereignty in host property, off-book obligations, or exit chaos.
- `823-contracting-boundary-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-light-support-buying-principal-owned-commissioning-chartered-concessions-change-control-and-no-heavy-power-by-contract-escape-hatch.md` — When the archive has already established that a cross-boundary problem is real, chosen the honest form, and said who governs, pays, operates, votes, hears disputes, owns the assets, and can unwind the map, it should still require one compact **contracting-boundary chain**: thin connectors may buy only light support and must not become hidden commissioners of core public systems; shared-service backbones may buy pooled administrative tools and support services while political title remains visibly with the principals; bounded functional authorities may procure, franchise, or concession the named system they are chartered to govern, but only through a visible commissioner spine, hard change-control, and full public review; and general-purpose territorial tiers may use contracts as delivery instruments without letting procurement, concessions, PPPs, or managed-service deals become constitutional escape hatches for powers that should remain politically owned.
- `828-mandate-exit-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-recall-municipal-dismissal-confidence-loss-bounded-dissolution-and-treaty-lapse.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should governing mandates end when they fail, expire early, or lose their public basis?** with scope-matched exit defaults rather than one romantic removal myth: simple recall or replacement for tiny steward bodies, council-centered dismissal and tightly bounded mayoral removal at municipal scale, explicit confidence-loss and successor grammar for metropolitan and regional governments with real power, bounded parliamentary exit and dissolution rules for most national governments, and fixed reauthorization, for-cause removal, or treaty-lapse rules for plurilateral and global bodies that must never drift into ambient permanence.
- `835-emergency-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-readiness-municipal-incident-command-regional-civil-protection-national-derogation-discipline-and-treaty-alerting.md` — The archive should answer the question **what emergency and exception grammar should ordinarily fit each scope?** with scale-matched escalation rather than one panic state fetish: **micro-local bodies should default to readiness, warning, mutual aid, and witness rather than emergency sovereignty; municipalities should be the first ordinary home of incident command, continuity, sheltering, and short-horizon emergency operations under ordinary law; metropolitan governments should carry shared-system disruption management where the functional city is one risk field; regional or provincial governments may honestly house civil-protection, wildfire, flood, logistics, and mutual-aid platforms where those risks are territorially real; national government should hold the thickest declaration, derogation, reserve, and exceptional coordination powers under legislative renewal, judicial review, and strict handback discipline; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound, specializing in alerting, coordination, standards, pooled assistance, and tightly authorized collective action rather than becoming ambient permanent emergency government**.

## procurement-governance

- `408-procurement-clauses-for-exit-escrow-and-public-continuity.md` — Public procurement should treat **continuity at supplier exit** as a design requirement from day one, with contract clauses, tested handovers, and fallback assets that make the public service survivable.
- `516-markets-and-company-power-by-scope-local-entry-metro-space-national-antitrust-and-fair-global-rules.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern markets by keeping entry barriers, permits, public procurement access, and everyday consumer signal detection close to local life; using metropolitan and regional institutions to manage commercial geography, logistics, and market systems that cross municipal borders; reserving competition law, merger control, company law, securities rules, labour and consumer floors, and strategic industrial discipline to the nation; and using the global layer for trade predictability, anti-cartel cooperation, tax-base protection, and narrow common rules that prevent regulatory arbitrage without constitutionalizing corporate power above democracy.
- `519-innovation-and-industrial-policy-by-scope-local-entrepreneurship-regional-clusters-national-missions-and-open-global-coordination.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern innovation and industrial policy by keeping entrepreneurship support, practical diffusion, local supplier development, and maker or skills ecosystems close to firms and workers; using metropolitan and regional institutions to cultivate clusters, applied research linkages, transition strategies, and shared innovation infrastructure; reserving mission setting, major R&D finance, competition-safe sector policy, strategic trade and resilience choices, and national innovation floors to the nation; and keeping the global layer narrow, focused on open science, standards, subsidy transparency, technology cooperation, and anti-arbitrage trade rules rather than a world ministry of industry.
- `533-waste-and-materials-by-scope-local-collection-regional-recovery-national-producer-responsibility-and-global-hazard-controls.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat waste as failed material design rather than municipal fate: households, shops, workplaces, and neighbourhood institutions can sort, return, repair, and surface illegal dumping but should not carry the whole burden of circularity; municipalities should guarantee clean streets, universal collection, public-space litter control, reuse access points, and safe everyday interfaces with residents; regional bodies should run the real recovery geography of transfer stations, composting, remanufacturing, recycling markets, and final disposal capacity that usually outruns one city; nations should shift cost and design responsibility upstream through product standards, extended producer responsibility, deposit and take-back systems, right-to-repair rules, public procurement, data reporting, and labour protections; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in hazardous-waste controls, waste-trade rules, and common floor disciplines that prevent one country’s circular rhetoric from becoming another country’s toxic burden.
- `563-public-procurement-institutions-and-review-by-scope-local-needs-regional-shared-buying-national-rules-independent-challenges-and-no-government-by-emergency-sole-source-fog.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat public procurement as a governed public institution rather than a clerical back office: keep need definition, user-facing specification, and day-to-day contract management close to the service; use metropolitan, county, provincial, state, or other regional shared-buying bodies where market structure, scarce expertise, or repeated categories make pooling sensible; reserve national government for the procurement code, standard documents, core e-procurement rails, integrity controls, supplier-access baselines, independent complaint review design, and open-contracting discipline; keep the global layer narrow in interoperable standards, anti-rigging and anti-corruption cooperation, and fair cross-border conditions of competition; and never let emergency exemptions, framework sprawl, or vendor dependence turn public spending into shadow executive power.
- `645-scope-standstill-defaults-suspensory-effect-interim-relief-and-no-stack-change-by-racing-the-clock.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should give timely, credible challenges to materially stack-altering acts a visible **scope-standstill** or equally fast **interim-relief lane**, so the live constitutional stack cannot be rewritten simply because deployment moved faster than review.
- `685-shared-regime-procurement-constitutions-competition-thresholds-exceptions-award-records-protest-debarment-and-no-regime-by-sole-source-habit.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed procurement constitution** that separates planning, solicitation methods, competition defaults, threshold rules, emergency and sole-source exceptions, award records, debriefing, complaint or protest lanes, vendor-sanctions logic, contract-change control, and exit capacity — so the regime is not governed by incumbent vendors, emergency habit, or off-book buyer discretion.
- `688-shared-regime-private-law-claims-constitutions-contracts-torts-procurement-disputes-standing-claims-bodies-arbitration-insurance-and-no-immunity-without-remedy.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed review-and-remedy constitution** for private-law disputes that separates contract claims, procurement complaints, property and personal-injury claims, insurance recovery, amicable settlement, standing claims bodies where needed, arbitration clauses, waiver decisions, and payment authority — so the regime can preserve functional immunity from ordinary local courts without sliding into immunity without remedy.

## prosecution-governance

- `499-public-integrity-by-scope-local-disclosure-conflict-checks-lobbying-transparency-asset-declarations-and-anti-capture-routing.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat integrity as institutional infrastructure rather than moral decoration: small governments need simple, enforceable disclosure and procurement rules; larger governments need stronger conflict controls, lobbying transparency, asset declarations, cooling-off periods, and independent verification; and audit, prevention, prosecution, and adjudication should remain distinct enough that no one office becomes both ethics mascot and political weapon.
- `514-justice-by-scope-local-resolution-city-legal-aid-regional-courts-national-codes-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern justice by keeping low-stakes dispute resolution, legal help, and problem sensing close to daily life; sizing trial and appellate institutions to real catchments rather than arbitrary municipal lines; reserving criminal codes, procedural guarantees, judicial independence, prosecution architecture, and equal access floors to the nation; and treating the global layer as a narrow guarantor of rights, cooperation, and last-resort review rather than as a substitute domestic judiciary.
- `551-public-prosecution-by-scope-local-diversion-regional-ordinary-charging-national-integrity-cases-and-no-government-by-prosecutor.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should keep prosecution lawful, impartial, and scale-matched: use community-near intake and diversion for ordinary low-level harm, size ordinary charging offices to regional or metropolitan court catchments large enough for competence and independence, reserve national prosecutors for public-corruption, state-integrity, and interjurisdictional serious crime, and keep cross-border prosecutorial cooperation narrow, reviewable, and rights-bound so neither local vendetta nor central spectacle can govern by charge.
- `557-detention-corrections-and-reentry-by-scope-local-contact-and-release-links-regional-custody-probation-national-rights-floors-and-no-government-by-warehousing.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **detention, corrections, and reentry** as a **strictly limited, rights-bound, reintegration-oriented part of justice** rather than as a hidden warehousing system: keep local roles focused on family contact, service continuity, diversion support, and release preparation rather than long-term cage sovereignty; use metropolitan or regional institutions for most remand custody, prisons, probation, parole, health continuity, and professionally managed inspectionable facilities; reserve national government for penal law, decarceration incentives, independent monitoring, and non-negotiable humane-treatment floors; and never allow **jails, prisons, or release systems to become opaque human storage insulated from courts, health systems, and society**.
- `564-anti-corruption-bodies-and-integrity-commissions-by-scope-local-routing-regional-case-development-national-specialization-and-no-government-by-heroic-commission.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not rely on one heroic anti-corruption commission: keep local complaint intake, disclosure routing, whistleblower handoff, and ordinary integrity advice close enough to be usable; place regional or state-level investigative and inspection capacity where corruption markets, procurement webs, and patronage chains cross municipalities or where tiny jurisdictions are too captured to investigate themselves; reserve national government for the preventive architecture required by law, high-level and cross-regional corruption, asset-declaration verification, beneficial-ownership tracing, international cooperation, and strategy coordination; keep the global layer narrow in standards, peer review, and transnational case support; and never let anti-corruption institutions become either decorative ethics theater or unreviewable prosecutor-states.
- `770-internal-audit-inspection-and-inspector-general-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-risk-based-plans-direct-reporting-hotlines-case-routing-quality-review-and-no-self-inspection-by-line-command.md` — Ideal governments should treat internal audit, inspection, and inspector-general functions as **the state’s inside-assurance lane rather than an internal public-relations unit or a duplicate prosecutor**: they should run risk-based workplans, receive protected allegations, inspect controls and operations without taking over management, route cases to the right coercive or disciplinary forum, publish what can lawfully be published, and undergo quality review, so institutions are not forced to choose between silence, scandal, and waiting for external audit alone.
- `789-impartial-decision-maker-separation-of-functions-and-ex-parte-contact-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-recusal-staff-firebreaks-record-discipline-and-no-adjudication-by-backstage-influence.md` — Ideal governments should ensure that **administrative decisions are made by people and processes insulated enough from partisan, investigative, prosecutorial, commercial, and personal bias to be trusted**: require recusal for personal interest, maintain workable separation between case-building and deciding roles, ban or sharply discipline off-record merits communications, and force decisive inputs onto the file rather than allowing adjudication by backstage influence.
- `814-fiscal-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-dues-and-service-payments-assigned-revenues-equalization-keys-capital-lanes-and-no-heavy-power-by-shadow-treasury.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary form is honest** and **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what fiscal chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should live on modest dues and project-preparation money with no disguised distributive budget, shared-service backbones should run on principal-owned service payments and declared cost-sharing plus reserve rules, bounded functional authorities should use assigned revenues, user charges, or rule-bound transfers matched to their narrow charter with explicit capital discipline, and general-purpose territorial tiers should have a public budget constitution with own-source or rule-bound shared revenues, equalization, and visible borrowing limits rather than living by discretionary grants, annual pleas, or off-book vehicles.
- `831-fiscal-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-tiny-commons-municipal-own-source-metro-shares-regional-equalization-national-solidarity-and-treaty-dues.md` — The archive should answer the question **how should each scope ordinarily be financed?** with scale-matched fiscal defaults rather than one treasury fetish: micro-local bodies should live on tiny discretionary funds, member contributions, and visible small grants rather than debt or payroll empires; municipalities should be the first level with meaningful own-source revenue, rule-bound transfers, ordinary operating reserves, and capital access for durable local assets; metropolitan governments should use assigned revenue shares, formula transfers, and user-charge lanes where systems justify them rather than annual pleas from member municipalities; regional and provincial governments should combine own revenues, shared taxes, equalization, and platform-scale capital budgets; national government should carry the broad tax base, macro-stabilization, and solidarity machinery; and continental or global bodies should usually rely on treaty dues, assessed contributions, and tightly bounded common finance rather than counterfeit world taxation or donor-whim constitutions.

## public-defense-governance

- `514-justice-by-scope-local-resolution-city-legal-aid-regional-courts-national-codes-and-global-rights.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern justice by keeping low-stakes dispute resolution, legal help, and problem sensing close to daily life; sizing trial and appellate institutions to real catchments rather than arbitrary municipal lines; reserving criminal codes, procedural guarantees, judicial independence, prosecution architecture, and equal access floors to the nation; and treating the global layer as a narrow guarantor of rights, cooperation, and last-resort review rather than as a substitute domestic judiciary.
- `558-public-defense-and-legal-aid-by-scope-local-entry-municipal-navigation-regional-provider-capacity-national-independence-and-no-justice-by-unaffordable-counsel.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **public defense and legal aid** as a **core constitutional capacity for equal justice** rather than as charity or courthouse aftercare: keep first contact, rights information, and navigable entry close to daily life; use metropolitan, county, provincial, state, or other regional institutions for most ordinary defender offices, provider networks, and specialist capacity; reserve national government for the right itself, independent legal-aid authority design, fair funding, quality floors, and territorial equalization; and never allow **freedom, family life, housing, status, or civil survival to depend on whether a person can privately purchase counsel on short notice**.
- `673-shared-regime-officer-and-secretariat-powers-chairs-bureaus-procedural-control-neutral-support-legal-advice-and-no-government-by-convening-clique.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed officer-and-secretariat constitution** that separates presiding officers, bureau steering, secretariat support, legal and drafting assistance, document control, and emergency administrative acts — so the regime is not actually governed by whoever controls the agenda email, the microphone, or the drafting room.
- `788-representation-counsel-nonlawyer-assistance-and-support-person-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-choice-capacity-qualification-confidentiality-and-no-rights-by-solo-navigation.md` — Ideal governments should ensure that **people facing administrative power can choose not to face it alone**: preserve the right to be accompanied, represented, advised, or otherwise assisted; distinguish full legal representation from limited nonlawyer help and ordinary support-person presence; verify authority without turning authorization into obstruction; and type stronger assistance duties where stakes, complexity, disability, language barriers, or vulnerability make solo navigation an unfair fiction.

## public-enterprise-governance

- `543-special-purpose-authorities-and-arms-length-bodies-narrow-remits-hard-charters-open-books-and-sunset-review.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should use special-purpose authorities, public corporations, and arm’s-length bodies only where a bounded cross-municipal or regional function — such as transit, utilities, watershed management, market regulation, or other impartial technical tasks — genuinely requires them; give them narrow remits, hard-law charters, published financing, public accountability, and periodic review; and never let them become shadow governments, patronage shelters, or constitutional escape hatches.
- `546-public-enterprises-and-state-owned-enterprises-explicit-rationales-separated-roles-hard-budget-constraints-and-open-books.md` — An ideal polity may own and operate enterprises where public ownership is genuinely justified — for natural monopolies, essential network infrastructure, strategic resilience, mission-critical finance, or other clearly stated public purposes — but it should publish why it owns them, separate ownership from regulation and policy-making, state public-service obligations explicitly, compensate them transparently, impose hard budget constraints, keep boards and books professional and visible, and review the portfolio often enough that public enterprise does not become a hiding place for patronage, off-balance-sheet debt, or anti-competitive favoritism.

## public-records-governance

- `429-material-change-notice-and-public-record-refresh-discipline.md` — When a consequential public AI system changes in scope, data, model, provider, phase, or operating context, every public record about it should be refreshed before or at the moment the change takes effect.
- `465-confusability-budgets-disambiguation-floors-and-alias-collision-registers.md` — Consequential public-AI archives should budget confusability across system names, case states, model families, source labels, and decision routes, and require explicit disambiguation when nearby labels could cause misrouting or mistaken authority.
- `466-umbrella-records-instance-narrowing-and-no-authority-by-family.md` — Family-level, program-level, supplier-level, or umbrella governance artifacts for consequential public AI should not be treated as authority-bearing for a specific deployment, workflow, or decision route until the archive narrows them to a named instance or explicitly states the residual gap.
- `467-native-evidence-lanes-normalized-packets-and-no-semantic-reownership.md` — Consequential public-AI archives should keep native logs, vendor exports, raw witnesses, replay references, normalized packets, and downstream summaries in distinct evidence lanes so portability does not silently rewrite source semantics, missingness, or authority.
- `470-intake-failure-classification-handoff-vs-artifact-and-manual-fallback-lanes.md` — When consequential notices, appeals, evidence packets, or supplier submissions fail to arrive, open, or register, the archive should distinguish bad artifact from bad delivery or handoff and preserve a typed manual fallback lane so rights do not disappear into one broken digital path.
- `474-stewardship-transfers-publisher-continuity-and-no-inherited-trust-by-move.md` — When a third-party model, dataset, API, repository, document host, or supplier changes steward, publisher, domain, or ownership, prior trust and approval should not silently carry forward; stewardship transfer should trigger continuity proof or trust reset.
- `475-official-communications-as-evidence-correction-chains-and-channel-registries.md` — Consequential public-AI communications should be treated as first-class evidence surfaces with an official-channel registry, explicit correction linkage, and capture rules for what was said where and when, so public notice cannot drift into silent edits, split-view updates, or screenshot folklore.
- `517-public-revenue-and-taxation-by-scope-local-own-source-taxes-metropolitan-base-sharing-national-progressivity-and-global-anti-evasion-floors.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should fund government by keeping visible own-source revenues tied to place and service at the local level; using metropolitan and regional revenue-sharing where commuters, land values, logistics, or extractive burdens cross borders; reserving progressive income taxation, broad consumption taxes, social insurance contributions, debt management, and equalizing transfers to the nation; and using the global layer for narrow anti-evasion, information-exchange, and minimum-tax rules that stop mobile capital from hollowing out democratic finance.
- `522-culture-and-heritage-by-scope-local-belonging-municipal-institutions-regional-ecologies-national-pluralism-and-global-commons.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern culture as a rights-bearing public good rather than propaganda, luxury, or folklore storage: neighborhoods and communities keep living practices, memory, and language-use close to life; municipalities should sustain libraries, museums, venues, festivals, archives, arts education links, public space, and fair local cultural access; regional bodies should support linguistic and heritage ecologies, touring circuits, landscape-scale memory, and cultural production systems that outrun one city; nations should guarantee cultural rights, artistic freedom, public support, restitution and heritage law, and plural national institutions without imposing one official culture; and the global layer should protect humanity’s shared heritage, support cultural diversity, and coordinate anti-trafficking and cooperation without becoming a world ministry of taste.
- `533-waste-and-materials-by-scope-local-collection-regional-recovery-national-producer-responsibility-and-global-hazard-controls.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat waste as failed material design rather than municipal fate: households, shops, workplaces, and neighbourhood institutions can sort, return, repair, and surface illegal dumping but should not carry the whole burden of circularity; municipalities should guarantee clean streets, universal collection, public-space litter control, reuse access points, and safe everyday interfaces with residents; regional bodies should run the real recovery geography of transfer stations, composting, remanufacturing, recycling markets, and final disposal capacity that usually outruns one city; nations should shift cost and design responsibility upstream through product standards, extended producer responsibility, deposit and take-back systems, right-to-repair rules, public procurement, data reporting, and labour protections; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in hazardous-waste controls, waste-trade rules, and common floor disciplines that prevent one country’s circular rhetoric from becoming another country’s toxic burden.
- `571-public-records-archives-and-official-publications-by-scope-community-memory-municipal-record-discipline-regional-repositories-national-gazettes-and-no-government-by-disappearing-state.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **public records, archives, and official publication** as a **constitutional memory layer**: keep firsthand witnessing, local minutes, notice, and records help close to communities and municipalities; pool preservation, repository, and disaster-recovery capacity at regional scale where fragmentation would otherwise erase public memory; reserve national or constitutional-state law for records duties, transfer rules, authentic promulgation, and archival independence; and use continental and global layers for interoperability, documentary-heritage protection, and common access norms rather than for a fantasy of one world archive sovereign.
- `581-mandate-finance-congruence-unfunded-mandates-vertical-fiscal-imbalance-and-no-decentralization-by-fiscal-theater.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **mandate-finance congruence** as constitutional law rather than budget etiquette: no level of government should be assigned a durable public function unless the same settlement also names the revenue basket, transfer formula, equalization rule, borrowing limits, and capability backstop that make the function actually dischargeable; delegated tasks must come with commensurate resources, local self-government must include at least some real own-source fiscal room, and upward rescue must be visible and reviewable rather than leaving decentralization to degrade into blame-shifting.
- `585-conditional-grants-matching-funds-competitive-programs-and-no-government-by-grant-maze.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **intergovernmental grants as constitutional instruments rather than administrative weather**: ordinary local discretion and equal citizenship should rest mainly on own-source revenue plus predictable general and equalization transfers; earmarked, matching, performance, capital, or competitive grants should be reserved for narrow cases where rights floors, spillovers, transition priorities, or shared investment genuinely justify them; co-financing duties should scale to fiscal capacity; application, reporting, and audit rules should be harmonized and limited; and no higher tier should be allowed to govern municipalities, metros, or regions mainly by forcing them to live inside a permanent grant maze.
- `586-function-transfer-packs-staff-assets-records-contracts-liabilities-and-no-reassignment-by-legal-text-alone.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **any transfer of a public function across levels of government as a full transfer pack rather than a sentence in a law**: whenever a competence moves, the same settlement should also name the effective date, service standard, staff lane, asset and lease inventory, contract and procurement treatment, records and data custody, ongoing-case handoff, fiscal lane, liability rule, transition authority, dispute route, and review clock, so that decentralisation or recentralisation cannot occur by moving the headline power while leaving the receiving government to inherit an empty shell.
- `601-publicity-of-local-deliberation-open-meetings-agenda-notice-closed-session-limits-and-no-government-by-chamber-obscurity.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **the publicity of local and regional deliberation as a constitutional operating condition rather than as optional etiquette**: plenary meetings and decision-shaping committees should be open by default, agendas and core papers should be published with usable notice, closed sessions should be narrow and reasoned, minutes and vote records should remain durable and searchable, and open meetings should complement rather than substitute for broader participatory methods so self-government does not retreat into chamber obscurity.
- `603-order-of-operations-for-ideal-multilevel-government-vocation-assignment-kits-connectors-asymmetry-and-no-reform-by-layer-shopping.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should be designed in a disciplined order: start from the class of problems and the real geography they inhabit, assign responsibilities by explicit scope tests, fit each chosen level with a minimum complete institutional kit, bind that kit to finance and capability, add coordination/review/equalization connectors, and only then allow principled asymmetry and transfer rules; reject reforms that start by picking a favored level first and inventing reasons afterward.
- `624-territorial-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-boundaries-membership-accession-exit-review-and-no-government-by-opt-in-map.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it should stop living on voluntary membership residue, project geography, or host-city convenience and instead acquire an explicit territorial home: a publicly declared boundary, named member units, clear rules for accession, exit, annexation or detachment, periodic but not perpetual review, and one authoritative map that matches the powers, money, plans, and obligations the territory actually carries.
- `654-scope-promulgation-authentic-heads-effective-dates-and-no-stack-change-by-unpublished-object.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require every **materially stack-altering act** to become operative through one **authentic public head** — a canonical promulgation object with legal basis, adoption date, effective date, status, and upstream links — so the scope stack cannot be changed by unpublished memo, side letter, private deck, quiet platform switch, or stale mirror.
- `656-scope-transition-rules-for-pending-matters-cutover-queues-file-transfer-and-no-stack-change-by-midstream-grab.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require every **materially stack-altering act** to carry explicit transition rules for pending applications, permits, investigations, appeals, contracts, liabilities, records, and service queues — with named cutover dates, forum rules, file-transfer duties, and clock-preservation — so old matters do not silently jump sovereigns, stall in limbo, or get re-decided by midstream grab.
- `658-scope-evidentiary-continuity-record-provenance-and-no-proof-laundering-by-migration.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require every **materially stack-altering reform** to preserve **evidentiary continuity** across record transfer, system migration, redaction, archival cutover, and platform replacement — with stable identifiers, provenance metadata, chain-of-custody, transformation logs, and certified retrieval routes — so responsibility can still be proven after a function moves and rescoping cannot dissolve proof through administrative or technical migration.
- `667-differentiated-commitments-in-shared-regimes-reservations-opt-outs-derogations-transition-periods-territorial-application-review-clocks-and-no-uniformity-by-false-claim.md` — Shared regimes should maintain a **typed differentiation register** that distinguishes reservations, interpretive declarations, opt-outs, temporary derogations, transition periods, territorial applications, and enhanced-cooperation rings — with legal basis, scope, duration, review clock, and accession or withdrawal path — so a regime can use lawful variable geometry without lying that every member carries the same obligation.
- `669-shared-regime-entry-ladders-observers-signatories-provisional-application-accession-admission-thresholds-depositaries-entry-into-force-and-no-membership-by-affiliation-claim.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed participation ladder** that distinguishes observer, applicant, signatory, provisional applier, party/member, and deeper-module participant — with actor eligibility, admission body, deposited instrument, effective date, rights bundle, and reviewable public status — so the public can tell who is merely near a regime and who is actually bound.
- `674-shared-regime-records-and-publicity-public-private-sessions-document-registers-meeting-records-vote-records-authentic-texts-corrections-and-no-governance-by-missing-papertrail.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed documentary constitution** that separates session publicity, agenda and paper circulation, official document registers, meeting-record formats, vote records, authentic texts, correction notices, and retention or access rules — so public authority does not vanish into missing minutes, unofficial drafts, or document folklore.
- `687-shared-regime-privileges-and-immunities-constitutions-functional-independence-jurisdiction-tax-customs-inviolability-waiver-and-no-sovereignty-cosplay.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed privileges-and-immunities authority map** that separates juridical personality, inviolability, immunity from legal process, archives and communications protection, fiscal and customs facilities, visa and entry support, category-specific treatment for representatives and officials, waiver authority, and abuse-control lanes — so institutional independence is protected without decaying into sovereignty cosplay, perk inflation, or unreviewable impunity.
- `693-shared-regime-personal-data-and-privacy-constitutions-legal-basis-purpose-limits-minimization-subject-rights-transfers-breach-response-and-no-mission-by-data-drift.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed personal-data-and-privacy constitution** that separates lawful basis, purpose limitation, necessity and minimization, role allocation, sensitive-data treatment, retention, transfer rules, subject-rights handling, breach response, and accountability review — so mission work does not quietly become mission by data drift, uncontrolled onward sharing, or privacy promises with no operating spine.
- `698-shared-regime-implementing-partner-and-pass-through-constitutions-due-diligence-workplans-cash-transfer-assurance-suspension-closeout-and-no-mission-by-subaward-fog.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed implementing-partner-and-pass-through constitution** that separates partner eligibility, due diligence, engagement risk, workplans, funding modality, milestone and expenditure reporting, assurance activity, corrective action, suspension, and closeout — so delivery through external partners does not dissolve into subaward fog, unreviewed dependency, or mission by pass-through habit.
- `699-scope-spine-for-ideal-governments-seven-default-tiers-label-to-vocation-crosswalks-two-exception-ladders-and-no-new-tier-theory-every-time.md` — The archive should treat ideal government from micro-local to global as one reusable **scope spine** — micro-local witness-and-stewardship units, municipalities as the first complete governments of ordinary life, metropolitan bodies for shared urban systems, regions for territorial platforms and shared rule, nations as guarantor states, continental bodies as bounded compacts, and global institutions as treaty narrow waists — while mapping ambiguous labels like county, district, province, state, and union back to those archetypes and using collapsed-stack and shared-regime exception ladders where the default seven do not fit.
- `700-minimum-design-packet-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-archetype-vocation-boundary-kit-fiscal-proof-exception-ladder-upgrade-triggers-and-no-essay-length-restatement.md` — Any later archive note that claims what the ideal government at a given scope should be should default to one small **design packet** — name the scope archetype, state the vocation, define the boundary logic, specify the minimum complete kit, show the fiscal and capability proof, declare any exception ladder, and list upgrade or reversibility triggers — so the archive can compare designs, merge revisions, and stay compact without re-arguing the whole multilevel constitution every time.
- `701-adjudication-matrix-for-competing-ideal-governments-of-the-same-function-packet-comparison-dominance-tests-reversible-tie-breaks-and-no-scope-choice-by-ideology-alone.md` — When the archive faces several plausible claims about which scope should govern the same function, it should compare the rival **design packets** through one compact adjudication matrix — vocation fit, boundary honesty, minimum kit completeness, fiscal and capability proof, spillover handling, solidarity and rights-floor fit, democratic proportionality, reversibility, and machinery cost — so the archive can choose or bracket the better packet without collapsing into ideology, naming habit, or essay-length restatement.
- `702-unbundling-mixed-function-claims-before-scope-choice-lane-split-first-packet-second-rivalry-third-and-no-one-tier-answer-to-a-composite-field.md` — Before the archive decides which scope should ideally govern a field, it should first test whether the field is really a **composite bundle of different lanes with different scale logics**; if so, it should split the field into lane-sized claims, build packets for those lanes, and run rivalry only on the pieces that remain genuinely contested, rather than forcing one total jurisdictional answer onto a mixed-function question.
- `703-interface-packets-for-lane-typed-government-stacks-lead-lanes-handoffs-shared-facts-escalation-clocks-and-no-governance-by-glue-folklore.md` — Once the archive has split a composite field into lane-sized scope packets, it should also publish one **interface packet** for the resulting typed stack: name the lead for each lane, the handoff triggers between lanes, the shared facts and records that must travel, the timing and escalation rules, the fiscal and liability crosswalks, and the public route map, so distributed government does not collapse back into blame circulation, duplicate work, or quiet recentralization by whoever controls the glue.
- `704-control-plane-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-priorities-common-ledger-exception-queues-and-no-hidden-center-by-coordination.md` — Once the archive has split a field into lane-sized governments and published the seam rules between them, it should also publish one narrow **control-plane packet** for the field as a whole — naming the common goals, rights floors, shared metrics, review rhythm, exception queue, budget and capacity crosswalk, and upgrade triggers — so the stack can be steered and inspected as one public system without quietly inventing an undeclared super-tier that governs by coordination alone.
- `705-mode-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-normal-degraded-emergency-recovery-handback-clocks-and-no-permanent-government-by-exception.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, and a field control plane, it should also publish one **mode packet** for the field — naming normal, degraded, emergency, and recovery operation, the triggers for entering each mode, what powers and duties change, what rights and service floors remain non-negotiable, and what handback clock returns the stack to ordinary routing — so a stressed system does not quietly adopt emergency pathways as its permanent constitution.
- `709-challenge-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-entry-routes-complaints-petitions-second-look-lanes-feedback-duties-and-no-public-voice-by-consultation-theater.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, and an evidence packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **challenge packet** naming who may raise what kind of challenge, through which front door, with what triage into complaint, petition, appeal, ombuds, whistleblowing, or regulatory lanes, on what clocks, with what feedback and anti-retaliation duties, so the field can be corrected by the governed instead of merely observed by them.
- `710-participation-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-agenda-windows-method-fit-inclusion-duties-response-ledgers-and-no-public-input-by-one-off-hearing.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, an evidence packet, and a challenge packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **participation packet** naming which design and priority questions are open to public participation, at which policy-cycle phase, by which method, with which inclusion and response duties, so public input shapes the field before harm, drift, or redesign battles are forced into the complaint system.
- `711-oversight-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-audit-inspection-ombuds-parliamentary-scrutiny-follow-up-ledgers-and-no-self-certification-by-the-same-office.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, an evidence packet, a challenge packet, and a participation packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **oversight packet** naming which independent bodies outside the live control plane may inspect which questions, on what triggers and calendars, with what access powers, response duties, and follow-up ledger, so the field is not left certifying itself by the same office that designed, funded, or operated it.
- `712-amendment-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-change-classes-ratification-ladders-version-ledgers-drift-logs-and-no-field-redesign-by-memo.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, an evidence packet, challenge and participation packets, and an oversight packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **amendment packet** naming which changes are merely tuning and which are constitutional, who may propose them, what participation and scrutiny gates apply, what ratification ladder adopts them, when they take effect, and what version ledger plus drift log keeps the field from being redesigned by memo, queue custom, temporary exception, or software default.
- `713-delegation-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-principal-lane-reserved-powers-operator-chains-step-in-rights-and-no-public-duty-by-outsourced-wrapper.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, and amendment discipline for a field, it should also publish one narrow **delegation packet** saying which slice of the field is still constitutionally owned by the public lane, which execution work may be delegated to public bodies, contractors, concessionaires, nonprofits, co-operatives, or platforms, what powers remain non-delegable, what contract-management and records capacity the principal must retain, what step-in and handback rights keep continuity real, and what review route prevents public duty from disappearing into an outsourced wrapper.
- `714-fiscal-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-operating-base-equalization-spine-reserves-capital-lanes-and-no-government-by-grant-fog.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, and delegation rules for a field, it should also publish one narrow **fiscal packet** saying what recurring operating base actually funds the field, which lane holds budget and treasury authority, what equalization or solidarity rule corrects uneven burdens, what reserve and contingency ladder keeps shocks from becoming constitutional panic, what capital and debt lane is lawful, and what grants may supplement but not substitute for an honest money constitution.
- `715-capability-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-employer-lane-merit-floor-training-ladders-surge-rosters-and-no-government-by-borrowed-payroll.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, operating modes, repair rules, sunset rules, evidence, challenge, participation, oversight, amendment discipline, delegation rules, and a fiscal packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **capability packet** saying which lane is the employer of record and capability steward, what minimum in-house core the field must retain, what merit and qualification floor applies, what training and profession ladders sustain scarce skills, what secondment and surge rules are allowed, and what vacancy or churn triggers open repair or redesign — so the field does not rely on borrowed payroll, consultant memory, or permanent emergency staffing to remain governmental at all.
