- `470-intake-failure-classification-handoff-vs-artifact-and-manual-fallback-lanes.md` — When consequential notices, appeals, evidence packets, or supplier submissions fail to arrive, open, or register, the archive should distinguish bad artifact from bad delivery or handoff and preserve a typed manual fallback lane so rights do not disappear into one broken digital path.
- `475-official-communications-as-evidence-correction-chains-and-channel-registries.md` — Consequential public-AI communications should be treated as first-class evidence surfaces with an official-channel registry, explicit correction linkage, and capture rules for what was said where and when, so public notice cannot drift into silent edits, split-view updates, or screenshot folklore.
- `479-governance-diff-surface-registries-canonical-review-planes-and-drift-funnels.md` — Consequential public-AI programs should maintain a canonical registry of governance diff surfaces so review, release, and audit can say which change planes exist, which ones were checked, and which new surface types require explicit admission instead of silently creating fresh drift territory.
- `515-digital-public-infrastructure-by-scope-local-access-city-service-design-national-rails-and-global-open-standards.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern digital public infrastructure by keeping assisted access, trust-building, and service usability close to people; letting municipalities and metropolitan institutions integrate place-based services and local data uses under strong law; reserving identity, payments, base registries, secure data exchange, notifications, cybersecurity baselines, and universal-access duties to the nation; and keeping the global layer focused on open technical standards and narrow identifier coordination rather than allowing either platform monopolies or a fantasy world digital state to swallow public governance.
- `527-end-of-life-and-death-care-by-scope-local-accompaniment-municipal-death-administration-regional-palliative-capacity-national-rights-and-global-pain-relief.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat dying, death care, and bereavement as governed phases of civic life rather than hospital leftovers: households, friends, and community institutions can accompany the dying and mourn the dead but should not be left alone to navigate pain, paperwork, and impossible choices; municipalities should make death registration, burial or cremation access, bereavement navigation, and culturally plural local practice legible and reachable; regional bodies should coordinate palliative-care networks, hospice and specialist capacity, coronial or medical-examiner functions, and referral pathways that outrun one city; nations should guarantee consent law, advance directives, surrogate decision rules, equitable palliative access, medicine availability, and vital-registration baselines; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in essential pain-relief access, rights norms, and knowledge exchange rather than pretending to legislate every intimate end-of-life question for the whole world.
- `537-outer-space-and-orbital-commons-by-scope-local-hosting-regional-spaceports-national-authorization-and-global-sustainability-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat outer space as a global commons of use rather than a frontier of silent enclosure: local communities should hold real say over launch sites, tracking stations, astronomy impacts, land use, emergency planning, and public benefit where space infrastructure touches the ground; regional institutions should coordinate spaceport corridors, environmental review, disaster interfaces, and research ecosystems where activities spill across jurisdictions; nations should authorize and continuously supervise national activities in space, register objects, govern liability, spectrum and orbital use discipline, public research, procurement, and security constraints, and prevent private launch markets from becoming lightly regulated sovereignty proxies; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in non-appropriation, peaceful use, registration, debris mitigation, conjunction information-sharing, and long-term sustainability rather than letting orbit become an unmanaged congestion market.
- `562-civil-registration-vital-statistics-and-legal-identity-institutions-by-scope-local-event-capture-municipal-service-access-regional-backstops-national-trust-frameworks-and-no-government-by-documentary-erasure.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat civil registration, vital statistics, and legal identity as a linked but non-collapsed public infrastructure: keep event notification and ordinary registration close to births, deaths, marriages, divorces, and residence reality; make municipal or county-level offices, health interfaces, and mobile service routes the ordinary access layer; use regional or provincial backstops where geography, federalism, or sparse settlement require them; reserve national government for the legal-status framework, secure and privacy-bounded identity trust architecture, interoperability rules, consular extension, and systemwide statistics coordination; and never let personhood, kinship, or access to basic rights depend on surviving a hostile documentary maze.
- `568-land-administration-and-cadastre-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-parcel-service-regional-coordination-national-tenure-rules-and-no-government-by-documentary-dispossession.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat land administration as a scale-matched constitutional infrastructure rather than a clerical property office: community and customary institutions should help witness real people-to-land relationships, municipal or county offices should be the ordinary parcel-service front door, metropolitan or regional layers should pool cadastre and geospatial coordination where fragmentation would break the map, national or constitutional-state law should own tenure forms, identifiers, interoperability, and register integrity, and continental or global bodies should provide standards and support rather than pretending a world cadastre exists.
- `570-legal-entity-business-and-beneficial-ownership-registries-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-entry-desks-regional-coordination-national-public-truth-and-no-government-by-paper-shell.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat organizational identity as constitutional infrastructure rather than clerical residue: communities can help witness real economic and associational life, municipalities or counties should usually provide the reachable entry desk for ordinary business-facing registrations and permits, regional or state layers should coordinate where federal structure or market geography requires it, national or constitutional-state law should own the authoritative registry of legal persons and the rules for unique identifiers, lifecycle events, disclosure, and strike-off, beneficial ownership should be held through a public authority or tightly governed equivalent with rapid lawful access and strong update discipline, and continental or global bodies should provide interoperability rails rather than pretending there can be one sovereign company register for the world.
- `576-base-registries-identifiers-reference-data-and-interoperability-by-scope-community-error-surfacing-municipal-data-stewardship-regional-brokers-national-authoritative-sources-and-no-government-by-contradictory-copies.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **base registries, identifiers, reference data, and interoperability** as the **constitutional integration layer** of government: keep error surfacing, assisted correction, and local fact challenge close to people and firms; use municipalities and other frontline bodies as disciplined stewards and consumers of authoritative data rather than rival sovereign databases; pool interconnection, exchange infrastructure, and semantic support above fragmented local jurisdictions where scale adds competence; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for designating authoritative sources, assigning identifier rules, governing access, and maintaining shared code lists and metadata; and keep continental or global roles narrow enough to support cross-border evidence exchange, schemas, and semantic alignment without becoming a world master database.
- `632-scope-audit-triggers-review-packets-evaluation-lanes-and-no-constitutional-sleepwalk.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should keep a standing **scope audit registry** that uses territorial-impact, fiscal, democratic, and operational tripwires to trigger a typed **review packet** whenever real responsibility drifts away from the nominal map, so repair begins from evidence and laddered choice rather than from crisis improvisation or silent constitutional sleepwalk.
- `633-canonical-scope-registers-responsibility-matrices-exception-ledgers-and-no-government-by-jurisdiction-folklore.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should keep one **canonical public scope register** that shows, for each major function and lane of authority, the default legal home, territorial footprint, finance path, real delivery chain, exceptions, temporary deviations, review route, and next review date, so the stack is governed as an inspectable object rather than inferred from scattered statutes, grants, habits, and insider folklore.
- `634-scope-jurisprudence-digests-precedent-registers-and-no-multilevel-government-by-constitutional-amnesia.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should preserve competence, self-government, and rescoping rulings in a public **scope-jurisprudence digest** linked to the canonical scope register, so settlements of who may govern what become accessible constitutional memory rather than specialist folklore, serial relitigation, or unpublished administrative custom.
- `635-scope-diff-packets-before-after-register-amendments-and-no-constitutional-change-by-side-effect.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require any legally or operationally material change to who governs what to ship with a public **scope-diff packet** against the canonical scope register, showing the before-and-after allocation, legal lane, consultation or consent route, jurisprudence impact, exception clocks, and review duties, so the stack cannot be rewired by side effect across statutes, grants, budgets, software, or emergency residue.
- `637-scope-overrides-explicit-departure-statements-review-clocks-and-no-constitutional-clearance-by-quiet-disregard.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should allow departure from a negative or conditional **scope opinion** only through one explicit public **scope-override statement** naming the disagreement, legal authority, reasons, rejected alternatives, temporary or permanent status, review and challenge clocks, and required register updates, so the review lane is neither a hidden veto nor a decorative memo and the stack cannot be changed by quiet disregard.
- `639-scope-conformance-before-go-live-implementation-attestations-readiness-gates-and-no-stack-change-by-deployment-drift.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require one public **scope-conformance attestation before go-live** for any materially stack-altering measure: budgets, regulations, grants, contracts, staffing, digital workflows, supervisory routines, public communications, and remedy routes should be checked against the adopted packet, opinion, override, and live register so that implementation cannot quietly move power farther than law and consent actually authorised.
- `640-post-launch-scope-observability-variance-ledgers-rollback-lanes-and-no-stack-change-by-runtime-custom.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should treat materially stack-altering reforms as **actively observable after go-live**, with one linked post-launch variance ledger, short review clocks, named correction and rollback lanes, and explicit closure criteria, so the lived operation of budgets, staff, systems, supervision, and remedies cannot quietly become a different constitutional settlement by runtime custom.
- `643-scope-reactivation-certificates-dormancy-fresh-clearance-and-no-constitutional-necromancy.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should require one public **scope-reactivation certificate** before any materially stack-bearing authority, exception lane, shared body, or supervisory hold returns from retirement, dormancy, suspension, or expiry: old text, old systems, old habits, and old crisis muscle memory should not make public power live again without fresh legality, current rights checks, updated scope classification, and a visible register change.
- `648-scope-functional-equivalence-rules-anti-circumvention-tests-and-no-stack-change-by-relabeling.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should classify **materially stack-altering moves by their real effect rather than by their chosen label**: if a grant condition, procurement framework, software default, model contract, coordination protocol, “pilot”, guidance note, or emergency instruction functionally reallocates who decides, who must comply, who pays, who may object, or which tier now governs in practice, it should travel through the same packet, opinion, override, register, and review lanes as any openly named scope change.
- `653-scope-source-hierarchies-authority-ladders-and-no-stack-change-by-the-loudest-surface.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should settle disputes about **who governs what** against a declared **source hierarchy** rather than against whichever surface is loudest, newest, easiest to find, or already wired into daily operations: constitutional and statutory text, authoritative judgments, and explicit scope acts should outrank derivative registers, and derivative registers should outrank budgets, contracts, software behavior, dashboards, FAQs, and public-relations residue.
- `662-global-institution-toolkit-by-problem-class-assemblies-secretariats-scientific-panels-registries-inspection-compliance-funds-and-no-world-state-monoculture.md` — The ideal global layer should be built from a **small toolkit of treaty-bound institutional forms matched to problem class** rather than from one fantasy model of world government: use assemblies and councils for norm-setting, secretariats and focal-point networks for continuous coordination, scientific panels for shared factual baselines, registries and reporting systems for comparability, inspection or verification where cheating matters, dispute and compliance lanes where interpretation recurs, and dedicated funds where solidarity is required — while refusing both fake world-state domesticity and empty declarations with no operating spine.
- `667-differentiated-commitments-in-shared-regimes-reservations-opt-outs-derogations-transition-periods-territorial-application-review-clocks-and-no-uniformity-by-false-claim.md` — Shared regimes should maintain a **typed differentiation register** that distinguishes reservations, interpretive declarations, opt-outs, temporary derogations, transition periods, territorial applications, and enhanced-cooperation rings — with legal basis, scope, duration, review clock, and accession or withdrawal path — so a regime can use lawful variable geometry without lying that every member carries the same obligation.
- `668-shared-regime-change-ladders-review-conferences-amendments-protocols-annex-updates-tacit-acceptance-version-registers-and-no-regime-rewrite-by-secretariat-faq.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed change ladder** that distinguishes political guidance, interpretive guidance, implementing decisions, annex or technical updates, formal amendments, optional protocols, and refounding texts — each with its own adoption body, consent rule, objection or non-acceptance lane, entry-into-force logic, version register, and domestic landing path — so the regime can evolve without either paralysis or quiet constitutional rewrite by circular, dashboard, or FAQ.
- `674-shared-regime-records-and-publicity-public-private-sessions-document-registers-meeting-records-vote-records-authentic-texts-corrections-and-no-governance-by-missing-papertrail.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed documentary constitution** that separates session publicity, agenda and paper circulation, official document registers, meeting-record formats, vote records, authentic texts, correction notices, and retention or access rules — so public authority does not vanish into missing minutes, unofficial drafts, or document folklore.
- `677-shared-regime-external-participation-constitutions-accreditation-observer-categories-submissions-hearings-transparency-registers-and-no-public-power-by-lanyard.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed external-participation constitution** that separates membership from observer or accredited-participant status, standing accreditation from session registration, document access from floor rights, written submissions from negotiation rights, and consultation from decision power — so public authority does not drift toward whoever got a badge, a side-room invitation, or a privileged mailing list.
- `695-shared-regime-enterprise-risk-and-internal-control-constitutions-risk-appetite-owners-registers-control-testing-exceptions-assurance-maps-and-no-governance-by-unknown-exposure.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **typed enterprise-risk-and-internal-control constitution** that separates risk appetite, risk taxonomy, owner assignment, principal-risk review, key-control design, control testing, exception handling, assurance mapping, and governing-body reporting — so operational exposure does not disappear into unknown exposure, stale registers, control folklore, or audit surprise government.
- `704-control-plane-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-priorities-common-ledger-exception-queues-and-no-hidden-center-by-coordination.md` — Once the archive has split a field into lane-sized governments and published the seam rules between them, it should also publish one narrow **control-plane packet** for the field as a whole — naming the common goals, rights floors, shared metrics, review rhythm, exception queue, budget and capacity crosswalk, and upgrade triggers — so the stack can be steered and inspected as one public system without quietly inventing an undeclared super-tier that governs by coordination alone.
- `707-sunset-packets-for-obsolete-government-lanes-bodies-and-temporary-machinery-review-triggers-successor-homes-residue-registers-closure-proof-and-no-immortal-institutions-by-inherited-backlog.md` — Once a field has repair packets, it should also publish one **sunset packet** whenever review shows that a lane, body, or temporary governance machine no longer deserves to exist in live form — naming the trigger, the successor home or true extinction rule, the rights and service floors that still bind during wind-down, the residue register for cases, contracts, assets, staff, records, data, debt, and public-facing channels, the closure proof, and the reactivation rule — so obsolete institutions do not stay alive merely because they still have backlog, leases, websites, or logos.
- `708-evidence-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-shared-indicators-trigger-maps-blind-spot-registers-assurance-rhythm-and-no-government-by-dashboard-vibes.md` — Lane-typed government fields should publish one compact **evidence packet** that names the shared indicators, signal owners, trigger map, blind-spot register, and assurance rhythm used to judge the field — so control planes, mode shifts, repair packets, and sunset reviews run on explicit evidence with known gaps rather than on anecdotes, heroic operator memory, or dashboard theater.
- `710-participation-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-agenda-windows-method-fit-inclusion-duties-response-ledgers-and-no-public-input-by-one-off-hearing.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, an evidence packet, and a challenge packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **participation packet** naming which design and priority questions are open to public participation, at which policy-cycle phase, by which method, with which inclusion and response duties, so public input shapes the field before harm, drift, or redesign battles are forced into the complaint system.
- `711-oversight-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-audit-inspection-ombuds-parliamentary-scrutiny-follow-up-ledgers-and-no-self-certification-by-the-same-office.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, an evidence packet, a challenge packet, and a participation packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **oversight packet** naming which independent bodies outside the live control plane may inspect which questions, on what triggers and calendars, with what access powers, response duties, and follow-up ledger, so the field is not left certifying itself by the same office that designed, funded, or operated it.
- `712-amendment-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-change-classes-ratification-ladders-version-ledgers-drift-logs-and-no-field-redesign-by-memo.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, an evidence packet, challenge and participation packets, and an oversight packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **amendment packet** naming which changes are merely tuning and which are constitutional, who may propose them, what participation and scrutiny gates apply, what ratification ladder adopts them, when they take effect, and what version ledger plus drift log keeps the field from being redesigned by memo, queue custom, temporary exception, or software default.
- `731-cutover-witness-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-effective-state-old-holder-new-holder-exception-ledger-and-no-transfer-by-folklore.md` — Once the archive has a continuity packet for scope shifts (`730`), it should also keep one compact **cutover witness packet** for the handoff moment itself: every materially consequential move across scopes should leave behind one contemporaneous public-and-reviewable witness saying what changed, when it changed, which holder lost authority, which holder gained authority, what remained transitional, which queues, records, contracts, and budgets were still in flight, which exceptions stayed live, and what fallback path still existed — so later review does not have to reconstruct the transfer from rumor, screenshots, or contradictory portal residue.
- `733-bridge-closure-packets-for-ideal-government-scope-shifts-host-release-channel-retirement-records-signoff-and-no-temporary-forever.md` — Once the archive has a transitional-hosting packet (`732`), it should also require one compact **bridge-closure packet** before anybody may claim the scope shift is operationally complete: classify the closure state, retire or rewire every legacy front door, release host-side powers and keys, freeze and hand over the final evidence package, settle the residual exceptions ledger, and refuse to relabel an unresolved dependency as “complete” merely because the cutover date has passed.
- `739-residual-estate-packets-for-post-custody-government-closeout-shells-claims-record-access-financial-tail-review-clocks-and-no-ghost-state-by-leftover-residue.md` — Once the archive can place named surfaces into temporary neutral custody (`736`), release them out again (`737`), and discharge the custodian itself (`738`), it should also keep one compact **residual-estate packet** for the narrower afterlife that sometimes honestly remains: a typed closeout shell for surviving claims, residual funds, record-access duties, litigation or audit tails, and other bounded obligations, with one public route, one residue ledger, one accountable owner, and one termination proof so a leftover estate does not quietly become a ghost state by residue.
- `745-tombstone-consolidation-and-register-absorption-packets-for-retired-government-bodies-scopes-and-shells-directory-merge-alias-preservation-correction-chain-retention-and-no-disappearance-by-tidying.md` — Once the archive can create a tombstone (`741`), reroute it (`742`), correct it (`743`), and steward it (`744`), it should also keep one compact **tombstone-consolidation and register-absorption packet**: one bounded proof object for folding a standalone dead-page surface into a broader historical register, catalogue, or directory without losing discoverability, correction history, or the plain statement that the old authority is dead, so the polity does not mistake tidier information architecture for permission to erase institutional memory.
- `746-historical-register-rehousing-and-cross-catalog-migration-packets-for-absorbed-tombstones-register-home-change-stable-entry-identifiers-alias-continuity-and-no-disappearance-by-replatforming.md` — Once the archive can absorb standalone tombstones into grouped historical registers (`745`), it should also keep one compact **historical-register rehousing and cross-catalog migration packet**: one bounded proof object for moving absorbed dead-object entries from one register, catalogue, directory, or memorial platform to another without losing individually addressable identity, alias coverage, correction lineage, or the plain statement that the authority is dead, so the polity does not mistake platform migration for permission to break historical lookup.
- `747-register-deconsolidation-and-standalone-restoration-packets-for-absorbed-tombstones-reversible-grouping-object-specific-re-expansion-and-no-permanent-flattening-by-catalog-convenience.md` — Once the archive can absorb standalone tombstones into grouped historical registers (`745`) and later move those grouped registers across homes or catalogues (`746`), it should also keep one compact **register-deconsolidation and standalone-restoration packet**: one bounded proof object for pulling one absorbed dead-object entry back out into its own standalone memorial surface when grouping proves too lossy, disputed, high-traffic, symbolically weighty, or operationally confusing, so the polity does not mistake one successful consolidation step for permission to keep every dead authority permanently flattened inside a catalogue.
- `748-historical-object-boundary-repair-packets-for-retired-government-bodies-scopes-and-shells-split-merge-creator-links-and-no-one-dead-authority-by-cataloguing-accident.md` — Once the archive can absorb tombstones into grouped historical registers (`745`), move those grouped registers across homes (`746`), and restore one absorbed entry back into a standalone memorial surface (`747`), it should also keep one compact **historical-object-boundary-repair packet**: one bounded proof object for the harder case where the memorial object boundary itself turned out to be wrong — one entry actually conflated several distinct dead authorities, or several entries were really one dead authority all along — so the polity can split, merge, or relink historical objects without rewriting closure history, losing aliases, or mistaking successor routing for object identity.
- `766-lobbying-transparency-and-revolving-door-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-registers-meeting-logs-gift-rules-cooling-off-advice-lanes-and-no-policy-by-invisible-influence.md` — Ideal governments should treat lobbying and influence as **a legitimate democratic input that becomes dangerous when it is invisible, unequal, or privately entangled with officeholding**: they should disclose who seeks to influence whom, on whose behalf, about what, through which channels, under which gift and hospitality rules, and with what pre- and post-public-employment constraints, so policy is not quietly written by invisible influence.
- `767-conflict-of-interest-and-asset-and-interest-disclosure-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-risk-tiering-recusal-divestment-verification-publication-and-no-office-with-a-private-shadow-ledger.md` — Ideal governments should treat conflicts of interest and asset-and-interest disclosure as **a live decision-integrity system rather than a yearly paperwork ritual**: officials in risk-bearing roles should disclose relevant interests and assets under tiered rules, update them when circumstances change, recuse from affected decisions, divest or use stronger separation tools where conflicts are not manageable, and face real verification and sanction, so office is not shadowed by a private ledger the public never sees.
- `769-supreme-audit-and-public-accounts-follow-up-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-independence-open-reports-opposition-chaired-hearings-implementation-ledgers-and-no-accountability-by-unread-audit.md` — Ideal governments should treat supreme audit and legislative follow-up as **a standing ex post accountability engine rather than a publication ritual**: an independent external auditor should be able to choose and conduct audits within its lawful mandate, access records, publish findings, and report to the public and legislature, while a public-accounts or equivalent committee should hold hearings, require executive responses, track implementation, and distinguish correction from repetition, so audit does not end as an unread PDF or ceremonial annual hearing.
- `771-public-policy-evaluation-and-management-response-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-workplans-independence-publication-response-ledgers-reopen-triggers-and-no-learning-by-unanswered-recommendation.md` — Ideal governments should treat public-policy evaluation as **a standing learning-and-accountability lane rather than a report genre**: significant policies, programmes, and reforms should be selected through visible workplans and triggers, evaluated with enough independence and methodological fit to say what is working and for whom, answered through time-bound management responses, tracked through public recommendation ledgers, and reopened where implementation stalls or the policy context materially changes, so learning is not reduced to ceremonial “lessons learned” prose with no decision route.
- `793-maintenance-calendars-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-benchmark-refresh-stress-drill-cadence-trigger-overrides-public-registries-and-no-constitutional-care-by-sporadic-panic.md` — The archive should pair its ideal-government answer key, benchmark cards, stress cards, and scope-audit triggers with one compact **maintenance-calendar rule** for each scope — fixed benchmark refreshes, typed drill cadence, trigger-based overrides, publication and follow-up duties, and explicit closure or rescoping lanes — so multilevel constitutions are maintained as routine public infrastructure rather than rediscovered only during reform waves or crisis embarrassment.
- `795-public-proof-packs-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-benchmark-publication-stress-summaries-maintenance-ledgers-transition-boards-and-no-constitutional-claim-without-outward-evidence.md` — The archive should pair its answer-key, benchmark, stress-test, maintenance, and upgrade-path notes with one compact **public proof-pack rule** for each scope: **publish the minimum outward evidence that lets residents, auditors, legislatures, journalists, courts, and peer polities verify what the arrangement is, how it scored, what failed under stress, what is due next, and where any transition actually stands**.
- `801-finding-registers-for-scope-assessments-lane-specific-scores-confidence-classes-severity-clocks-contradiction-residue-and-no-constitutional-verdict-by-blended-number.md` — The archive should pair its answer-key, benchmark, assessment-mission, proof-pack, and contestability notes with one compact **finding-register grammar**: **every serious scope review should express its result lane by lane, state confidence and severity separately, preserve unresolved contradiction residue, allow no-score where proof is thin, and attach next-action clocks, so constitutional judgments are not collapsed into one blended number or one breezy headline verdict**.
- `802-management-responses-and-corrective-action-ledgers-for-scope-governance-finding-by-finding-owners-dependencies-budget-closure-proof-and-no-verdict-without-a-repair-docket.md` — The archive should pair its assessment-mission and finding-register notes with one compact **management-response grammar**: **every material scope finding should receive a finding-by-finding response that states acceptance posture, named owner at the right scope, dependency chain, budget and legal posture, delivery clock, closure proof, and escalation rule, so review does not end in literary recommendations, political nodding, or an unowned pile of next steps**.
- `803-close-out-verification-and-reopen-rules-for-scope-governance-repair-ledgers-mid-term-checks-field-revisit-residual-risk-and-no-closure-by-self-certification.md` — The archive should pair its finding-register and management-response notes with one compact **close-out and verification grammar**: **every material scope repair item should face a typed follow-up review that tests closure proof against live conditions, declares residual risk, decides close / continue / reopen / rescope, and names the next verification clock, so corrective-action ledgers do not turn into self-closing spreadsheets or polite fiction**.
- `804-tracer-routes-and-lived-path-verification-for-scope-governance-user-journeys-fund-flows-case-walks-handoff-tests-and-no-constitution-by-org-chart.md` — The archive should pair its assessment-mission, finding-register, management-response, and close-out notes with one compact **tracer-route grammar**: **every serious scope review should follow a small set of real or lawfully simulated paths — case, payment, referral, complaint, permit, incident, data handoff, or handback — across institutions, clocks, and records, so governments are not judged only by statutes, org charts, or curated meetings instead of by the routes people and work actually travel**.
- `806-evidence-registers-and-provenance-chains-for-scope-assessments-exhibit-ids-source-typing-redaction-ledgers-finding-links-and-no-verdict-by-orphaned-exhibit.md` — The archive should pair its assessment-mission, sampling, tracer-route, finding-register, and close-out notes with one compact **evidence-register grammar**: **every serious scope review should keep a stable exhibit register that says what each evidence object is, where it came from, what version or date it belongs to, what was redacted or withheld, which finding it supports or contradicts, and how later reviewers can reuse it, so constitutional judgments are not built from orphaned exhibits, floating screenshots, or unverifiable quotations**.
- `807-assessment-team-independence-and-conflict-discipline-for-scope-reviews-recusal-rosters-secondment-firebreaks-host-picked-experts-donor-pathways-and-no-constitutional-judgment-by-interested-mission.md` — The archive should pair its assessment-mission, evidence-register, contestability, and close-out notes with one compact **mission-integrity grammar**: **every serious scope review should declare who is judging, who is only informing, what interests and funding pathways each reviewer carries, what firebreaks apply to secondees and host-nominated specialists, when recusal is mandatory, and how outsiders can challenge the composition of the team before findings harden into the live constitution, so the archive does not mistake expertise, proximity, or funding convenience for independence**.
- `808-calibration-packs-moderation-loops-and-precedent-banks-for-scope-assessments-score-anchors-difficult-case-conferences-documented-departures-and-no-benchmark-by-reviewer-mood.md` — The archive should pair its benchmark, mission, evidence-register, and mission-integrity notes with one compact **review-calibration grammar**: **every serious scope assessment should keep a small calibration pack with lane-specific score anchors, worked examples, threshold splits, precedent notes, moderation checkpoints, and documented departures, so that different review teams can reach comparably disciplined judgments without collapsing everything into one blended score or one charismatic reviewer’s mood**.
- `817-participation-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-open-dockets-hearings-user-councils-deliberative-mini-publics-response-ledgers-and-no-heavy-power-by-consultation-theater.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **who owns it**, **how money moves through it**, **where its operating spine lives**, and **where scrutiny and redress live**, it should also be able to say **what participation chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should publish open dockets and simple input windows rather than staging fake popular mandates, shared-service backbones should run structured user and accessibility input without pretending pooled operations are a substitute for elected politics, bounded functional authorities should carry recurring hearings and response duties plus deliberative methods where long-horizon tradeoffs justify them, and general-purpose territorial tiers should own a full participation constitution rather than borrowing legitimacy from consultation theater.
- `834-information-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-ledgers-municipal-record-homes-metro-observatories-national-statistics-and-treaty-registries.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should authoritative public facts, records, and decision visibility ordinarily live at each scope?** with scale-matched defaults rather than one dashboard fetish: **micro-local bodies should keep simple minutes, noticeboards, steward ledgers, and escalation logs rather than miniature data states; municipalities should be the first level with a full public information constitution of clerks or record stewards, open meeting packets, service and permit records, publication calendars, and reusable public data; metropolitan and regional governments should own their own observatories, geospatial baselines, and cross-boundary performance records rather than parasitic dependence on a host city or ministry; national government should carry the thickest official-statistics, gazette, archive, and interoperability spine; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound but still maintain comparability standards, registries, alerting channels, and shared reporting rather than private dashboards or counterfeit world omniscience**.

## regulatory-governance

- `410-public-deployment-registries-for-automated-state-action.md` — When public institutions use automated or AI-assisted systems that shape decisions, entitlements, enforcement, or public interaction, there should be a **living deployment registry** that shows what is in use, in what phase, under whose authority, and with what transparency record.
- `447-audience-exact-disclosure-classes-exposure-boundaries-and-review-lanes.md` — Governance artifacts for consequential public AI should carry exact audience and exposure labels so public, affected-person, operator, reviewer, regulator, supplier, and privileged-admin lanes cannot be silently mixed or widened.
- `503-intelligence-by-scope-no-local-secret-police-judicial-authorization-minimization-and-multi-key-oversight.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should keep intelligence and surveillance narrowly scoped to genuine national-security functions under public law, forbid local secret-police formation and routine law-enforcement drift, require prior independent authorization and minimization for intrusive measures, and place the whole system under layered executive, legislative, judicial, privacy, and redress oversight so secrecy never matures into ungoverned power.
- `516-markets-and-company-power-by-scope-local-entry-metro-space-national-antitrust-and-fair-global-rules.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern markets by keeping entry barriers, permits, public procurement access, and everyday consumer signal detection close to local life; using metropolitan and regional institutions to manage commercial geography, logistics, and market systems that cross municipal borders; reserving competition law, merger control, company law, securities rules, labour and consumer floors, and strategic industrial discipline to the nation; and using the global layer for trade predictability, anti-cartel cooperation, tax-base protection, and narrow common rules that prevent regulatory arbitrage without constitutionalizing corporate power above democracy.
- `534-extractive-resources-by-scope-local-consent-regional-cumulative-impacts-national-public-rents-and-global-just-transition-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat subsoil wealth as a temporary public endowment rather than a permanent license for frontier sacrifice: affected communities and Indigenous peoples should hold real consent, monitoring, grievance, and benefit-sharing power close to the site; regional bodies should govern cumulative impacts on water, housing, health, roads, labour markets, tailings, and emergency corridors across the wider extraction zone; nations should own licensing architecture, contract disclosure, beneficial-ownership rules, royalties, sovereign wealth or stabilization policy, closure liability, anti-corruption enforcement, and diversification strategy; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in transparency standards, trade and due-diligence rules, conflict prevention, and just-transition principles rather than letting a scramble for critical minerals recreate colonial extraction under green branding.
- `536-oceans-coasts-and-fisheries-by-scope-local-stewardship-regional-seascapes-national-jurisdiction-and-global-high-seas-guardrails.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat the ocean as both a lived coast and a shared planetary system: coastal communities, ports, and small-scale fishers should hold real stewardship, monitoring, harbour, and livelihood voice close to place; regional or sea-basin institutions should govern migratory stocks, coastal erosion, estuaries, shipping spillovers, marine protected networks, and cumulative seascape impacts at the ecological scale that actually exists; coastal states should own marine spatial planning within their jurisdiction, fisheries law, labour and safety enforcement, port-state control, public marine science, and fair distribution of marine rents; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in the law of the sea, high-seas biodiversity, shipping pollution, seabed restraint, and shared fish-stock rules rather than letting coastal nationalism or flag-of-convenience arbitrage hollow out the ocean commons.
- `539-banking-credit-and-financial-stability-by-scope-local-relationship-lending-regional-development-finance-national-prudential-oversight-and-global-backstops.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat banking and credit as a public-risk-bearing capability rather than a private allocation game: households, workers, firms, and local institutions can surface credit exclusion, predatory products, and place-specific capital starvation but should not be left to self-insure against systemic finance; municipalities can convene local credit intelligence, public banking interfaces, and anti-exclusion measures but should not act as miniature prudential sovereigns; regional institutions should govern development banks, housing and infrastructure finance platforms, and sectoral transition tools where production systems and catchments are wider than one city; nations should own licensing, prudential supervision, macroprudential policy, deposit insurance, resolution, lender-of-last-resort functions, and the constitutional line between utility banking and speculative risk; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in supervisory standards, cross-border resolution cooperation, correspondent-finance continuity, and anti-arbitrage floors rather than pretending world technocracy can substitute for domestic democratic control.
- `540-trade-customs-and-border-procedures-by-scope-local-port-interfaces-regional-gateways-national-trade-policy-and-global-rules.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat trade governance as both a rules system and a border operations system: households, workers, firms, and local communities can surface chokepoints, corruption, hazardous shipments, and the lived burden of gateways but should not each define external trade law; municipalities should govern port-adjacent land use, truck conflict, inspection-site interfaces, market transparency, and emergency support for traders without becoming fragmented customs sovereignties; regional institutions should coordinate corridors, dry ports, airports, inland terminals, and gateway ecosystems across the geography through which goods actually move; nations should own tariff schedules, trade agreements, customs law, single-window architecture, revenue collection, sanctions and strategic controls, and the constitutional balance between openness, security, labour, and environment; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in trade rules, customs standards, interoperable data models, and facilitation norms rather than pretending that one city or one ministry can govern cross-border exchange alone.
- `545-regulators-inspections-and-enforcement-role-clarity-risk-based-proportionality-due-process-and-no-government-by-shakedown.md` — An ideal polity should treat regulators and inspectorates as bounded public-law institutions whose job is to reduce real harm, preserve fair conditions, and keep essential systems trustworthy; give them clear missions, enough independence to resist improper influence, enough accountability to remain public servants, risk-based and proportionate enforcement tools, visible appeal routes, and budgets not addicted to penalties; and never let licensing, inspection, or fines become a substitute tax system, a patronage machine, or a theatre of arbitrary power.
- `557-detention-corrections-and-reentry-by-scope-local-contact-and-release-links-regional-custody-probation-national-rights-floors-and-no-government-by-warehousing.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **detention, corrections, and reentry** as a **strictly limited, rights-bound, reintegration-oriented part of justice** rather than as a hidden warehousing system: keep local roles focused on family contact, service continuity, diversion support, and release preparation rather than long-term cage sovereignty; use metropolitan or regional institutions for most remand custody, prisons, probation, parole, health continuity, and professionally managed inspectionable facilities; reserve national government for penal law, decarceration incentives, independent monitoring, and non-negotiable humane-treatment floors; and never allow **jails, prisons, or release systems to become opaque human storage insulated from courts, health systems, and society**.
- `564-anti-corruption-bodies-and-integrity-commissions-by-scope-local-routing-regional-case-development-national-specialization-and-no-government-by-heroic-commission.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should not rely on one heroic anti-corruption commission: keep local complaint intake, disclosure routing, whistleblower handoff, and ordinary integrity advice close enough to be usable; place regional or state-level investigative and inspection capacity where corruption markets, procurement webs, and patronage chains cross municipalities or where tiny jurisdictions are too captured to investigate themselves; reserve national government for the preventive architecture required by law, high-level and cross-regional corruption, asset-declaration verification, beneficial-ownership tracing, international cooperation, and strategy coordination; keep the global layer narrow in standards, peer review, and transnational case support; and never let anti-corruption institutions become either decorative ethics theater or unreviewable prosecutor-states.
- `572-standards-metrology-testing-accreditation-and-conformity-assessment-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-inspection-regional-labs-national-quality-infrastructure-and-no-government-by-unverified-measurement.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **standards, metrology, testing, accreditation, and conformity assessment** as a **constitutional measurement layer**: keep user witnessing, complaint, and local inspection close to communities and municipalities; pool expensive laboratories, calibration, and specialist technical capacity at regional scale where fragmentation would waste money or degrade competence; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the quality-infrastructure core — measurement units, national metrology, accreditation, legal metrology, standard-setting mandates, and recognition rules — and use continental and global layers for equivalence, interoperability, and trade discipline rather than for a fantasy of one world product ministry.
- `573-administrative-procedure-permits-and-licenses-by-scope-community-witnessing-municipal-front-doors-regional-technical-review-national-procedure-codes-and-no-government-by-permit-maze.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **administrative procedure, permits, and licenses** as the **constitutional authorization layer** of government: keep lived fact-finding, pre-application help, and ordinary place-based intake close to communities and municipalities; pool specialist review and cross-boundary technical assessment regionally where risks or spillovers justify it; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the core procedural guarantees, common clocks, appeal architecture, and recognition rules that make the whole system legible; and use continental and global layers for interoperability, evidence exchange, and mutual recognition rather than for a fantasy of one world permit desk.
- `578-open-data-and-public-information-reuse-by-scope-community-scrutiny-municipal-publishing-regional-aggregation-national-standards-and-no-government-by-pdf-fog.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **open data and public-information reuse** as the **constitutional public-reuse layer** of government: keep community scrutiny, correction demand, and context close to the people and places described by the data; require municipalities and frontline bodies to publish routine local information in genuinely reusable ways rather than as decorative PDF dumps; pool regional aggregation, comparison, and cross-boundary publication where fragmented local release would make the public blind to shared systems; reserve national or constitutional-state authority for the legal framework on reuse, licensing, metadata, machine-readable publication, privacy and confidentiality boundaries, high-value dataset rules, and catalog standards; and keep continental or global roles narrow enough to support interoperable metadata, cross-border discovery, and common high-value publication patterns without becoming one world data ministry.
- `591-concurrent-competences-lead-lane-typing-paramountcy-defaults-and-no-government-by-overlap-fog.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **concurrent or shared competences as a typed constitutional settlement rather than as a vague admission that “everyone is involved”**: where more than one level must legitimately act in the same field, the law should split the field into visible lanes — such as rights floors, finance, planning, delivery, inspection, data, and remedy — assign a lead level for each lane, state what happens on conflict, preserve lower-tier headroom where that is the point of the arrangement, and publish a coordination rulebook so citizens are not forced to infer government structure from a pile of overlapping claims.
- `615-service-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-service-authorities-operator-chains-commissioning-continuity-and-no-government-by-memorandum-network.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **service home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, and knowledge one: a visible split among authority, operator, and regulator; a named territorial service map showing what stays local and what becomes shared; lawful commissioning, franchising, or direct-operation routes where system services are real; service standards, continuity duties, and fallback rules that survive contracts and politics; and clear public entry and complaint handoffs — so the territory stops being governed through memoranda, host-city favors, improvised consortia, and operator clubs.
- `618-regulatory-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-licensing-permits-standards-inspection-enforcement-and-no-government-by-operator-rulebook.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **regulatory home** as well as democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, service, planning, and capital ones: a visible territorial rulebook, named licensing and permitting lanes where risk demands them, a clear separation among rule-maker, regulator, operator, and reviewer, proportionate inspection and enforcement, and no government by operator rulebook.
- `619-contract-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-procurement-franchising-change-control-exit-capacity-and-no-government-by-concession-patchwork.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **contract home** as well as a democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, service, planning, capital, and regulatory one: a visible buyer-or-commissioner function, explicit make-buy-franchise tests, lawful procurement and concession routes, disciplined contract and change control, published performance and amendment trails, real handback and step-in capacity, and no territorial government by concession patchwork.
- `623-redress-homes-for-shared-territorial-power-complaints-hearings-appeals-ombuds-and-no-government-by-jurisdiction-hunt.md` — Once shared metropolitan or regional power becomes real government, it needs an honest **redress home** as well as democratic, fiscal, administrative, accountability, public-law, intergovernmental, participatory, knowledge, service, planning, capital, regulatory, contract, workforce, digital-operating, and emergency ones: one visible territorial path for complaint, reconsideration, hearing, appeal, ombuds, and judicial review, with reasons, clocks, and no government by jurisdiction hunt.
- `652-scope-desuetude-limits-abandonment-fictions-and-no-stack-change-by-atrophy.md` — An ideal multilevel polity should not let **non-use, weak use, under-enforcement, dormancy, or degraded capacity** silently extinguish protected competence: materially stack-bearing authority may require review, repair, reactivation, or even lawful reassignment, but it should not be treated as lost merely because it was not exercised often, boldly, or recently enough.
- `662-global-institution-toolkit-by-problem-class-assemblies-secretariats-scientific-panels-registries-inspection-compliance-funds-and-no-world-state-monoculture.md` — The ideal global layer should be built from a **small toolkit of treaty-bound institutional forms matched to problem class** rather than from one fantasy model of world government: use assemblies and councils for norm-setting, secretariats and focal-point networks for continuous coordination, scientific panels for shared factual baselines, registries and reporting systems for comparability, inspection or verification where cheating matters, dispute and compliance lanes where interpretation recurs, and dedicated funds where solidarity is required — while refusing both fake world-state domesticity and empty declarations with no operating spine.
- `663-cross-border-integration-ladders-information-sharing-minimum-standards-mutual-recognition-common-enforcement-budget-tools-and-no-union-by-slogan.md` — Ideal continental or plurilateral governance should climb an explicit **integration ladder** — information exchange, benchmarking, minimum standards, mutual recognition, shared operational rails, pooled enforcement, common financing, and only then deeper legislative or fiscal union where truly necessary — so polities can co-govern real spillovers without pretending every problem requires the same depth of union or drifting by slogan into competence creep.
- `666-compliance-ladders-for-shared-regimes-reporting-peer-review-inspection-dispute-settlement-remediation-suspension-and-no-treaty-by-voluntary-vibes.md` — Shared regimes should publish a **graduated compliance ladder** matched to the problem class — from reporting and peer review through technical verification, corrective action, dispute settlement, and where necessary suspension or other consequence — so co-operation does not depend on vibes and enforcement does not jump straight from silence to punishment.
- `709-challenge-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-entry-routes-complaints-petitions-second-look-lanes-feedback-duties-and-no-public-voice-by-consultation-theater.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, and an evidence packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **challenge packet** naming who may raise what kind of challenge, through which front door, with what triage into complaint, petition, appeal, ombuds, whistleblowing, or regulatory lanes, on what clocks, with what feedback and anti-retaliation duties, so the field can be corrected by the governed instead of merely observed by them.
- `711-oversight-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-audit-inspection-ombuds-parliamentary-scrutiny-follow-up-ledgers-and-no-self-certification-by-the-same-office.md` — Once the archive has lane packets, interface packets, a control plane, mode rules, repair rules, sunset rules, an evidence packet, a challenge packet, and a participation packet for a field, it should also publish one narrow **oversight packet** naming which independent bodies outside the live control plane may inspect which questions, on what triggers and calendars, with what access powers, response duties, and follow-up ledger, so the field is not left certifying itself by the same office that designed, funded, or operated it.
- `722-effect-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-activation-ladders-compliance-clocks-stay-rules-and-no-government-by-effective-date-alone.md` — Once the archive has service, case, decision, and notice packets for a field, it should also publish one narrow **effect packet** saying what a consequential act actually changes in the world, which lane executes that change, which clocks, cure ladders, and stay rules govern it, what proof closes it, and how escalation stays proportionate — so the field does not decay into government by effective date alone, paper decision, or cliff-edge enforcement.
- `723-review-packets-for-lane-typed-government-fields-reconsideration-appeal-remand-interim-relief-finality-and-no-government-by-remedy-maze.md` — Once the archive has challenge, decision, notice, and effect packets for a field, it should also publish one narrow **review packet** saying which second-look lanes exist, which acts must pass through reconsideration before appeal and which may go straight outward, who hears each route, what record and standard of review apply, what interim relief or stay is available, what remand or substitution powers exist, and when finality blocks endless reopening — so the field does not decay into government by remedy maze, sponsor-friendly reconsideration, or hidden no-review zones.
- `761-vacancy-and-acting-office-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-succession-order-time-limits-limited-powers-public-reporting-and-no-government-by-permanent-interim.md` — Ideal governments should treat vacancies, succession, holdover service, and acting appointments as **continuity bridges rather than alternate constitutions of rule**: they should publish who succeeds automatically, who may serve temporarily, what powers are narrowed during interim service, how quickly the permanent appointment lane must reopen, and why courts, regulators, watchdogs, ministers, and public-service leadership should never be governed indefinitely by serial temporary placeholders.
- `770-internal-audit-inspection-and-inspector-general-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-risk-based-plans-direct-reporting-hotlines-case-routing-quality-review-and-no-self-inspection-by-line-command.md` — Ideal governments should treat internal audit, inspection, and inspector-general functions as **the state’s inside-assurance lane rather than an internal public-relations unit or a duplicate prosecutor**: they should run risk-based workplans, receive protected allegations, inspect controls and operations without taking over management, route cases to the right coercive or disciplinary forum, publish what can lawfully be published, and undergo quality review, so institutions are not forced to choose between silence, scandal, and waiting for external audit alone.
- `777-execution-of-administrative-and-judicial-decisions-against-public-authorities-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-compliance-clocks-budget-home-escalation-and-no-judgment-by-non-execution.md` — Ideal governments should treat **execution of administrative and judicial decisions against public authorities** as part of the rule-of-law core rather than as post-judgment housekeeping: when a ministry, municipality, agency, regulator, police body, prison authority, benefits office, land registrar, or treasury loses, the system should have clear compliance clocks, named responsible officials, budget and payment homes, interest and penalty rules, supervisory escalation, and user-visible follow-up so the state cannot turn delay, fragmentation, or lack-of-funds claims into a second victory after losing on the merits.
- `778-administrative-justice-timeliness-and-delay-remedies-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-priority-lanes-case-management-clock-publication-and-no-rights-by-queue-decay.md` — Ideal governments should treat **time in administrative justice as constitutional substance rather than an operational afterthought**: complaint, review, appeal, and enforcement lanes should publish meaningful clocks, triage urgency visibly, give adjudicators active case-management powers, maintain surge and backlog disciplines, and provide acceleratory and where needed compensatory remedies for unreasonable duration, so legality does not decay into rights by queue endurance.
- `782-administrative-guidance-circulars-and-soft-law-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-publicity-legal-status-clarity-consultable-updates-and-no-hidden-law-by-guidance.md` — Ideal governments should treat **administrative guidance, circulars, manuals, FAQs, enforcement policies, and advisory opinions as a compliance-support and interpretation layer rather than as a covert lawmaking lane**: guidance should be typed by legal status, publicly accessible when it matters to outsiders, consistent with enacted law, versioned and dated, consultable when it materially reshapes burdens, and reviewable when it hardens into de facto law.
- `816-oversight-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-member-scrutiny-external-audit-ombuds-routes-judicial-review-and-no-heavy-power-by-self-marking.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **who owns it**, **how money moves through it**, and **where its operating spine lives**, it should also be able to say **what oversight chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should remain mainly reviewable through the member governments that delegate into them, shared-service backbones should preserve visible principal-side scrutiny plus independent audit and complaint routes, bounded functional authorities should carry named external audit, maladministration review, legality or regulatory checks, and judicial remedy proportionate to their power, and general-purpose territorial tiers should own a full public oversight constitution rather than marking themselves through internal committees alone.
- `824-regulatory-and-enforcement-boundary-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-signal-routing-joined-up-inspections-bounded-permitting-public-sanctions-and-no-heavy-power-by-shared-badge.md` — When the archive has already established that a cross-boundary problem is real, chosen the honest form, and said who governs, pays, operates, votes, publishes, contracts, owns, and can unwind the arrangement, it should still require one compact **regulatory-and-enforcement-boundary chain**: thin connectors may align standards proposals, share risk signals, and route cases but must not issue permits or sanctions in their own name; shared-service backbones may pool intake, inspection support, and specialist process while the political principals retain visible legal title to permissions and coercive acts; bounded functional authorities may license, inspect, direct, and sanction only inside a named public remit with risk-based proportionality, separation from operation, and live review routes; and general-purpose territorial tiers may carry broader permitting and enforcement constitutions without letting host badges, fee addiction, or delegated vendor discipline become hidden sovereignty.
- `833-coercion-defaults-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-local-witness-municipal-civil-enforcement-regional-police-platforms-national-force-monopoly-and-treaty-bound-restraint.md` — The archive should answer the question **where should coercive and enforcement power ordinarily live at each scope?** with scale-matched restraint rather than one badge fetish: **micro-local bodies should default to witness, de-escalation, and referral rather than general coercive authority; municipalities should be the first ordinary home of civil enforcement, inspections, nuisance abatement, and everyday public-order administration under ordinary law; metropolitan governments should hold only those bounded cross-boundary enforcement and emergency-coordination powers that shared systems actually require; regional or provincial governments may honestly house large territorial police, emergency, and regulatory platforms where the constitutional order truly assigns them; national government should carry the thickest monopoly over criminal law, armed force, borders, and exceptional emergency concentration under the strongest rights and review discipline; and continental or global bodies should remain treaty-bound, relying mainly on inspection, reporting, sanctions, certification, and tightly authorized operations rather than ambient upper-state police sovereignty**.

## rural-governance

- `518-public-investment-and-procurement-by-scope-local-maintenance-metro-systems-national-capital-discipline-and-narrow-global-standards.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should govern public investment by keeping routine maintenance, small capital works, and user-visible asset stewardship close to the institutions that see failure first; using metropolitan and regional bodies for networked systems and place-wide project coordination; reserving capital budgeting rules, appraisal standards, equalizing finance, strategic procurement discipline, and infrastructure pipeline governance to the nation; and keeping the global layer narrow, focused on open technical standards, development finance, and anti-rigging or integrity cooperation rather than remote project micromanagement.
- `531-rural-remote-and-peripheral-places-by-scope-local-agency-intermunicipal-service-backbones-regional-catchments-national-territorial-solidarity-and-global-learning.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat rural, remote, island, mountain, and other peripheral places not as residual territories waiting to shrink quietly but as legitimate political communities with distinct distance, sparsity, ecology, and production constraints: local institutions should set priorities, steward place knowledge, and surface service failure early; intermunicipal compacts should provide the shared administrative and service backbones that low-density places often need to remain capable; regional bodies should govern labour markets, referral systems, transport, watershed and land-use spillovers, and adaptation systems that cross many small jurisdictions; nations should guarantee territorial solidarity through fiscal equalization, connectivity, service floors, fair resource revenue, and public employment and investment rules that do not punish distance; and the global layer should remain narrow but real in fair trade, climate and connectivity support, and shared learning rather than imposing metro-centric metrics on every place.
- `580-asymmetric-decentralization-special-status-territories-and-no-one-size-fits-all-stack.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should treat **asymmetry** as a disciplined constitutional tool rather than as a taboo or a patronage trick: keep a clear default stack for ordinary places, but allow differentiated powers, institutions, and finance for metropolitan areas, capital districts, islands, remote regions, indigenous or plurinational territories, and other genuinely exceptional geographies when functional scale, capacity, history, identity, remoteness, or constitutional settlement justify it; pair that flexibility with equal-rights floors, transparent criteria, published finance rules, review clocks, and routes into and out of special status; and reject both one-size-fits-all map worship and ad hoc dealmaking that turns territorial difference into permanent favoritism.
- `582-capability-congruence-minimum-viable-jurisdiction-intermunicipal-backstops-and-no-subsidiarity-by-fiction.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should pair subsidiarity with **capability congruence**: public functions should sit at the closest level that can actually staff, finance, procure, supervise, and lawfully discharge them; when small jurisdictions cannot sustain that floor on their own, the constitution should prefer **intermunicipal shared-service backbones, regional technical corps, explicit fallback lanes, and only then carefully justified consolidation** rather than pretending every map unit is a fully capable government.
- `590-multilevel-impact-packets-subsidiarity-territorial-effects-rural-proofing-and-no-lawmaking-by-placeless-abstraction.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should require any higher-tier law, regulation, spending program, or platform reform that materially affects lower-tier powers, finances, administrative burden, or territorial outcomes to ship with a **published multilevel impact packet** — a compact subsidiarity, proportionality, territorial-effects, implementation, and consultation record — so central action is argued openly rather than smuggled through placeless abstraction.
- `605-repair-ladders-for-multilevel-government-lane-fixes-connectors-kit-completion-cooperation-territorial-upgrades-map-surgery-and-no-reform-by-single-instrument.md` — An ideal multi-level polity should repair scope misfit through an ordered ladder: diagnose the exact pathology first, then clarify lanes, add missing connectors, complete the minimum institutional kit at the live tier, use intermunicipal or intergovernmental cooperation where scale outruns unit size, create or strengthen narrow special-purpose machinery only where a real functional geography demands it, upgrade to an honest metropolitan or regional tier when shared politics and multi-sector system governance are unavoidable, and reach for mergers, splits, or boundary surgery only after lighter repairs have been tested, consulted, and continuity-proofed.
- `661-collapsed-stack-rules-for-microstates-city-states-fused-tiers-shared-capacity-and-no-full-ladder-cosplay.md` — When a polity is too small, too urban-concentrated, too remote, or too capacity-constrained to sustain the full municipal–regional–national ladder as separate apparatuses, the ideal answer is not ceremonial duplication but **honest scope collapse**: fuse tiers openly where necessary, preserve functional separation inside the fused institutions, keep neighborhood and municipal voice where lived place still matters, pool specialist capacity through explicit shared-service or treaty arrangements, and refuse both fake federal pageantry and centralized one-office government.
- `749-ideal-governments-by-scope-micro-local-voice-municipal-competence-county-rural-pooling-metropolitan-systems-regional-platforms-national-solidarity-continental-compacts-and-global-narrow-waists.md` — An ideal multi-level order should not ask every scope to impersonate a sovereign state; it should give each scope the **minimum complete governing kit** that matches its real problem class — micro-local voice and upkeep, municipal everyday place government, county or rural pooling where density is low, metropolitan systems democracy where spillovers are urban, regional territorial platforms and shared rule, national rights-and-solidarity government, continental problem-specific compacts, and global treaty narrow waists for peace, planetary commons, and interoperability.
- `750-polity-morphology-archetypes-for-ideal-government-stacks-dense-metro-polycentric-federal-sparse-archipelagic-and-cross-border-overlay-with-no-one-world-default.md` — The archive should stop implying that one ideal government stack fits every country-form: before designing tiers, it should classify the polity’s **morphology** — dense metro-dominant, polycentric unitary, federal or plurinational, sparse and peripheral, archipelagic, or border-interlocked — and then choose the thinnest honest stack for that morphology rather than copying one universal ladder.
- `786-right-to-be-heard-and-oral-hearing-necessity-tests-for-ideal-governments-notice-of-adverse-case-paper-default-credibility-triggers-remote-option-and-no-decision-by-unanswered-file.md` — Ideal governments should require that **no materially adverse administrative decision is taken without a real chance to answer the adverse case**, while also treating **oral hearing as a triggered safeguard rather than a theatrical default**: written procedure can be the ordinary lane for many routine matters, but live hearing becomes necessary when credibility, disputed facts, severe sanction, stigma, complex expert conflict, or serious irreversibility make paper process too thin to be fair.
- `810-threshold-dossiers-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-metro-triggers-county-pooling-regional-platform-proof-fiscal-floors-legitimacy-thickness-and-no-tier-thickening-by-anecdote.md` — When the archive reaches a **live threshold question** rather than a settled scope doctrine question, it should require one compact **threshold dossier**: a declared threshold claim, the right territory and comparator cohort, a small set of named evidence lanes, visible contradiction residue, and a provisional confidence statement, so judgments such as **when metro democracy is now required, when sparse territories need pooled county-scale service backbones, when a region is a real platform, or when a lower tier is fiscally non-hollow** are made by typed evidence rather than by population fetish, prestige case imitation, or crisis anecdote.
- `812-institutional-form-choice-ladders-for-ideal-governments-of-each-scope-thin-connectors-shared-service-backbones-bounded-authorities-general-purpose-tiers-and-no-new-tier-by-spillover-alone.md` — When the archive has already established that a cross-boundary problem is real, it should choose institutional form through one compact **choice ladder**: use a **thin connector** when alignment and information-sharing are enough; a **shared-service backbone** when capacity pooling is the real need; a **bounded functional authority** when one system needs continuous cross-boundary operations or asset stewardship; and a **general-purpose elected tier** only when recurring distributive, land-use, borrowing, coercive, or multi-sector balancing powers make thinner forms constitutionally dishonest.
- `813-legitimacy-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-delegated-councils-principal-owned-backbones-double-key-authorities-directly-elected-tiers-and-no-heavy-power-by-convenience-composition.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, it should also be able to say **what legitimacy chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should be run by delegated elected principals with no hidden hard powers, shared-service backbones should remain clearly owned by the member governments whose duties they support, bounded functional authorities should carry an elected anchor plus explicit double-key gates for major debt, rule, boundary, or remit changes, and general-purpose territorial tiers should normally rest on directly elected chambers with their own scrutiny and executive responsibility rather than on convenience boards pretending to carry full constitutional weight.
- `814-fiscal-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-dues-and-service-payments-assigned-revenues-equalization-keys-capital-lanes-and-no-heavy-power-by-shadow-treasury.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary form is honest** and **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what fiscal chain belongs to that form**: thin connectors should live on modest dues and project-preparation money with no disguised distributive budget, shared-service backbones should run on principal-owned service payments and declared cost-sharing plus reserve rules, bounded functional authorities should use assigned revenues, user charges, or rule-bound transfers matched to their narrow charter with explicit capital discipline, and general-purpose territorial tiers should have a public budget constitution with own-source or rule-bound shared revenues, equalization, and visible borrowing limits rather than living by discretionary grants, annual pleas, or off-book vehicles.
- `815-administrative-chain-templates-for-cross-boundary-scope-forms-host-secretariats-principal-owned-backbones-chartered-operators-records-homes-and-no-heavy-power-by-borrowed-bureaucracy.md` — Once the archive has said **which cross-boundary institutional form is honest**, **what legitimacy chain belongs to it**, and **what fiscal chain belongs to it**, it should also be able to say **what administrative chain belongs to it**: thin connectors should use small secretariats with no hidden command over member administrations, shared-service backbones should keep declared principals, employer-of-record rules, records homes, and service agreements, bounded functional authorities should have chartered operating cores with explicit staffing, asset, procurement, and incident-command authority, and general-purpose territorial tiers should normally own their own civil-service, records, and operating spine rather than ruling through borrowed host bureaucracy.
